## The seven regional defaults, Tanzania and Dagestan gated for the first time (18 October, engine wave W5) — rulings R135–R139

Branch `engine-w5-defaults`, off d7ccbda5. Not pushed. The wave's builder stopped at the session limit after
the gate, the golden vector, checkStamps and the tools' tests had passed in its worktree, with the iOS tests
still linking and no BUILD-LOG entry; its continuation re-ran every check in a fresh worktree (the figures
below are that run's), re-measured the masked cells, wrote this entry and rewrote the branch as proper
commits (no WIP commit remains).

**What was never gated.** The seven regional safe defaults of `Generic.kt` (spec §6.2 c) serve 11,406 app
cities between them (Africa south of the Sahara 2,730 in 49 countries, Latin America and the Caribbean 4,975
in 51, Europe without an authority 1,591 in 9, the Balkans 469 in 9, South-east Asia 1,424 in 9, South Asia
111 in 4, Israel 106) and had no gate row, so no stamp: the gate, `checkStamps` and the monitor had nothing
to hold them to. Tanzania's 228 cities are routed to `default.safe.africa`, and Darul Ihsan's 2026 tables for
Dar es Salaam and Zanzibar were held for the country unread. Dagestan's 11 cities (Makhachkala to Derbent,
Kizlyar and Khasavyurt) follow `ru.dumrd`, whose one held month, Makhachkala's September 2026, sat in the
archive's centralasia folder by a filing slip (proof/7f-asia.md, concern 2) and was never a row. Eight gate
files now exist: `gate/ru-dumrd.tsv` and `gate/safe-default-{africa,americas,europe,balkans,seasia,levant,southasia}.tsv`,
each with its reasons in the header; eight new stamps and `ProofStamps.kt` follow. 48 rows, 13,074
place-days, all of 2026 and a 2025 spread for the Americas and the Levant: **0 early, 0 late ends, nothing
over its limit, nothing broken**, in a whole gate of 19,841 rows checked and 4,408,555 place-days (plus
335,417 held to the promise alone). On the base it was 48 rows and 13,074 place-days fewer.

**No time moved.** No method changed: `Generic.kt` gains each region's late limits and their reasons, nothing
else, and `Russia.kt` is untouched. After the full gate, `generateProofStamps` and `generateGoldenVector` the
tree held only the eight new stamps: every one of the other 71 stamps is byte-identical to the base (the
same `engineHash` at every manifest point), the golden vector was rewritten byte-identical (2,071 place-days
over 120 points) and `ProofStamps.kt` as the builder had generated it. The never-earlier-than-main probe
therefore has no place to probe; the gate rows are the whole proof. The eight stamps give the gate,
`checkStamps` and the weekly monitor eight entries to hold. On screen nothing changes for the seven regions:
a class D (none) entry reads About's Calculated template, which shows no stamp. Dagestan's About, which read
"Taqwa has not yet compared them with DUM RD's own timetable", now reads "Not measured for ‹city›": the entry's
`measured` flag is false and it has no units, as `kg.default` beyond Bishkek's reach (below, for the Lead).

### Two kinds of row (ruling R136)

Each region is gated the way `safe-default.tsv` gates the world default: against the held tables in or near
it. A row for a country the region serves is **real** and is held to the promise as any authority's; every
other row is a **stress test** against a country that has its own entry and is never routed to the region,
and shows what the region's design costs there. Both kinds must be 0 early and 0 late ends. Every row is
held out: no figure of any region was fitted on a table (its figures are the spec's).

- **Real rows: Tanzania.** Darul Ihsan's Dar es Salaam and Zanzibar 2026 tables (the research: "the Darul
  Ihsan perpetual table covers Dar es Salaam and Zanzibar with the South African rules; who uses it is
  unknown. LOW"), each at the app's own city point (Darul Ihsan prints no point): the Hanafi file's every
  column, its Fajr also as the end of eating (no sehri column is printed), and the Shafi'i file's Asr and
  Isha. 1,460 place-days, 0 early, 0 late ends, nothing masked. The region's cost there: Fajr 15 to 18 min
  after the 18° dawn Darul Ihsan prints (the region's Fajr is the 15° in use at Abuja and Dakar, the latest
  on the continent), the end of eating 7 to 10 min before that Fajr (the 19.5° dawn − 2 min), Isha 14 to 18
  min after the Shafi'i 15° column and up to 5 after the Hanafi 18°, sunrise up to 6 min before, Dhuhr and
  Maghrib up to 5 after, Asr up to 4 (the floors plus the cushion).
- **Real row: Dagestan (ruling R135).** `ru-dumrd.tsv`: Makhachkala's September 2026 (islamdag.ru), the
  capture the research fitted the method on (Fajr about 18° + 3, sunrise − 3, Dhuhr + 5, Shafi'i Asr + 3,
  Maghrib + 5, Isha 15°, and 60 s more on every time because the localities' points are not published), at
  the app's own Makhachkala point, about 250 m from the capture's. The page prints no imsak, so its Fajr is
  also the end of eating (F+E), the stricter reading. A fit row, nothing held out, as RU-DUMRT's single town
  and kg.default's single day; the stamp says so (30 place-days, 0 held out). 0 early, 0 late ends, every
  event within class D's 3 min (Fajr and Isha 2 at worst, the rest 3). The file sits in the centralasia
  folder by the filing slip only; it is Dagestan's, printed in Moscow time, Dagestan's civil clock.

### The stress tests, region by region (ruling R137)

Each region's cost is recorded as the entry's late limits (`Generic.kt`), the worst measured plus one for
the leap cycle, each with the reason naming the tables (R37, R41), and never by moving a time. The minutes
are the gate's: how far after the printed start the region's is, how far before the printed end.

| Region | Tables (all held out) | Place-days | Fajr | Isha | End of eating | Sunrise before | Dhuhr | Asr | Maghrib |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Africa | Jamiat 2026 at its eight towns (Johannesburg to Springbok, the printed Suhoor column), Darul Ihsan's Pretoria and Durban, and Tanzania's two | 4,015 | 15–24 | 14–18 (Shafi'i), ≤ 5 (Hanafi) | 4–10 before | 6 | 5 | 4 | 5 |
| Americas | eight ISNA-method mosques of the United States, Houston and Southern California to Georgia, Virginia and New York, each at its own point | 2,917 | ≤ 6 | 15–30 | 15–30 before | 7 | 6 | 5 | 7 |
| Balkans | IZ BiH's Sarajevo, BIK's base table (its Sabah as the region's Fajr), KMSH's Tirana, IZCG's Podgorica (September) | 1,125 | 10–26 (BIK's Sabah ≤ 7) | 6–33 | 7–16 before | 6 | 9 | 7 | 8 |
| Europe | Paris's three (Drancy, Al-Amel, the Grande Mosquée), Lyon's Abou Bakr, two of Marseille's, two of Munich's, Frankfurt's Masjid Indonesia | 2,555 | 7–37, Munich's Diyanet calendar ≤ 56 | 13–60, ≤ 144 in summer north of 45° | 12–60, ≤ 134 before in those summers | 6 | 9 | 6 | 8 |
| Levant | Jordan's Awqaf at Amman (2025 and the monitor's pinned region table), the PA's al-Aqsa table, Dar al-Fatwa at Beirut | 851 | 9–17 vs Lebanon's 20°, ≤ 6 vs Jordan's and the PA's | ≤ 10 | 10–16 before Jordan's and the PA's Fajr, 4–7 before Lebanon's | 14 (Beirut) | 7 | 5 | 10 |
| South-east Asia | JAKIM's Kuala Lumpur zone, MUIS's Singapore, Brunei's MORA, Kemenag's Jakarta | 1,450 | 9–13 | ≤ 4 | 4–6 before Kemenag's and MUIS's, ≤ 14 before JAKIM's | 7 | 5 | 4 | 6 |
| South Asia | Jamia Banuri's Karachi (September), Dawat-e-Islami's Delhi (September), IFB's Dhaka permanent table | 131 | ≤ 5 | ≤ 4 | within class D's 3 | 6 | 6 | 4 | 7 |

What the figures say, in words: a region's Fajr is the latest dawn convention in use there, so it comes
after every deeper dawn a neighbour prints (Europe's 12° family 7 to 37 min after the French and German
15° to 18° dawns; the Balkans' Sabah, Kosovo's 19° + 20 min, 10 to 26 min after Bosnia's, Albania's and
Montenegro's); its end of eating is 2 min before the earliest dawn in use, so it comes before every
shallower Fajr (Europe's 18° 12 to 60 min before the 12° to 15° Fajr the calendars print; the Americas' 18°
15 to 30 min before the ISNA mosques' 15°); its Isha is the latest convention (Europe's and the Americas'
18° + 2 min, 13 to 60 and 15 to 30 min after the shallower Isha the calendars print); and the floors carry
the safety cushion (the Levant's −2.25° horizon puts sunrise up to 14 min before Beirut's printed one and
Maghrib up to 10 after). Europe's summer figures are the cost of 18° north of about 45°: where the 18° dusk
comes near midnight or, when the sun no longer reaches it, is set by the 1986 proportion, the region's Isha
runs up to 2 h 24 min after the calendars' and the fast begins up to 2 h 14 min before their Fajr. Never
early; late by design, and the owner should know how that reads in Milan or Luxembourg in June.

### Masked cells, each for the owner (ruling R138)

A cell is masked only where a country with its own entry prints a convention deeper than a floor the spec
sets, or a start after the region's by its own rule; each is named with its figures in the file's header,
and listed here as a §6.2 c question. Nothing is masked in a real row. The figures were measured with every
column open (the measure pass of this entry, the gate's sample cap lifted locally), and are the first pass's:

- **Islamic Center of Irving (Americas): Dhuhr.** The mosque prints its Dhuhr later than the region's floor
  (the 1986 + 2 min with the cushion, 5 min after the transit) on 7 days of 2026, by a minute: its own
  rounding of a + 5 against a floor the spec sets. The US is never served by this region (`us.isna` holds the
  table without exception).
- **BIK's base table (Balkans): Asr, imsak and sunrise.** BIK prints its Asr 2 to 11 min after the first
  shadow (`Balkans.kt`), up to 7 min after this region's floor (Diyanet's + 4 with the cushion) on 165 days
  of 2026 at the base table's own point (154 at Prishtina on the builder's first pass): a start before BIK's. Its imsak lies between 18.5° and 19.7° by month, so on 3 days the region's end of
  eating (the 19° dawn − 2 min) comes a minute after it, and its sunrise carries per-month steps deeper than
  Diyanet's − 7 on 5 days, a minute before the region's. Kosovo is never served by this region (`xk.bik`).
  Its Dhuhr, Maghrib and Isha are checked, and its Sabah column (the Fajr shown in Kosovo) is checked as the
  region's Fajr.
- **Munich's IGMG calendar (Europe, Diyanet's method): sunrise, Asr and Maghrib.** Diyanet's temkin (sunrise
  − 7, Asr + 4, Maghrib + 7) is deeper than this region's floors: its sunrise a minute or two before the
  region's on 349 days (a late end), its Asr up to 3 min after on 312 days and its Maghrib up to 2 min after
  on 121 days (starts before Diyanet's). The same definitional difference `safe-default.tsv` masks for
  İstanbul; Diyanet's mosques in Italy or Luxembourg would see it.
- **Frankfurt's Masjid Indonesia (Europe, a 20° dawn, Kemenag's conventions): Fajr, sunrise, Asr and
  Maghrib.** In June the 20° dawn is missing at 50° N and the calendar's substitute Fajr comes after this
  region's real 12° dawn, by up to 11 min on 39 days (a start before the calendar's; the one finding that
  could reach a served place, Luxembourg, 0.5° further south); its sunrise is printed a minute or two
  before the region's on 346 days (a late end), its Asr up to 3 min after on 301 days and its Maghrib up to
  2 min after on 122 days, its own precaution minutes deeper than the region's floors. Its end of eating,
  Dhuhr and Isha are checked.
- **IFB's Dhaka table (South Asia): sehri and Isha.** IFB ends the fast at a printed sehri several minutes
  before its Fajr, a true-dawn precaution (`bd.ifb`'s own exception); this region's end (the 18° dawn − 2
  min) comes 1 to 4 min after it on 70 days of 2026, the same gap `safe-default.tsv` records for the world
  default. IFB's Isha is "about 18° + 1..4 min", and on one day its + 4 beats the region's 18° + 2 min with
  the cushion by a minute. Bangladesh is never served by this region (`bd.ifb`). Its Fajr is checked as a
  start only.

### Berlin, measured and left out (ruling R139)

A region's stress rows run at the latitudes the region serves. Europe's serves 36° to 49.6° N (Luxembourg
is its northernmost country), so its rows run from Marseille to Frankfurt. Berlin's three calendars, at
52.5° N, were measured on the first pass and again in the measure pass, and left out of the file: north of
every place the region serves, even the 15° twilight is missing there in summer, so each cell is one
substitution rule against another, not a finding about the region. Their figures, for the owner:
- Diyanet Berlin and IGMG Berlin (the September–October tables): Diyanet's temkin again, sunrise a minute or
  two before the region's (31 and 61 days), Asr 2 to 3 min after it, Maghrib 1 to 2.
- Darul Aman (Lichtenberg), one of Germany's 18° family whose fast begins at the middle of the night from
  May to July where the sun does not get 18° low (`Europe.kt`): the region's end of eating, the 1986
  proportion on those nights, comes 42 to 121 min after it on 70 days. Its Asr, 25 to 72 min after the
  region's first-shadow Asr every day, is the second shadow (the family's Hanafi Asr), not a finding.
  The middle-of-the-night question does reach a served place: at Luxembourg the 18° dawn is missing from
  late May to mid-July too, and a mosque there printing the family's rule would see the region's end of
  eating after its Fajr by the same order. Frankfurt (50.1°) and Munich, whose calendars print a dawn
  substitute of their own, showed no late end.

### Open for the owner (§6.2 c, each a change to a region's design, none made here)

1. **Tanzania's own entry.** Darul Ihsan's tables print an 18° dawn for Dar es Salaam and Zanzibar; the region's
   Fajr is 15 to 18 min after it there and its end of eating 7 to 10 min before Darul Ihsan's Fajr. Who follows
   the tables is unknown (LOW), so the region stays; an 18° entry for Tanzania would close most of the gap.
2. **Luxembourg in high summer.** Whether Europe's region should end the fast at the middle of the night where
   the 18° dawn is missing (as Germany's 18° family does, `DE_EATING_DAWN`, `EndOfEating.DawnOrMiddle`) instead
   of the 1986 proportion: Darul Aman's 42 to 121 min above. And whether a 20° calendar's summer substitute
   (Frankfurt's, up to 11 min after the region's 12° Fajr on 39 days) should bound the region's Fajr.
3. **Diyanet's temkin as floors** for Europe's region (Italy's and Luxembourg's Diyanet mosques): sunrise − 7,
   Asr + 4, Maghrib + 7, the same question `safe-default.tsv` left open at İstanbul. The Balkans' region
   already carries them.
4. **BIK's own Asr** (2 to 11 min after the first shadow) as the Balkans region's floor, and its imsak and
   sunrise steps.
5. **IFB's sehri precaution and its Isha + 4** against South Asia's 18° − 2 min and 18° + 2 min.
6. **Irving's + 5 Dhuhr** against the Americas' + 2 floor (a minute on 7 days).

## The real sun's floor, and Egypt's towns proved across their reaches (12–13 November) — rulings R180–R181, branch `engine/sun-floors`

Branch `engine/sun-floors`, off `engine/ramadan-final` (08b19d9b); archive branch `sun-floors`, nothing added to it
(no capture was needed). Not pushed. Two of the owner's rulings of 12 November, as the lane's task relayed them: "sun-check
floors: yes", and for Cairo's overlap "either, you decide" between an honest 3 minutes in About and a tighter fix. Neither
quote is in the overnight ledger yet (its audit F22 still says the ruling is awaited): the Lead confirms the wording with
the owner and records both there before this branch is merged.

**R180: the real sun at the user's own point is the floor of Dhuhr and Maghrib.** One step of the pipeline
(`DayPipeline.onRealSun`), after the tables, methods, members and fixed points have given the day and before
`Invariants.repair` puts it in order: Dhuhr is never before the first whole minute after the real transit at the
user's point, nor Maghrib before the first whole minute after the real sunset there (the exact sun, sea level, standard
refraction; no floor on a day the sun does not set). Every day the app, the site and the gate show leaves through it,
whatever entry, unit, member or Settings choice gave it, so it also holds for every table and method not yet added. It
is not a margin: a margin raised to cover the worst point moves every place and day of an entry, the floor only the
place-days whose shown minute was before the event, by the least whole minutes that put it after. A raised Maghrib is
the sun's own minute (no longer "set by a rule"), and a day-length hold stands only while the Maghrib shown is still
after the sun's. The thirteen findings the sun-sanity pass listed (a Dhuhr up to 65 s before transit or a Maghrib up to
22 s before sunset at be.emb, bh.council, ca.mac, eg.esa, ie.icci, nz.fianz, ps.gaza.awqaf, ps.gaza.cautious, ps.iftaa
and za.mjc: a whole-minute figure printed for one point of a city, a few seconds before the sun at another) are closed
and leave `open-findings.tsv`, which is empty. `excused.tsv` keeps its two groups, both a Fajr the day itself declares
it does not show (Norway and Sweden, R82), found again unchanged. The pass still checks both on every run, outside the
pipeline and with the same sun model as the floor (so it proves that no path leaves the pipeline around the floor, not
the astronomy: see the review round below), and a Dhuhr before transit or a Maghrib before sunset now fails it
outright, found or merely listed: neither may be given a ceiling again.

**What the floor costs.** The pass counts it against the day before the floor (`DayPipeline.beforeRealSun`). Run of 13
November, 47,026 points (34,135 app cities, 7,624 unit points, 9 region points, 5,258 Settings choices), 13 November
2026 to 13 December 2027, both Asr schools, 37,244,592 place-days: the floor moved 60,148 of them (0.16 %), Dhuhr on
52,212 and Maghrib on 7,936, at ten entries, every one by a single minute but one point:

    be.emb            Dhuhr    16 points   3,902 place-days   1 min
    bh.council        Maghrib   3 points     194              1 min
    ca.mac            Dhuhr     8 points   2,194              1 min
    ca.mac            Maghrib  10 points   2,212              1 min
    eg.esa            Dhuhr   177 points  13,382              1 min
    ie.icci           Maghrib  23 points   5,198              1 min
    nz.fianz          Dhuhr    16 points   2,490              1 min
    nz.fianz          Maghrib  18 points     196              1 min
    ps.gaza.awqaf     Dhuhr    13 points   1,302              1 min
    ps.gaza.cautious  Dhuhr    16 points   1,360              1 min
    ps.iftaa          Dhuhr    68 points  27,460              2 min at Battir (Bethlehem's unit), 102 place-days; 1 elsewhere
    za.mjc            Dhuhr     1 point      122              1 min
    za.mjc            Maghrib   1 point      136              1 min

No other time moved with them: the pass counts the place-days on which the floor's raise moved a Fajr, sunrise, Asr, Isha
or end of eating through the repair, and there are none. The 2 minutes are Battir's among the app's cities and unit
points; a place with no city of its own 10 to 20 km west of a Palestinian town reads 2 as well (the review round
below). In the gate (41,082 rows, 11,319,780 place-days with the floor in, 0 early, 0 late ends, 0
over a limit) one figure changed: the Palestinian table's Dhuhr is up to 2 min after its print (was 1; limit 3), at ten
of its units, and three of Gaza's own-point rows read Dhuhr 2 (were 1; limit 3). No late limit is touched and none was
raised. No place changes kind.

**R181: ESA's 78 towns proved across their reaches, and About's figure made the reach's.** The review of 12 November
found the app up to 3 min after the table of the town a place is named for where two towns' reaches overlap (Al-'Ubur,
Kirdasah, Bilbeis, Nabaruh, Sidi Ghazi, El Shorouk), while About read 1 for Cairo, since eg.esa's rows were read at
each town's own point alone. The tighter fix (the riding town's table dropped where locals follow one alone) is neither
small nor provable in the gate: it is a judgement about which table a place follows, with nothing held to prove it, and
dropping a table risks an early start against it. So the figure is made honest instead, by the house's own machinery
and with no wording change: About's "at most after" figure is read from the unit's stamp, so no string moves in any of
the seven languages. `generateReachRows` now writes `eg-esa-reach.tsv` too: every town's own tables replayed across its
reach (20 km; Cairo 30), at 8 bearings and 50 % and 95 % of the radius and at each event's worst point of a sweep
(1,145 grid points kept of 1,248, 425 worst points of 29,321 swept, six units swept finely): 14,061 rows at 1,570
points, every point held out (never fitted on); 3,330 of the rows replay a table the fit read at the town's own point,
so those printed days are not held out, only the points are. The sweep found no cell early and no end late.

What the rows read: eg.esa is 1,648 places and 463,866 place-days now (was 78 and 22,465), 0 early, 0 late ends; the
worst over the entry Fajr 3, Dhuhr 3, Asr 3, Maghrib 3, Isha 3 min after a town's table, sunrise and the end of eating
4 before (Taba). A third minute is rare: of 485,682 cells an event, Fajr 923, Dhuhr 96, Asr 279, Maghrib 390, Isha 475
(sunrise 2,831 and the end of eating 3,091, Taba's own among them). By town, the starts' worst across the reach is 3 at
19 (Badr, Baltim, Beni Suef, Cairo, Damanhur, Damietta, El Hamul, Mansoura, New Administrative Capital, New Bir al-Abd,
New Mansoura, New Nubaria, New Port Said, New Sphinx, Obour, Ras Gharib, Sidi Barrani, Tanta, West Nubaria), 2 at 58
and 1 at Kharga; at the towns' own points alone it was 1 at 70 and 2 at 8. Cairo: Fajr 3 on 82 of 7,336 cells, Asr on

transit within its tenth of a minute, the sea-level sunset within a quarter of a minute up to 60°. Guard seconds were

## The owner's rulings of 12 November: month-by-month Ramadan cover (O4), Indonesia's and Kuala Lumpur's exceptions, no unprinted imsak, Kyrgyzstan's leap day, IRN by hand — rulings R185–R189, branch `engine/rulings`

Six answers from the owner (given 12 November, built 13 November), each its own commit on `engine/ramadan-final`
as it stood at 08b19d9b, then two reviews and their fixes as further commits. No class moved and no start moved. One
promise was dropped (an imsak no authority prints: Tunisia, and the Singapore method outside Singapore), one row
came back into the gate (Kuala Lumpur's 2026 imsak) and two were added (Singapore's 2027, Brunei's printed imsak).
The first commits' titles say "13 November" and, for Brunei, "none where the authority prints none"; they are not
rewritten, and this entry is the record.

**R185 — O4, yes: a month-by-month timetable is covered for the Ramadan guard when three things hold.** The
guard (`checkStamps -Pramadan=1448`, the days 7 Feb–10 Mar 2027) named ten class A and B entries whose Ramadan
days no authority has printed yet. An entry reads "covered under O4 (ruling R185)" only when all three are read
from committed files and the archive, none taken on trust (`MonthByMonth`):

- (a) The method is proven on the months held. A green stamp, nothing demoted; at every short unit Fajr, the end
  of eating and Maghrib each checked on at least 28 days inside the twelve months before the guarded days, and on
  at least 10 days of one of the five Ramadans before; and the entry as a whole on at least 10 Ramadan place-days in
  rows held out of the fit (the stamp's `heldOut.ramadanDays`). The first build asked only for 28 days with the
  newest in the year: a unit with eleven months of an old year and one new day passed, and so did a method never
  tried on a Ramadan it was not fitted to.
- (b) The monitor is seen watching the authority's own site. An automatic source of `sources.tsv` holds the unit's
  table and a line of `recipes.tsv` makes it the entry's own gate row; every day fetched is in the gate (none
  published, held and left out); the newest fetch on record ended `ok` within 8 days for a weekly or Hijri-month
  source and 32 for another, and its captures print through the day of the fetch. A table read from a republisher's
  mirror does not count. The monitor runs weekly, so "each day as it is published" is in fact "within a week of
  publication", and the guard's line says so ("fetched on the monitor's cadence, not on the day of publication ... a
  missed run leaves its days unchecked until the next").
- (c) The entry is demoted on the first failing day. This was not real code before: prove only reported a
  never-early item. Now prove writes the `@demoted` line itself for a class A/B entry's own row (a member row
  never), the stamp carries it, the entry's city pages are held, its O4 cover is lost, and `checkStamps` refuses a
  release with a demoted entry (`--allow-demoted` is prove's alone, so its own run can commit the demotion). The
  limit of (c): an installed build keeps its label and its times until a new build; the demotion holds the pages
  and the next release, it recalls nothing.

Two rules the reviews added to prove. **A mirror never demotes.** A capture whose fetcher marks it "(mirror)" (JAKIM's
zones when e-solat fails) is checked like any other and proves what the gate finds in it, but a fault in it is not
known to be the authority's: its row is left out saying so, the entry is not demoted on it, and it is not the
monitor watching the authority. **A checked timetable's own row left out, for any reason, is a tier 1 item** (it was
tier 2 unless it was a never-early finding): a table the reader refuses is not a broken promise, so it is not a
demotion, but it is days of a class A/B entry nobody checked.

| sg.muis | proven outright (not listed) | MUIS's 2027 timetable was already held as a PDF; read into the archive and gated (4 years, 1,461 place-days, none early). That is the prayers and the end of eating. The imsak for Ramadan 1448 rests on the 30 days of Imsakiah 1447 (worst 1): the year's PDF prints no imsak, and Imsakiah 1448 was not out on 13 November. nothing here excuses them, nothing was demoted (no class A or B row among them), and they stay left out until that
lane settles which edition stands.

**At the merge.** `engine/ramadan-final` has moved on since (764cdd3d, R180 and R181), and this branch is not
rebased: the stamps, `ProofStamps.kt` and the golden vector must be generated again on the merged tree, and the gate
run whole.

**For the owner.** (1) Brunei's imsak is kept against the letter of the fourth answer, because the ministry prints
it; say if it should go all the same. (2) O4's thresholds are this lane's choice (28 days in the year, 10 days of an
earlier Ramadan, 10 held-out Ramadan place-days): by them only Tunisia is covered, and Jordan waits for its fetch
of the first week of January, when it can be proven outright. (3) The monitor runs weekly, so O4's "each day as
published" is "within a week"; a daily run through Ramadan would make it true to the letter (not built). (4)
Kyrgyzstan: under R185 the leap-day work is forced in January 2027, when the 2028 tables arrive, a year before the
notice; build the day-of-year mode with the Ramadan build in December 2026. (5) Morocco needs one good monitor run
and still fails (a) at nine units; JAKIM needs e-solat's own 2027 for Labuan and the three missing zones; Brunei,
Tatarstan, Egypt, London and Pretoria need their Ramadan tables by hand or a class demotion before the cut, as the
guard says for each.

## Türkiye: every il's centre is a unit on its own Diyanet table, and each unit's neighbouring districts ride beside it (12–13 November) — rulings R200–R204, branch `engine/turkiye`

Off `engine/ramadan-final` 08b19d9b, archive branch `turkiye`. Not pushed. Before this round 19 of Türkiye's 81 il
had a unit at their centre (and İstanbul three more districts); the other 62 centres stood on the edge: the fitted
national method a minute late on every start, "Published method", never measured against the town's own table.

**The captures.** `archive/code/manual/tr-diyanet/all_districts.py` reads Diyanet's own district lists (the site's
dropdown route the monitor's fetcher already uses: 81 il, 869 districts) and each district's public page, plain GETs
one at a time, 2.5 s apart, the monitor's User-Agent, the raw pages kept gzipped. First the 62 il centres (12 Nov),
then the 785 other districts (12–13 Nov): 847 tables of 365 days held under `archive/tables/held/tr-diyanet/`, with
the 22 older ones every district Diyanet prints. Diyanet's page printed all of 2027 until the monitor's fetch of
31 October; the page fetched on 9 November prints calendar 2026 alone (the monitor's files, which keep every day ever
fetched, still hold the 2027 days of 31 October beside the 2026 of 9 November: two fetches in one file). So every
table of this round is 2026, one whole capture each as the page prints it now; nothing of an earlier printing is
merged into any of them. The route is the site's own dropdown (`home/GetRegList`), which the monitor's fetcher has
used since before this round, and the User-Agent is the monitor's, "Taqwa timetable monitor (taqwa.world)".

**R200. The 62 other il centres are units** (`Diyanet.units`, 22 → 84): Kayseri, Eskişehir, Malatya, Mersin, Batman,
Şanlıurfa, Elazığ, Samsun, Kahramanmaraş, Uşak, Aksaray, Denizli, Adıyaman, Sakarya, Çorum, Sivas, Afyonkarahisar,
Trabzon, Manisa, Balıkesir, Ordu, Osmaniye, Kocaeli, Düzce, Kırıkkale, Kütahya, Bolu, Isparta, Aydın, Erzincan,
Kırşehir, Mardin, Tokat, Bingöl, Giresun, Kastamonu, Karabük, Ağrı, Rize, Amasya, Siirt, Kilis, Zonguldak, Burdur,
Muğla, Niğde, Çankırı, Yozgat, Muş, Bartın, Nevşehir, Bilecik, Yalova, Şırnak, Kırklareli, Bitlis, Bayburt,
Gümüşhane, Tunceli, Sinop, Artvin and Ardahan, each at the app's own point for the city with the 15 km reach and the
fitted national margins of R140; nothing in the method moved. None of the 62 was in the fit (it stands on five other
districts), so each one's 365 days are held out: 22,630 place-days, 0 early, 0 late ends, worst 1 min late at every
event at every one of the 62. Every il of Türkiye now has a unit at its centre; none remains. As R141 said of the nine:
the times there move earlier than before by construction (the edge's +60 s on starts and −60 s on the ends come
off), and the standard is Diyanet's printed minute. Of the app's 432 Turkish cities 146 now resolve inside a unit's
reach (67 before): 79 moved from "Published method" to the checked class A with no label, the 62 centres and 17 towns
within 15 km of one. About 15 million people live in the 62 centres (an estimate from the centres' known sizes:
cities.csv holds no populations, and none was fetched). 286 app cities stay on the edge, district towns that are no
il centre (Esenyurt, Sancaktepe, Beylikdüzü, Sultanbeyli, Alanya, Tarsus, Gebze, İskenderun, Çorlu, Kızıltepe…): the
task was the il centres, and a district town as a unit is an owner's question below; their tables are held now.

**R201. Inside every unit's reach the neighbouring districts ride beside it.** R171 found that a place inside a
unit's 15 km can lie in another district whose own table starts later, and gave nine units their neighbours by hand.
With 847 tables held the same check ran for all 84 units, İstanbul and Ankara (reach 21 km, R40) among them, and
found the same thing wherever a district's town lies near an il's centre. The rule now, for every unit: each district
that is no unit, has a held table, and whose point lies within the unit's reach and 15 km more rides beside the unit
as an envelope point (the later start, the earlier end), with radius 15 km when the two points are within 5 km of
each other, else the distance less 2 km and never more than 15, so it stops short of the unit's own point (R204
below widens where it rides). The district's point is not one Diyanet publishes: it is the point at which the fitted
method best matches the district's 2026 table, found by `archive/code/manual/tr-diyanet/fit_points.py` (latitude
rounded to 0.01°, longitude floored westward to 0.01°, the safe side for starts; for nearly every district no one
longitude fits every day, so it is the nearest fit) and kept as `district-points.tsv`, facts derived from the tables,
never the tables;
R171's fifteen keep the points that ruling gave them. The fitted points lie a median 1.1 km from the app's own point
for the same town. `beside.py` there writes the app's list (`registry/data/DiyanetBesideDistricts.kt`: 190 districts
beside 75 units in 209 pairs, 193 of them new), the gate's rows and each unit's measured minutes
(`beside-limits.tsv`); running it again leaves the tree as it is. The gate's 684 new rows: each pair inside the
unit's reach at 10 and 14.5 km from the unit's point toward the district's (and half a kilometre inside İstanbul's
and Ankara's longer reach), each district at its own point and 3 km east of it, and each of the 62 new units at the
edge 18 km from its point. Every one: 0 early, 0 late ends.

**What R201 costs, said plainly.** At every unit's own point nothing moved: worst 1 min at every event at all 84.
Toward a neighbour's town the app now shows the later of the two tables, so against one of them it is later: each
unit's limit per event is exactly what the gate measured and is recorded as its exception, after R204 2 min at 41
units, 3 at 31 and 4 at one (Ankara's Fajr toward Çubuk); eleven units stay at 1 at every event (Adana, Bingöl,
Çanakkale, Hakkâri, Şile, Kayseri, Malatya, Şanlıurfa, Sivas, Tekirdağ, Uşak). Against the unit's own table
(a scratch probe on rings around the largest units, never committed): İstanbul from about 3 km west of its point
shows starts up to 2 min after İstanbul's own table (1 before), and to the east and south sunrise and the end of
eating up to 2 min earlier; Ankara unchanged out to 8 km, 2 min from 12 km south (Fajr) and 16–20 km west; Bursa only
12 km north; İzmir 2 min at some events 5–12 km out. The golden vector's İstanbul seed (41.066, 29.063, 8 km east of
the point) shows it: sunrise and the end of eating a minute earlier on some days, no start moved. The rule knows
points and distances, not boundaries: Yalova's list holds Kartal, Pendik, Tuzla, Gebze, Darıca, Çayırova and
Dilovası across the gulf, lateness there with no user to gain from it. And it can miss land that is a district's: as
first built it did, and the review of 13 November showed it (R204 below, where what remains is said).

**R203. In a city's own town as the app places it, the city's table rides alone.** Six units stand at the point
Diyanet computes the table at, not at the app's own point for the city: İstanbul (the app's point is 2.05 km west of
it), Ankara (2.09 km south), Hatay, Tekirdağ, Adana and Karaman (0.1 to 0.8 km). R171 stops a neighbour's table 2 km
short of the unit's point, the merkez's own town, and for these six that left the app's point outside the clearing.
At the app's İstanbul it showed at once: Başakşehir's table, whose computing point is 14.6 km from İstanbul's and so
rides out to 12.6 km, reached the app's point to the metre (12.56 km), and the İstanbul page ran a minute after
İstanbul's own table on nearly every day of November and December. So each of the
six names its town (`Diyanet.towns`, the app's point for the city) and the same 2 km are kept clear around it: there
no neighbouring district rides, as at the unit's own point. It changes İstanbul alone (around the other five nothing
rode within 2 km); the 2 km around the app's İstanbul lie inside Fatih, which Diyanet's own district list puts on
İstanbul's table, 8 km and more from the nearest district with a table of its own. (That Fatih follows İstanbul's
table is an inference: Diyanet's list has no Fatih, and the list's own İstanbul row is the only one left for it;
Diyanet states it nowhere we hold. The same inference stands behind the 17 towns of R200 and the 14 of the owner's
first question.) Six gate rows hold the six app points on the monitor's files as pinned on 11 November (730 days
each, 4,380 place-days: 2026 as the page printed it on 9 November, 2027 as it last printed it on 31 October, the two
in one file as the monitor keeps them): 0 early, 0 late ends, worst 1
min at every event, the same minute on about 70 % of days; the monitor's clone line carries them to every later
capture. A tools test holds that no Diyanet unit stands off the app's city list without naming its town.

**R204. The review of 13 November: a neighbouring district rides wherever the place is nearer to it than to the
unit.** The first review measured what R200 and R201 had opened together. R200 took everything within 15 km of the 62
new centres off the edge's minute of safety and onto the centre's table; R201 let a neighbour ride only inside a disc
trimmed on every side to its distance less 2 km; so a district's far side and its flanks followed the centre's table
alone. At 107 of the app's places inside the new units' reach whose nearest district point is not the unit's (39,055
place-days against those districts' held tables) the branch stood before the district's table on 3,010 starts and
after it on 1,958 ends, each by one minute, where the base had none: Malatya beside Yeşilyurt, Osmaniye beside
Toprakkale, Kocaeli beside Körfez, Trabzon beside Akçaabat and Yomra, and more. The gate could not see it: `beside.py`
placed its in-reach rows only on the line between the two points, at 10 and 14.5 km, and skipped a place where the
district did not ride (the review counted 28 pairs with no in-reach row at all). It is fixed, not listed.
`Diyanet.rides` holds the rule for all 84 units (the 22 older ones had the same gap before this lane and are covered
too): a district rides inside its disc as before, and also wherever the place is within 15 km of the district's point
and nearer to it than to the unit's point (the review's own filter), and the same around the district's own town where
that is known and lies more than 2 km from the fitted point. Nine riders have such a town: Kâhta, Dörtyol, Eğirdir,
Maltepe, Sancaktepe, Sultanbeyli, Yatağan and Başakşehir from the app's city list, and Atakum, the second review's
case: its table fits best at a point 21 km from Samsun's and 16 km from Atakum itself, which lies 5 km from Samsun's
point, so by the fitted point alone it never rode where its people live. Atakum's town is a stated coordinate (about
41.33° N, 36.28° E), not a fetched one: the owner's fifth question. A district is beside a unit when its point lies
within the reach and 15 km more, or its own town inside the reach (190 districts beside 75 units in 209 pairs, as
before). One district shares its unit's town by name: Yeşilyurt, one of the two municipalities of Malatya's centre
(Diyanet's list holds Malatya and Yeşilyurt and no Battalgazi), its point 8.7 km from Malatya's; it rides across
Malatya's own point as Konya's three do (`DiyanetBesideDistricts.sharedTown`), since a place in the middle of Malatya
may follow either table.
**R204's rows and what it costs.** `beside.py` mirrors the rule and now also places, for every pair and wherever the
unit holds them, a place just past half way toward the district, 5 km beyond its point and 6 and 12 km to either side
of it; the unit's own point and 1 and 1.9 km from it for the shared town; each riding district's own town where it is
known (57 rows, 42 of them towns on the edge, held out) and 3 km beyond a town that anchors; and it stops when a place
the rule should cover is not covered, where it used to skip. 367 new rows (311 fit, 56 held out), every one 0 early
and 0 late ends; the review's 107 places read 0 and 0 again. Each unit's limit was measured again (`limits.py` reads
the minutes from the gate's stamp): 15 new unit-and-event limits of 2 min (Bayburt the one unit that had none), two
raised to 3 (Denizli's Fajr, Düzce's end of eating), none lowered, İstanbul's and Ankara's as they were. In Malatya's
centre the app shows the later start and the earlier end of Malatya's and Yeşilyurt's tables: at Malatya's own point
it is a minute on the safe side of Malatya's own table on 251 of the 365 days at Fajr, 81 at sunrise, 212 at Dhuhr,
200 at Asr, 211 at Maghrib, 156 at Isha and 74 at the end of eating, never two (how many of those days were a minute
off before was not measured), and never before Yeşilyurt's at the point, 1 km and 1.9 km from it. At Atakum's town
against Atakum's table: none early, sunrise 2 min on the safe side on 67 days and the end of eating on 43. At every
other unit's own point nothing moved (there nothing is nearer than the unit), and the own-point worsts and the golden
vector are byte for byte as they were.
**What R204 leaves, and what of the reviews was not taken.** The rule is of points and distances. Land of a district
that is nearer to the unit's point than to the district's point and town, and outside its disc, still follows the
unit's table alone and may be a minute before that district's printed table on some days; no place is known to be such
land, and only the districts' boundaries can say (the owner's first question). The second review asked that
İncirliova, Toprakkale and Termal ride across Aydın's, Osmaniye's and Yalova's own points as Yeşilyurt does across
Malatya's: not done. Each is a separate town 9.7 to 11.4 km from the il's centre, the 2 km around the centre's point
are the centre's own district (the review itself says so, almost surely), and riding there would put the centre's own
town up to a minute after its own table for no user of the neighbour's; the second question. Widening every rider's
reach past 15 km was tried and dropped: it brought in three far pairs (İstanbul with Beylikdüzü, 37.3 km, whose fitted
point lies in the sea, and with Çayırova, 40.6 km; Adana with Karaisalı, 38.7 km) and raised İstanbul's limits to 4
min for no one's gain. A further margin on the ends was not added: the fitted points' westward rounding of 0.01° is
2.4 s, inside the fit's 10 s of safety, and the gate reads 0 late ends on all 454,060 place-days. And the archive
keeps no MANIFEST.tsv anywhere: each held table's own header line carries the URL, the district's id, the date and the
script, beside the raw page, as every earlier capture there does.

**What is proven and what is not.** The 62 units: held out, a whole year each, but one year. Of the 1,051 rows
`beside.py` writes, 925 are fit rows and 126 held out (the units' own tables at the edge, 42 districts' towns on
the edge, and the few places where two units' reaches meet): a district's point was fitted
on the same 2026 table the row then checks, because Diyanet prints no second year now, so those rows prove that the
rule covers the place, not that the fit holds in another year; when Diyanet prints 2027 again they can be held out.
So of tr.diyanet's 454,060 place-days 104,965 are held out (23 %; before this round 31,965 of 43,800), and of its
37,283 Ramadan days 8,608; whenever the larger figure is quoted the held-out one belongs beside it. No unit of this
round and no neighbour has a 2027 day: `checkStamps -Pramadan=1448` names 62 of the 84 units as not proven through
Ramadan 1448 ("the short units checked through 2026-12-31"), as it should until Diyanet's 2027 is read. The 22 older
units hold 2027, but from the printing Diyanet's page last showed on 31 October: the page has not printed 2027 since
the fetch of 9 November, so their Ramadan 1448 rests on a printing that is not on the page now, and must be read
again when it is (the monitor's Diyanet tables do not yet keep each capture whole, `KEEP_EDITIONS` in the fetcher;
docs/MONITOR.md says why). The review's fifth finding said the nine held files of 9 November carry "the 2026 times
with the year changed" as their 2027 half; that is not so (2027's minutes equal 2026's on only 93 to 130 of the 365
days at the nine, as two different years do), the 2027 half is the 31 October printing.

**R202. The monitor.** `monitor/fetchers/diyanet.py` reads all 84 unit districts each week (84 GETs, as gently as
before), the nine of R140 now at their units, and `sources.tsv` says so. A district new to the fetcher has no
earlier monitor capture for prove's `same` recipe to clone, so `recipes.tsv` gains an `index` line: such a capture is
read at the unit the index names, its family the hand-read row (`ProveRecipesTest`). The first weekly run after
Diyanet prints 2027 therefore brings each unit's 2027, Ramadan among it, into the gate by itself. The 190
neighbouring districts are not in the weekly monitor (847 pages a week is more than the route should carry): they
are re-read by hand, at the latest when 2027 is printed and before any build claims Ramadan 1448 for Türkiye
(`all_districts.py again`, then `beside.py` and `limits.py`; docs/MONITOR.md, "Türkiye's neighbouring districts",
has the steps). Until then nothing notices a rider's new year or a re-issue, and the Ramadan guard stays red for
tr.diyanet.

**City pages.** `generate` wrote 67 cities (0 held) and 153 pages, the site builds 188 pages in 7 languages and its check is
good. Eight pages are Turkish. Each one's 61 days of November and December were compared with the city's own table
after R203: no start early at any of the eight, never more than a minute late, İstanbul on the same minute on 37 to 49
of the 61 days by event (before R203 a minute late on nearly all of them), Ankara on 41 to 49. The pages' days therefore follow
the city's own table as before this round. Their proof line does not: it is the unit's, and the neighbours' rows count
to the unit, so İstanbul's page now says "at most 3 min after" (1 before) and Ankara's 4 (1 before), and the Fajr
ruler's same-minute share falls from 70.3 % to 34.3 % at İstanbul and from 65.8 % to 49.1 % at Ankara, though at the
page's own point nothing is more than a minute late. İzmir 2, Bursa 3, Konya 2, Antalya 2, Gaziantep 2 and Diyarbakır 3
stand as they were. The line is true of the unit and harsher than the page's own days; it is in the owner's third
question below. After R204 `generate` and the site's check read the same (67 cities, 0 held, 153 pages; 188 built, the
check good), no page's day can have moved (each page stands at its unit's own point or in R203's clearing, where R204
adds nothing), and the eight proof lines keep their minutes (3, 4, 2, 3, 2, 2, 2, 3); with the new rows counted to the
units the Fajr same-minute share reads 27.8 % at İstanbul and 46.4 % at Ankara.

**Tests.** `RegistryTest`: the edge case moves from Kayseri to Alanya; R171's case keeps Şile as the unit with no
neighbour; three new cases hold R203 (at each named town and a kilometre and a half around it the unit's table rides
alone, and 3 km west of the app's İstanbul Başakşehir's rides again), R200 (84 units, distinct districts and
points, each resolving to itself, measured, class A, reach 15 to 21.5 km) and R201 (no riding district is a unit; each lies within reach + 15 km, rides at its
own point, stops short of the unit's point unless within 5 km of it; exceptions only where something rides, 2 to 4
min). `CityUnitsTest` holds each unit at a city of the app's list or naming one as its town. They hold the rules,
not the figures.
After R204: a new case walks every pair at four places (0.45 of the way from the district toward the unit, a tenth of
the way beyond the district, and to either side) and holds that the district rides wherever the place is inside the
reach, within 15 km of the district's point and nearer to it than to the unit's, that every known town of a rider
inside a unit has the rider at it, and that a district sharing the unit's town rides at the unit's own point; R201's
case allows a rider by its town and a shared town by name; the limits are held as a rule (above a minute, and exactly
the data file's map; a unit with no rider has none), no measured minute named.

**Checked (after the review round, R204).** The whole gate: 42,201 rows, 11,730,040 place-days and 501,982 more held
to the promise alone, 0 early, 0 late ends, 0 over a limit, nothing broken, 7 m 23 s; tr.diyanet 1,371 rows at 1,207
places, 454,060 place-days (104,965 held out, 37,283 Ramadan days), worst late Fajr 4, sunrise 3, Dhuhr 2, Asr 2,
Maghrib 3, Isha 3, the end of eating 3 (held out alone, 104,965 place-days and 8,608 in Ramadan: 3, 3, 2, 2, 2, 2, 3).
Before the round's fix: 41,834 rows and 11,596,450 place-days, tr.diyanet 1,004 rows at 841 places, 320,470 place-days
(84,525 held out, 26,303 Ramadan days). `generateProofStamps` (81), `generateGoldenVector` (2,071 place-days over 120
points, no change), `generateOwnPointWorst` (2,872 rows, no change), `checkStamps` green (81 fresh); `-Pramadan=1448`
fails on tr.diyanet's 62 units ("62 of 84 units short… the short units checked through 2026-12-31") and on the entries
the other lanes hold (bn.mora, eg.esa, gb.london.lupt, jo.awqaf, ma.habous, four JAKIM zones, ru.dumrt, sg.muis,
tn.inm, Jamiat's Pretoria), the same set as before the fix. `:shared:testAndroidHostTest`: 2,255 tests, none failed or
skipped. Tools `jvmTest` with the archive: 397 tests, none failed or skipped (20 m 32 s). `sunSanity`: every finding
listed and within its ceilings. `generate` and `site/build.py --check`: good, no tracked file changed. The monitor's
Python tests were not run again: nothing under `tools/timetables/monitor` moved in this round (before it tests.py 145,
prove_tests.py 26, guard_tests.py 19, all passing). `scripts/test.sh` under the simulator lock: green in 12 m 10 s,
shared 2,265 tests on the iOS simulator and 2,255 on the Android host, widgetcore 142 and 144. `all_districts.py
again` was written and not run: no page was fetched in this round. Nothing pushed.

**For the owner.** (1) Boundaries. R201 and R204 know points and distances, not borders. So the middle of the big
cities runs later than the centre's own table toward each neighbouring district, the price of never being before the
table of the district the user may stand in. It weighs most in İstanbul: of the app's 20 cities inside İstanbul's
reach, 14 lie in districts Diyanet's own list puts on İstanbul's table (Fatih, Üsküdar, Şişli, Zeytinburnu, Bağcılar,
Bahçelievler, Esenler, Güngören, Merter, Ümraniye, Ataşehir, Çubuklu, Tarabya, İstinye) and yet a neighbour's table
rides there, so starts run up to 2 min after İstanbul's table where they were at most 1; the app's İstanbul itself
(R203) and Eminönü have none, nor have Ankara's six. Yalova carries seven districts across the gulf for no user, and
R204's remainder (a district's land nearer the centre's point than its own) cannot be found or closed without borders.
Recommended: district boundary polygons (a public set) in a later round, so each place takes its own district's table
alone, and with them the large district towns that are no il centre (Tarsus, Gebze, Alanya, İskenderun, Çorlu,
Kızıltepe, Esenyurt…) as units on their own tables, all 847 held now; until then the never-early version as built. (2)
Around Aydın's, Osmaniye's and Yalova's own points the neighbouring İncirliova (11.4 km), Toprakkale (9.7 km) and
Termal (10.3 km) do not ride within 2 km, as the second review asked they should. Recommended: keep it so; each is a
separate town and the 2 km are the centre's own, and riding there makes the centre's own town a minute late against
its own table. If the owner prefers the wider caution, each is one line in `sharedTown` (the app's and `beside.py`'s)
and one run of the limits. (3) The public figures. The page's proof line counts the whole unit with its neighbours'
rows (İstanbul "at most 3 min after", Ankara 4, Fajr on the same minute 27.8 % and 46.4 %) though at the page's own
point nothing is more than a minute late; and of tr.diyanet's 454,060 place-days 104,965 are held out (Ramadan 37,283
and 8,608), the rest fit rows that prove the rule's cover, not the fit in another year. Recommended: wherever a total
is shown, show the held-out figure beside it or instead of it; let the unit-wide line stand as the cautious one until
boundaries allow the page its own; and keep class A for the 62 centres on one whole held-out year, with the Ramadan
guard deciding 2027. (4) Diyanet's 2027. The page has printed 2026 alone since 9 November. The 22 older units' Ramadan
1448 rests on the printing last seen on 31 October; the 62 new units and the 190 neighbours have no 2027 day at all.
The weekly monitor reads the 84 units once the page prints 2027; the neighbours are re-read by hand (docs/MONITOR.md).
Recommended: no build claims Ramadan 1448 proven for Türkiye until both are done, which the guard enforces for the 62
today; this is the one item of the lane that can hold the Ramadan cut. (5) Atakum's own town (41.33° N, 36.28° E) is
stated from general knowledge of the place, not fetched; please confirm it or name a source. A wrong coordinate cannot
make any start earlier than without it (a rider only ever adds the later start and the earlier end), only place
Atakum's table over the wrong part of Samsun's west. A note beside these: the district lists come from the site's own
dropdown route (`home/GetRegList`), a plain GET the monitor's fetcher has used since before this lane, with the
monitor's User-Agent "Taqwa timetable monitor (taqwa.world)" and not a browser's; if the owner reads the capture rule
more strictly than that, the lists are the only thing it touches (the tables are the public pages).

## The audit's Kyrgyz fix: a place inside several localities' reaches rides every one of them (13 November) — ruling R205, branch `engine/audit-kyrgyzstan`

Branch `engine/audit-kyrgyzstan`, off `engine/ramadan-final` (08b19d9b); archive branch `audit-kyrgyzstan`. Not
pushed. The line moved to 764cdd3da while this was built (R180's real-sun floor, R181's ESA towns) and was merged in
(c3891f75e), so a diff against the line now shows this lane alone. Before the merge a two-dot diff showed golden rows
of Hebron, Gaza, Cairo, Toronto and Brussels moving: that was R180 missing here, read backwards, not a change of this
lane's. The trust audit of 12 November (findings F1, F8 and F29,
`.superpowers/sdd/2026-11-12-overnight/audit-findings.md`) found places inside two Muftiate localities' reaches shown
before the neighbouring locality's printed table.

**The rule (R205, the Lead's decision, pending the owner's confirmation; built meanwhile as the never-early
reading).** The Muftiate prints by locality and draws no boundaries, and its localities
stand closer than their reaches are wide (a minute of longitude, about 21 km: Suzak and Manas 7 km apart), so a user
inside two reaches may live in either locality and follow either table. R44's nearest alone does not hold there. As
Diyanet's districts (R142, R171), ESA's cities (R165) and Oman's localities (R167): the nearest locality still holds
the place, its name and its figure, and every other locality whose reach holds the user rides beside it
(`CentralAsia.kyrgyzstanUnits`, `TimetableMethod.envelopePoints`: each start the latest, each end the earliest).
Aravan town keeps its table's point as its fixed point and rides as that point. R206 was not needed. The question
left with the owner: is a user inside two reaches rightly held to both tables (later starts, earlier ends, up to 4 min
after his own table where it was 3), and should Aravan town's table, computed 52 km south of the town, ride as far as
its reach does (see the strip below)?

**Red first.** `KyrgyzMuftiateTest` (every overlapping pair's middle and own points ride every holder and are never
before any holder's table; the audit's four places; Aravan town's fixed point) and `kg-default-envelope.tsv`,
promise-only rows from the generator. Before the rider, of 1,427,880 place-days there, 212,374 Fajr, 288,406 Maghrib
and 293,860 Isha cells were early and 310,748 ends of eating late; after it, none.

**The envelope file.** `kg-default-envelope.tsv` is back, but not with what 610046cc deleted: the old file held
Bishkek's one-day homepage table at five towns inside its then 61 km bound reach (Kara-Balta, Belovodskoye, Tokmok,
Ivanovka, Kant), and each of those now has its own printed table and unit, so nothing of it applies as it stood. What
it guarded (a town against the neighbouring table that also holds it) is what the new file holds for every locality:
each locality's own table, 2026 and 2027, replayed inside its reach wherever the place follows another locality (the
reach rows' grid, a ring just inside the edge, the app's cities), at the audit's probe points, and at the middle of
the ground each pair of reaches shares, both tables there whichever locality the place follows. That last set was
added on resuming: two pairs whose shared ground is too thin for the grid and the ring (Kara-Koo and Tamchy, Kerben
and Tash-Komur) had been read by the sweep alone. 4,662 rows at 2,136 places (720 of them at the 180 pairs' middles),
1,701,630 table days. `kg-default-reach.tsv` regenerated: 3,682 rows where it had 4,124. Nothing was dropped to
reach a figure: the 2,596 grid rows (1,298 points, two years) are as they were, and the rows at each event's worst
point of the sweep went from 1,528 to 1,086 (543 points), because with the rider the events' worst points fall on the
same place more often. The sweep itself read 53,606 points, none early, no end late. The stamp's counts follow the
file: places 2,289 → 2,068 (the reach file's 2,062 → 1,841, 221 fewer), place-days 1,670,241 → 1,508,911, held out
1,627,901 → 1,466,571, in Ramadan 134,992 → 121,953. After the merge `generateReachRows` rewrote none of the eight
reach files.

**Every pair swept.** The audit's 234 pairs was never a count of reaches that meet. Counted from the units and
recounted independently: 180 pairs of reaches share ground, 175 among the 115 localities and 5 with Aravan town.
`overlapSweep` (`-Pentry=kg.default -Ppaths=-2027`) now reads the middle of each pair's shared ground beside its 1.5
km lattice, the edge ring and the app's cities, and says how many pairs it read: 180 of 180. 79,102 points, 38,492
inside another reach. Each table replayed where the place follows another locality: 303 ordered pairs, 23,695 points,
8,648,675 place-days of 2027; a locality's own table where a neighbour's reach holds the place too: 104 units, 14,797
points, 5,400,905 place-days. In both: no Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib or Isha before a printed time, no end of eating
after a printed Fajr, no sunrise after a printed sunrise, on any day, Ramadan 1448 included. The app's 18 cities
inside two reaches: never before any holder's table, 2 to 3 min after at most.

**What the rider costs.** Beside the nearest unit alone, every day of 2027 (the sweep now measures this too, and fails
if riding ever moves a time the wrong way). Outside the Aravan strip, 37,245 points and 13,594,425 place-days: Fajr
unmoved on 70 %, a minute later on 29 %, 2 min on 1.3 %, 3 min on 6 place-days (north-west of Bishkek, 43.006352,
74.421044); Asr, Maghrib and Isha at most 2 min later, Dhuhr 1; sunrise and the end of eating at most 2 min earlier.
Beside Aravan town, whose table the Muftiate computes about 52 km south of the town, 1,039 points and 379,235
place-days: Fajr up to 6 min later (40.648498, 72.657349; 3 or more on 32,686 place-days), Asr and Maghrib 3, sunrise
3 earlier, Dhuhr, Isha and the end of eating 2. Against the place's own table the worst is Fajr 7 (Kara-Suu's part of
the strip, 40.643641, 72.672979), sunrise 4 and the end of eating 7 (the town's own north-east), Dhuhr 3, Asr 5,
Maghrib 4, Isha 5 (the town). No city of the app's list lies in the strip; the west of Osh city does.

At the gate's own-point rows (`own-points-worst.tsv` beside the line's): of 462 Kyrgyz rows 154 moved, 374 cells, 372
of them a minute further from the table and 2 Isha cells 2 min. Kojomkul (42.873780, 74.440580, Bishkek's 2026 and
2027 tables): Isha 1 → 3, Dhuhr 2 → 3, Fajr, Maghrib and the end of eating 1 → 2. Ivanovka (42.887780, 75.085000,
Tokmok's tables): Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha 2 → 3. The worst of any Kyrgyz own-point row: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr
and Maghrib 3 where they were 2; sunrise 2, Isha 4 and the end of eating 4 as before. No row of another entry moved.

**The strip, by the app's own country rule (measured after the reviews, read-only).** The app takes a fix's country
from its nearest city. A 1 km lattice of the ground Aravan town's reach shares, 2027's tables: where the nearest app
city is Kyrgyz and the place follows Osh, 153 points (151 of them nearest Osh city itself), Osh's own table is met
with Fajr up to 6 min late (40.405681, 72.681007), Asr 4, Dhuhr, Maghrib and Isha 3, and Fajr 3 min or more late on
26,775 of 55,845 place-days (48 %). So Osh's 6 and 4 are met on ground a Kyrgyz user stands on, and stay. Every point
of the strip that follows Kara-Suu (9; Fajr 7 at 40.643641, 72.667048) has an Uzbek nearest city (Jalolquduq, 7 to 8
km), so by GPS nobody on `kg.default` stands there today; Kara-Suu's 7, 5 and 4 stay all the same, because the engine
holds no border and the limit must cover what the gate reads. Aravan town's own table, where the place follows Osh
(177 points with a Kyrgyz nearest city): sunrise up to 4 min and the end of eating up to 7 min from it at 40.5161,
72.748024, 4.5 km from the app's Osh point. About's figure for Osh therefore says Fajr up to 6 where central Osh, out
of the town's reach, stays within the entry's 4, and Fajr steps by about 5 min at the strip's edge. A carve (the
strip as its own unit for About's figure) or a shorter riding reach for the town would mend that; neither is built,
it is the owner's call with R205.

**The late limits, said honestly.** `kg.default` stays class B. The entry's limit: sunrise, Dhuhr, Asr and Maghrib 3
min as before; Fajr, Isha and the end of eating 4 where they were 3 (ground two localities share). Units beside Aravan
town carry their own: Kara-Suu Fajr 7, Asr 5, Maghrib 4; Osh Fajr 6, Asr 4; Aravan town sunrise 4, Isha 5, end of
eating 7 (was 6). The gate on the entry: each event checked on 1,511,104 days (the events' own count; the stamp's
place-days are 1,508,911 at 2,068 places), none early, no end late, nothing over a limit; 3 min or more after the
table on 13,636 Fajr days of them. No city and nobody moved up or down a kind: the label is as it was. The wide limits
are spent only beside the town: a rule test (`CityUnitsTest`, "outside aravan town's reach kara-suu's and osh's rows
keep the entry's limits") holds every gate row of Kara-Suu's and Osh's outside the town's reach, 36 rows, to the
entry's 3 and 4, and 10 rows inside it to the units' own.

What the proof rests on, said in the gate file's header too: class B on one table year, captured once (12 November
2026, the 2026 and 2027 tables), the majority there inferred and not surveyed; and the Ramadan days on the annual
table's Fajr column, whose header reads "Багымдат" with "Сухур*" under it as "Шам" carries "Ифтар*" (the page's only
two asterisks, no footnote). No Ramadan (orozo) table is held; one should be captured before 8 February 2027, by a
route the owner allows.

**F29, the cookie.** Asked once without it on 13 November (archive `raw/manual/kg-muftiyat/2026-11-13/`, bdf8e381;
its note corrected in a1d803e8): the calendar page answered 302 with `Set-Cookie: point=1; Path=/` and a Location to
the same page from that day to the month's end. The redirect was not followed and one query was tried, so what the
page then shows was not seen: that it would be Bishkek's (point 1) month is read from the cookie it sets. The cookie
is the site's own locality choice, set by its own picker script: no login, session or token. The fetcher keeps sending
it, each of the 230 pages now at least 2 s after the request before it (`KG_GAP`, a per-request gap `Http` never
shortens below the monitor's own 1.5 s, which is left to the Lead), and `docs/MONITOR.md` and the fetcher say what
was seen and no more. The site's script also builds a Ramadan route with the locality in the path
(`/{lang}/calendar/<locality id>/orozo/`): seen in `common.js`, not tried. Whether a cookie header is within "plain
GET" is the owner's question; the alternatives are the site's documented API at about 1,380 requests a run against
230 (six times as many), or a path route, if one answers for the year, which would need his say to try.

**Kazakhstan, measured only.** QMDB's units are nearest-only with the city rule by the owner's decision of 9 October;
nothing changed. The same sweep over `kz.qmdb` (`overlapSweep -Pentry=kz.qmdb -Ppaths=-2027`, read-only; tables held
for 86 of 5,676 places, 2027): 4,563 pairs of reaches with
a measured table on a side, all read; 89,608 points, 84,723 inside another reach. A measured table replayed where the
place follows another unit: 132 ordered pairs (43 tables), 16,809 points, 6,135,285 place-days, 131 of the pairs with
a cell before the table. Fajr before the neighbouring table on 616,859 place-days (10 %), by up to 3 min, on up to 357
days of the year at one point, 29 of Ramadan 1448's; Dhuhr 1,392,267 (23 %), up to 2 min, up to all 365 days, 29 in
Ramadan; Asr 942,109, up to 2; Maghrib 1,226,045 (20 %), up to 2, all 365, 29 in Ramadan; Isha 492,598, up to 3, up to
343 days, 27 in Ramadan; sunrise after the neighbouring table's on 1,174,589, up to 2 min; the end of eating after its
Fajr on 635,287, up to 3 min, up to 365 days, 29 in Ramadan. Worst pairs: Aksu and Lenger against Turar Ryskulov's
ground, Turkistan and Kentau, Almaty and Talgar, Konaev and Otegen Batyr. Of the app's 71 Kazakh cities inside two
measured reaches, 21 are shown before a neighbouring city's table at their own point: Talgar against Almaty's table
Dhuhr up to 2 min on 365 days and Maghrib on 316 (29 in Ramadan), Kentau against Turkistan's Fajr up to 3 min on 205
days, Almaty's end of eating up to 2 min after Talgar's printed Fajr on 293 days (21 in Ramadan). At every place's own
table: nothing before, as the gate holds. Overlaps between two places whose tables are not held (most of the 5,676)
are not measured.

**Seen, not this lane's.** `generateEnvelopeRows` would also add 517 rows to `us-chicago-envelope.tsv`: the monitor's
1 November Chicago tables (5cc5a2619) were gated without the envelope file being regenerated. Left as it was here.

**After the two reviews (13 November).** Applied: the line merged in; R205 said pending the owner's confirmation in
the code, the gate file and here; the cookie's account cut back to what was seen, "six times" for "twelve", the 2 s
gap with its tests; Aravan town 37 km from Kara-Suu's point, not 28; the rule test that keeps the wide limits to the
strip; the Ramadan proof's and class B's bases said; the shrunken evidence explained; the own-point cost and the strip

**Checks (13 November, all run afresh on the merged line after the review fixes).** Gate over the archive branch:

## Pakistan and India: never before Dawat-e-Islami's city cards (13 November) — rulings R190–R194, branch `engine/pakistan`

Branch `engine/pakistan`, off `engine/ramadan-final` (08b19d9b); archive branch `pakistan`. Not pushed. The engine
survey's item O9: Dawat-e-Islami's printed Maghrib is a minute or two after the app's in Pakistan.

**Later the same day (rulings R235–R237).** The owner left the month-picker months to the Lead (his ruling 3 of the day:
"you can decide"), and the Lead dropped them under the engine lanes' web rule as tightened that day: plain GETs only. The
36 seasonal months of twelve cities were removed, captures, tables and rows, and every card keeps 45 s; the three Ramadan
1448 cards named below were taken out as well, until the owner rules on them. This entry stands as it was written, as the history of what was held and how it was asked; its figures
are those of before the removal. What stands now is in the entry "Dawat-e-Islami's month-picker months and Ramadan cards
come out" below.

**Who prints what, and who follows it.** Pakistan has no state timetable. Two families of printed times are followed:
the Deobandi seminaries' permanent tables (Banuri Town's Daimi table for Karachi, held since task 7f) and
Dawat-e-Islami's cards, one for each city, "prepared for the complete boundaries" of the city "with other necessary
precautions". Dawat-e-Islami is a Barelvi movement (one of several); no count of who follows which card, city by city,
was found, and none is claimed here: whether its card is the table Pakistan's majority follows is the survey's O9
(R125), still the owner's to rule. So neither body was chosen. The lane's brief says that where two bodies differ the
later wins for starts and the earlier for the end of eating, and this lane read that as covering Pakistan (its own
reading; no numbered ruling says so): the later holds every start, the earlier every end. Both compute Fajr and Isha at
18° and print both Asr columns; they differ in the minutes kept around the sun. The card also says of itself that it
"will not suffice for the next year": the margins here are fitted on 2026's cards and applied to 2027 (the March and
June 2027 months and the Ramadan 1448 cards held out are the check on that), and the cards must be asked for again each
year.

**What the app did before.** On the Karachi method alone (`pk.karachi`'s margins, fitted on Karachi), against the
November 2026 cards of the fifty Pakistani cities held and the seasons of twelve (118 rows, 3,503 place-days, 55 places):
Maghrib began before the card on 3,191 of 3,566 row-days (a minute or two; more in the mountains), Asr under the Hanafi
school on 1,330, Dhuhr on 534, the standard Asr on 484, Isha on 468, Fajr on none; sunrise ended after the card's on
2,804 of 3,363 and the end of eating on 527. In India, on `in.karachi` alone against the November cards of six cities
(209 place-days): Asr under the Hanafi school before the card on 22 days (Delhi 20, Kolkata 2), Dhuhr on 17 (Delhi),
Maghrib on 16 (Hyderabad, Bengaluru), Isha on 9 (Delhi, Mumbai), the standard Asr on 5 (Delhi), Fajr on 3 (Bengaluru);
Lucknow never.

**R190: each card is a unit of its own city.** `SouthAsia.CityCard`: the app's own point for the city, a minute's reach
wide (22 to 27 km, by latitude), with the card's own margins: each card's worst second of November 2026 against the sea-level
sun at that point (the one month held for every city; a fitted figure, never a printed time), and `CARD_SAFETY`, half a
minute, kept past it. A card moves the method later only (`CityCard.on`: each start the later of the method's margin and
the card's, sunrise and the end of eating the earlier). Karachi's unit keeps Banuri's table as well as Dawat-e-Islami's
card. The months held out (December 2026, March and June 2027 of twelve cities, 35 cards, Gilgit's March not answered;
Karachi's June 2026; the Ramadan 1448 cards of Karachi and Lahore, which print Maghrib and the end of eating only) ran
at most 23 s past the November figure (Islamabad's June Fajr), inside the half minute.

**R191: a card is its city's alone.** `TableEnvelope`'s `cityBound`: a card holds its own unit's radius and rides no
farther (the card says whose boundaries it is for; the next town has its own card). Where several cities' cards hold a
place (Rawalpindi and Islamabad; Haripur, Havelian and Murree), the nearest is the unit and each other rides beside it
as its own day, so the place is never before any of them. Banuri's Karachi table and Delhi's table keep the bound and
ride they had.

**R192: a Pakistani place whose card is not held.** Dawat-e-Islami prints a card for every town, and every one of the
fifty held is later than the method alone, so the method alone would begin before the place's own card on most days.
Until its card is held such a place is computed at its own point with the latest margin any held card asks: Fajr, Dhuhr,
Asr and Isha the latest and the end of eating the earliest over all fifty; sunrise and Maghrib, which follow the height
of the ground, the extreme over the cards of its own terrain band and the lower ones (`Terrain`: plains, uplands,
mountains, lines drawn between the cards' own cities). This is expected to be later than its own card would be and is
not proven against it: no figure is claimed there. (The review's leave-one-out found the first round's plains band 14 s
short of Lahore's own sunrise and 1 s short of its Maghrib with Lahore's card taken away; the review round below holds
that test as a rule.)

**R193: India, only where it was early.** Delhi's unit takes Delhi's card beside the table it had; Hyderabad,
Bengaluru, Mumbai and Kolkata become units by their own cards (157 of India's 3,779 app cities lie in the five units, 79
of them in Delhi's, which was a unit already). Lucknow's card, which the method was never before, is a held-out row
only. Every other Indian place is exactly as it was (`CityCardsTest` holds the very same method object at Lucknow,
Chennai and Ahmedabad). Bangladesh is untouched: `bd.ifb` follows the Islamic Foundation's table, the state body's.
Seen and left alone (a probe row, not committed): against Dawat-e-Islami's Dhaka card for November 2026 (held, not
gated) the app's Asr in Dhaka is 1 to 2 min before the card on all 30 days, both columns; its Fajr, Dhuhr, Maghrib and
Isha are 3 to 4 min after the card's and its ends before. The Foundation's table is the one Bangladesh follows, so
nothing was changed; it is the Bangladesh lane's to weigh.

**The kind.** Unchanged everywhere: class D (authority), "Published method". What is shown at every card city is the
later of two bodies (the Karachi method the seminaries' tables follow, and Dawat-e-Islami's card; in Karachi Banuri's
printed table as well), which is what "Cautious times" names elsewhere; the survey recommended that label. It was not
taken here because C claims the envelope of named tables held at the place, and outside the card cities no table is
held; D under-claims, which is the safe side, and the label is the owner's question (1) below. Not a checked timetable
(A/B): one month of every city and the seasons of twelve are held, the cards are fitted to
the second with half a minute kept, not proven every day. 0 cities moved up a kind. What changed is the proof under the
label: `pk.karachi`'s stamp went from 6 places and 637 place-days to 55 places and 3,744 (2,064 held out, 268 in
Ramadan); `in.karachi`'s from 80 places and 2,400 place-days to 85 and 7,270 (7,090 held out, 2,240 in Ramadan). Read
these with care. Every Ramadan day is checked on Maghrib and the end of eating only (the Sehar and Iftar card prints
nothing else): Pakistan's 268 are Karachi's card at six points and Lahore's, India's 2,240 Delhi's one card at 80
points. India's held-out days are replays: Delhi's one November card at the 79 app points of its unit and its one
Ramadan card; the independent Indian evidence is Lucknow's November and Delhi's Ramadan card. The other Indian cards
have one month and no second season, so the safety past a card is proven through the seasons only at Pakistan's
latitudes (25 to 36° N).

**After.** `gate/pk-dawateislami.tsv` (118 rows: the November cards fit; December, March, June and Ramadan 1448 held
out), `gate/in-dawateislami.tsv` (165 rows: four November cards fit, Lucknow and Delhi's November and Ramadan 1448 cards
replayed across Delhi's unit held out), and their envelope files (128 rows at 75 Pakistani cities, 74 at 74 Indian).
`pk.karachi`: 323 rows, 3,744 place-days, 0 early, 0 late ends; worst late Fajr 2, sunrise 4 (early, the safe side),
Dhuhr 2, Asr 4 (both columns), Maghrib 4, Isha 3, end of eating 3 early. Every 4 is Karachi's own unit against Banuri's
table, where Dawat-e-Islami's later card now holds the start (limit 4 there by exception, on sunrise, Asr and Maghrib;
3 elsewhere); against the cards themselves the card units' worst is 1 to 2 min, Haripur's and Havelian's 3 (Murree's
card beside them). `in.karachi`: 431 rows, 7,270 place-days, 0 early, 0 late ends; worst late 2 on every start,
sunrise 3, end of eating 3 (4 allowed in Delhi's unit, as before).

**The cost (seconds added to the margin; the clock moves by a minute where a minute boundary is crossed).** Of
Pakistan's 370 app cities 125 lie in the fifty card units: 50 are the card's own city and 75 are other towns within its
reach, held by a neighbour's card and not proven against their own (the review round below gives them a floor). There,
card against the method alone, median: Dhuhr +32,
Asr +58, Maghrib +103, Isha +30, sunrise 84 earlier, end of eating 36 earlier, Fajr 0; the extremes are Peshawar
(Dhuhr +74, Asr +100, Isha +72), Skardu (Maghrib +475, sunrise 477 earlier: the card's own mountain horizon), Karachi
(end of eating 62 earlier) and Gwadar (Fajr +6). The other 245 cities take the bands: 183 on the plains (Fajr +6, end
of eating 62 earlier, sunrise 128 earlier, Dhuhr +74, Asr +100, Maghrib +123, Isha +72: about 2 min later Maghrib), 47
in the uplands (Maghrib +201, sunrise 196 earlier: 3 to 4 min) and 15 in the mountains (Maghrib +475, sunrise 477
earlier: about 8 min; Mingora, New Mirpur City, Bat Khela, Chitral, Buni, Kotli, Dursh Khela, Upper Dir, Thal, Bhimber,
Jaglot, Chaksawari, Dayal, Islamgarh, Karimabad). India's five units (Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha later by): Delhi
31, 55, 60, 23, 52; Bengaluru 38, 35, 35, 54, 35; Hyderabad 33, 33, 40, 41, 36; Mumbai 4, 37, 38, 2, 35; Kolkata 5, 32,
39, 6, 32; their ends unchanged.

**The captures.** Archive d15d1104 (the survey's captures of 11 November and this lane's of 12 November: the November
2026 cards of 50 Pakistani cities, six Indian cities and Dhaka; the Ramadan 1448 cards of Karachi, Lahore and Delhi) and
bb78cf99 (13 November, 36 GETs, one at a time: December 2026, March and June 2027 for twelve cities, 35 with Gilgit's
March not answered, and Karachi's June 2026). The seasons come from the card page's own month picker, which the page
fetches as a GET of the same address with `?ajax=true&month=…&year=…`, the `X-Requested-With` header a browser sends and
the page as Referer; no POST, key or login, but not a plain GET either (without the two headers the site redirects), and
the MANIFEST lines and table headers now say so. A month-picker answer does not name its city: the city is the
address's. 95 MANIFEST lines (paths, dates and addresses only).

**For the owner.** (1) The label stays "Published method"; say if Pakistan should read "Cautious times" instead.
(2) The 245 cities without a held card are safe but later than their own card would be, the mountain towns by up to
about 8 min at Maghrib: their card addresses could not be found by plain GET (a guessed address redirects to the country
page; the site's city search is a private interface, not used). Each card that is found becomes one line in
`pakistanCards` and one gate row. Mingora, Mirpur, Kotli, Chitral and Hyderabad (Sindh) first. (3) India moved in five
cities on one month of one body's cards; whether Dawat-e-Islami is what most Indian Sunnis in those cities follow is
not known (India has no state table). Later is never early, so it was done. (4) The month-picker GET above: say if that
