### The review round (13 November) — ruling R194

Two reviews: "never early" (two blockers, three major, five minor) and "provenance and honesty" (no blocker, nine
findings). Both were right on nearly everything; what was not taken is said with its reason. The wording they faulted
in the entry above is corrected in place.

**1. India outside the five card cities was still before the city's own card (blocker): right, fixed.** The reviewer
fetched four more November cards and replayed them at the app's points: Asr under the Hanafi school before the card at
Chennai, Pune, Jaipur and Ahmedabad on 12, 21, 18 and 3 days of 30, with Dhuhr, Isha or Fajr early on some days at the
first three and Fajr on 2 days at Ahmedabad. So R193's "only where it was early" was five cities' luck, not India's.
The four are held (four plain GETs, archive 3322b3ba) and are units by their own cards, and every Indian place outside
the nine units is now computed at its own point with the latest margin any held Indian card asks
(`SouthAsia.indiaBeyondCards`, the same `latestOf` Pakistan uses; no terrain bands, since no hill town's card is held):
Fajr 62 s later than the method alone, Dhuhr 75, Asr 87, Maghrib 69, Isha 75, sunrise 15 s earlier, the end of eating
as it was. That is 3,555 of India's 3,779 app cities about a minute to a minute and a half later; 224 lie in the nine
units (Delhi 79, Chennai 50, Kolkata 29, Hyderabad 26, Mumbai 14, Pune 10, Bengaluru 9, Ahmedabad 6, Jaipur 1). The
reviewer offered keeping the method's own Maghrib beyond the units; not taken, because Bengaluru's card asks 145 s after
sunset and Hyderabad's 132 against the method's 121, so the never-early version takes the latest there too. Lucknow's
card stays a held-out row with no unit, the one Indian card the rule was not made from; the rule covers it (worst late
3 min). It is expected to be later than any Indian town's own card and is not proven against the ones not held; the
Himalayan towns (Srinagar, Shimla, Darjeeling), whose own cards may ask more at Maghrib, are the least sure.

**2. Kallar Kahar, an app city inside Chakwal's unit, showed Maghrib before its own card (blocker): right, fixed.** Its
card needs 244 s past sunset at the app's point; Chakwal's with its safety gave 227 s, and so did the upland band.

## Algeria: the 24 wilayas of Algiers's calendar and Dellys become printed units (13 November) — rulings R215–R219, branch `engine/algeria`

Lane "algeria", from `engine/ramadan-final` (08b19d9b); archive branch `algeria`, commits 0af58261, b48d279b and
ef47146b. Not pushed. The survey's upgrade "Algeria 55 wilaya" (its proposed R124/O10, a base table plus printed
offsets, never ruled): the rulings here are R215–R219 of this lane's block (R219 is the review round's, below).

**The tables.** The Ministry of Religious Affairs and Waqfs prints one calendar a Hijri year as three image-only PDFs,
one per base city (Algiers, Djelfa, Adrar). Each of the 12 month pages is the base city's daily table and beside it a
table of differences (الفروق الزمنية): one signed whole number of minutes per wilaya of the group and per start (Fajr,
sunrise, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha), valid for that page's month. The Ministry prints no daily table for any other
wilaya: a wilaya's table is its base city's plus its minutes. The 1448 edition runs 16 June 2026 to 5 June 2027
(Ramadan 1448 is its ninth page, 8 February to 9 March 2027); nothing later is published until the 1449 edition, about
early June 2027. marw.gov.dz did not answer from this Mac on 12–13 November, so this lane fetched nothing. The
`Alger.pdf` the archive holds is NOT from the Ministry's site: it is the Wayback Machine's copy of 30 July 2026
(`web.archive.org/web/20260730202403id_/https://marw.gov.dz/media/calendrier/1448/Alger.pdf`), taken by the engine
survey on 11 November. The capture note beside it (`archive/raw/manual/dz-marw/2026-11-11/README.txt`) gives the
address, the dates and the sha256 (a507117fddb58bcf3a9fa06346facb2d73f2a6f24779ad9c1950f194975c01e9). Two things bind
it to the Ministry's own file: Oran's whole column rebuilds the Oran table read directly from marw.gov.dz on 25
September (355 rows, the script's third check), and its Ramadan page's 30 daily rows equal that round's Algiers table
(the review, by eye). The three base tables are those direct reads of 25 September; no raw PDF of that round is held.
Djelfa's and Adrar's PDFs are not held, so their difference pages could not be read.
`archive/code/manual/dz-marw/marw_wilayas.py` holds Algiers's 12 difference pages as read by eye from the page images
(25 places: 24 wilayas and the town of Dellys, 1,800 cells) and checks them three ways before it writes anything: "by
eye against the OCR: 1800 cells, 13 the OCR left unread, 0 differ" (a second, independent reading; of the 13 cells the
OCR left unread nine are zeros and four are figures, each since read a second time by eye, below); "against the sun's
own difference: 0 figures outside the month's range by more than 1.5 min (worst 1.1)" (each figure against the
difference of the sun's own times between the place and Algiers across the page's month; it cannot tell four pairs of
neighbouring columns apart, whose identity rests on the header as read); and "Oran rebuilt against the September
round's table: 355 rows, identical". It then writes each place's derived table (Algiers's day plus the page's minutes,
355 rows each, `archive/tables/manual/dz-marw/2026-11-13/`) and, with `--kotlin`, the app's
`AlgeriaPrintedMinutes.kt`.

**Which kind, and why.** The 24 seats and Dellys are class B (a checked official timetable, no label), each within 20
km of its point. What the app shows there is the Ministry's own figure for the place, not a fit to it: Algiers's day
as the engine reproduces Algiers's printed table (class B on its own proof: fitted on Algiers's 1448 table, held out
on Djelfa's, Adrar's and eight days of the 1447 calendar) plus the printed minutes. Nothing is fitted at any wilaya,
but the 25 derived tables are no independent evidence either: each is Algiers's own fit table plus whole minutes,
written by the script that writes the app's minutes. In the gate they are fit rows, as COSIM's derived towns are, and
the independent held-out proof stays what it was: Djelfa's and Adrar's tables and eight days of 1447 (718 place-days,
58 in Ramadan). The gain of this lane is 25 places moved onto the Ministry's own printed minutes, not new independent
proof. It is B, not A, as Algiers itself: the Ministry's reference points are not published. The honest limit of the
proof: the Ministry prints no independent full table of a wilaya to prove base plus minutes against (the task's wish);
the derived tables are the Ministry's own definition, so the gate proves that the engine reproduces that definition
every day (Algiers's 355 days times each place's 12 pages), and the reading of the minutes is proved by the three
checks above, not by the gate. The rest of each wilaya (beyond 20 km) stays as it was, "Published method" and not
measured; Oran's fitted band stays "Published method", measured: on its one fit row, replayed at the seat, which the
band itself serves only for a place whose region is not known (R219); nothing printed is held for a place of the band
beyond the 20 km.

**R215.** A method may carry pages of printed minutes (`TimetableMethod.printedMinutes`): on a page's dates the day is
the base table's at the base table's own point (`FixedPointMode.TABLE`) plus the page's minutes per start; on a date
no page holds it is the method named for beyond the pages (here the seat's computation the place had before). The
pages are whole minutes the authority prints, held in the public repo as the PA's town minutes and COSIM's are; no
printed time is.

**R216.** Under printed minutes Dhuhr is never before the user's own noon nor Maghrib before the user's own sunset
(the month's one figure cannot follow a place's own sun day by day, and a user up to 20 km from the seat has a sun of
their own). R219 (the review round, below) carries the floor to every start, each with the method's own margin.
Measured across every reach after it: at a seat no start is more than a minute after the printed one, and within the
20 km at most 2.

**R217.** Each printed place is a unit of 20 km around its seat (Dellys around the app's point for the town), a table
carried to a town by a printed figure, as R118's are. (The 20 km is that of Egypt's and Oman's printed cities, R163;
they are computed as the later of the city's point and the user's own and so are no precedent for the table itself:
R219 gives it the user's own sky as a floor instead.) Oran's seat keeps its fitted class D band around that unit as
`31-seat` (to about 70 km: Gdyel, Bou Tlelis, Aïn el Bya, Arzew are unchanged), and Dellys is a unit inside
Boumerdès's wilaya. The gate's rows carry no region, so the gate reads a row's named unit as itself where it shares
its point with the one the point resolves to, or where its set chooses by region and the row's point lies within the
unit's own radius: Oran's September table is still replayed on the band and its derived table on the unit.

**R218, an early start closed.** The 24 printed tables are the first ever held for seats computed "as the later of
Oran's and Tamanrasset's fitted margins" (`dz.marw.wilaya`). Against them that computation was a minute before the
printed Dhuhr at 16 of the 24 seats, on 1,745 seat-days of 8,520 (M'Sila 212 of its 355 days, Annaba 188, Mila 187,
Jijel 184, Bordj Bou Arréridj 181, Médéa 167, Boumerdès 130, Aïn Defla 108, Souk Ahras 82, Tipaza 79, Tizi Ouzou 72,
Relizane 54, Guelma 41, Sétif 27, Skikda 22, Bouira 11), and a minute after the printed sunrise on 15 seat-days (El
Tarf 10, Tizi Ouzou 4, Souk Ahras 1); every other start was never early. The apps in the stores show this today in
those wilayas. `dz.marw.wilaya` now carries a minute more at Dhuhr (21 → 81 s) and a minute less at sunrise (62 → 2
s): with it the computation is before no printed start and after no printed sunrise at any of the 25 points on any of
the 355 days, and Dhuhr there is at most 3 min after the printed (1–2 at the seats, 3 at Dellys, which is computed at
Boumerdès's seat) and sunrise up to 4 before it. It applies to every computed place of Algeria: the rest of these 24
wilayas and the about 33 wilayas of Djelfa's and Adrar's groups are a minute later at Dhuhr and a minute earlier at
sunrise than before. The evidence is Algiers's group alone; for the other two groups the minute is caution, not a
measurement (the same calendar and the same rounding, and no table of theirs read to say otherwise), and they stay
unmeasured. Oran's own fitted method was before nothing.

**The gate** (as it stands after the review round). The whole gate writing stamps: "41107 rows checked (11328300
place-days) and 501982 more place-days held to the promise alone", 0 early, 0 late ends, 0 over a limit, 0 broken.
dz.marw: 31 rows at 29 places (5 before), 10,303 place-days (1,783 before), 10,658 cells per event: 0 early, 0 late
ends, 0 over a limit. Held out: 718 place-days, 58 in Ramadan (Djelfa, Adrar, eight days of 1447), worst 1 min at
every start and end. The 25 derived tables are fit rows: 8,520 new place-days at 24 new places, and Oran's 355 on days
the place already had. Of the 841 Ramadan place-days (29 places), 87 come from the tables the Ministry prints day by
day (Algiers, Djelfa, Adrar) and 754 from tables derived by its differences. Each of the 25 printed units: 355
place-days, limit 2, worst 1, 0 broken. The other fit rows keep their figures (Algiers's fit, Tamanrasset's 3 and Asr
6, Oran's band 3). Every other stamp moves its engine hash alone (the method's fingerprint carries `printedMinutes`,
and the day computer's floors are part of the engine); `generateProofStamps` 81, `checkStamps` 81 fresh and green,
`generateOwnPointWorst` unchanged. The golden vector is as on the base: its Oran point carries no region, so by R219
it stays on the fitted band.

**The app's own day across each reach.** A scratch probe (never committed): `PrayerEngine.dayTimes` with the wilaya
named, against the place's derived table on all 355 days, at each unit's point, on rings at 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17 and
19.9 km on eight bearings, and at the app's cities inside the unit: 1,506 places, 534,630 place-days, 0 starts early,
0 sunrises after the printed, worst late 1 min at every start (and sunrise at most 1 min before). The app's 173 cities
of the 24 wilayas: 81 are now inside a printed unit (Tizi Ouzou 12, Blida 11, Oran 8, Boumerdès 8, Constantine 6,
Annaba 4, Chlef 4, Mila 4, Guelma 3, two each at Sétif, Bordj Bou Arréridj, Jijel, Relizane and Tipaza, one each at
the other ten and at Dellys), 73 of them up from "Published method" unmeasured and Oran's 8 up from "Published method"
measured, to a checked timetable. After R219 (the review round's probe, also never committed): each unit's seat and 16
ring points at 10 and 19.8 km, with the region, 150,875 place-days: 0 starts before the printed, 0 sunrises after it,
no start of either school before its sign over the place's own point (least margins: Fajr 14 s, Dhuhr 7 s, Asr 10 s,
Maghrib 130 s, Isha 14 s), and later than the printed by at most 1 min at a seat and at most 2 within the 20 km (Fajr
19.8 km south of Oran in late June; Dhuhr, Asr and Isha 19.8 km west of Tizi Ouzou; Maghrib 1). The other 92 stay as
they were; against their wilaya's printed table (which the Ministry prints for the seat) they are, after R218, before
it on none of 32,660 city-days and after it by up to 9 min at Fajr, 4 at Dhuhr, 7 at Asr and Maghrib, 8 at Isha
(before R218: Dhuhr a minute before it on 2,922 city-days).

**Ramadan 1448.** The 1448 calendar holds it, so all 29 dz.marw units are checked through it (each printed unit to
5 June 2027; 841 Ramadan place-days). `checkStamps -Pramadan=1448` does not name dz.marw; it still fails on the
entries the line already named (bn.mora, eg.esa, gb.london.lupt, jo.awqaf, ma.habous, four JAKIM zones, ru.dumrt,
sg.muis, tn.inm, Jamiat's Pretoria), none of them this lane's.

**After 5 June 2027.** No page holds a later date until the 1449 calendar is read, so the 25 units fall back to the
seat's computation (R218's: never before this year's printed figures, up to 4 min after them, 6 at Dellys's Fajr),
their checked days end, and by R219 they are shown as what they then are: "Published method", not measured
(`Resolution.on`, which the engine's day carries for its own date). The monitor's new manual source `dz-marw` is due
2027-06, names the script and says the 1449 minutes must ship before 6 June 2027.

**City pages.** `site/cities.tsv` un-holds oran-algeria and constantine-algeria (the owner's to confirm, below): both
resolve to their own printed units, class B, measured, and show November and December. `generate`: 69 cities (0 held),
159 pages. `site/build.py --check`: 194 pages in 7 languages, all good.

**Tests.** `DayComputerTest`: a page moves every time of the base table by its own minutes on its dates; a date no
page holds is the day of the method beyond; Dhuhr and Maghrib never before the user's own sun; the pages need the base
table's point and to be apart and in order. `MaghrebProofTest`: each printed place is its own B unit of 20 km on
Algiers's table; beyond 20 km a wilaya stays as it was and Oran's band stays around its unit; on every page's first
and last day a printed wilaya is Algiers's day plus the page's minutes; and the seat's computation is never before the
calendar's Dhuhr on any of the calendar's days (red with R218's minute taken away). `RegistryTest` and
`RegistryCitiesTest` name Oran's band and Dellys's unit. The review round's (R219): under printed minutes no start of
either school is before its sign over the user's own point with the method's margin, Asr never before the shadow's
exact moment, and the floors move no sunrise; without its region no place is handed a printed table (Oran's seat is
then its band, and Rouiba, in Algiers and nearer Boumerdès's seat, is not given Boumerdès's minutes); a printed wilaya
is a checked timetable on its pages' dates and a published method beyond them, and the engine's day carries the date's
own label. Tests hold the rules and the Ministry's printed minutes, no printed time.

**Not done.** (1) Djelfa's and Adrar's groups, about 33 wilayas (Djelfa's: the High Plateaus and the north-east
Sahara; Adrar's: the south): their difference pages are in `Djelfa.pdf` and `Adrar.pdf`, which the archive does not
hold. marw.gov.dz did not answer from here; the only other copy known is the Wayback Machine's, where the survey's
`Alger.pdf` itself came from, and this lane took nothing from it (its web rule is the authority's own pages, and the
session's permissions refused the fetch). With the two PDFs in hand the same script and unit pattern take them
(Adrar's group prints a difference per half month: R215's pages hold that as they are). Their seats keep
`dz.marw.wilaya`, with R218's minute. (2) The rest of each wilaya beyond 20 km is not moved onto the wilaya's printed
table (for the owner, below). (3) The check list's `:shared:jvmTest` does not exist in this project; the JVM suite is
`:shared:testAndroidHostTest`, run in its place. (4) Oran is read twice in the gate, one place: its September table by
the band `31-seat` and its derived table by the unit `31`. (5) No Hanafi row is held for dz.marw (the Ministry prints
the Standard Asr alone): the other school's Asr is proved by R219's floor, its test and the probe, not by the gate.
(6) The ends (sunrise, the end of eating) follow the print and are not capped by the user's own sky (R118; the
review's fourth finding, below). (7) A place whose region is not known is computed at the nearest seat, as before the
lane, and that seat can be a neighbouring wilaya's (the review's third finding, below); the shipped app always passes
the region.

**For the owner.** (1) The Ministry's difference minutes (1,800 whole numbers) are in the public repo as
`AlgeriaPrintedMinutes.kt`, as the PA's town minutes and COSIM's are; the calendar's footer forbids copying it without
the Ministry's permission, and R69 bars copying a table. No printed time is copied, and nothing is pushed: this lane
must not be squashed to main until he has answered. If he would rather not carry them, the alternative is fitted
margins per seat from the same tables (class D, "Published method", up to 3 min late), which needs no figure of the
Ministry's in the repo. Recommended: keep the minutes (they are what makes these 25 places exact), and ask the
Ministry when the Complex-style permissions are next written. (2) All 1,800 minutes rest on the Wayback Machine's copy
of `Alger.pdf`, bound to the Ministry's own file by Oran's column and Algiers's Ramadan rows. Before the release:
fetch `Alger.pdf` from marw.gov.dz by hand (or from the monitor's runner), compare its sha256 with the capture note's,
and store it beside the copy; `Djelfa.pdf` and `Adrar.pdf` fetched the same way finish the country. (3) Oran's and
Constantine's city pages are un-held on this branch (both are printed units, class B, checked to 5 June 2027).
Recommended: confirm; to keep them held, put the two rows of `site/cities.tsv` back. (4) The 1449 calendar must be
read by hand in early June 2027 (about 1,800 cells a base city) and its minutes must ship in a build before 6 June
2027; from that day a build without them shows the 25 units as "Published method", computed, never early, a few
minutes late. (5) Whether the whole wilaya, not 20 km around its seat, should take the wilaya's printed figure
(mosques across a wilaya plausibly call by it): today the rest is never before it and up to 9 min after. Recommended:
yes for the towns within the class's reach of the seat, after one season of the printed units; left as it is
meanwhile. (6) The ends follow the Ministry's coarse monthly minute: at a seat the sunrise shown can be up to about 3
min after the real one and the end of eating up to about 3 min after the 18° dawn, as the Ministry prints them.
Recommended: keep (R118: an end follows the print), unless he would rather the app end both by the user's own sky in
these 25 units, which shows as 3 to 4 min before the Ministry's figure.

### The review round (13 November)

Two independent reviews of ffcceff76 (never early; provenance and honesty) re-ran the whole gate, `checkStamps`, the
lane's tests, the script's three checks, the OCR reading and the generated minutes (all as the lane reported), read
all 12 difference pages against the page images, and probed the units and the 295 Algerian app cities. Neither found a
start before the Ministry's printed time. Their findings, and what was done (ruling R219; app commits 21a8aa78,
ded9a0c7, fcc91b6a, a9e70fca; archive ef47146b):

**R219.** (a) Under printed minutes every start is the later of the printed table's and its sign over the user's own
point with the method's own margin for that start and none of the authority's minutes: Fajr the user's own dawn, Dhuhr
the transit, Asr of either school the user's own (the later of the method's model's and the shadow's exact moment),
Maghrib the sunset, an angle Isha the dusk. The ends still follow the print (R118). (b) A printed table is a place's
only by its region: a place without one, or with a name that is none of the 58, is computed at the nearest seat as
before the printed units, never handed a printed table by distance alone. (c) A resolution stands as of its date
(`Resolution.on`): on a date no page holds, a printed unit is the authority's published method, class D, not measured.

**1. The other school's Asr was before the real one, at seats too (review 1, major): right, fixed.** The calendar
prints the Standard Asr alone, and the lane gave the other school Algiers's own plus a figure printed for another
shadow: early at seven seats (M'Sila on 11 seat-days; 13 s at Oum El Bouaghi's on 12 January 2027), up to 73 s within
the 20 km, 690 city-days in 30 app cities to 5 June 2027; before the lane those places held 195 s. R219 (a) floors it
by the user's own Asr of that school. After: 0 early at every seat, ring point and city of the probe, least margin 10
s.

**2. Fajr, Asr and Isha on default settings were before the user's own sky within the 20 km (review 1, major, for the
owner's ruling): right, fixed without waiting for a ruling, on the never-early side.** A seat's printed minute is its
centre's, and a place to its west or south sees each sign later: Fajr up to 63 s early (19.8 km south-west of Mila),
Asr 49 s, Isha 65 s; in app cities 191, 282 and 143 city-days. R219 (a). Cost: nothing over the print at the seats'
gate rows (still at most 1 min late), and within the 20 km at most 2 min after the printed figure where the lane was
at most 1. The precedent cited for the unit was wrong, as the review says: R163's cities are the later of two points;
the like is R118 (corrected above and in `Maghreb.kt`).

**3. Without a region a place could be handed a neighbouring wilaya's printed table (review 1, minor): right, fixed.**
Rouiba, Reghaïa and Aïn Taya (Algiers) took Boumerdès's, Naciria (Boumerdès) Tizi Ouzou's, Kolea (Tipaza) Blida's.
R219 (b): of the 295 app cities read without their region, none is on a printed table now. What is left is the path
much as it was before the lane (the nearest seat's unit, with R218's minute), which only the gate, the tools and a
location stored without a region take: against their own wilaya's printed table 12 cities are before it on 5,509
event-days, at most 3 min (Larbaâ, in Blida, read as Algiers's), and 11 have a sunrise after it on 1,027; the review
counted 27 such cities on the lane's head and 92 on the base. Not closed here: it needs every place's wilaya from its
point (the wilaya borders), which the registry does not hold for Algeria.

**4. The ends follow the Ministry's coarse monthly minute (review 1, minor, the owner should know; its cap optional):
the cap is not taken.** Sunrise is never after the printed one and the end of eating never after the printed Fajr;
against the real sky the review has the sunrise up to 168 s late at a seat (Relizane) and the end of
eating up to 196 s after the 18° dawn (M'Sila), 215 s and 206 s at Zemoura. That is the Ministry's own
print (its Fajr at M'Sila is 16 to 196 s after the 18° dawn), and R118 has an end follow the print. The cap would put
both 3 to 4 min off the Ministry's figure at the seats themselves, over class B's limit of 2: the 25 units would stop
being the Ministry's table. For the owner (6).

**5. R216's floor carried no margin (review 1, minor): right, fixed.** Dhuhr 19.8 km south-west of Blida stood 1 s
after the user's transit where the method holds 7. Every floor of R219 (a) carries the method's own margin; least
Dhuhr margin now 7 s.

**6. R218 makes every computed Algerian place a minute more cautious on Algiers's evidence alone (review 1, info;
review 2's fourth): said so,** in R218 above and in `Maghreb.kt`.

**7. The only raw capture is the Wayback Machine's copy, and only a private docstring said so (review 2, high): right,
fixed.** The capture note now exists beside the PDF (address, capture time, the survey's date, the full sha256, what
binds it); the script, the 25 derived tables' headers, the 25 MANIFEST notes, the monitor's source line, the gate's
comment and this entry say "the Wayback Machine's copy of 30 Jul 2026". For the owner (2).

**8. "Held out" was overclaimed (review 2, high): right, fixed.** The 25 derived rows are `fit`, as COSIM's are, and
the stamps are regenerated: dz.marw's held-out is 718 place-days (58 in Ramadan), where the lane's stamp said 9,238
(754). The About screen's count (29 places, 10,303 place-days) is the gate's count of places and days reproduced,
which it is; `ProofStamps.kt` carries no held-out figure and did not change.

**9. From 6 June 2027 the 25 units kept class B, no label, on a computation (review 2, medium): right, fixed,** R219
(c), with the release line in the monitor's source. For the owner (4).

**10. Owner decisions taken on the branch (review 2, medium): right, listed.** For the owner (1) and (3); the 33
unmeasured seats in R218.

**11. The primary reading was not stored as a capture (review 2, medium): right, fixed.** `MANIFEST.tsv` now has lines
for the reading, its OCR second reading and the raw PDF (with its sha256), and each of the 25 notes names the direct
read of 25 September, the Wayback address, its timestamp and the fetch date.

**12. Four figures rested on one reading (review 2, low): right, fixed.** Of the 13 cells the OCR left unread nine are
zeros and four are figures: month 5 Skikda's Dhuhr and month 6 Bordj Bou Arréridj's Maghrib, read again by eye from
page crops in this round, and month 8 Boumerdès's Maghrib and Isha, read again by the review; all four as first read.
The script says so, and that the sun check cannot tell Constantine from Mila, Bordj Bou Arréridj from M'Sila, Tizi
Ouzou from Dellys or Blida from Médéa: those columns' identity rests on the header (the review confirmed it on two
pages).

**13. Oran's band is "measured" on a row at a point it did not serve (review 2, low): right, said,** in R217's text,
the gate's comment and above; and by R219 (b) a place at the seat without a region is the band again, so the row is at
a point the band serves.

**Checks after the round.** The whole gate (stamps written): "41107 rows checked (11328300 place-days) and 501982 more
place-days held to the promise alone", exit 0, 6 m 22 s. `generateProofStamps`: 81, the file unchanged.
`generateGoldenVector`: 2,071 place-days over 120 points, the file as on the base. `generateOwnPointWorst`: 2,872
rows, unchanged. `checkStamps`: "81 entries — every stamp fresh and green, ProofStamps.kt matches the committed
stamps." `sunSanity`: every finding listed, every excused group within its ceilings. The monitor's Python tests: 145,
19 and 26, OK. `:shared:testAndroidHostTest` (in place of `:shared:jvmTest`): 2,262 tests, 0 failed. `generate`: 69
cities (0 held), 159 pages; `site/build.py --check`: 194 pages in 7 languages, all good. `scripts/test.sh` under the
simulator lock: BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 8 m 26 s (`:shared` 2,272 tests on the iOS simulator and 2,262 on the host, 0
failed; `:widgetcore` up to date).

**For the merger.** The Ramadan line has moved past this lane's base and nothing of it is merged here. On the merged
line regenerate: `tools/timetables/official/stamps/*.json` (the whole gate, writing stamps: the engine hash moves in
all 81), `ProofStamps.kt` (`generateProofStamps`), `GoldenVectorData.kt` (`generateGoldenVector`),

is not committed.

## Algeria: the 25 places of Algiers's calendar are fitted units, and none of the Ministry's minutes is in the app (13 November) — rulings R230–R234, branch `engine/algeria-fitted`

Lane "algeria-fitted", from the Ramadan line (47ebb5bff); archive branch `algeria-fitted` (from efe95a3b), commits
b72e89af and 608ab153. Not pushed. Amended on 13–14 November after two reviews (never early; provenance and honesty):
R231 and R234 read below as revised, and "The review round" at the end says what each replaced. It answers the
question the entry above left with the owner (its "For the owner" (1)): his ruling of 13 November is fitted margins costing up to 3 minutes late, and none of the Ministry's printed difference
minutes in public code. Everything the entry above says of printed units, of `TimetableMethod.printedMinutes`, of
`AlgeriaPrintedMinutes.kt`, of class B at the 25 places and of the two un-held city pages is superseded here; its
reading of the calendar, its three checks of that reading, R218's minute and R219 (a) and (b) stand.

**What left the public repo.** `AlgeriaPrintedMinutes.kt` (the 1,800 difference figures of Algiers's twelve month
pages) is deleted, and with it the mechanism that carried them: `TimetableMethod.printedMinutes`, the day computer's
page lookup and its floors, the engine's and the registry's date-bound resolution (`Resolution.on`) and their tests
(a small date-bound piece of another kind came back in the review round, carrying no figure of anyone's: R231).
No other authority used the mechanism (the PA's towns and COSIM's ride as R118's fixed offsets, a different path), and
keeping it would have kept a door for printed pages in public code, so it is gone, not left unused. The figures and
the 25 tables they make stay where they were read: in the private archive
(`archive/tables/manual/dz-marw/2026-11-13/`), where the gate reads them. The archive's `marw_wilayas.py` no longer
writes a Kotlin file. In public code, tests, the gate's header, the monitor's line, `MANIFEST.tsv` and this log the minutes
are described, never listed, and how the Ministry's monthly figure sits against a place's own curve (the private script's
reading of it) is not described at all: it is beside the tables, in `marw_fit.py`.

**R230. The 25 places are fitted units, class D.** Within 20 km of its seat, each of the 24 wilayas of Algiers's
calendar, and Dellys, is Algiers's method computed at the seat's own point with one margin per time, constant through
the year (`Maghreb.fittedSeats`, 25 seats by 7 times, whole seconds, Taqwa's own). The margins are the smallest that
put no start before, and no sunrise or end of eating after, the place's privately held table on any of its 355 days
(16 June 2026 to 5 June 2027), and that keep the spare of R231. The class is D, "Published method", measured on the
calendar's days (R231: through its last day and no further), with the figure the fit found: at most 3 minutes after
the Ministry's time. It is no longer B: a checked timetable is the
table itself, and the app no longer carries it. Algiers, Djelfa and Adrar keep class B on their own directly held
tables, unchanged. Oran: the table held for it since September is itself Algiers's and Oran's monthly differences
(the same 355 rows as the derived one), so what it earns is what it earned before the printed units: class D, fitted,
measured, at most 3 minutes late. Tamanrasset is unchanged on the held days (class D, 3 and Asr 6).

**R231 (as revised in the review round). The days the calendar does not hold: the spare, and the last held day.** A
fit sees one whole minute a month, so the held days alone do not bound a day the calendar does not hold (6 to 15 June
2027 before the 1449 calendar begins; every later calendar): the Hijri months fall about eleven days earlier each
year, and a month's one figure then sits over other days of the seat's own curve. Two things answer that.

*The spare.* The private script reads how the Ministry's monthly figure sits against the place's own curve (its own
reading, set out beside the tables and not here; not a statement of the Ministry's). Each margin is also past a bound
on what that reading can give on any day from 6 June 2027 to 30 June 2028, for every 30-day window at each of its 30
phases (wherever the month pages may fall), with 8 s allowed for where the held figures leave the reading, and
Algiers's own time taken as late as the app shows it. Of the 1,800 held cells 1,702 keep the reading exactly and 98
miss it, by up to 7 s: 83 one way by 1 to 7 s, 15 the other by 0 to 7 s. In all 175 seat-times the bound is past what
the held days alone need: the margin stands 9 to 77 s beyond the held days' bare need (29 s at the middle one; 4 to
72 s beyond a plain fit with its 5 s of safety). Why not more: at 9 s of allowance Relizane's Fajr would be 4 min
late on some held days, at 12 s three more times (Oran's Fajr, M'Sila's and Relizane's Isha); the owner's bound is 3.

*What the spare is not.* It is a reading of one calendar, made on the same days the margins were fitted on, and the
bound still leans on those pages: the allowance is taken from them. On the side that can make a start early it has
one second to spare: the widest miss is 7 s, at Béjaïa alone, and the other 24 places would have given 6 s (their
widest, 5 s, and one), so with Béjaïa left out of the reading the allowance would not have covered Béjaïa. No day of
these 25 places is held out, and every gate row of theirs is a fit row. The spare is spare, not proof.

*The last held day.* So the margins stand as they are only through 5 June 2027, the calendar's last day
(`Maghreb.lastHeldDay`). After it, at the 25 places, in Oran's band and at Tamanrasset (both fitted on a derived 1448
table in the same way, with nothing held out), every start is a whole minute later, and sunrise and the end of
eating a whole minute earlier, than the margins give (`Maghreb.beyondHeldDays`: the same method with each margin a
minute to the safe side, as a day alongside that rides only after the date, `Alongside.after`). And the place claims
no figure there: the label stays "Published method", and About says the place is not measured, with no "checked on
N days" and no "up to N minutes" (`AuthorityUnit.measuredThrough`, `Resolution.on`, applied by the engine to each
day's own date). A figure of the 1449 calendar would have to pass the reading by 68 s, where 8 s was allowed, to be
before the time shown. The cost, and where: from 6 June 2027 until the 1449 calendar is read, fitted, proved at the
gate and the day moved on (R234), these places are a minute later than the margins alone would show, so up to 4 min
after the Ministry's time if 1449 behaves as 1448 did. Nothing changes on a held day: the gate reads the same days as
before, with the same result.

Oran's band (`31-seat`, the rest of its wilaya to about 70 km and the seat where the region is not known) carries the
same margins as its seat, since the plain fit it carried had no such spare: later than before by 44 s at Fajr, 41 at
Isha, 28 at Asr, 24 at Maghrib and 5 at Dhuhr, and earlier by 21 s at sunrise and 29 at the end of eating; still at
most 3 min after the table at the seat.

**R232. The user's own sky, as R219 built it, and the 20 km kept.** Beside the seat's fitted day ride two days at the
user's own point (`Maghreb.ownSky`, `Alongside`): every start is the later of the seat's and its sign over the user's
own point with Algiers's own margin and none of the authority's minutes (Fajr the dawn, Dhuhr the transit, Asr of
either school the user's own and never before the shadow's exact moment, Maghrib the sunset, Isha the dusk). New
here, on the safe side: no sunrise or end of eating is after the seat's own margin over the user's own point either,
so a place east of a seat ends up to a minute before the seat's table where R219 let the end follow the seat. A
seat's fitted day is a place's only by its region (R219 (b), unchanged). The ring check (a scratch probe, kept
privately as `ring_check.kt`, never committed here; its whole output of 14 November is kept beside it, the first
run's was not): every seat, 12 bearings, all 355 held days, the wilaya named.
At the seat, at 10 km and at 19.8 km the seat's unit answers and no start is before the seat's table and no end
after it; at 20.2 km the wilaya's rest (or Oran's band) answers, and nothing is early there either. Worst after the
table over all 25 seats — at the seat: Fajr 3, Dhuhr 2, Asr 3, Maghrib 3, Isha 3, sunrise and the end of eating up to
3 before; at 10 km: the same, the end of eating up to 4 before; at 19.8 km: the same, sunrise up to 4 before; at
20.2 km (the unmeasured rest, on `dz.marw.wilaya`, unchanged): Fajr 6, Dhuhr 3, Asr 5, Maghrib 5, Isha 5, the ends up
to 5 before. The only early lines of the probe are points 30 km from Boumerdès and from Dellys that lie inside the
other's own unit and follow that place's table (the two seats are about 43 km apart; the discs do not meet). So the
20 km stays. The figure About shows for a unit is its own stamped worst start, read at the seat's point: on the 10
and 19.8 km rings the worst start is no later than that at any of the 25 places (1 min at one, 2 at fourteen, 3 at
ten), though a single time can be a minute later on the ring than at the point (Jijel's Isha, Béjaïa's Asr and Isha:
1 at the point, 2 on the ring, within the place's own worst of 2).

**R233. The site: Oran and Constantine are held again.** A city page needs class A, B or C at the city, measured, a
green stamp and every day of the month checked. Both cities are now class D, so `site/cities.tsv` holds both again in
the file's own style, with the reason. Algiers's page is unchanged.

**R234 (as revised in the review round). The monitor and the yearly read.** The monitor fetches nothing for dz.marw
(image-only PDFs); its source line says so, what is held privately, and what is done by hand each year: read the base
tables and the difference pages with `marw_wilayas.py` (into the archive only), fit the margins on the new tables
with `marw_fit.py`, then the gate rows, the gate and the stamps, and only then move `Maghreb.lastHeldDay` on to the
new calendar's last day. The fitted units do not stop with the 1448 pages, but they do change (R231): after 5 June
2027 they are a whole minute to the safe side and claim no figure until that read is done. The 1449 calendar is
expected by early June 2027; a read in its first days keeps the wider minute to days, not months.

**What got later, and where.** Against the line this lane left (printed units, at most 1 min after the Ministry's
time at a seat, 2 within the 20 km), on the held days at the 25 seats: Fajr is 1 min late at most at 1 seat, 2 at 15,
3 at 9; Dhuhr 1 at 23, 2 at 2 (Tizi Ouzou, Relizane); Asr 1 at 2, 2 at 21, 3 at 2; Maghrib 1 at 2, 2 at 17, 3 at 6;
Isha 1 at 3, 2 at 12, 3 at 10; sunrise up to 1 before at 4, 2 at 19, 3 at 2; the end of eating up to 1 before at 2, 2
at 18, 3 at 5. Seats whose worst is 3: Oran, Chlef, Sétif, Médéa, Mostaganem, M'Sila, Bordj Bou Arréridj, Oum El
Bouaghi, Aïn Defla, Relizane; 2: Tizi Ouzou, Blida, Béjaïa, Bouira, Jijel, Skikda, Annaba, Guelma, Constantine, El
Tarf, Souk Ahras, Tipaza, Mila, Dellys; 1: Boumerdès. No seat needs more than 3. The label: the 81 app cities inside
the 25 units go back from no label (a checked timetable) to "Published method", as the apps in the stores show them
today; none moves up a kind. Against the apps in the stores those 81 cities are measured where 73 were not, never
before their place's table where 16 seats' Dhuhr was a minute before it (R218), and at most 3 min after it where the

### The review round (13–14 November)

Two independent reviews read the lane. What each found, what was done, and what was not.

*Never early.* (1) R231's 8 s of allowance had about one second to spare and failed with one place left out (Béjaïa
needs 7; the others give 6), and every gate row of the 25 places was a fit row: the spare was a reading of the fitted
days, not proof of a later day. Answered with the reviewer's first remedy, the hard last held day (R231 as revised):
the margins stand through 5 June 2027 alone, and after it every start is a whole minute later and each end a whole
minute earlier, with no figure claimed, until the next calendar is read. It replaced "the spare speaks for a day not
held", and R234's "the fitted units do not end with the 1448 pages". Two things differ from the remedy as the reviewer wrote it. It had
the places fall back to the wilaya's unmeasured method after the date; here they keep the fit and take a whole
minute, with the place's own sky beside it as before. The wilaya's method was itself set against these same tables
on these same days (R218), so it is no footing the fit lacks, and at the seats whose margins are the largest (Oran,
M'Sila, Relizane) it stands, at the seat, only 7 to 12 s beyond the fit at Fajr and Isha, where the minute stands 60. And the
margins themselves were left as reviewed: the second remedy (an allowance per place and time, moving three margins,
and month pages held out of the fit) and the third (9 to 12 s for all, which puts Relizane's Fajr 4 min late on held
days, over the owner's bound) are not needed once no day rests on the allowance alone. Holding pages out of the fit
is worth doing at the 1449 read, when there is a second calendar to hold out. (2) Nothing bounded a day after 30 June 2028: answered by the same date. (3) A
test asserted that a sunrise and an end-of-eating margin are positive, which guards nothing (a smaller margin is the
safer end): the assertions are gone and the test is named for what it holds. The reviewer's replacement ("no end's
margin above Algiers's own") is not true of the data and was not written: Boumerdès's fitted sunrise and
end-of-eating margins are above Algiers's and are proved at the gate against Boumerdès's own table. (4) `Gate.kt`'s
two comments: not edited (another lane's file this round); the wording is under "Not done" (1). (5) The merge notes
are under "For the merger".

*Provenance and honesty.* (1) The to-do to compare the held Alger.pdf with the Ministry's own file had dropped out of
this log: it is "For the owner" (1), in the gate's header, in the monitor's line and in the capture note, reworded as
the release's to-do. The comparison itself was not made: this round downloaded nothing. (2) "Measured" rested on fit
rows and on a ring run whose output was not kept: the output of a fresh run is kept beside the probe, the entry says
in plain words that no day of the 25 places is held out, About's figure is shown not to be passed on the ring, and
after 5 June 2027 About claims none. (3) R231's wording claimed too much: "does not rest on where 1448's pages
happened to fall" is gone (it does lean on them), "two more times at 12 s" was three, and "to within 7 s" now has its
count (98 of 1,800). (4) The reading of the Ministry's monthly figure was described in public KDoc and here: both now
point to the private script and describe nothing. (5) The deleted mechanism is a question for the owner ((5)). (6)
"Stamped so" was not true (the stamp has no mark for a fit row): reworded under "The gate". (7) The gate's header
said the copy's Oran column and Ramadan page "agree"; it now says which rows are the same and that the rest is not
compared. (8) The local branches that hold the printed-minutes commit are named under "For the merger". (9) Notes:
About's shared class-D sentence is left for the owner ((6)); `:shared:jvmTest` does not exist ("For the merger" (3));
the three approximate seat points (Boumerdès, Tipaza, El Tarf) are harmless, as the reviewer found, and stay.

What changed in code: `Alongside.after` and `rides(date)` (the day computer and the day pipeline skip a day alongside
that has not begun); `AuthorityUnit.measuredThrough`, `Resolution.measuredThrough` and `Resolution.on(date)` (the
engine applies it to the day's resolution and to the effective one); `Maghreb.lastHeldDay` and `beyondHeldDays`. On a
held day no time and no figure moved: the gate's lines for dz.marw are the same to the digit. The golden vector moved
in 11 lines, all at Oran's own point on days after 5 June 2027 (each start a minute later, sunrise and the end of
eating a minute earlier); own-point worst did not move (its days are held ones).

## Morocco: every place Habous prints a table for becomes a unit (12–13 November) — rulings R195–R199, branch `engine/morocco`

Branch `engine/morocco` off `engine/ramadan-final` at 08b19d9b; archive branch `morocco` (dd2d14e4, be4129e9,
c49cf9e4, b2779599). Not pushed. Until now `ma.habous` was class B at ten fitted cities and the authority's edge
everywhere else (sunrise −510 s and Maghrib +510 s, recorded exceptions of 7 and 6 min): 28 of the app's 180 Moroccan
cities sat inside a unit. Built on 12–13 November and amended the same day after two reviews (never early; provenance
and honesty): R196, R198 and R199 read below as amended, and each amendment says what it replaced.

**The tables.** Since its site became a maintenance notice (26 Oct 2026) the Ministry serves whole Gregorian months for
every place as two static files, `habous.gov.ma/data/horaires-<yyyy>-<mm>.js`. October's and November's were read on
12 Nov 2026, one plain GET each (December's was not posted): 190 places, 11,590 place-days, read back one table a place
and month by `archive/code/manual/ma-habous/habous_months.py` (380 tables, `ville-<id>-2026-10.txt` and `-11.txt`, each
in `MANIFEST.tsv` with its address and date). The responses' headers were not kept, only the two raw files. Nothing
else was fetched. The nine cities' Wayback pages of 2015–2025 and the live month of 13 Sep–12 Oct 2026 were already in
the archive (the round's files, the 29 hand-read places of 6 Oct, the monitor's captures of 13 Oct).

**Where each unit sits (R195).** Each place but Sebta (24) and Melilla (40) is a unit of 25 km at Habous's own
computing point for it, which Habous does not publish: fitted from the place's November Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr and Isha
(which no elevation moves), rounded to 0.01°. 188 printed places make 187 units: Agoudal is printed twice (ville 309,
and 310 for a lower horizon), both held against the one unit. Three units sit at the app's town and read their table at
Habous's point besides: Souk El Arbaa (its table fits as if computed at Sidi Yahia El Gharb's coordinates, 45 km away:
a reading of the fit, nothing Habous says), Ksar El Kebir and Beni Enzar (each nearer another place's point than its
own). Inside a unit the app's starts are the later of the user's own point and the unit's point and its ends the
earlier, as before. `registry/data/HabousCities.kt` holds derived facts only (ville id, point, horizon, two margins),
never a printed time; `archive/code/manual/ma-habous/habous_units.py` derives it, and the committed file is its output.

**Names.** A unit's name is the app's romanisation of Habous's Arabic name, and Habous's own Arabic name now stands
beside every unit in `HabousCities.kt` (the monitor's test holds it to the fetcher's list). Which town a table belongs
to is read from Habous's name; where the name alone does not say, from the fitted point, and two identifications rest
on the fitted point alone: ville 50 (رأس الماء, fitted at 35.17, −2.39) is the Ras El Ma on the coast by Nador, shown
as "Ras El Ma (Nador)" because the app's own Ras el Ma is by Fes, 281 km away; ville 302 (أولاد عياد, 34.12, −4.57)
sits among the places by Tahla (16 km from Tahla, beside Khemis Sidi Abdeljalil) and is shown as "Oulad Ayad Tahla",
298 km from the app's Oulad Ayad, which lies beyond every unit. A fitted point can lie some km from the app's point for
the same town (Taroudant, Tiflet and Meknes 8.5 to 11.2 km), always inside the unit's reach. `HabousNamesTest`: a unit
that shares an app city's name holds a city of that name within its reach, and no two units share a name.

**Sebta and Melilla.** Habous prints both; neither is a unit, because the app places Ceuta and Melilla in Spain
(country ES), where this entry does not apply: a user there gets Spain's default, "Calculated by Taqwa". Measured
against Habous's two tables for October and November 2026 (the four files are held, 122 place-days): no start is
early (Fajr up to 40 min later, Dhuhr up to 4, Asr 3, Maghrib 4, Isha 8) and sunrise is never late, but the end of
eating falls 2 to 3 min after Habous's Fajr on all 122 days (Spain's default ends eating 2 min before an 18° dawn;
Habous's Fajr is 19°). Not changed here: it is Spain's entry and the owner's decision which timetable the Muslims of
the two cities follow (question 5).

**R196 (amended).** A unit's sunrise and Maghrib follow its own table: the horizon is read from the table to 0.1°
(0.3° to 1.7° below the plain horizon over the 187, Habous's correction for the place's elevation) and the two margins
are the ones that keep every printed November minute, then a safety: 20 s at the nine cities held over other seasons,
40 s at a place held for this autumn alone. The amendment: a one-autumn place's table is also read 0.05° of latitude
(5.5 km) north and south of its fitted point, every start the latest of the three and every end the earliest. One month
fixes a point's latitude to 0.01° at best, and an error in latitude is what grows in the other seasons (Fajr and Isha
in summer most), so this widens exactly the days the autumn says least about. What the held days cover, by class: the
nine cities are held over other seasons and years; 30 one-autumn units are held from 13 September to 30 November 2026
(the sun's declination from +3.5° to −21.7°); the other 148 from 1 October to 30 November only (−3° to −21.7°). The
same declinations return from 12 January to 13 March, which contains Ramadan 1448 (−15° to −4.5°). Not covered at the
178: the half of the year with the sun north of those ranges (mid-March to mid-September, which rests on the horizon's
effect being the same at +δ and −δ and on the latitude band), the solstice weeks beyond 21.7° (1 December to
12 January, 1 June to 12 July), and anything Habous does that is not symmetric (a seasonal change of a margin). The
evidence that the allowances are enough is the nine cities': fitted on their November alone and held to every other
month they have, their need rose above November's by at most 8 s at Fajr (June–July), 2 s at Dhuhr, 8 s at Asr
(January), 2 s at Isha, 8 s at the end of eating, 9 s at sunrise (February, Laayoune) and 4 s at Maghrib, and in July
all nine needed less than November at sunrise and Maghrib; no December is held at any of them. The triage's O13 (the
edge's wide sunrise and Maghrib margins at a one-autumn unit outside its fitted months, until a year is held) is not
built: a departure from the safest version, awaiting the owner (question 3).

**R197.** The national margins for Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Isha and the end of eating are the largest need of any held day,
fit or held out, and 5 s (Fajr −39, Dhuhr +290, Asr 0, Isha −10, end of eating −2); a one-autumn place takes 10 s
beyond them (10 s later at the four prayers, 10 s earlier at the end of eating).

**R198 (amended).** Every other unit whose own 25 km holds the user rides there as its own day at its own point (every
start the later, every end the earlier), at a unit's own point too. The first rule let a table ride only where its
point was less than 5 km further than the nearest one, a band that shrank to nothing at a unit's own point: the review
found the app could be before a printed table there (Ait Ourir's day against Kers's table, 3 km away; Oulad Ayad Tahla
against Khemis Sidi Abdeljalil). Habous's points are fitted to 0.01° and the app's town points lie off them, some by
more than the distance between two of Habous's places, so which table a place follows is not known to the kilometre;
no table whose reach holds the place is now ever shown early. 74 of the 187 units have another unit's point within
their own 25 km. The cost is lateness against the place's own table where a higher neighbour rides: in the gate
sunrise is 3 min or more before the place's own table on 2,265 of 27,366 days (8.3 %) and Maghrib 3 min or more after
it on 1,406 (5.1 %), worst 6 and 5 min; under the first rule the worst was 3, at Agoudal alone. Of the large cities
Casablanca, Marrakesh, Tangier, Kénitra, Oujda and Tétouan stay within 2 min at every gated point; Rabat and Agadir
reach 3, Meknes 4 (Zerhoun's table) and Fes 5 (Moulay Yacoub's). This is the safest reading and an owner's decision
(question 2).

**R199 (amended).** Beyond every unit sunrise and Maghrib take ±650 s on the plain horizon, recorded exceptions of 9
and 8 min. The figure is held by a test, not by a note: the edge's day is never before, and its ends never after, any
unit's own day at that unit's point on 24 days of 2027 (650 s holds at all 187; the shipped 510 s fails first at
Zaouiat Ahansal's sunrise of 6 January). The edge's Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr and Isha margins are the shipped build's (31,
353, 72 and 53 s: the first build of this branch had them 10, 3, 12 and 3 s earlier, which the review caught), and its
end of eating is a minute before the national margin (−62 s; the shipped build's was −40). A unit's own limit: 2 min
at sunrise and Maghrib at 148 units; where another table rides, what the gate's worst needs: 3 min at 19 units, 4 at
14 (Agoudal among them, held to both its tables), 5 at five (Bouskour, Fes, Matmata, Tifentane, Zaouiat Moulay
Brahim) and 6 at Moulay Yacoub; and 3 min at Rabat's and Ain El Aouda's Asr and Souk El Arbaa's end of eating, where
the rider lies to the west. A test holds that a limit above 2 min stands only where another unit's reach meets the
unit's (or at Agoudal).

**The gate.** `ma-habous.tsv`: 834 rows. Fit (356): each unit's November 2026 (187) and November at each app city
inside a unit (169). Held out (478): every October 2026 table (188, Agoudal's two) and Agoudal's second November; the
29 hand-read live months and the monitor's ten of 13 Sep–12 Oct at their own units; the ten cities' live month, their
Wayback pages of 2015–2025 and two older tables of Rabat's (22 rows); the app's own point for a town against the
town's table (59 rows, Imilchil's among them at about 2,150 m); and October at each of the 169 app cities. The 169 are
every app city of Morocco and Western Sahara inside a unit, each against its own unit's table with every riding table
beside it, so the "at most" figures above are measured where people are, not at Habous's points alone. With
`ma-habous-envelope.tsv` (604 rows: every riding table at the app's cities and at Habous's other points, held to the
promise alone): 1,438 rows, 354 places, 20 Feb 2015 to 30 Nov 2026, 23,966 place-days, 13,805 of them held out, 126
in Ramadan (all at the older cities; of the five Ramadans before 1448 only Rabat's 1445), 27,366 days an event with
the envelope's. 0 early, 0 late ends, nothing over a limit, 0 broken. To the minute as printed: Fajr 47.9 %, sunrise
22.1 %, Dhuhr 50.7 %, Asr 39.5 %, Maghrib 20.1 %, Isha 49.7 %, end of eating 51.4 %. Worst late 2 min at Fajr, Dhuhr
and Isha, 3 at Asr (6 days) and the end of eating (5 days), 6 at sunrise and 5 at Maghrib. Held out alone (16,686
days an event): Fajr 50.0 %, sunrise 24.5 %, Dhuhr 51.7 %, Asr 38.0 %, Maghrib 21.8 %, Isha 50.6 %, end of eating
53.0 % exact, none early. "Held out" means not used to fit a unit's point, horizon or two margins. It is not fully
independent: the national margins (R197) are the largest need of any held day, October's among them (the held-out
days asked for 2 s more at Fajr, 1 s at Dhuhr and 3 s at Asr than November alone), the limits (R199) are the gate's
own worst, and October is the month next to the fitted one.

**Class B and the reach.** Class B's "within 2 minutes" is true at a unit's own table and point where no other table
rides (148 units' limit) and is a recorded exception elsewhere, as above. Across a unit's 25 km it is not a committed
proof: Morocco's reach rows (an R181-style replay of each unit's table across its reach, `ReachRows.SPECS`) are not
built, since they need a recorded reach exception per unit and this lane has no ruling number left. A scratch sweep
under the amended R198 (never committed: `Spec("ma.habous", "ma-habous", "MA")`, the generator run into a scratch
copy, then the gate on that file): 7,061 rows (2,107 grid points kept and the 852 worst
points of 84,672 swept), 212,755 place-days, 234,071 days an event: 0 early, 0 late ends. Against the unit's own table
across its reach: within 2 min on 99.6 % of those days at Fajr, 99.8 % at Dhuhr, 99.4 % at Asr, 99.7 % at Isha and
99.3 % at the end of eating, worst 4 min (Asr 5); sunrise 3 min or more before the table on 6.8 % (worst 7) and
Maghrib 3 min or more after it on 4.1 % (worst 6). The sweep keeps its worst points, so the shares lean to the worst.
So towards the rim of a unit, up to 25 km from Habous's point, the app can be 4 or 5 min later than the unit's table
at the other times and 7 and 6 min wide at sunrise and Maghrib; nowhere early. That caveat goes with every "class B"
said of Morocco here.

**What moved.** 165 of the app's 180 Moroccan cities and all four in Western Sahara now sit inside a unit (169 of 184;
28 before), class B on the place's own table. One of the 165 is GeoNames's "Dakhla" of Souss-Massa (30.41, −9.55), a
district of Agadir inside Agadir's unit; the city of Dakhla is the Western Saharan one, its own unit. The 15 left on
the edge (Published method) are towns 26 to 37 km from the nearest printed place: Had Soualem, Laâttaouia, Sebt
Gzoula, Tamallalt, Aguelmous, Sidi Rahal, Bir Jdid, Amizmiz, Souk et Tnine Jorf el Mellah, Aoulouz, Oulad Barhil,
Oulad Ayad, Boumia, Outat Oulad Al Haj and Aïn Beni Mathar (Mechraa Bel Ksiri, listed here before, is inside Souk El
Arbaa's unit, 13 km from its point). For them the edge's sunrise is 140 s earlier and its Maghrib 140 s later than
the shipped build's (±650 s where it was ±510 s) and the end of eating 22 s earlier: the safe side at each; Fajr,
Dhuhr, Asr and Isha do not move. The app's cities file carries no population, so the people moved are an estimate:
most of the survey's 28 million on Published method, Fes, Marrakesh, Agadir and Meknes among them.

## Bangladesh: the Foundation's 64 district pages are held, as its published method (13 November) — rulings R220–R224, branch `engine/bangladesh`

Branch `engine/bangladesh` on `engine/ramadan-final` (08b19d9b); archive branch `bangladesh`, commits 8a9a6661,
74ca2122, 48c0f8e8 and d1e46035. Not pushed. R220–R224 are this lane's block, all five used; R224 is the review
round's. This entry was rewritten after two reviews: the first cut called the districts class B and counted fitted
rows as held out, and both were wrong (see "The review round" below).

**What the Foundation publishes.** Only its own public pages and files were read, plain GET, one at a time: the pages
on islamicfoundation.gov.bd, and the files those pages link, which sit on its object store
(objectstorage.ap-dcc-gazipur-1.oraclecloud15.com, the `office-islamicfoundation` bucket); no POST, key or login; the
archive's README lists each address. Two rules stand side by side. The 1993 committee's rule: sehri ends three
minutes before true dawn (18°), the Fajr azan is three minutes after it, iftar three minutes after sunset, and a
district is Dhaka's day moved by its printed minutes, which is very nearly the district town's own day; the Ramadan
1445 (2024) notice is its last printing held (Dhaka's 30 days and the districts' minutes, a scan read by eye). Since
Ramadan 1446 (its press release of 27 February 2025) the Ramadan calendar is computed a district a page with no
precaution minutes: sehri ends at the dawn of the district's east edge with the seconds dropped, the Fajr azan is the
dawn of its west edge and iftar the sunset of its west edge, each made a full minute. The Ramadan 1447 (2026)
calendar is eight division files, 64 pages, 30 days each, posted on 20 January 2026, thirty days before Ramadan. No
Ramadan 1448 (2027) calendar was up on 13 November 2026 (by last year's timing it comes about 10 January 2027). A
district page prints three times only: the end of sehri, the Fajr azan and iftar.

**The year-round Dhaka table is a mirror, said plainly.** The entry's base, `off-ifb-perm-2026.txt` (72 days read by
OCR), was on the line before this lane. It comes from a republisher's copy of the Foundation's permanent calendar
(kivabe.com), the PDF was never stored, and its address and date are unrecorded. No year-round table was found on the
Foundation's own site on 13 November, and no year-round district table anywhere. So nothing held shows that the
Foundation prints the 1993 rule today: the newest print of it held is Ramadan 1445. The app keeps that rule because
dropping it could only make a time earlier, not because the Foundation is known to print both. MANIFEST.tsv now has
the table's line (it had none) and the archive's file a note, both saying this; kivabe.com was not fetched again
(not the authority's own site). The 2018 and 2020 scans are captured, not transcribed.

**What the app holds (R220, R221, R224).** `SouthAsia.bangladeshMethod` (the 1993 rule fitted on the Dhaka table,
with its 60 s district edge) at the user's own point, as on main, and beside it `Bangladesh.held`, which only ever
moves Fajr and Maghrib later and the end of eating earlier. The app holds no district borders, so a district may be
the user's when its town is within 120 km and the user is not west of its fitted west edge (0.02° allowed). For
those districts: (a) the exact rule: Fajr and Maghrib wait the seconds dawn and sunset take to reach the westmost
west edge, and eating ends as many seconds sooner as the eastmost east edge's dawn comes sooner, 30 s to spare, four
minutes a degree; a page is held up to 0.12° past its fitted east edge, because the fit is of one Ramadan at the
town's latitude and just past the edge the hold used to drop to nothing; (b) the 1993 rule (R224): Fajr and Maghrib
wait for the westmost of those districts' towns and eating ends by the eastmost town, for districts whose band
(0.02°) holds the place. Carried as far as (a), Tangail's town alone would cost Dhaka two minutes, so (b) keeps to
the band. Each edge is fitted from the district's own page, odd days of Ramadan 1447 (the archive's `fit_edges.py`);
only fitted longitudes are in the public code (R69). `Bangladesh.units`: the 64 district towns, 20 km, measured
places with no class of their own.

**Which kind, honestly (R224).** Every place in Bangladesh is the Foundation's published method, D_AUTHORITY,
"Published method": Dhaka, the 63 other district towns and everywhere else. No label changes against main. The first
cut's class B is withdrawn: a district's printed days are 30 of one Ramadan, three events; outside Ramadan no
district day is printed anywhere; a unit is a 20 km circle round a town, not the district, and 20 km circles cross
district borders; and the year-round table is a mirror. The gate cannot prove a checked timetable from that. The
research file rates the Foundation's following "YES (MEDIUM; no survey)"
(docs/research/2026-09-prayer-times/authorities-asia-africa-europe-americas.md): no survey of what mosques follow is
held either. Hanafi Asr stays the default (the Dhaka table's Asr, 147 days, never early, at most 2 minutes late).

**What changes for a user.** Against main, at the app's 137 Bangladeshi cities: Fajr later at 129 (median 58 s, nine
in ten within 93 s, the most 148 s at Rangpur, which waits for Dinajpur's town); Maghrib later at 128 (median 53 s,
nine in ten within 93 s, the most 148 s); eating ends sooner at 133 (median 49 s, nine in ten within 96 s, the most
137 s). Dhaka: 14 s, 14 s and 30 s; Chattogram 0, 0, 43; Khulna 85, 85, 67; Rajshahi 1, 1, 84; Sylhet 72, 25, 1;
Barishal 62, 59, 39; Mymensingh 3, 0, 4. So about a minute at a typical city, on the minute shown usually one, never
earlier at Fajr or Maghrib and never later at the end of eating. Dhuhr, Asr, Isha and sunrise do not move.

**The proof's shape (R223, R224).** `gate/bd-ifb.tsv`: 1,027 rows (3 on the line). Counted with the fit, 769 rows:
Dhaka's year-round table on 2026 dates (1); each district's odd days of 1447 at its town (64) and at its two fitted
edges (128; the first cut called these held out, and the edges were fitted on exactly these cells); and 576 probe
rows added by the review round, all marked fit because they re-read cells already counted: the derived 1445 tables
at both fitted edges (128), the even days of 1447 a tenth of a degree past each east edge (64), and the 1447 pages a
quarter of a degree north and south of the town at both edges (384). Marked held out, 258 rows: see the next
paragraph. One printed cell is blanked, never guessed: Jamalpur's Fajr azan of 18 March 2026 is an hour off its
neighbours.

**What "held out" means here, by the count.** The gate counts 4,867 held-out place-days (4,877 day lines in the
rows), of 20,297 in all; 19,334 of the 20,297 are in Ramadan and 4,545 of the held-out ones. They are: 960 printed
district-days, the even days of Ramadan 1447 on the 64 pages, at the town, which no fit saw; the same 960 printed
days read twice more, at the two fitted edges (1,920 place-days: new places, the same printed cells); 1,920 derived
district-days of Ramadan 1445 (Dhaka's printed day moved by each district's printed minutes; a district's Fajr azan
there is an inference: the scan prints a district's minutes for sehri and iftar, and the azan is moved with sehri,
six minutes after it); and Dhaka's year-round days, 5 of October from a second digitization and 72 that are the same
printed table set on 2027's dates (the line's own row from before this lane: new for the sun's year, not for the
print). Fresh printed district-days that no fit saw: 960.

**How well the fitted edges give the even days.** With the edges fitted on the odd days, the exact rule gives the
even days' printed cells to the minute in 2,713 of 2,879 (94.2%): Fajr azan 917 of 959, iftar 891 of 960, sehri's end
905 of 960. Twelve districts give all 45 of their cells; the lowest are Lalmonirhat 34 of 45 (iftar 7 of 15), Bhola
37 (iftar 10), Cumilla 38 (sehri 9), then Cox's Bazar, Habiganj, Pabna and Patuakhali 39. A west edge fitted by Fajr
and by iftar can part by up to about 0.1°. The misses are why the hold carries 30 s and 0.02° to spare, and the gate
finds no early day on any of them; `fit_edges.py` prints the count for each district.

**The gate.** bd.ifb alone: "1027 rows checked (20297 place-days)", class D (authority), 640 places, 4,867 held out,
19,334 in Ramadan; early 0, late ends 0, over a limit 0, 64 units, 0 broken. Fajr 20,299 days (+0 102, +1 1,468, +2
5,365, +3 and more 13,364), worst 8 late; Maghrib 20,305 days (+0 77, +1 993, +2 3,408, +3 and more 15,827), worst
8; end of eating 20,302 days, worst 10 early; on Dhaka's table sunrise 147 days worst 4, Dhuhr and Hanafi Asr worst
2, Isha worst 4. Held out only: Fajr 4,873 days worst 6, Maghrib 4,875 worst 7, end of eating 4,871 worst 10, sunrise
4, Isha 3. The whole gate: "42106 rows checked (11339935 place-days) and 501982 more place-days held to the promise
alone (the envelope's rows)", none early (576 rows and 12,480 place-days more than the first cut's 41,530 and
11,327,455).

**The limits are the worst seen, not a bound (R222, R224).** On the entry, for every place: Fajr 8, Maghrib 8, end of
eating 10, sunrise 4, Isha 4. The first cut's 5, 6 and 8 were the 1993 rule against the exact pages at the towns and
edges; the 1993 hold from a neighbour's town adds up to 164 s to Fajr and Maghrib (Dinajpur's) and 143 s to the end
of eating (Cumilla's), and the held rows then show 8, 8 and 10. Each limit equals its observed worst, so there is no
headroom, and the reasons in the code say so. They are measured against the Foundation's exact page, the later rule's
price; against the 1993 rule's own rows iftar is 0 to 2 minutes late. The limits sit on the whole entry, the 63
districts having no limits of their own now that they have no class of their own.

**What is not held, so nobody reads more into this.** (1) District borders: a neighbour's page and town are held
too, the later side. (2) Dhuhr, Asr and Isha for a district: no district table prints them; they are the Dhaka
method at the user's own sun, checked only on Dhaka's table. (3) The year-round district minutes (Dhaka plus or
minus a fixed number): not transcribed; the town term stands in for them. (4) The hold has no dates and runs all
year, though the pages are Ramadan's: its cover off the town's latitude is checked only on the held Ramadan days
(February to April) a quarter of a degree north and south; in June dawn moves about 3.4 minutes a degree of latitude,
and nothing printed checks a district then. BangladeshDistrictsTest holds the rules themselves on Ramadan 1448 days
and the 21st of every month of 2027, by the engine's own sun. (5) Edges are of one Ramadan, to be fitted again on
each new calendar. (6) The Foundation's own year-round print (above).

**The Ramadan guard.** `checkStamps -Pramadan=1448` no longer names bd.ifb: it is class D again and outside the
guard. The run still exits 1 on the ten entries the line already knew (bn.mora, eg.esa, gb.london.lupt, jo.awqaf,
ma.habous, my.jakim with 4 of 13 units, ru.dumrt, sg.muis, tn.inm, za.jamiat's Pretoria).

**The monitor.** `monitor/sources.tsv`: `bd-ifb`, read by hand, due 15 January 2027: read the 1448 calendar with the
archive's `ifb_ramadan.py`, fit the edges again with `fit_edges.py`, and look for the Foundation's own year-round
table. MANIFEST.tsv: the lane's 192 district-table lines (3,840 rows) and now a line for the year-round table on
2026 dates, which had none.

**City pages.** The five Bangladeshi rows of `site/cities.tsv` stay held; the comment no longer says "class B": a
page needs every day of its month checked, and the district pages are printed for Ramadan alone. `generate`: "Wrote
67 cities (0 held) and 153 pages", as before; `site/build.py --check`: "built _site: 188 pages in 7 languages", "check:
links, assets, structured data, sitemap and timetables all good".

**Tests.** BangladeshDistrictsTest (6): the 64 districts are units at their towns and every place is the published
method; the hold only ever moves Fajr and Maghrib later and the end of eating earlier; every place on a page waits
for its west edge and stops eating by its east; under the 1993 rule every place on a page waits for its town at dawn
and sunset and stops eating by its town; the district rule on Ramadan 1448 and across 2027; a place between two

**Checked (13 November, after the review round).** The whole gate with the archive, exit 0, as quoted.

`:shared:testAndroidHostTest`: 2,257 tests, 0 failures (`:shared:jvmTest` is not a task of this project; the Android
