### The review round (13 November, ruling R224)

Two reviews; every finding was right and none is rejected. (1) Class B could not be proven (Ramadan-only pages,
circles across borders, a mirrored year-round table): every district is D_AUTHORITY, with the hold kept. (2) "Held
out" was claimed for the 128 odd-day edge rows the edges were fitted on, 1,920 place-days: they are marked fit, the
stamps and ProofStamps.kt are regenerated, and the counts above are broken down. (3) The 1993 rule was held only at
the 64 towns: it is held now for every place on a district's page, from the town (the new term in
`Bangladesh.held`, a test of its own, 128 gate rows). (4) Fajr's hold fell to nothing just past a fitted east edge:
0.12° more, and 64 gate rows a tenth of a degree past. (5) Test and gate points sat on the town's latitude: a
quarter of a degree off it now, 384 gate rows. (6) "While the Foundation prints both" had no capture behind it: the
wording is gone and the mirror is named in the manifest, the archive, the gate file and the monitor's source line.
(7) The limits are said to be observed worsts; the fetch host is named; the per-district reproduction of the even
days, the 1445 Fajr inference and the "MEDIUM; no survey" rating are in the entry; Ramadan's total stands beside the
held-out count.

**For the owner.**

1. Hold both rules, as built, or follow the exact district pages alone? Holding the 1993 rule beside the pages
   costs about a minute at a typical city (up to two and a half), and against the Foundation's current Ramadan page
   Fajr is up to 8 minutes later, iftar up to 8 and sehri ends up to 10 sooner. Recommended: keep both for this
   Ramadan; the 1993 minutes are what the last full print and the year-round table carry, and dropping them can only
   make a time earlier. Decide again when the 1448 calendar and a year-round print of the Foundation's own are read.
2. The kind. Built: "Published method" everywhere. A checked timetable for the districts needs a year-round district
   table or district borders, or your ruling that a Ramadan page is enough in Ramadan. Recommended: stay as built.
3. The Ramadan 1448 calendar is expected about 10 January 2027, after the Ramadan build's planned submission.
   Recommended: read it the week it is up, fit the edges again, and ship a patch only if an edge or a rule moved;
   until then the 1447 edges stand (district geography) with their spare.
4. The year-round Dhaka table is only a republisher's copy. Recommended: you obtain the Foundation's own permanent
   calendar (its print, or a file on its own site) so it can be captured properly; nothing was fetched from the
   mirror.

**For the merger.**

- Do not merge the Ramadan line into this lane; squash the lane onto the line (ruling 5 of the round).
- Merge the archive branch `bangladesh` (8a9a6661, 74ca2122, 48c0f8e8, d1e46035) first: the gate rows read
  `archive/tables/manual/bd-ifb/2026-11-13/`.
- On the merged line regenerate, never hand-merge: the whole gate with the archive (stamps), `generateProofStamps`,
  `generateGoldenVector` (the Dhaka rows move with the hold), `generateOwnPointWorst`, then `checkStamps`. Expect
  conflicts in `stamps/*.json`, `ProofStamps.kt`, `GoldenVectorData.kt`, MANIFEST.tsv, `monitor/sources.tsv` and
  this log.
- Rulings R220–R224 are all used; none is free in this block.
- New files: `registry/authorities/Bangladesh.kt`, `registry/BangladeshDistrictsTest.kt`; `gate/bd-ifb.tsv` grows to
  1,027 rows. `shared/` changes, so Bangladeshi times move in the app (later Fajr and Maghrib, sooner end of eating,
  as above); no label changes; the site does not change (the five city rows stay held).
- bd.ifb is class D and is not named by the Ramadan guard.

## Malaysia: every JAKIM zone is a unit on its own e-solat table (13 November) — rulings R225–R229, branch `engine/jakim-zones`

Branch `engine/jakim-zones`, off `engine/ramadan-final` at 08b19d9be; archive branch `jakim-zones`. Not pushed. The
survey's upgrade "JAKIM's 46 zones": until this round thirteen zones were units, each a circle around its point, and
every Malaysian place outside those circles took JAKIM's method at the peninsula's or Borneo's latest edge, labelled
"Published method" (class D), up to several minutes late and checked against no table of its own.

**R225: 37 more zones are units, fifty in all (sixty since the review round below).** The zone list held (60 zones,
`archive/raw/manual/my-jakim-zones/2026-11-11`) was laid over the app's 355 Malaysian cities: 47 zones hold at least
one, ten of them units already, so 37 are new (`JakimZones.towns`). Each is read against its own e-solat year tables:
2026 for all 37 and 2027 for thirty of them, the hand capture of 13 November
(`archive/code/manual/my-jakim/esolat_zones.py`: the fetcher's two requests a zone and no other, 74 requests 2.5 s
apart: 37 plain GETs for 2026 and, for 2027, 37 HTTP POSTs of the date-range form e-solat's own site posts, no key and
no login; raw answers, tables, imsak tables and `notes.txt` on the archive branch, 81 lines added to `MANIFEST.tsv`). A
zone's point is its first town in the app's list. Its start point is a fitted effective point, not JAKIM's reference
point, which is not held: the point of a search around the zone at which the printed starts fit with the smallest
margins (two points in SGR03). In KDH02 to KDH06, SGR02 and NGS03 it lies outside the zone, at sea or in a neighbouring
zone. Subuh 18°, Isyak 18° (17° in Kelantan's KTN02, as KTN01), starts rounded up, syuruk down, the classic noon. The
margins are fitted over every day held, as the first thirteen's were: a fit on 2026 alone was clean on the days it did
not see in 32 of the 37 zones and not in KDH02, KDH04, KDH05, NGS02 and PRK02 (one to three days each; all five are
among the thirty with a 2027 table, so five of thirty failed the forward test). So every day held sets the margins: no
day of a zone's own table is held out, the unit rows' "held-out" days are in-sample, and the towns below read the same
tables at other points, which measures the lateness there and is not an independent proof. Imsak is from the printed
Subuh (`ImsakFrom.PrintedFajr`) with each zone's own margin fitted on its printed imsak; the data shows no zone whose
table changes with the year as Kuala Lumpur's does, so no per-year exception was added.

**R226: a city is attached to a zone by the zone list; a place the list does not settle takes the nearest listed town's
zone, with every zone that could hold it beside it.** `JakimZoneCities` holds, zone by zone, the cities of the app's
list that the zone's list of districts and places names: 344 of the 355, 300 of them besides the zones' own points (by
the review's count the list names 97 of them by name; the other 247 are placed by the district the builder read them
into, general geography that no test checks). A place takes the zone of its nearest listed town within 10 km
(`CITY_KM`). The district borders are not held, so the zones that could own the place ride alongside it, its starts
never before theirs and its ends never after (the rule as the review round left it, `Jakim.beside`): every zone of the
plain with a listed town or named place within 25 km of the user; every zone with one less than three times as far as
the nearest of the user's own zone, at most 50 km; a hill zone's named place only within 5 km of it; and nothing rides
at a listed town's own point, where the list itself settles the zone. Eleven cities are on no zone's list (`unattached`)
and are attached to none: six of them lie within reach of a listed town or of one of the first thirteen's points and
take that zone's table, on distance alone, with the zones around riding beside it (Cheras with Kuala Lumpur's, Bandar
Saujana Utama and Kampong Dungun with Shah Alam's, Kampong Sidam with KDH05's, Padang Besar with Kangar's, Siburan with
Kuching's; since the review round each is a gate row at its own point, held to the promise against every table that
rides there), and five stay at the edge as "Published method": Beluru, Tebedu, Selangau and Pakan in Sarawak and Bandar
Tun Razak in Pahang. Every listed town is a gate row at its own coordinates for every table its zone is read against
(`gate/my-jakim-cities.tsv`, 1,220 rows; their split says `test` because no margin was fitted there, but they read the
tables the units are fitted on, so they measure the lateness at each town and are not an independent proof), and
`JakimZoneCitiesTest` holds the rules: a town in one zone only, every Malaysian city either attached or named
unattached, every town resolving to its own zone as a checked timetable, an unattached city never claiming a table
without a unit, every unit table read at each of its towns.

**R227: the zones' own late limits, measured, each with its reason.** One printed time serves a whole zone, and the
app counts the place's own sun beside the zone's point, so at a town far from the point the print fits a start comes
later or the sun rises and the dawn breaks before the print. Class B's 2 minutes hold in most zones; the exceptions
the gate measured are recorded per zone and event (`JakimZones.Late`): the sunrise up to 3 min before the print in
PHG02, SBH03, SWK02, SWK05 and SWK06, 4 in JHR04 and SWK03, 7 in SWK04 (Sibu's zone, which runs about 130 km east to
Kapit); the end of eating 5 min before the printed Subuh in PHG02, SGR02, SWK03, SWK05 and SWK06 and 8 in SWK04 (the
entry's own 4 elsewhere). Kedah's KDH02, KDH04 and KDH05 are a different case (`Why.STEPPED_TABLE`): their e-solat
tables shift for stretches of days (Asar by about 4 min, the others by a minute or two), so no one point fits them;
the margins hold the latest stretch, and on the other stretches the starts and the imsak are up to 3 min late (4 in
KDH05) and the sunrise up to 3 min before the print in KDH02 and 4 in KDH04. The towns' rows also moved five of the
first thirteen: Shah Alam's end of eating 5, Johor Bahru's sunrise and Asar 3, Sandakan's sunrise 4 and end of eating
5, Kuching's starts 3, Kangar's sunrise 3 to 4. No start was moved earlier to shorten any of these.

**R228 (revised in the review round): a day JAKIM prints later than the days around it is held as printed, never left
out.** SBH09's 2026 table prints 28–31 March LATER than the days either side in five columns (Subuh and Syuruk 10–11 min
later, Zohor 6–7, Asar 19–20, Maghrib 3; Isyak in line). The builder's round called that a fault in the published data
and left the four days out of the gated copies, which showed the app's starts on those days up to 20 min BEFORE the
times e-solat printed for them: an early start listed away. Now the days are in the gated copy as printed, and SBH09
holds them as printed (`PrintedLater`, a run of days on a method: Fajr 660 s, Dhuhr 420 s, Asr 1,200 s and Maghrib 180 s
later on those four days alone), so no start is before the print. The sunrise, the end of eating and the imsak are never
moved later, so on those days they come up to 13 min before the print (`Why.PRINTED_LATER`). The hold rides with SBH09
wherever SBH09 rides beside another zone: at SWK09's point the starts were up to 11 (Fajr), 8 (Dhuhr) and 20 min (Asr)
after SWK09's own print on those four past days, and at most 4 on every other day (`Why.NEIGHBOUR_PRINTED_LATER`).
`fetchers/jakim.py` never leaves a day out any more: a day 8 min or more off the middle of the days around it in two or
more columns is kept as printed; if it is a run the engine holds (`HELD_AS_PRINTED`, held equal to the engine's by
`JakimZoneRulesTest`) the run notes it, and any other such day fails the run with the direction and the minutes, for a
person to rule. SBH08's printed imsak of 3 April 2026 is a slip of another kind (616 min off its Subuh, hours not
minutes) and is left out of its imsak table, a note of the run.

and SGR03 in Selangor), as it does for four of the first thirteen (SBH01, SBH07, SGR01, WLY02). Their 2026 table is held

### The review round (13 November)

Two reviews of the builder's round, one for the never-early rule (A) and one for provenance and honesty (B). Nineteen
findings; eighteen were right and are fixed, one asked for a request the lane may not make and is the owner's (A8, with
B6's second half). Nothing pushed. App commits 4f2deab0b, 3f9711bc6, ca9461f39, 17112683c, 1698a41ce, 226f9fb0c and this
entry's; archive commits 775f9498 and f88e7d07.

**A1 (blocker), border places took the neighbouring zone's table and their own zone did not ride: right, fixed.** Pulau
Sebang (MLK01), Hulu Bernam (SGR01) and Selama's Kedah bank (KDH05) each lie nearer a listed town of the zone across the
border than three times the distance to a town of their own, so the old riding rule left their own zone out. The rule is
now the one in R226 above (a 25 km floor beside the three-times ratio), and the three places, with Mahang (A6) and the
hill places (A2, A5), are gate rows at their own points in `gate/my-jakim-envelope.tsv` (289 rows, written by
`generateEnvelopeRows` from `EnvelopeRows.JAKIM_PLACES`): each is held to the promise against every table that rides
there, its own zone's among them. Read against its own zone's table each is 0 early and late by at most: Pulau Sebang 3
min on a start and the sunrise 4 before the print; Hulu Bernam 3 and 1; Selama's Kedah bank 4 and 3. The coordinates of
these named places are general geography, as the district readings are.

**A2 (major), hill zones without a unit; A5 (major), Genting Highlands and Fraser's Hill; B3 (high), places of zones
with no table shown as checked: right, fixed.** All ten zones that hold no city were captured (ten plain GETs of the
year table, 2.5 s apart, 13 November; archive 775f9498) and are units on their own 2026 table (`JakimZones.named`), each
at a place its list names: KDH07 at Gunung Jerai's summit, PHG05 at Bukit Tinggi (Genting Sempah a named place of it),
PRK07 at Bukit Larut, SBH06 at Gunung Kinabalu, PHG07 at Kuala Rompin, PRK04 at Pulau Banding, SBH02 at Beluran, SWK09
at Kampung Patarikan, TRG02 at Jerteh and TRG03 at Kuala Berang. A hill zone's table (`hill`: PHG06, KDH07, PHG05,
PRK07, SBH06) reaches 5 km from its named place and no further, and the plain's zone rides beside it there; PHG06 gained
Genting Highlands and Bukit Fraser as named places. Measured, 0 early: Genting Highlands and Bukit Fraser against PHG06
at most 3 min late on a start (ends 3 to 5 before the print), Genting Sempah against PHG05 4 (Asr), Bukit Larut 4 (Asr),
and Gunung Jerai's summit 8 min on Fajr, because the plain's Subuh rides beside the summit's earlier one. SBH06's 2026
table breaks its own run (days printed minutes after the days around them); it is held as printed, never repaired, and

and PRK07 are the fitter's (`JakimImsakFitTest`).

**Not fixed, said plainly: SBH02's imsak of March 2026.** e-solat prints SBH02's imsak 20 min before its Subuh on all 31

app's imsak there is the Subuh less 10, so on those 31 past days, part of them in Ramadan 1447, it stood about 10 min
AFTER e-solat's printed imsak; its Subuh, where the fast begins, is in line. The 31 cells are not in SBH02's imsak
table: the archive's own rule from the imsak round of 12 November (`code/imsak/imsak_tables.py`, an imsak more than 15
min before its Subuh is not read) writes them '-', with a note. That is R228's first shape again, for an end and not a
start: a print the app was on the wrong side of, left out of the proof. It is left so in this round because holding an
imsak as printed needs the engine to carry an imsak on a held run (`PrintedLater` moves starts alone), the days are
past, the zone holds no city of the app's list, and the monitor's captures carry no imsak column at all, so a 2027 table
that did the same in Ramadan 1448 would not be seen by any check today. Question 5 below.

   Recommended: keep it, since a later print is never to be judged away by a machine, and tell JAKIM; if JAKIM corrects

2. The POST approval. 37 of the builder's hand requests and, from October, 60 of the monitor's a run are HTTP POSTs of
   e-solat's own public date-range form. The lane's brief says you approved this on 13 November for e-solat only;
   neither repository records it. Recommended: confirm it in a line the Lead can commit to `docs/MONITOR.md`, or say no,
   and the fetcher goes back to the mirror for the year ahead.

3. Seventeen zones rest on 2026 alone (seven with app cities: SBH03, SBH04, SBH05, SBH08, SBH09, SGR02, SGR03; the ten
   without), beside four of the first thirteen. They are class B with 15 s more margin. Recommended: leave them so and
   let the monitor add 2027 when JAKIM loads it; if it is still missing at the Ramadan cut, decide then between their
   2026 proof and "Published method" for the 21.

4. The zone list and the 247 district readings. Recommended: allow one plain GET of e-solat's own zone page before the
   release (or a hand comparison of the 60 lines); the riding rule keeps a wrongly placed town from being early
   meanwhile, at the cost of a few minutes late.

5. The imsak e-solat prints is read by hand only, and SBH02's March 2026 imsak (20 min before Subuh, the app's about
   10 min after it on 31 past days) is left out of the proof by the archive's 15-minute rule. Recommended: before the Ramadan
   cut, read every zone's 2027 imsak for 7 February to 10 March by hand as the imsak round did; if any zone prints an
   imsak earlier than Subuh less 10 there, hold it as printed (a small engine change, an imsak on `PrintedLater`) and
   change the archive's rule to keep such a run and raise it; say whether SBH02's past March should be held too.

6. JAKIM's other oddities, all held never early, for the same letter if you write one: SBH06's broken run, SBH08's imsak
   of 3 April 2026, Kedah's stepped tables (KDH02, KDH04, KDH05: up to 3 to 4 min late on the stretches printed earlier;
   recommended: keep).

**For the merger, added.**

1. Merge the archive's 775f9498 and f88e7d07 too; the ten zones' rows and SBH09's fit copy read them.

2. `TimetableMethod` gained a last field, `printedLater`, and `DayComputer`'s `Offsets.total` one term; the stamps and
   `ProofStamps.kt` carry this branch's engine hash (85f3029596fe1b63), so regenerate after the merge.

   `us-chicago-envelope.tsv` back unless its drift is settled.

   `STEPPED_TABLE`'s sentence changed. Their sentences are English in the stamps, as the others are.

5. The cloud monitor's JAKIM step grows from 13 to 60 zones: 60 GETs a run and 120 requests from October, about five

6. `JakimZoneRulesTest`'s one-year rule is one-directional by design: a zone that gains its second year must be refitted

## The audit's Indonesia fixes: the edge on a kab/kota's own ground beyond its circle, a city on another regency's table, and Kemenag's tables named as myQuran's copy (13 November) — rulings R211–R212, branch `engine/audit-indonesia`

Branch `engine/audit-indonesia`, off `engine/ramadan-final` (9339211fd); archive branch `audit-indonesia`, no commits
(nothing was fetched and nothing in the archive changed). Not pushed. The trust audit of 12 November (findings F4, F6,
F9, F11, F23, F24, F26 and F28, `.superpowers/sdd/2026-11-12-overnight/audit-findings.md`) found two ways an
Indonesian place was shown before its own kab/kota's Kemenag table, a monitor that would have fetched again what the
round holds, and a claim the app could not make: that Kemenag's tables were checked against Kemenag. Each finding was
reproduced before it was fixed. Two reviews followed on 13 November; this entry is the lane as it stands after them,
and what they changed is told at its end.

**The rule (R211, finding F6, a blocker).** A kab/kota's circle stops short of the nearest other kab/kota (R103), so
the ground just beyond it is, on every other side, still the unit's own, and its people follow the unit's table, which
Kemenag computes at one point for the whole kab/kota. The edge there (class D_AUTHORITY, "Published method") was
Kemenag's method at the user's own point with 2 min for an unknown capital. That is before the unit's table in two
ways. Two units' own allowance is more than the whole edge's, because their print departs from the method itself: Kab.
Puncak Jaya (Mulia, 3322) and Kab. Lanny Jaya (Tiom, 3311), whose Isya comes about 4.5 min after the 18° dusk and
whose Subuh, and the end of eating with it, about 4 min before the 20° dawn; just outside their circles the app showed
Isya up to 4 min before their own tables and let eating run up to 4 min after their Subuh. And around every unit the
sun reaches a place east of the table's point earlier than the table says, four minutes a degree, and a place north or
south of it at another hour of dawn, Asar and dusk: towards 55 km the edge's 2 min no longer cover it (red first,
below).

Now `Kemenag.outsideAt(user)` is the edge. Beside a unit the capital is known, so the edge carries that unit's own
allowance with what the distance from its point needs on top, wherever that is more than the plain edge's: 240 s a
degree of longitude (east of the point on each start, west of it on sunrise and the end of eating), 150 s a degree of
latitude either way on every event but Dhuhr, and 15 s; less 225 s at sunrise and Maghrib beside a lowland unit, whose
table reads a horizon a degree shallower than the edge's. A later start and an earlier end only; the unit's earlier
Subuh is never carried, the edge's own Fajr stays. Several units in reach: the largest of each. It reaches 55 km
(`CARRY_KM`) from every unit's point, a degree (`DEPARTING_CARRY_KM`, 111 km) from the point of a unit whose allowance
is more than the plain edge's somewhere (found by rule, not by name: today the two above), and six listed far grounds
(`Kemenag.farGrounds`), below. Muhammadiyah's edge (its own 18° Subuh) carries the same. The two rates and the 15 s
are fitted to these tables, not derived alone: with them every unit's 2026, 2027 and 2028 hold on the rings the tests
read; they are not held-out evidence. The 55 km and the degree are distances, not any kab/kota's extent: no kab/kota
boundary is held.

**The far grounds.** Ground of a unit's own kab/kota beyond 55 km of its point, where the plain edge was seen before
the unit's table, each listed by a point and a radius: Bawean (Kab. Gresik, 145 km north of Gresik; the app's
Sangkapura), the Kangean islands and the Sapeken islands east of them (Kab. Sumenep, 150 to 270 km east of Sumenep),
the Banda islands (Kab. Maluku Tengah, 170 km south-east of Masohi), Serawai on the upper Melawi (Kab. Sintang, 130 km
east of Sintang) and the Balantak headland (Kab. Banggai, 65 km east of Luwuk). Whose each is and where it lies is the
builder's reading, with no held source: the island grounds are drawn wide over open sea, the two on the mainland 15
and 22 km around the review's point. The list is what was seen, not every such ground.

**What the carry does not reach.** Beyond a carry and off the far grounds the edge is the plain one: Kemenag's
published method at the user's own point with 2 min, "Published method", which claims no table and is read against
none. A kab/kota that reaches more than 55 km east, north or south of its table's point elsewhere is there still
before that table, by the same nature as the six grounds; and west of the point the ends can be late. The review of 13
November measured two such places that are left as they were, for want of a point of record and because the carry's
charge there would be many times the need (for Long Nawang about 9 min on the end of eating against a need of one):
Okaba (Kab. Merauke), the end of eating a minute after Merauke's table on 156 of 1,096 days; Long Nawang (Kab.
Malinau), sunrise a minute after Malinau's on 553 days and the end of eating on 1,047. These are the review's own
figures, held by no test here; neither is a start, and at neither is any time on the wrong side of the sun's own event
at the place. Without the boundaries, or a table for each of the 271 kab/kota that has no unit, "never before its own
kab/kota's table" is proved inside the circles, to the end of each carry and on the six grounds, and not beyond: for
the owner (2).

**R212 (findings F4, a blocker, and F11).** (a) Every app city on a Kemenag table lies in that table's own kab/kota.
GeoNames has "Batang, Central Java" (Kab. Batang's town, id 1649881) at −6.4846, 110.7083, which is in Kab. Jepara,
12.7 km from Jepara's point and inside its circle: the app showed Jepara's table under Batang's name, with no label.
No held source gives the town's true point, so the row leaves the bundle (`tools/build-city-db.py`'s `DROPPED`, with
the reason; 34,134 cities) until one does; Kab. Batang has no unit, so the town will be "Published method" when it
returns. A phone that picked Batang before keeps the row's point in its settings, so the row is also withdrawn there
(`WithdrawnCities`): a location picked from a withdrawn row reads as none and the app asks for the place again; a GPS
fix standing at the same spot keeps its location. `WithdrawnCitiesTest` holds the withdrawn rows to the builder's
`DROPPED` list, both ways. `RegistryCitiesTest` holds every Indonesian city inside a circle to be the unit's own seat,
or one of 32 district towns listed by GeoNames id with the unit each follows, never a town of another province, and
the list to be exactly what applies; the 32 towns' membership is one reading, mine, from their kecamatan. (b) No two
circles overlap but over open sea that is neither's land (`KemenagCirclesTest`). Of the 246 circles one pair overlaps:
Kab. Halmahera Utara's (Tobelo, 3203) and Kab. Pulau Morotai's (Daruba, 3207), 47.78 km apart, a lens 7.7 km deep over
the strait. The audit's default was to cut Halmahera Utara's radius to 21.5 km; that would have pushed its own ring
from 21.5 to 29.5 km out to the edge, about 2.5 min later and "Published method", for no never-early gain, since the
round's boundary figures show the lens holds neither's land (no other kab/kota within 30 km of Tobelo; Halmahera
Utara's nearest boundary 28.868 km from Daruba, beyond Morotai's 26.0 km). Both radii stay and the pair is listed with
those figures, which the test holds. This goes against the audit's default and is provisional until the owner says:
(6).

**Red first.** The first build: `KemenagEdgeTest` (shared), "just beyond a circle the edge never allows less than the
unit it borders", failed on Isya; `KemenagRingTest` (tools, against the archive) 2 of 3; `RegistryCitiesTest`'s new
test on Batang; `KemenagCirclesTest` on the Halmahera pair before it was listed; `RepublishedSourceTest` 2 of 3; the
monitor's `KemenagFetch` tests 2 failures and 8 errors. After the reviews, each ring test was run with the plain edge
in place of the carry. Just outside the circles: 16 points around the two departing units. Around every unit to the
carry's end: 142 points around 54 units failed, Asar before the unit's table at 99 points on 11,706 place-days (Kota
Surabaya on 12 days, Kota Banda Aceh on 2 at 54.8 km), sunrise after it at 35. Around the two departing units for a
degree: 331 points, Isya early on 263,325 place-days (worst 7 min), the end of eating late on 239,272 (6 min), Asar on
26,832 (3), Dhuhr on 25,812 (2), Maghrib on 23,515 (2), sunrise late on 37,520 (3); the first build's flat 55 km left
44 points at 55.3 and 60 km with Isya 3 min early (the review's figure). On Bawean: 33 points, Asar early on 647
place-days (worst 2 min), Isya on 1,648, Subuh on 161, the end of eating late on 102; at Sangkapura's own point Asar
on 13 days and Isya on 32. On the five other grounds, 33 points each (the ground's point and 16 bearings at half and
at the whole radius): all 66 of Kab. Sumenep's two, Subuh, Dhuhr, Asar and Isya early on every one of 1,096 days at
every point (worst 8 min) and Maghrib on 37,020 place-days (4 min); all 33 of Kab. Maluku Tengah's, Dhuhr on 31,900,
Asar on 27,593, Subuh on 21,920 and Isya on 21,181 (5 min); all 33 of Kab. Sintang's, each of the four on 33,619 to
36,168 (4 min); 22 of Kab. Banggai's, Dhuhr on 4,622, Asar on 4,200, Subuh on 2,611 and Isya on 2,419 (1 min). With
the carry all five ring tests pass.

**What got later, and where.** Nothing inside a circle moved, and nobody moved up or down a kind: every place the
carry touches was and stays "Published method". These figures are one reading on the lane's head against the plain
edge, held by no test (the tests hold the rule: never less than the unit beside it nor than the plain edge, and never
before the unit's table on the rings).

- Of the 447 Indonesian cities in the app's list, 278 are in a unit's circle and 61 on the plain edge, both as before;
  108 are on the edge within a carry. Among those the allowance moved by seconds: Asar later at 63 cities (median 14
  s), the end of eating earlier at 76 (median 13 s), Subuh later at 19 (median 3 s), Isya at 16 (median 3 s), sunrise
  earlier at 13 (median 14 s; the most 26 s, at Buaran beside Kota Pekalongan), Dhuhr at one (3 s, Pamanukan beside
  Kab. Subang), Maghrib at none. One city moved by a minute or more: Sangkapura on Bawean, Subuh 74 s later, Asar 95
  s, Isya 75 s, the end of eating 93 s earlier; Dhuhr, Maghrib and sunrise as before. No city of the list on the edge
  lies within a degree of Mulia or Tiom, and none but Sangkapura on a far ground.
- Around the 244 common units, read on 16 bearings every 2.5 km to the carry's end (72,698 points): at most 25 s later
  at Subuh and Isya, 46 s at Asar and 11 s at Dhuhr (all beside Kota Dumai at 54.4 km), 12 s at Maghrib (Kota
  Tasikmalaya); sunrise at most 38 s earlier (Kota Tomohon), the end of eating 36 s (Kota Malang).
- Within a degree of Mulia or Tiom and outside the circles (GPS only): Isya up to 417 s later (about 7 min), the end
  of eating up to 396 s earlier, Asar up to 178 s later, Maghrib 153 s, Dhuhr 124 s, sunrise up to 177 s earlier,
  Subuh 4 s. This is paid by neighbours too. Kab. Jayawijaya (Wamena, 58 km from Tiom) is its own unit, with a 13.3 km
  circle; its ground outside that circle takes the departing allowance, later than Jayawijaya's own table needs (the
  review measured, on the first build's shorter carry, at −3.92, 138.73: Isya 9 min after Jayawijaya's own table and
  at least 3 min on every day, the end of eating 7 min before it, Asar 5 min and Subuh, Dhuhr and Maghrib 4 min
  after). The seats of regencies with no unit lie inside the degree as well, Ilaga (Kab. Puncak) and Karubaga (Kab.
  Tolikara) among them: no table of theirs is held, so whether they print the same dip, and whether the carry is
  needed there or only late, is not known. Later, never early: the accepted cost of not holding their tables, for the
  owner (3).
- On the far grounds (GPS only, but for Sangkapura), from the rule's own figures at each ground's point and its four
  sides: Bawean, Subuh and Isya 52 to 108 s later, Asar 73 to 128 s, the end of eating 71 to 128 s earlier. Kangean,
  Subuh, Dhuhr and Isya 3 to 6 min later, Asar 3.5 to 6 min, Maghrib up to 2 min (at Arjasa: Subuh 234 s, Dhuhr 219 s,
  Asar 254 s, Isya 233 s, Maghrib 7 s). Sapeken, Subuh, Dhuhr and Isya 5 to 8 min later, Asar 5 to 8 min, Maghrib 1 to
  4 min (at Sapeken itself: 354, 361, 374, 353 and 127 s). Banda, Subuh and Isya 3.5 to 5.5 min later, Asar 4 to 6
  min, Dhuhr 1 to 3 min, Maghrib up to 2 min, the end of eating 42 to 118 s earlier (at Banda Neira: Subuh 280 s, Asar
  300 s, Isya 279 s, Dhuhr 107 s, Maghrib 52 s, the end of eating 80 s). Serawai, Subuh and Isya 3 to 4 min later,
  Asar 3.5 to 4.5 min, Dhuhr 1.5 to 3 min, Maghrib up to 22 s. Balantak, up to 66 s later at Subuh, 62 s at Dhuhr, 85
  s at Asar, 64 s at Isya. The carry charges for the whole distance from the table's point: on these grounds the times
  are close to the regency's own table and never before it, which is what one table for a regency 270 km wide costs
  its east end.
- Batang, Central Java can no longer be picked from the list, and a phone that had picked it is asked for its place
  once.

**F9, left.** Kota Subulussalam's point (2.662, 97.8827, GeoNames') is about 13.7 km west of the town by the audit,
and its circle is 6.4 km: the town itself is on the edge, "Published method", later than the table and never before it
(the edge never allows less than the unit it borders). No held source and no page of the authority's proves the town's
point (myQuran's answers carry no coordinates), so it stays.

**The monitor (F23, F24, F28).** A month the round holds under `archive/tables/round/kemenag-kabkota/` now counts as
held, so the round's 228 places' 2027 and 2028 are not fetched again (the next run would have made 2,736 requests for
nothing); the next year comes 20 places a run. An answer that does not hold every day of the month asked, or holds
another month's, is an error, and a place no row was read for is raised. Each run one month held beyond the next is
read again for every place that holds it (a cycle of 36 weeks) and a held day that changed is a note, in days, never a
printed time. Every request is a plain GET to api.myquran.com, no faster than one in two seconds (the fetcher's own
gap, held by a test: the monitor's common 1.5 s was under the rule for a third party's host); at most 978 requests a
run, about 33 minutes. It is the feed in use since September (R104); whether it is accepted as the source is owner
question 1, and the run's size owner question 4. No new host. `docs/MONITOR.md` and `sources.tsv` say so.

**Whose copy (F26).** Every held kab/kota table was read from the open myQuran API, which republishes Kemenag's
figures; none from Kemenag's own pages, and no plain address of Kemenag's for a year's table is held (its page's own
script was not imitated). The source is unchanged; what the app and the site say about it is now true.
`RegistryEntry.republisher` (a name only where a checked timetable is claimed) is "myQuran" on `id.kemenag`. Every
sentence that names the comparison has a twin that says whose copy, and a republished timetable always gets the twin:
the Prayer screen's card ("Kemenag’s times for Jakarta, reproduced by Taqwa and checked against myQuran’s copy of its
published timetable."), About these times' source line, the tile under its nought and its days-so-far sentence (the
app picks each through `CheckedClaim`, so none is added without its twin), and on the site the city page's
description, replay step and source line and the checks page's row and gate sentence (the generated document carries
the republisher). Seven languages (`scripts/check-strings.sh`: clean). `RepublishedSourceTest`, `DocumentTest` and the
site's `RepublishedCopyTest` hold it, and that the edge beyond the circles still carries the republisher.
`MANIFEST.tsv` lists the round's 684 kab/kota tables (249,888 days) with the address each was read from, and says of
the headerless `off-kemenag-jakarta.txt` that its 61 days are day for day the round's; the manifest is 1,911 tables,
516,994 days. `official/README.md` has a section on what the gate proves there: never before myQuran's copy of
Kemenag's table.

**The gate.** "64518 rows checked (12027493 place-days) and 3230751 more place-days held to the promise alone (the
envelope's rows)", exit 0, 15 m 11 s; no early start, no late end, nothing over a limit, 0 broken in every entry and
unit. Against the base: 3,272 rows and 1,170,528 promise-only place-days more, all of them `id-kemenag-envelope.tsv`
(every unit's 2026, 2027 and 2028 at 1,068 points: just outside its circle, to its carry's end, and up to 9 points on
each far ground; promise-only rows from the generator), the place-days as they were. `id.kemenag`: class B, 4,695
places, 5,145,720 place-days an event (413,160 in Ramadan), none early; worst late Fajr 2, sunrise 2, Dhuhr 2, Asr 2,
Maghrib 2, Isya 2 min, the end of eating 3 (the listed units' exception), imsak 2; to the minute on 75.5 % of Fajr,
77.6 % of sunrise, 77.0 % of Dhuhr, 56.5 % of Asr, 75.8 % of Maghrib and 75.4 % of Isya. The stamp calls 4,966,140 of
those place-days held out, and that is not what the words say (audit finding F17, not this lane's to fix): the reach
rows are marked held out while they replay the unit's own fit tables at other points, so the figure, and "days at
places" with it, is inflated about 19-fold; the year truly held out is each unit's 2028 (246 rows). All 81 stamps were
rewritten (the engine hash moved; every count as before).

**Checks (13–14 November, on the lane's head, beside five other lanes on the same Mac).** `gate`: above.
`generateProofStamps`: "Wrote 81 proof stamps", the file unchanged. `generateGoldenVector`: "Golden vector: 2071
place-days over 120 points", unchanged. `generateOwnPointWorst`: "Wrote 3885 own-point rows", unchanged.
`checkStamps`: "81 entries — every stamp fresh and green, ProofStamps.kt matches the committed stamps."
`:shared:jvmTest` does not exist in this project ("task 'jvmTest' not found in project ':shared'");
`:shared:testAndroidHostTest` stands in for it, inside `scripts/test.sh`. Tools `jvmTest` with the archive: 436 tests,

**For the merger.** The Ramadan line has moved past this lane's base and nothing of it is merged here. On the merged
line regenerate: `tools/timetables/official/stamps/*.json` (the whole gate, writing stamps: the engine hash moves in

**For the owner.** (1) Kemenag rests on myQuran's copy (F26). Recommended: accept it in words, or check a sample of
days by hand against Kemenag's own publication (a few kab/kota, a few months); a table that can only be had through
the page's own script was not fetched. Meanwhile the app, the site and the manifest say whose copy it is, and class B
stays. (2) Beyond a circle, which standard: the regency's printed table, or the published method at the place. The
lane takes the first wherever it can tell whose ground it is (the carries, the six far grounds) and the second
elsewhere. Recommended: keep the first, and close the rest either with the kab/kota boundaries (a held, licensed
boundary set; none is held and none could be fetched under the lane's web rule) or with a table for each of the 271
kab/kota that has no unit, the wide and the island regencies first; and say whether Okaba's and Long Nawang's late
ends are to be carried at the cost above once a point of record is held. The six grounds' membership is my reading; a
second reading would not hurt. (3) Kab. Puncak Jaya's and Kab. Lanny Jaya's degree, and the highland regencies around
them: recommended to fetch their neighbours' tables (Puncak, Tolikara, Nduga, Mamberamo Tengah, Intan Jaya, Yalimo and
the rest of the highlands) through the feed in use, in a later round; then each neighbour follows its own table and
the degree can shrink to what Puncak Jaya and Lanny Jaya themselves need. Meanwhile those places are later than they
may need, never early. (4) The monitor's run against a third party's API: at most 978 requests, about 33 minutes, once
a week. Recommended: keep it; the safe fall-back, if that is more than the owner wants asked of myQuran, is the 492
requests of the months ahead alone (about 16.5 min), without the re-reading of held months and the next year's 20
places. (5) Batang, Central Java: recommended to hold the town's true point from a source and return the row then, and
to fetch Kab. Batang's table through the feed in use. (6) Smaller, each as it stands unless the owner says: Halmahera
Utara's and Pulau Morotai's circles both kept over the strait against the audit's default cut (the cut costs Halmahera
Utara's outer ring about 2.5 min and its label); Kota Subulussalam's point, left for want of a source; the 32 district
towns' membership, one reading.

### The review round (13 November)

Two reviews of the first build, no blocker in the first and one in the second; every finding was taken but where said.

*Never early.* (1) The flat 55 km carry stopped too soon for the two departing units: at 55.3 and 60 km 44 points,
Isya 3 min early. Taken: a degree around a departing unit, and the carry made to follow the distance (longitude and
latitude) instead of a flat 150 s. (2) Around the other 244 units the first build's claim, that the plain edge holds a
unit's table on its own ground, was true only just outside the circle. Taken as far as it can be without boundaries:
the carry is general (every unit, 55 km), the rings read to each carry's end, the review's measured far places with a

## The audit's regions: Tajikistan and Côte d'Ivoire held on every town their bodies print, and told truthfully (13 November; review round 14 November) — rulings R207–R209, branch `engine/audit-regions`

Branch `engine/audit-regions`, off `engine/ramadan-final` (9339211fd); archive branch `audit-regions`, off b8069020.
Not pushed. The trust audit of 12 November (`.superpowers/sdd/2026-11-12-overnight/audit-findings.md`) raised eight
findings on the two countries the safe defaults lane had given their own entries: F16 (Tajikistan proven on one
in-sample month with no spare), F2 (Côte d'Ivoire's Dhuhr running to the fixed 16:00), F3 and F5 (towns COSIM prints
that the engine did not hold), F21 (what the Ivorian proof is, said too kindly), F30 (both countries told "no local
timetable is known" while the engine holds and uses the bodies' tables), F31 (About's method sentence silent on the
clocks and floors) and F36 (the end of eating 25 min before Fajr all year). Each was checked first and each held.

**What was captured (archive 82a1a9db; plain GETs of the bodies' own public pages, one at a time).** The Council of
Ulama's nine Ramadan calendars of 2018 to 2026, nine posts of its own news list (the 2026 one an image, read by
hand), each with its footnote of the towns' minutes after or before Dushanbe; between them they cover 19 February to
15 June. Nine more November tables for the footnote towns the app does not list: derived, the November page already
held moved by its footnote's minutes, no new request. COSIM's calendar of Joumada al-Thaniya 1448 (10 November to 8
December 2026; one image, read by hand; since the review round no cell is left out: three misprinted cells are read
by their column and bind, and where the image prints thirty Maghreb and Icha rows beside twenty-nine days each day
is held to the later of the two that may be its own), and a derived table for every town of its correspondences in
all four editions held. Not captured, by the
owner's rule of 13 November: the Council's other months, which its page gives only through a month picker (a form);
no such request was sent.

**Tajikistan (F16, ruling R207).** The audit was right, and it was worse than one month without spare. Against all
124 rows now held (19 towns, both footnote sets; 10 rows are Dushanbe's own print and 114 are derived town rows, 50
of them at the nine approximate points), the entry as the safe defaults lane left it showed Asr a minute
before the printed Asr on 7 place-days, Maghrib a minute before the printed Shom on 7 and Isha a minute before the
printed Khufton on 5: 17 of the 19 at Asht in November 2026, a town of the footnote the app does not list, so a user
there took a neighbour's lower figure, and 2 in the 2020 edition (Bokhtar and Shahritus, a day each). Maghrib had no
spare on 64 place-days. And two ends were late, which no one had seen because no Ramadan calendar was held: the
sunrise shown after the printed one on 465 place-days, up to 8 min (at Dushanbe itself on 32 of 239 days), and the
end of eating after the printed Subhi sodiq on 511 place-days, up to 8 min (at Dushanbe on all 29 days of the 2025
edition).

R207, as built (`Generic.tajikistanAt`, `Generic.councilTowns`):
1. Every town of every footnote in print is held, listed by the app or not. Two footnote sets are in print (an older
   and a newer, up to 4 min apart for the same town): a town takes the latest figure either prints for its starts and
   the earliest for its ends.
2. A place takes the figures of the nearest printed town; where a town is held at an approximate point (the nine the
   app does not list, 30 km, one 60), every town that may be the nearest binds: the latest minutes for a start, the
   earliest for an end, over the place's own sun.
3. The sunrise is shown 12 min before the sun's own (the 2021 edition prints it up to 10 min before).
4. The end of eating is 2 min before the 19.5° dawn, never Fajr less a fixed span (the 2025 edition's dawn sits near
   19.4°).
5. Isha is the later of the 18° dusk + 2 and Maghrib + 90 min: the Council's Khufton is Shom + 90 on every day held,
   and nothing is held for summer, when 90 min after sunset comes before the 18° dusk.
6. Dhuhr is never before 12:45 anywhere in the country. Maghrib stays as the first lane set it, 13 min after the
   sunset and the cushion (16 shown): what closed its days without spare is the town's figure, not a wider margin.

After it, on tj.default: 124 rows, 3,705 place-days (3,117 of them in Ramadan), 0 early, 0 late ends, 0 over a
limit. Every start is at least 3 min after the printed one but Dhuhr, held by the national floor, and every
sunrise at least 2 min before. Worst late against the
printed rule: Fajr 31 (Isfara, Ramadan 2025; Dushanbe 26), sunrise 21 before (Ayni, 2020), Dhuhr more than 20 (Murghob), Asr
11, Maghrib 15, Isha 10, the end of eating 34 before Bomdod (Asht, 2020). Nothing is held out and the stamp says so:
every margin was read off these very tables, so this is proof that the
build holds the tables it was made from and no proof of a table nobody has seen. Two margins rest on one edition
each: the sunrise's 12 min on 2021's alone (the other editions print the sunrise 0 to 9 min before the sun's own; at
Dushanbe the app's is up to 17 min before a printed sunrise) and Maghrib's 13 on the June days of 2018 (2026 prints
the sunset + 7 to 8.5, so against the newest calendar Maghrib is shown about 8 min later than it prints). Both are
kept: the Council has withdrawn neither edition. And every one of the 3,117 Ramadan place-days is a day of a past
Ramadan: Ramadan 1448 begins about 8 February 2027 and the earliest day any edition prints is 19 February, so its
first eleven days or so fall where no printed day is held; there the times rest on the margins and the sun.

What got later for users (2027, the app's 31 Tajik cities, 11,315 place-days, against the line before): Fajr later
on 6,480 place-days, by up to 13 min (Isfara, Istiqlol, Shahriston; Khujand, Konibodom and Buston 11; Dushanbe 1 min
on 15 days); Dhuhr on 643, up to 6 (Shahriston); Asr on 6,673, up to 10; Maghrib on 6,646, up to 9 (Isfara,
Shahriston; Khujand and Konibodom 6; Dushanbe 1 min on 13 days); Isha on 8,035, up to 22 (Moskovskiy, Kolkhozobod;
Sughd up to 18; Dushanbe up to 15 on 96 summer days). The sunrise is 7 to 19 min earlier on every day and the end
of eating 13 to 26 min earlier on every day; Dhuhr's end is later on 6,730 place-days (up to 9) and Asr's end
earlier on 5,881 (up to 13). No start came earlier anywhere.

What is not held: any day from 16 June to 31 October or from 1 December to 18 February; Peshin, Asr and Khufton
outside November. Whether the Peshin clock holds all year and Khufton stays Shom + 90 in summer is not known; the
12:45 floor and the 18° dusk are the safe side of both.

**Côte d'Ivoire (F2, F3, F5, F21; ruling R208).**
1. *F2.* `fixedAsrLocalMinutes` moved Dhuhr's end with Asr's start, so Dhuhr ran to the conventional 16:00, up to
   45 min after the Standard Asr the sky gives. A fixed Asr clock now holds Asr's start only; Dhuhr ends at the
   sky's Standard Asr (`DayComputer`, a rule test in both schools). No table prints an end of Dhuhr, so no row can
   check it.
2. *F3 and F5.* COSIM's correspondences list 67 towns beside Abidjan; the engine held the 46 the app lists. With
   the other 21 added as rows, Fajr was a minute before the derived Soubh at Madinani on 50 place-days (25 days of
   each Ramadan edition): a place there took the nearest listed town's lower figure. Every town COSIM prints is
   now held, listed or not (`Generic.cosimTowns`); the 21 are held at approximate points with a band (30 km, 60 for
   the villages), and a place takes the latest minutes of the towns that may be its nearest for its starts and the
   earliest for its ends. No margin moved for a derived row.
3. *F21.* The gate file and the stamp say what the proof is: four real tables, all Abidjan's; 268 derived rows of
   67 towns (Abidjan's table moved by COSIM's printed minutes), which prove that the engine holds COSIM's rule and
   that a town's own sun never crosses it, not that COSIM printed a table for the town; every derived row is a fit
   row. One table is held out: Abidjan's Joumada al-Thaniya 1448, fetched after the floors were set (28 place-days:
   its 29 days less 10 November, which the month before also prints). Since the review round it is held out for the
   starts only: the end-of-eating margin and late limit were set with it in view.
   Nothing is held from 9 December to 17 June, the season of Ramadan 1448 included, or from 9 August to 11 October.

After it and the review round (below), on ci.default: 408 rows (272 and the 136 ends-only rule rows, which add no
place-day), 68 places, 8,160 place-days (4,216 in Ramadan, 28 held out), 0 early, 0 late ends, 0 over a limit. Worst
late: Fajr 12, sunrise 12 before, Dhuhr and Asr 0 (the conventional clocks, on the minute), Maghrib 16 (COSIM's own
construction puts its Maghreb before the northern towns' sunset in summer), Isha 27, the end of eating 32 before
Soubh (Seydougou; 28 at Abidjan). On the held-out month alone: Fajr 5, sunrise 8, Maghrib 8, Isha 16, the end of
eating 28.

What got later for users (2027, the app's 183 Ivorian cities, 66,065 place-days): Fajr later on 3,786 place-days,
Asr on 1,118, Maghrib on 3,561 and Isha on 3,324, each by up to 6 min (Dianra); the sunrise earlier on 1,989 (up to
7, Dabakala) and the end of eating on 1,900 (up to 6); Dhuhr unchanged; no start earlier, no end later. And by F2,
Dhuhr's end is up to 45 min earlier on every day; by the review round, the end of eating is a further 2 min earlier
on every day, everywhere in the country.

**The labels (F30, F31, F36; ruling R209).** Both entries stay class D (none), "Calculated by Taqwa": a month page
and nine Ramadan calendars, or four Abidjan tables and a rule for the other towns, are not a checked timetable, so
no place moves up a kind. What was false was the sentence under the label. R209: an entry of Taqwa's own
calculation may name the body whose timetable it holds in part (`RegistryEntry.safeSideOfKey`, refused on every
other class); the card then reads "Taqwa holds only part of the timetable [body] publishes, so it calculates these
times on the safe side of that part" (the review round's wording: the safe side of what is held, not of a timetable
nobody has seen whole), and About says the same with the method and the not-affiliated line, where both said
no official Sunni timetable had been found. The bodies are named as the app names every authority
(`authority_council_ulama_tj`, `authority_cosim`).

About's method sentence now reads what the method carries beside its angles (`methodExtras`, a pure helper): a
Dhuhr or Asr never before a local clock time, an Isha never less than so many minutes after Maghrib, an end of
eating at least so many minutes before Fajr ("at least" since the review round: the Fajr shown carries its own
cushion, so the gap is the rule's minutes or more, 30 or more in Côte d'Ivoire), and, for Taqwa's own calculations,
an end of eating at a deeper dawn than
Fajr's. So Tajikistan's reads its 12:45, its 90 minutes and its 19.5°, and Côte d'Ivoire's its two conventional
clocks and its 25 minutes (F36: the 25-minute end of eating is kept on every day of the year, the safe side, and
is now said; whether to keep it out of Ramadan is put to the owner). The same reading now says, truthfully, the
12:00 Dhuhr clock of Tatarstan's DUM RT and Jamiatul Ulama's end of eating 5 min before Fajr, which the sentence
had left out. Nine new strings in seven languages, `values-in` the twin of `values-id`; the site's Checks
page and the README say "or Taqwa holds too little of one to check it" beside "no official Sunni timetable is
known". Not changed: the store listing's and the support page's conditional sentence ("where no timetable is
known, it calculates on the safe side"), true as it stands; store text is the owner's.

**Tests hold rules.** `DayComputerTest` (a fixed Asr clock leaves Dhuhr's end at the sky's Asr, both schools);
`SafeDefaultsFloorsTest` (a Tajik town is never before Dushanbe's day moved by the latest minutes the Council
prints for it, nor its ends after it moved by the earliest; every town COSIM prints that the app does not list is
held to its own minutes and never a neighbour's lower ones; a printed town's figure never makes a start earlier or
an end later than the region gives at the place itself; Isha never before the 18° dusk; since the review round,
every one of
the Council's 19 towns, not a sample, is held to the latest minutes it prints for it after Dushanbe and its ends to
the earliest, the nine approximate ones also 0.2° to the north and to the west; and Côte d'Ivoire's fast begins the
rule's 25 min and at least the region's 2 min margin before the dawn, 30 min or more before the Fajr shown);
`MethodAngleRangesTest` (no clock, floor or end of eating any registry method carries is left out of the sentence;
only Taqwa's own calculation names a part-held body; both bodies have a string); `AuthorityNamesTest` (the registry's
keys, `safeSideOfKey` included, all resolve).

**The review round (14 November; archive 78b24cfb).** Two independent reviews read the lane: one for an early start
anywhere, one for where each figure comes from and whether each sentence is true. What they found and what was done:
1. *A late end in Côte d'Ivoire (major).* The lane had measured the end of eating "0 to 1 min before the imsak, at
   least 40 s on every day" on the 1436 edition alone and carried it to every month with no margin. COSIM's 1448 months
   print no imsak, so no row checked it there. With COSIM's own 1436 rule (Soubh − 25) laid on the Soubh it prints for
   the two 1448 months, as 136 ends-only rows over its 68 places (derived by rule, not printed, and said so in each
   table and in the gate file), the end of eating came a minute after the rule on three days of those two months.
   Fixed: `endOfEatingMarginSeconds = -120`, the margin every region takes (the fitter asks 38 s). After
   it the end is at least 1 min before the rule everywhere, up to 3 at Abidjan and up to 7 at Seydougou; the late limit
   went from 31 to 33 and its sentence says the new figures. The cost: the end of eating 2 min earlier on every day; no
   start moved.
2. *Cells left out.* Five cells had been left out of the tables as misprints (three of the Council's, two of COSIM's),
   and a day nobody checks is a day an early start could hide on. All are now read and bind as a printed cell would:
   the Council's Shom of 27 May 2019 (printed an hour after the days on either side, its minute between theirs, read
   an hour earlier) and Bomdod of 26 and 27 February 2026 (printed an hour before the days on either side, read an
   hour later, through its 17 town tables too); COSIM's sunrise of 5 and 6 December and its second Icha row. COSIM's doubled Maghreb and Icha row is read as
   the later of the two (Maghreb a minute later on six days, Icha on eight; no day earlier). Every reading is named in
   its table's head and in the gate file. Nothing came early on any of them.
3. *What the proofs are, said plainly.* Tajikistan has no held-out proof and the gate file says which edition binds
   which margin, how many of its rows are derived (114 of 124) and that the opening of Ramadan 1448 is not covered by
   any printed day. Côte d'Ivoire's held-out month is held out for the starts only. The capture notes say what was and
   was not kept, and the survey's November page of 11 November has the manifest line it lacked.
4. *The words.* The card's sentence (English and Arabic; the other five already said "that part") and About's "at least
   so many minutes before Fajr" in all seven languages, as above; the costs of the sunrise's 12 min and Maghrib's 13
   are in the KDoc, the gate file and this entry.
5. *Not changed, with the reason.* The Tajik rows were not relabelled as test rows: every one is a fit row and is said
   to be, which is the truth of it. Dhuhr in the east (more than 20 min after its own Peshin at Murghob, more than 10
   at Khorugh) keeps the one 12:45 floor: a floor by town would rest on one November page, and later is never early; it
   is put to the owner.
   The approximate points of the unlisted towns were not looked up: the lane fetches only the bodies' own pages. The
   base line was not merged in: the merger regenerates the stamps.

**Left with the owner.**
1. The Council's other months. Its page shows them only through a month picker, which the lane does not send.
   December's page can be had by a plain GET on or after 1 December, and so each month in its turn. Until then
   Peshin, Asr and Khufton are proven on November alone and held by the 12:45 floor and the 18° dusk. And the
   Council's Ramadan 1448 calendar, when it is posted (its opening days, about 8 to 18 February 2027, are the one
   stretch of a Ramadan no printed day holds): fetch it before the Ramadan build is cut.
2. All nine Ramadan editions bind, the oldest from 2018. Binding only the recent ones would give back a few minutes
   of the sunrise and of the end of eating; the lane kept all nine, since the Council has withdrawn none.
3. The 25-minute end of eating out of Ramadan in Côte d'Ivoire (F36). Kept, now with the region's 2 min margin:
   COSIM prints an imsak in Ramadan only, and an end of eating that changes rule with the month would be a second
   thing to prove. It costs up to 28 min before COSIM's Soubh at Abidjan (32 at Seydougou) on days nobody fasts by
   a printed imsak.
4. The unlisted towns' points (9 Tajik, 21 Ivorian) are approximate and carry a band that costs neighbours a few
   minutes (Shahriston up to 6, Boundiali up to 4). A gazetteer lookup of each would let the band go.
5. The Council's and COSIM's town minutes stand in public code (`Generic.kt`), as the PA's and COSIM's did before
   the Algeria ruling; the lane followed the precedent.
6. Six cells are readings, not the print (three of the Council's, three of COSIM's), and they bind. Each is an
   hour or a digit put right by its neighbours; the lane holds them rather than leave a day unchecked.
7. Dhuhr in eastern Tajikistan runs more than 20 min after the town's own Peshin (Murghob), by the one 12:45 floor.
   Kept until a second month page is held; a floor by town would give those minutes back.

## The audit's Egypt findings: a belt past every town's reach, the 48 towns kept by the monitor, a place called by its own name, Oman's reach proved (13 November) — ruling R213, branch `engine/audit-egypt`

Lane "audit-egypt", from `engine/ramadan-final` (9339211f); archive branch `audit-egypt` (from b8069020), nothing
added to it: no capture was needed and nothing was fetched. Not pushed. Six findings of the trust audit of 12 November
(`audit-findings.md`: F13, F14, F22, F25, F34, F35), each checked again here before anything was changed. One ruling,
R213, of this lane's block.

**F13, right, fixed: R213, a town's table rides beside the edge out to twice its reach.** The audit found the end of
eating and sunrise a minute after the town's table just west of Ras Gharib and Sidi Barrani, where `Egypt.kt` said
the edge had been checked with no late end. That check stood at the towns' own points alone. Replayed here on rings
past every reach, each town's own tables against the place as the app resolved it: a sunrise or an end of eating
after the table around 73 of the 78 towns (26,121 day-cells), the place's own sun running later than the town's to
its west, and a start a minute before the table around 27 (14,911 day-cells: Taba 11,386, Kharga 1,616, El Mahalla
El Kubra 1,230, Baltim 243, Sidi Barrani 150, Rafah 128, Cairo 76, the other twenty 22 or fewer), mostly east of
the towns ESA prints from a point off the town, whose own starts exceed the edge's allowance. The edge's allowances
are sized for a town ESA does not print, not for the printed town next door. So (`Egypt.beside`, `BESIDE_REACHES`
= 2.0): out to twice its reach (40 km, Cairo 60) a town's own day at its own point is a day alongside the place's
own, every such town's, and the day shown is the later start and the earlier end of them all. Inside a reach nothing
changes, and beyond every belt nothing changes. ESA prints by town, with no boundaries, so this near a town, where
no town's reach holds the place, a place is never before its table nor any end after it (a place inside one town's
reach follows that town alone, ruling R165, however near the next stands, and is a minute from the next town's
table on some days: that is R165's design, older than this lane, and the belt's rows leave those points out);
farther, the place's own sun runs more than a minute and a half from the town's and the town's table is no longer
the place's. The belt is still the edge: "Published method", no unit, no
figure in About. Of the app's 241 Egyptian cities 159 stand in a town's reach, 75 in a belt (Banha, Shibin al-Kawm,
Mit Ghamr, Girga, Samalut among them) and 7 beyond every belt (Kom Ombo, Mallawi, Dayrut, al-Qusiyah, Dayr Mawas,
Zaafarana, an-Najaylah). None moves up a kind. Proof: `gate/eg-esa-envelope.tsv`, written by `generateEnvelopeRows`
from `eg-esa.tsv`'s rows (8 bearings at 102.5, 150 and 197.5 % of each reach, and the 75 cities; a point another
town's reach takes is left out): 14,311 rows at 1,556 places, 430,183 place-days (27,930 in Ramadan), held to the
promise alone: no start early, no end late, on those sampled points and the 2025–2026 days the towns' tables hold.
It is a sample and no recipe grows it: a month `prove` adds to a town is replayed in the belt only when
`generateEnvelopeRows` is run again, which `docs/MONITOR.md` now asks at every release cut and at the yearly turn.
(The first review's own probe, 3,863 points on bearings and distances the generator does not use, 1,039,025
place-days, found no start early and no end late either.) What it costs (this lane's own measurement, which the
reviews did not reproduce): in the belt the day runs up to 6 min after the
neighbouring town's table (Fajr 6, sunrise 6 before, Dhuhr 5, Asr 5, Maghrib 6, Isha 6, the end of eating 6
before), where it ran up to 5 and was a minute on the wrong side on some days. That lateness is against a table
the place is not said to follow, so it is no unit's figure and no limit's. Two reaches and not more: farther out
the lateness grows with the distance, for a table that is less and less the place's own (owner question 3). The test
(`GulfEgyptProofTest`) holds the rule (inside a reach no alongside; in the belt the towns nearest first; beyond
none), never a figure. `generateEnvelopeRows` on this base also rewrites `us-chicago-envelope.tsv`; that file is

## The audit's Oman fix: a locality's table rides past its own circle on the edge, the edge stands a minute to the safe side of both roundings, and the hand reads say when they are due (13 November) — rulings R210 and R240, branch `engine/audit-oman`

Branch `engine/audit-oman`, off `engine/ramadan-final` (9339211fd); archive branch `audit-oman`, off `ramadan-final`
(b8069020). Not pushed. The line moved on while this was built and nothing of it is merged here. The trust audit of 12
November (findings F7, F10, F12 and F27, `.superpowers/sdd/2026-11-12-overnight/audit-findings.md`) found three things
at the line where an Omani locality's circle ends, and one in how the monitor holds the ministry's tables. The lane
was built, read by two reviewers, and fixed after them; this entry is the lane as it stands after the fix, and says
what the reviews changed.

**What was wrong.** The ministry (MARA) prints by locality and draws no boundaries; a unit's circle (20 km; Muscat 30
km; Al Hamra 12 km, R170) is this engine's line. Just past it, where no other circle holds the place, the place was
read at its own point with the edge's minute alone (class D), and the edge's minute was Muscat's: Muscat rounds up,
the 85 other localities round to the nearest, so the edge's sunrise stood only half a minute, and its end of eating
52 s, before the tables it lies beside. Measured before the lane on a ring 0.5 km outside every one of the 86
circles, on 8 bearings, against the unit's own held table (688 points):

- on the edge (445 points, 203,239 place-days): Fajr before the table on 134 place-days, Dhuhr 51, Asr 134, Maghrib
  84, Isha 202; sunrise after it on 8,315 (4.1 %, about one day in twenty-five: the audit's F12); the end of eating
  after it on 363;
- inside another locality's circle (243 points, 109,777 place-days): Fajr before the first unit's table on 15,520,
  Dhuhr 13,316, Asr 15,333, Maghrib 14,806, Isha 17,162; sunrise after it on 16,943 and the end of eating on 15,585.
  There the neighbour's own printed table holds the place, and two printed tables of the same ministry differ; the
  audit says of F12 that these bearings do not count, and the lane leaves them as they were (below).

The audit's own points: at Jebel Shams (23.24, 57.26; F7) sunrise was after Al Hamra's table on 58 of 450 held days,
the end of eating on 74 and Isha before it on 2; at As Sifah (23.44, 58.78; F10) Fajr was before Muscat's table on 228
of 877 days, Dhuhr 295, Asr 390, Maghrib 313, Isha 417.

**The rule (R210).** Beyond every circle, where no table holds the place, a locality's table rides half again its
circle (`Gulf.omanRideKm`, `OMAN_RIDE` 1.5: 30 km for a locality; 45 km for Muscat, which holds As Sifah at 41.2 km;
18 km for Al Hamra, which holds Jebel Shams at 13.9 km). The place keeps its own day at its own point with the edge's
margins, class D and its label; each riding table is read as its own day at its own point with its own margins beside
it (`TimetableMethod.alongside`: each start the later of the two, sunrise and the end of eating the earlier). Inside a
circle nothing changes: R167 as it was (the nearer locality holds, and a second rides only where its own circle also
holds the place). The factor is this engine's judgement, as the circles are; the ministry gives nothing to fit it to.

**The rule moves the line; it does not end it.** Half a kilometre past a ride's end the place is the plain edge again
and the same question stands there against the same table, only smaller, because the table is now 30 km away and not
20. That is why the edge itself was fixed too:

**The edge (R240, the audit's own fix for F12).** `omanEdge` is now `omanMethod.margins.widened(60, sunrise = -(60 +
NEAREST_SECONDS))`: the starts as before (a minute after Muscat's rounding up, a minute and a half after the
nearest's), sunrise and the end of eating a minute before the nearest rounding's (a minute and a half before
Muscat's). Before, the edge's sunrise margin left half a minute, and the end of eating 52 s, before the 85 tables it
lies beside. `widened(…, sunrise = …)` is what South Africa's, Egypt's and Russia's edges already do.

**What the reviews changed.** The builder's lane had a second tier: inside another locality's circle a table rode a
tenth past its own circle (`OMAN_RIM` 1.1). Both reviewers found it wrong, and it is gone: (1) it moved 7 of the 86
localities' own points and 5 of the app's 27 Omani cities off their own printed table by a minute, and the About
sheet's worst-late figure at six localities, for a neighbour's table; (2) with the Egypt lane's reach rows for Oman
(`engine/audit-egypt`, the audit's F14) it broke class B at Samail and Saiq (three minutes late against a limit of
two); (3) it had no measured gain the audit asks for: the audit says the in-circle bearings do not count, because the
neighbour's printed table holds there. Also after the reviews: the ring rows are written at three distances and only
where the rule holds a place (below); the build log no longer says the rule closes F10 and F12 everywhere; the
sentence about F27's line was false and is corrected (below); the web rule is the Lead's, not the owner's words; the
archive's reader refuses a careless re-read. No finding of either review was rejected.

## Pakistan and India: Dawat-e-Islami's month-picker months and Ramadan cards come out, and every card keeps the same 45 s (13 November) — rulings R235–R237, branch `engine/pakistan-plain`

Branch `engine/pakistan-plain`, off `engine/ramadan-final` (157b2fa6d); archive branch `pakistan-plain`, off 370a3a10.
Not pushed. No web request of any kind was made in this lane.

**Why.** Question (4) of the Pakistan entry above and question (3) of its review round asked the owner whether the 36
month-picker months may stay. His answer of 13 November (ruling 3 of the day) was "you can decide": he left it to the
Lead. The Lead dropped them, under the engine lanes' web rule as the Lead had tightened it that day: plain GETs of public
pages only, no script-style addresses, no headers imitating a page's own script, no month pickers. That is the Lead's
working rule for the lanes, not a rule the owner gave, and the owner can still rule otherwise (question 3 below). The 36
seasonal months held for twelve Pakistani cities had been asked of the card page's month picker, the way the page's own
script asks and not by a plain request (how exactly is in the Pakistan entry above, as history). Under that rule they are
not a source this engine stands on, so they are out of the tree: captures, tables, manifest lines, gate rows, the code
that read them and the tighter margin they had earned.

**R235: the picker months are removed and every card keeps the same 45 s.**

- Archive 1fdf2df4 (first committed as 5e5165fb; its message was reworded in the review round, the tree is the same): the
  36 tables and their 36 raw captures are removed from the tree (December 2026, March 2027 and June 2027 of
  Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Peshawar, Quetta, Faisalabad, Multan, Murree, Skardu, Gilgit and Muzaffarabad,
  35 with Gilgit's March never answered, and Karachi's June 2026). No stored script ever asked the picker (those
  requests were made by hand); the part that knew of it was the parser's branch for an untitled answer and two notes.
  `di_share_card.py` now refuses any capture without the card's own title, and `fetch_share_cards.sh`, the plain-GET
  card fetcher, stays as it was with its note reworded. The parser re-derives all 74 tables left, byte for byte. The
  36 captures are still in the private archive's local history (added in bb78cf99, merged at c7a1cad7); no remote holds
  that history, so the archive's GitHub copy never received them.
- App b54b30984: 36 MANIFEST lines and 124 gate rows are gone (56 of `gate/pk-dawateislami.tsv`, 68 of its envelope
  file). `SouthAsia.CityCard` loses its `seasons` flag and `ONE_MONTH_SAFETY`: there is one `CARD_SAFETY`, 45 s, kept
  past every card's worst second of November 2026. The twelve cities kept 30 s until now; they keep 45 s, so each of
  their starts is 15 s later than before or the same, and each sunrise and end of eating 15 s sooner or the same. No
  start anywhere is earlier than it was and no end later. `CityCardsTest` holds the rule (one safety for every card,
  never under 45 s), no figure.
- One recorded exception had to grow. Karachi's unit is held against Banuri's Daimi table as well, and the 15 s more
  carries the Hanafi Asr of one day in June 2026 from 4 min after Banuri's table to 5 (the gate: pk.karachi's Hanafi
  Asr 5 min late on that day, over the unit karachi limit 4). That is one point of the unit: the app's own Hub (25.02555,
  66.88534, 21.7 km from Karachi's point) against Banuri's June 2026 page (`own-points-worst.tsv`). Karachi's own point
  and the unit's three other app points stay at 4 under the Hanafi school, and the standard Asr stays at 4 everywhere.
  Karachi's unit now holds two limits: 4 min on sunrise and Maghrib as before, 5 min on Asr (`KARACHI_ASR_LATE`). A limit
  names a prayer, not a school (`TimedEvent` has one Asr), so the 5 covers the standard Asr column as well, a minute
  looser than anything seen there; the limit's reason says which column reaches it (question 4 below). Later, never
  earlier; said here because it is a later time than before.

- Golden vector: 16 lines move, all at the Karachi point (24.855, 66.922), each by one minute on one or two times.
  Own-point rows: 3,885 → 3,742.
