## The audit's gate findings: a table counts once, a fitted row is a fit row, the Ramadan guard reads held-out rows, and the far south of the Americas (13–14 November) — rulings R214, R246–R247, branch `engine/audit-gate`

Off the Ramadan line at 47ebb5bff and merged with it twice on 14 November (now on d3f4c4f35, which holds Bangladesh's
districts, JAKIM's zones, Algeria's fitted units, Oman, Tajikistan and Côte d'Ivoire, and Egypt); archive branch
`audit-gate`, off efe95a3b and merged with the archive's line at 910ff256, holding thirteen captures of its own
(19f3caae). Not pushed. Two reviews of 14 November (never early; provenance and honesty) were applied in full where
they were right: what they changed is said in place below and gathered under "The review round". The
audit of 13 November found that the figures a reader is shown (a stamp's places and place-days, About's "days at N
places", the site's checks page) counted a table again at every point it was replayed at, that rows a margin had been
fitted on were stamped held-out, that the Ramadan guard took a fitted row for proof and did not read the imsak, and
that the Americas' safe default was green only because the one far-south table held was left out of the gate. No time
shown changes anywhere but in the far south and at Saint-Pierre (R247); no entry changes kind.

**R214. A published table counts once, and a row the fit saw is a fit row** (findings F17 and F20; `gate/Counted.kt`).
The row that counts a table's days is the first row of the entry that reads its starts, a `-reach.tsv` row only where
no other file reads the table. Every other row reading the same table (a point of the unit's reach, a ring, the app's
own point, a town the one national table also serves) is a replay: checked like any row, an early start or a late end
breaking the gate as anywhere and its lateness in the stamp's worst, and adding no place, no place-day, no Ramadan day
and no held-out day to any figure shown. A stamp's `places`, `placeDays`, `ramadanDays` and `heldOut` are now the
tables' own; the replays are kept beside them under `replays` (places and place-days), so nothing is hidden. This is
the rule for every entry, read off the gate files alone and the same in whatever order they are read; no entry is
named in the code.

A cell is held out only when its row is `split=test` and no fit row of the entry reads the same event from the same
table: a reach row replaying a fitted table is in-sample whatever its own split column says. By event, since a row
reading ends alone can be fitted while the table's starts are held out. And by a new gate directive, `@fitted
<entry>[/<unit>] <table | prefix*> <columns | *> <reason>`: the cells of a test row that a margin was widened to, or
read off, are fit cells. The split column of those rows is left as it was (the fit's own tests read it); the line
beside them says what the margin saw.

*The sweep (F20).* Every gate file's notes and every authority's fit comments were read for a margin fitted on rows
stamped held-out. Marked on 13 November, 27 lines in 18 files (40 in 23 after the review round, below): JAKIM (every
zone's margins were fitted over the union of its 2025 and 2026 tables, three zones refitted on 2025–2027 on 4 November,
and each zone's imsak margin over every imsak column held: the 6,935 held-out imsak days are fit days), Brussels' EMB
(second half), Toronto's IFT, IIT and MAC (second halves and the monitor's capture of the same year), the Grande Mosquée
de Paris (Maghrib and Isha, October–December), Qatar's Calendar House (the website's Fajr and end of eating), Kazakhstan
(Kostanay's end of eating), Dublin's ICCI (second half), New Zealand's FIANZ (Fajr), Lebanon (Fajr and Dhuhr on the
dated captures), Palestine's Dar al-Ifta (the 2027 table, five columns), Tatarstan's DUM RT (the 18 towns' tables: the
margins are Kazan's fit widened by their excess, so they pass by construction), Syria (the held-out date's Dhuhr, Asr
and Maghrib), Mauritania (Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr), Diyanet's European tables (the Fajr, Isha and end-of-eating curves north of
44.5° N were derived on the capture of 28 September), Umm al-Qura (the end of eating over the first round's tables),
Cape Town's VOC (2027, both schools), Kosovo (the towns' sunrise) and ISNA's Culver City (Maghrib). Found honest
already: Kemenag (its imsak too), Kazakhstan's refit rows, Qatar's 2027, MUIS, Australia, Bahrain, Switzerland,
Ireland's IFI, Karachi's two entries, Egypt, Oman, the Emirates, Kuwait, Iraq, Sudan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Russia's
two other boards, Norway's IRN and Cape Town's MJC. Not re-marked, and said here so that it is not lost: Morocco's
Habous (187 units fitted this week by another lane, whose files these are; its rows' splits are that lane's to state),
the Dawat-e-Islami cards' 30 s safety (`SouthAsia.kt`, read off the cards it rides beside), Kazakhstan's later rounds
beyond Kostanay's end of eating, and the class C entries, which replay their members' tables under their own name and
have no margins of their own (the review round gave them a rule: a cautious row's cell is fit where its member's own
is).

**R246. The Ramadan guard reads held-out rows alone, the imsak too, and never hides behind green** (findings F15 and
F19; `gate/CheckStamps.kt`, `gate/StampSummary.kt`, `monitor/MonthByMonth.kt`). A unit's Ramadan is proven on the days a
held-out cell of Fajr, the end of eating and Maghrib was compared, each (the stamp's new `heldOutByEvent` by unit), and
on its imsak beside them where the unit shows one and a table of it prints one. A unit whose guarded days are all in the
gate and only in tables the method was fitted to is named apart ("checked and not held out") and refused by the Ramadan
build like a short one (`CheckStamps.FITTED_ONLY_REFUSES`, question 1). A unit that shows an imsak no table held for it
prints is named in a notice, since no row exists to add a day to (228 of Kemenag's units). The "Published method"
entries (class D with an authority) are read the same way and named in a notice, never refused: 38 of them are not
checked against their authority's own table on every day of Ramadan 1448 (36 on 13 November; Bangladesh and the line's
other new units since). And the plain `checkStamps`, which every build runs, now prints one line naming the checked
timetables not yet proven for the coming Ramadan, and stays green: "checkStamps: NOT YET PROVEN for Ramadan 1448
(2027-02-08..2027-03-09, guarded 2027-02-07..2027-03-10): 19 checked timetables (class A or B)" (18 on 13 November).
With `-Pramadan=1448` it exits 1, by design, until the 1448 calendars are published and held. O4's month-by-month cover
(R185) reads the same events at condition (a), and at (b) the imsak on its own: where the month's imsak is unchecked,
the unit's fetched captures must be seen printing one (on every day of the twelve months before that they print and the
unit's Fajr is checked on, its imsak is checked too), or the imsak waits for a table read by hand, which no source
fetches, and the entry stays named.

The 19 (14 November, on the merged line): short of the days (no table held prints them) `bn.mora`, `eg.esa` (78 of 78

**R247. From 43.5° of latitude a place of the Americas' safe default takes the app's model of the Moonsighting
Committee's day beside the region's** (finding F18; `Generic.americasAt`, `Generic.americasUnits`, one line in
`Units.kt`). What the table left out is: the Moonsighting Committee Worldwide's own calculator output for Ushuaia,
fetched with Puerto Williams' and Isla Hornos' on 11 October 2026 (`archive/tables/manual/mcw/2026-10-11/`), a
calculation at coordinates by the Committee's seasonal rule and not a timetable a mosque or a board printed. Whose
practice it reflects cannot be established from what is held; no mosque timetable of Tierra del Fuego, Magallanes, Santa
Cruz or the Falklands is in the archive. (On 13 November this lane fetched nothing. In the review round it fetched
thirteen more tables of the same calculator, below: they test the band, and say no more about local practice than the
first three.) It is nonetheless the only published times held for the far south, it is a Sunni body's, and the region's
Fajr (the 15° sign) was before it on 243 days of 2026 at Ushuaia, by up to 96 min on the midsummer nights, when the 15°
sign returns near the middle of the night. Under the standard that is closed, not listed away: from 43.5° north or south
each start is the later of the region's and the model's at the user's own point, and sunrise, the end of eating and
every end the earlier. What stands beside the region's day is the app's model of the Committee's rule (the engine's
"Other > Moonsighting Committee" method), not the Committee's figures: the calculator's tables check it. The Committee's
dawn first passes the 15° dawn near 43.9° N and 44.0° S, by seconds (the review found it; the lane's first edge, 44°,
stood on a grid too coarse to see it), so the band begins half a degree inside that. No app city lies between 43.5° and
44°; a place there has its Dhuhr up to a minute later, and nothing changes below the band.

*The cost, measured over 2026.* 16 of the region's 4,975 app cities are in the band: Ushuaia, Grytviken, Río Grande,
Punta Arenas, Puerto Natales, Stanley, Río Gallegos, El Calafate, Puerto Deseado, Pico Truncado, Las Heras, Caleta
Olivia, Comodoro Rivadavia, Coyhaique, Puerto Aysén and Saint-Pierre. Fajr is later by 3 to 10 min on 44 to 70 days
(mid-November to January) at 45–47° S, by up to 17 min at Puerto Deseado and 46 at El Calafate, and by up to 93–100
min on the nights the 15° sign is near midnight (October to February) at Río Gallegos, Puerto Natales, Stanley, Punta
Arenas, Río Grande, Grytviken and Ushuaia, where it is also up to 10 min later through the winter; by up to 11 min
from May to July at Saint-Pierre (46.8° N). Dhuhr is up to a minute later in the band. Isha and the end of eating do
not move (the region's are already the later and the earlier). The 24 app cities between 40° and the band are untouched.

*The gate.* The Committee's tables are held in `safe-default-americas-promise.tsv`, a hand-kept promise-only file
(`GateRow.promiseOnly` now takes a `-promise.tsv` file as it takes the generator's `-envelope.tsv`): an early start or
a late end breaks the gate, no late limit is asked (the region's Isha is up to 172 min after the Committee's and its
end of eating 129 before, by design of a safe default), and the rows are in no stamp and no count of published tables,
since a calculator's output is not a table a place is known to follow. Seventeen rows at ten points of the band and one
at sea. Fit, four: Ushuaia 2026 (the band was built on it), and Puerto Williams, Isla Hornos and the Drake Passage at
58° S, the tables the model's seventh of the night from 55° S was settled on in October (the lane's first entry called
the first two held out; they are not). Held out, thirteen, fetched on 14 November after the band and the model stood
and not looked at before: Comodoro Rivadavia, Río Gallegos, Punta Arenas, Stanley and Saint-Pierre for 2026 and 2027,
Gobernador Costa (44.0° S) and Paso de Indios (43.9° S), the two sides of the latitude where the Committee's dawn
first passes the region's, for 2026, and Ushuaia for 2027, the year of Ramadan 1448 at the farthest town. Each is one
plain GET of the Committee's own `praytable.php`, raw page and daily table under `archive/…/manual/mcw/2026-11-14/`
with its `MANIFEST.tsv` line. All thirteen read green on their first run, with the edge at 44° and again at 43.5°.
`safe-default-americas.tsv` says where the first table went. Proven both ways on 13 November, on the first three: with
the band the two groups pass; with the band's latitude set to 80° for the test, the gate fails with
"default.safe.americas fajr: 860 early".

*Antarctica is outside it.* The Committee's tables for Orcadas (60.7° S) and Esperanza (63.4° S), held since October,
are not rows: Antarctica is no country of this region, and a place there is shown the world default (`default.safe`,
18° throughout), whose Fajr is before the model's on every day of 2026 there (by 18 to 165 min at Orcadas, 12 to 183 at
Esperanza; at the Drake Passage's 58° S, were it not the Americas', 25 to 159). Read as rows of this region both are
green, so the band's model holds to 63° S. Inside the Antarctic Circle it is not proven: in the polar day at 67.6° S
the region's day beside the model's started Fajr before it. So Antarctica was not moved into the band, and the app has
no city there; question 2 below.

**The envelope rows are checked, not rewritten by surprise** (item 6; `units/GenerateEnvelopeRows.kt --check`, task
`checkEnvelopeRows`). `generateEnvelopeRows` is deterministic: two runs on the same tree write the same bytes.
Chicago's file changed on every run because it was behind: the monitor's prove of 1 November appended rows to
`us-chicago.tsv`, and nothing regenerates the envelope after prove (the file was last written on 17 October).
Regenerated once (517 rows added); `checkEnvelopeRows` names every committed envelope file a run would write, change
or remove and exits 1 on one, and is in this lane's checks and in `docs/MONITOR.md`.

**The monitor waits two seconds** (item 7; `monitor/common.py`). The client's shared interval between requests was 1.5
s and is 2 s at every source; its test holds two seconds as a floor. `muftiyat_kg.py`'s own gap was two seconds
already and stays written.

**The checks page** (finding F32; `ProofTotals.gateTables`, `ProofTotals.tableKey`, `gate/AcrossEntries.kt`).
"{tables} published tables" was already the distinct table files and no longer the gate's rows (the review of 13
November on the Ramadan line). It is the distinct publications an authority printed: a table the monitor captured
again on a later date, the two halves a year's table was cut into for the fit, and the side file that holds a table's
imsak column are one table; the Committee's calculator tables are none; and since the review round neither is a table
the archive worked out (a town's table made of the capital's plus printed minutes, a perpetual table laid on a year:
a file whose head says DERIVED, or "mapped onto" or "assigned to" a year), nor a publication another entry owns.
"{days} place-days" is the tables' own, each printed day once across the timetables: a day whose table two entries
read (a cautious entry and its member, a region's default and the authority inside it) is counted at the entry that
owns the publication (the authority's own, then a cautious entry, then a region's default) and is the other's
`sharedDays` in its stamp. On the merged line the gate's ordinary rows read 5,146 table files, which are 3,830
published tables; the stamps hold 948,682 place-days, 36,079 of them shared, so the page reads 912,603 (on 13
November, before the review and the merge: 4,052 tables, of which some 317 were worked out, and 909,501 place-days,
of which some 78,971 were counted twice). A stamp's own `placeDays`, and About's figure, stay the entry's own. No
string changed, in any language. Limits, said so that they are not lost: a perpetual table held only as years it was
laid on is counted as no table at all; a publication normalised differently under two folders may still count twice;
and the page's held-out and Ramadan totals, which it does not print, are still plain sums of the stamps.

**The review round (14 November).** Two reviews read the lane's work; every finding was applied except the three
parts named at the end.
- *A day the margins saw is a fit day in whichever file it is printed* (`Counted`, by date). The monitor pins every
  capture under its own date, so a fitted table fetched again lay at a new path and read as held out: 7,524 Fajr days
  of Diyanet's European cities and 399 days of every event at FIDS's Zürich. A cell is now held out only on a day no
  fit cell of the same event stands on at the same place (the entry, a cautious row's member, the unit or the point).
  Diyanet Europe's held-out Fajr tally went from 41,345 to 1,363, FIDS's from 1,676 to 29.
- *A cautious entry's member tables are fit where the member's are*, so Toronto's cautious entry no longer shows 175
  held-out days of tables its members were fitted on, and Belgium's, France's, Norway's, Sweden's, Ireland's and
  Australia's fall likewise (table below).
- *A held-out day two captures print is tallied once.*
- *A derived table is held out only where its source is.* `@fitted` lines now name the derived files whose source a
  margin was set on: Dar al-Ifta's towns (al-Aqsa's table plus printed minutes: 2012, 2026, and 2027 for Fajr,
  sunrise, Maghrib, Isha and the end of eating; 2027's Dhuhr and Asr stay held out), the Jamiat's three fitted towns in
  2029, IACAD's mapped years, Dar al-Fatwa's 2025–2027, the Daimi pages of Karachi for 2027, the Islamic Foundation's
  permanent calendar in 2027, and al-Aqsa 2026 under the Levant's region. JAKIM's lines were rewritten against the zone
  round's paths: every day of its 47 new zones' tables set its margins. Looked at in the same sweep and left as their
  files have them: Qatar's derived 2026, the African region's stress rows, Kosovo, Oman's 2029, Kemenag's 2028 imsak
  and Algeria; the Jamiat's other towns and Darul Ihsan's Pretoria stay held out.

- *The Americas' band*: 43.5°, thirteen held-out tables, the two mislabelled rows made fit, "the app's model" said in
  the KDoc and here, and `AmericasFarLatitudeTest` widened to what it claimed (both Asr schools, a grid of latitudes in
  both hemispheres, the day as shown with its ends, the region's Fajr below the band).

- *Not applied, and why.* (a) Dropping the capture date from the `@fitted` prefixes: the rule by date already makes a

Read with the table: `bd.ifb` shows no held-out day because the Bangladesh lane marked its own rows fit (its note:
the rule they check was written after the review found those cells early at such points), and Dhaka's even days fall
on dates the fitted permanent calendar holds; `ps.iftaa` and `lb.fatwa` show none because every table they hold is
the fitted source plus printed minutes or a year the perpetual table was laid on; `ae.iacad.dubai` likewise. An entry
with no held-out day is one whose margins have seen everything held for it, not one that was tested more.

The worst lateness of every entry is the Ramadan line's, with one exception that is not this lane's doing: Oman's
Dhuhr reads 2 where the line's committed stamp reads 1. The line's `stamps/om.mara.json` was written before its reach
rows landed (it counts 39,127 cells an event, the tables' own; with `om-mara-reach.tsv` the gate checks 670,490), and
the reach's worst Dhuhr is 2, within the limit of 2, as the Egypt lane's entry says. Every unit's own-point worst is
unchanged (`own-points-worst.tsv` is rewritten the same). Of the checked timetables the worst are Fajr 126, Isha 62
and the end of eating 132 min at Tatarstan's summer nights, and since the zone round JAKIM's sunrise 13, Dhuhr 8, Asr
20, Maghrib 9 and imsak 12.

**Tests.** `CountedTest` (new): a table counts at its first row and a reach row gives way to another file's; a test
row replaying a fitted table is a fit row, by event; a `@fitted` line makes its cells fit cells and names a prefix;
promise-only rows are in neither rule; and from the review round, a later capture of a fitted table is fit on the days
the fitted one holds and held out on the days it adds, a cautious row's cell is fit where its member's is, and a
held-out day two captures print is tallied once. `AcrossEntriesTest` (new): a publication two entries read is counted
at its owner and is the other's shared days; a derived table is no published table. `MonthByMonthTest`: an imsak that
only a table read by hand prints is fetched by no source and the entry stays named, and one the captures print is
covered like any other. `CheckStampsTest` and `StampSummaryTest`: a unit proven only in fitted rows is named apart and
refused with `--ramadan`, an imsak shown and printed is asked for, an imsak no table prints is a notice, a
Published-method entry is a notice and never a refusal, and the plain run prints the line and exits 0.
`GateManifestTest`: a `-promise.tsv` row is promise-only and no published table; `@fitted` parses and a malformed one
fails loudly. `ProvenTest`: the published tables are the distinct publications, never more than the files, a later
capture, a half and an imsak side file adding none. `EnvelopeCoverageTest`: the committed envelope files are what a
run would write. `AmericasFarLatitudeTest` (new, app): at far places of both hemispheres, in both Asr schools, on every
day of 2026–2027, no start of the day as shown is before the model's at the same point and no sunrise, end of eating
or other end after it; below the band the region's method stands alone, Fajr included; the band begins at the same
latitude in both hemispheres. `KemenagImsakTest` (new, app): the rule above. `AboutTimesUiStateTest` and
`ProofStampsTest`: Toronto's stamp is the tables' own days at one place; Umm al-Qura's places are those with a row of
their own, at least 173, the day's figure held nowhere. Monitor `tests.py`: the interval is at least two seconds, and
the curl fallback waits it.

**For the owner.** (1) Fitted rows and the Ramadan build. As built, a unit whose Ramadan 1448 days are held only in
tables its margins were fitted on is refused by `checkStamps -Pramadan=1448`, like a unit with no table at all:
Sarajevo, Dubai, Kemenag's 246 units, 85 of Oman's, Doha, Makkah and Madinah, and 39 of JAKIM's zones among them. The
times there are right on every one of those days (the gate compared them); what is missing is a table the fit never
saw. Recommendation: keep them named in the plain run, as now, and let the Ramadan build pass a unit that is checked
on every guarded day in a fitted table once the entry holds a held-out Ramadan elsewhere (O4's own test of the
method), which is one constant (`FITTED_ONLY_REFUSES = false`) and its test; the strict version stands until you say
so. (2) The far south, and Antarctica. The Committee's calculator is the only reference held there, and the cost is a
later Fajr at 16 cities, large on the summer nights of the far south (up to 100 min). Recommendation: keep it for the
Ramadan update (Ramadan 1448 begins on 8 February, at the tail of that season: by this lane's own rough arithmetic on
the Ushuaia table against the 15° dawn, not the gate's, Fajr there is later by some 25 min on its first days and about
5 on its last, and the end of eating does not move, so the fast itself is untouched), and ask the Muslim communities
of Ushuaia, Río Grande and Punta Arenas which timetable they follow; if a community's own table is found it replaces
the band there. Antarctica is the same question one step on: a research station is shown the world default, whose
Fajr is before the Committee's model on every day of the year (12 to 183 min at Esperanza). No app city is there and
no table a station follows is held. Recommendation: give Antarctica the band up to the Antarctic Circle in the engine
release after this one, with a decided rule beyond it (the model is not proven in the polar day), rather than tonight
in another lane's default. (3) The figures a reader sees fall by design: the checks page from 12,349,784 place-days
to 912,603 and to 3,830 published tables, Umm al-Qura's About from 2,493,800 days at 3,242 places to 132,866 at 173,
Toronto's from 1,400 days at 6 places to 350 at 1. Every one of the 12 million comparisons is still made at every
gate run, and the stamp keeps them under `replays`. Recommendation: ship the tables' own figures as they are, and if
you want the replays said, add one sentence to the checks page ("and replays them at N more points") in the seven
languages; not done here. (4) "Published method" entries are named for Ramadan and not refused (38 today).
Recommendation: keep that: a published method is shown as such, never as a checked timetable, and refusing a build
for it would hold the release on calendars most of those authorities never publish. (5) Four of the monitor's
fetchers send a POST, each to the authority's own public page as its own form or widget does: Libya's awqaf widget
and IRN's month page (the sites' own AJAX actions), JAKIM's e-solat date-range form, and Jordan's ASP.NET grid
paging. They are from 28 September and 2 October, before this lane, and tonight's web rule (plain GET only) was
written for the lanes' own fetching; the review asks whether it binds the monitor too. Recommendation: allow them by
name in the monitor's rules (a public form's own request, no login, no key, one at a time at the monitor's interval)
and keep "plain GET" for everything new; if you would rather have none, JAKIM's and Jordan's future years lose their
automatic source and become hand-read. (6) Kemenag's 228 units show an imsak that is the rule's (ten minutes before
the authority's dawn), checked against print at the 18 units whose tables carry the column and at no other.
Recommendation: before the Ramadan build, read Kemenag's Imsakiyah 1448 for a spread of those units when it is
published (January) and add the rows; the rule test holds the wording meanwhile.

## Reach limits: Bahla and Türkiye's 84 il centres are proven across their reaches, and no reach proof is owed (14 November) — rulings R254–R255, branch `engine/reach-limits`

Off the Ramadan line at 1ef4550ce; archive branch `reach-limits`, off 07a0ddd4. Not pushed. The release hold that came
with the Egypt belt lane (commit d3f4c4f35, that lane's review; ruling R213 itself is the belt) named two debts: Bahla
(Oman), left out of its reach file, and Türkiye's il centres, whose reach file had never been written. Both are paid here by measuring, never by excusing: no reach row of either is early and none
ends late, and where a unit's own table read across its reach is later than its limit said, the limit is raised to
the measured worst and About says the larger figure; no site page changes. No time shown changes anywhere. One other
thing a reader can meet does change with the limits, the point at which a manual adjustment is asked about a second
time in stronger words ("What a reader sees", below). No entry and no place changes kind (all stay checked
timetables).

**R254. Bahla's limits are its reach's worst: 3 min for Asr, Isha and the end of eating** (`ReachRows.kt`,
`om-mara-reach.tsv`, 4,213 rows, 39 of them Bahla's at 13 points). Two of Bahla's 13 reach points, (23.032758,
57.300367) and (23.033577, 57.225899), lie inside Al Hamra's circle, where the engine keeps the later start and the
earlier end of the two localities' tables (R210). There Bahla's table is met 3 min late on 150 place-days (May to
July 2027 and June to July 2029): 230 cells over the old 2 min (Asr 48, Isha 104, end of eating
78). The three limits go 2 → 3, by exception and with the reason said; Fajr, sunrise, Dhuhr and Maghrib keep 2.
Bahla leaves `Spec.leftOut`. About's figure for Bahla goes from "at most 1 min" to "at most 3 min": the own point
still reads 1, and the own-point guard (below) holds it there.

**R255. A Turkish il centre's limits are the worst the gate measures across its reach too** (`tr-diyanet-reach.tsv`,
5,029 rows at 1,760 points for 84 units; archive `code/manual/tr-diyanet/limits.py` and `beside.py`, whose
`beside-limits.tsv` now holds 552 unit-events and writes `DiyanetBesideDistricts.kt`). Before the limits moved the
reach rows read 0 early and 0 late ends, and 102,308 cells over the old limits in 71 of the 84 units, at 462 places
on 31,627 place-days (Fajr 20,618, sunrise 12,306, Dhuhr 7,774, Asr 10,052, Maghrib 11,037, Isha 14,413, end of
eating 26,108). 219 unit-events were raised and none lowered: 184 from 1 to 2 min, 15 from 1 to 3, 19 from 2 to 3 and
one from 2 to 4 (by prayer: Fajr 31, sunrise 40, Dhuhr 16, Asr 26, Maghrib 28, Isha 34, end of eating 44). Thirteen
units needed nothing (Afyonkarahisar, Bilecik, Burdur, Denizli, Giresun, Isparta, Karabük, Kilis, Kırklareli,
Nevşehir, Siirt, Trabzon, İzmir). The worst, each with the place and month of its worst:

- Ankara, end of eating 2 → 4: 1,299 cells at 3 places on 291 place-days, worst in June 2027 at (40.109744,
  32.941035); Isha 2 → 3: 860 cells, 188 place-days, May 2026 at (40.066643, 32.679745).
- Edirne, end of eating 1 → 3: 4,225 cells at 4 places on 897 place-days, May 2026 at (41.75589, 26.581299).
- Silivri, Fajr 1 → 3: 2,683 cells at 3 places on 566 place-days, May 2026 at (41.008293, 28.104688).
- Niğde Isha (736 place-days), Sinop Fajr (570), Çankırı end of eating (560), Samsun Fajr (559, at 10 places), Bolu
  Isha (509), Ardahan end of eating (507), Amasya Isha (408), Kastamonu Isha (397), Çorum end of eating (383),
  Kütahya Fajr (354), Yozgat Isha (344), Eskişehir end of eating (235), Malatya Isha (172): each 1 → 3, in May and
  June 2026.
- Bursa, end of eating 2 → 3 (424 cells, 88 place-days) and Isha 2 → 3 (334, 68); İstanbul, sunrise 2 → 3 (20 cells
  on 6 place-days, December 2026 at (40.885157, 29.141616)) and Fajr 2 → 3 (one cell, June 2026).
- The largest of the 184 from 1 to 2: Karaman Isha (3,945 cells), Çatalca end of eating (3,886) and sunrise (3,767),
  Hatay Fajr (3,268).

**What a reader sees.** About's "at most N min after" is the unit's worst over the five starts, the reach's now
included. Türkiye's 84 units read 2 min (44), 3 min (39) and 4 min (Ankara) where they read 1 (18), 2 (38), 3 (27)
and 4 (1): 26 units rose, 14 from 1 to 2 (Adana, Bingöl, Çanakkale, Gümüşhane, Hakkâri, Şile, Karaman, Kayseri,
Muğla, Şanlıurfa, Sivas, Tekirdağ, Tokat, Uşak), 4 from 1 to 3 (Silivri, Malatya, Niğde, Yozgat) and 8 from 2 to 3
(Artvin, Aydın, Bolu, Kırıkkale, Kocaeli, Kütahya, Sakarya, Samsun). No Turkish unit says 1 min any more. Oman:
Bahla alone, 1 → 3. The site's eight Turkish and two Omani city pages keep their figures (İstanbul 3, Ankara 4,
Bursa 3, Diyarbakır 3, İzmir, Konya, Antalya and Gaziantep 2; Muscat 2, Salalah 1). No string and no test pinned an
old figure. So that the larger limits cannot hide a slip at the place a table is printed for, `om-mara.tsv` and
`tr-diyanet.tsv` join the own-point guard (`OwnPointWorst.GROUPS`; 259 and 1,419 new rows in
`own-points-worst.tsv`, 6,252 in all).

The manual adjustment's stronger question moves with the limits (found by both reviews of 14 November; the first
write-up of this entry did not say it). Moving a prayer earlier by hand is always asked about ("Show Fajr before
Diyanet? A prayer prayed before its time must be repeated…"), and past the timetable's own margin it is asked again in
stronger words that state the margin ("Taqwa's Fajr is at most 3 min after Diyanet, so −4 min moves it before that
time…"). The margin is the same limit About prints (`marginMinutes`, `TimetableModels.kt`), so it rose where the
limit rose: at 135 Turkish unit-prayers (Fajr 31, Dhuhr 16, Asr 26, Maghrib 28, Isha 34; sunrise cannot be adjusted)
and at Bahla's Asr and Isha. At Silivri, Samsun and Sinop (Fajr) and Niğde (Isha), where the limit went from 1 to 3,
an adjustment of −2 or −3 min now gets the first question only and the stronger one starts at −4. The code is left as
it is, for a reason: the stronger words say "at most N min after", and with N below the reach's limit that sentence
would be untrue toward the reach's edge (Silivri's Fajr runs 2 or 3 min after the table on 566 place-days at three
of its reach points) and would contradict the figure About prints. No adjustment is ever made without the first question. It is the owner's
to decide (below).

**The hold stays and passes.** `ReachRows.PENDING` is empty, `ReachRows.outstanding()` returns nothing and
`checkStamps -Prelease=true` exits 0 without a notice; the mechanism, its test and its place in `scripts/release.sh`
are kept for the next debt, and their comments and `docs/MONITOR.md`, `docs/STORE-CHECKLIST.md` say nothing is owed.

**The monitor.** Two recipe lines at the end of `recipes.tsv` make the weekly proof add each capture's new days at
every point of the unit's reach under the same pinned copy as the own row: `tr-diyanet * tr-diyanet-reach.tsv same *
same all -` clones the reach rows of an earlier capture of the same key, and `… index - all all -` adds the capture
at every point the file reads its unit at, which needs the monitor's index to name the unit. The first write-up had
the index line alone and said "the index names each capture's unit"; the reviews found that untrue for nine keys of
the committed index (antalya, bursa, catalca, diyarbakir, gaziantep, izmir, konya, sile, silivri still name bare
`tr.diyanet` and a point; the 62 newer il centres have no line until the fetcher has run), so a proof run before a
fetch would have given those nine an own row and no reach rows. Shown, not asserted, on a scratch copy of the archive
and of the two gate files (real printed tables only; nothing in either worktree touched): `prove --only tr-diyanet
--date 2026-11-14 --dry-run` wrote "prove 2026-11-14 (dry run): 71 rows added, 0 left out; gate 6400 -> 6471 rows,
1252257 -> 1270381 place-days, green" — Ankara (index by unit) 1 own row and 23 reach rows, İzmir (index still bare)
1 and 20, Kayseri (one of the 62, its index line as the fetcher will write it) 1 and 23, and two rows of
`tr-diyanet.tsv` beside them (the old picker's method at Diyanet's point for Ankara, İzmir at the app's point). With the `same` line taken out the same run wrote "51 rows added": İzmir's 20
reach rows are the ones missed. `CityUnitsTest` asks for both lines of every table the fetcher grows under one key
(Diyanet's districts, ESA's towns) and for the index line where a unit's own table was read by hand; taking either
line out fails it (tried: lines 623 and 637). **Growth:** a reach row is added per point only for a capture that
brings days the unit's rows lack, and older pinned rows are not superseded. The 22 older units hold every day to
31 December 2027 and add nothing until Diyanet prints further; the 62 add their own row and about 1,300 reach rows
together on a run that brings them new days; with all 84 bringing new days a run adds about 1,760 (the file holds
5,029 today, 3,083 of them the 22 units' seven pinned captures). Folding older pinned rows is left as a follow-up
(`docs/MONITOR.md`, "How fast they grow").

**The second year.** The 62 il centres of 12–13 November hold their 2026 tables alone, so their limits are measured
on one year. In the 22 units that hold 2026 and 2027 whole, five of 154 unit-events (in four units: Ankara's end of
eating 3 → 4, Tekirdağ's and Konya's sunrise, Van's Asr and Maghrib 1 → 2) read one minute more across the reach in
2027 than in 2026, and 11 read less. That figure is now a committed test, not an estimate: `a turkish reach read one
year at a time is never early and the second year's move is measured` cuts each unit's own tables by year, reads
each year across the reach and prints "22 units whose tables hold 2026 and 2027 whole, 489 points, 154 unit-events; 5
read later in 2027 than in 2026, in 4 units (by at most 1 min), 11 less late". When Diyanet prints 2027 for the 62,
expect about one unit in five to run a minute over: the proof then leaves the new row out and demotes the unit (R185), the
units test goes red on the point left out, and the limits are measured again by hand (`docs/MONITOR.md`, "Türkiye's
limits are the reach's" and "A red to expect from Türkiye's reach rows"). Nothing is shown early meanwhile, and
nothing a reader sees changes: the row that is over is later, never early, and is not added; a demotion is a tier 1
item of the proof's issue and `checkStamps` refuses the next release until the unit's limits are measured again and
its `@demoted` line taken out. None of the site's eight Turkish city pages is among the 62, so no page is held by it.

**What keeps a limit honest (the review of 14 November).** Raising a limit to what was measured must not become a
way to excuse lateness, so four guards were added. (1) `a turkish limit is its reach's measured worst and none is
over the ruling's ceiling`: every one of the 588 unit-events' recorded limits equals the stamp's measured worst or
the class's minute ("552 on a limit of their own equal to the reach's measured worst, 36 on the class's"), and none
may pass 4 min, the highest measured (Ankara); a fifth minute needs a ruling. `an omani locality's own limit is its
reach's measured worst` does the same for Oman's exceptions. These replace what `RegistryTest` used to pin by
figure. (2) Class A's one minute, said plainly: it holds at each il centre's own point (238 own-point rows, every
one at most 1) and on 36 unit-events across the reach; elsewhere the reach's limit is the measured 2 to 4. (3) An
own-point row the weekly proof adds has no line in `own-points-worst.tsv` until that file is written again, and
used to fall back to the reach's limit; it is now held to the worst of the rows already measured at the same place

run `generateReachRows --args="--only tr.diyanet"`, the gate with `-Pentry=tr.diyanet` (never
`-PgateGroup=tr-diyanet`: its stamp leaves the reach out, and `limits.py` now refuses such a stamp), then the archive's

**For the owner.** Two questions he had been asked earlier (the entry of 13 November, questions 2 and 3: Bahla's

reads its reach's worst, and **the release hold no longer waits on him**. Both are taken pending his OK and both can
be undone by cutting the reaches instead. The questions as they stand:
(1) Bahla, and every Turkish il centre: the reach kept and the measured figure said (Bahla 3 min; Türkiye at least
2 min everywhere, 26 units more than before), or the reach cut where a neighbour's table rides, which would take
those places out of a checked timetable. Recommendation: keep the reaches; a checked table at most 2 to 4 min late
serves those places better than an unchecked method, and the figure shown is true.
(2) The 62 newer il centres' limits rest on 2026 alone, so about one in five is expected to be demoted by
the weekly proof when Diyanet prints 2027, and a release is refused until the limits are measured again by hand
(the procedure is written down in `docs/MONITOR.md`); that will fall in the Ramadan build's weeks. The other ways:
the proof could treat a reach row that is only later than its limit as "limits to measure again" without demoting
the unit, or the 62 could carry a stated minute of headroom now, which would have About say a figure nobody
measured. Recommendation: keep the measured limits and the demotion (it is the guard doing its work), and do the
by-hand measure in the week Diyanet's 2027 appears, together with the 2027 reading the Ramadan guard already owes.
(3) The manual adjustment's stronger question now starts past the reach's limit (above). The other way is to take
that margin from the own point's worst, so the stronger words come sooner in the middle of a city, at the price of
a sentence that is untrue at the reach's edge and differs from About. Recommendation: leave it equal to About's
figure.

## Kazakhstan: a place inside several QMDB reaches waits for every place whose reach holds it (13–14 November) — rulings R249–R253, branch `engine/kazakhstan-ride`

Branch `engine/kazakhstan-ride`, off `engine/ramadan-final` (157b2fa6d); archive branch `kazakhstan-ride` (370a3a10),
unchanged: every table read here was already held, and nothing was fetched from the web. Not pushed.

**The owner's ruling (13 November 2026): "Kazakhstan waits for the later of the two tables, as Kyrgyzstan now
does."** It replaces, for Kazakhstan, R44's nearest place alone (the owner's decision of 9 October, kept on 13
November morning as "measured only" in the R205 entry above, whose Kazakh paragraph is the red evidence: a measured
table replayed where the place follows another unit was met early on 131 of 132 ordered pairs, Fajr and Isha by up
to 3 min, Dhuhr, Asr and Maghrib by up to 2, and 21 of the app's cities were shown before a neighbouring city's
table). The city rule of 9 October stands: the place followed and named is still the app's city where its reach
holds the user, else the nearest place.

**The rule (R249).** QMDB prints by place and draws no boundary, and its 5,676 places stand far closer than their
reaches are wide, so a user inside several reaches may follow any of those tables. Every other place whose reach
holds the user now rides beside the place followed, as that place's own day at its own point
(`CentralAsia.kazakhstanUnits`' `around`, `UnitSet.holding`, `TimetableMethod.alongside`: its own band's minutes and
its curves at its own latitude, exactly what its own point shows). Every start is the latest of those days and the
user's own; sunrise and the end of eating the earliest. The same mechanism as R205's, with one difference forced by
the bands: the Kyrgyz localities share one method, so they ride as points of it (`envelopePoints`); QMDB's places
north of 46° N read their curves at their own latitude and the bands either side of 46° and 48° N carry different
minutes, so each rides as its own day (`Alongside`, as ESA's towns and Diyanet's districts do).

What rides is a place's day as the engine computes it at the place's own point. That is QMDB's printed table only
where the table is held and gated, which is 87 of the 5,676 places; for the other 5,589 it is Taqwa's own
calculation of the day QMDB would print there, by QMDB's published rule, with no table of theirs ever seen. So
"as Kyrgyzstan" is the same mechanism but not the same proof: every Kyrgyz locality's table is held. The proof
below says what is proven for which, and the cost says how much of the wait is for which (the review of 14
November, finding 4).

**The reach each place carries (R250).** The one it already had: the distance its own table was measured to carry
by itself on 9 October (`QmdbReach`; among the places with a table held, 3.1 km at Ayagoz to 36.5 km at Zhenis),
not widened and not shortened. The wait for a neighbour is no
part of how far one table carries, so `QmdbReach` measures a reach with the place's table alone
(`Registry.methodInUnit(alone = true)`) and its fingerprint and every reach in `QmdbPlaceList` are as they were. A
wider reach would make a place wait for tables QMDB's own nearer places already answer for; a shorter one would
leave ground where the neighbouring table is met early, which is what the ruling ends.

**What need not be computed (R251).** A place stands inside up to 183 reaches, and a day beside each is the cost. South of 46° N every place keeps one method with flat curves, so each time is the sun's at the
place's latitude less four minutes a degree of longitude, and over a reach's span each event moves one way from
south to north on any one day. A place with a neighbour to its north and one to its south, each at least 0.01° of
longitude (2.4 s of the sun) to its west, never starts a prayer after both; with two such to its east it never
ends one before both: its day can never be the one shown and is set aside (`CentralAsia.riding`,
`boundedOnEverySide`). The neighbours that bound it are the band's other places whose reach holds the user. The
place followed and the user's own point bound it too, but from the west alone (corrected on 14 November, the
first review's finding 1): each start shown is the later of those two, so no start comes before either's, but
Maghrib ends at the day's Isha and Dhuhr at its standard Asr (`PrayerDay.ends`), which are the later of the two
as well, so neither can bound those two ends from the east. As first built on 13 November they counted on both
sides, and a place set aside ended Maghrib, or Dhuhr, a minute before the day's own end on 194 of 872,899
southern place-days of 2027 (Maghrib's end on 172, Dhuhr's on 22; 18 of 2,939 points; 197 days of 2028), for
instance at 43.215074, 77.729564 on 12 May 2027, where qmdb-6977's Maghrib ended a minute sooner. No time shown
moved on any of those days, the app reads Fajr's and Asr's ends alone (`TimelineBuilder`), and no gate row reads
those two ends, so nothing on screen was wrong; the "need not be computed" was, and is now true of the whole day.
Where an event's time turns inside the span it passes both ends' by 0.2 s at most (measured at every tenth of a
degree from 40° to 46° N, every day of the year), inside the 2.4 s kept clear. From 46° N nothing is set aside.
`KazakhRideTest` holds the pruned day equal to the full ride's, the whole `PrayerDay` with its ends, to the
second: every day of 2027 and 2028 at three of the review's points, every day of 2027 at the two densest points
and every 11th day on the rest of the dense southern ground (it had sampled every 37th day, which is how the
defect passed). The review ran the corrected rule against every holder riding in full: 2,957 points, 1,079,305
days of 2027, the whole day equal on every one; it keeps 54,097 riders of 149,421 where the first rule kept
52,890, about 2 % more work. The days computed beside a place's own are 8 at the median over QMDB's points and
45 at the most (47 on the 0.05° grid), where the holders are up to 183.

**Red first.** `KazakhRideTest` (commonTest), the eleven tests it holds, by what each says: (1) a place inside
several reaches is never before any holder's own day nor ends after one; (2) the audit's three pairs (Talgar and
Almaty, Kentau and Turkistan, Konaev and Otegen Batyr) wait for each other at the app's own city points and at
the middle of the ground they share, every day of 2027; (3) the place followed and its name are still the city's
or the nearest; (4) from 46° N every other holder rides as its own point shows it; (5) a southern place set aside
is bounded by those that ride, so the day is the same with it; (6) a place set aside never ends a prayer before
those that ride, on any day of 2027 and 2028; (7) the place followed and the user bound from the west alone; (8)
the densest ground computes a bounded number of days; (9) south of 46° N the AngleBased rule never binds and
every place keeps one method; (10) a place's own late limit says the wait and is one the entry or the class does
not already give; (11) a reach is still measured with its own table alone. Tests 1, 3 to 5 and 8 to 11 are the
eight of 13 November, red before the ride. This paragraph then listed the audit's pairs as one of the eight and no
test held them (the second review's finding 1): test 2 was added on 14 November and seen red with the nearest
place alone (talgar at 43.30235,77.23811 against almaty on a day of January 2027: its Fajr a minute before the time printed for almaty). Tests 6 and 7
are the first review's finding 1, red on the rule as first built.

**The proof (R252).** Tables held for 87 of QMDB's places (86 measured units), 2026 and 2027, none new. What is
proven is therefore this and no more: inside the reach of any of those 87, no time is shown before that place's
printed table, whichever place is followed. Beside the other 5,589 places Taqwa waits for its own calculation of
their day; that the calculation is not before a table it has never seen rests on the 87 that were checked (the
same rule, bands and margins), not on a row of the gate.
- `kz-qmdb-reach.tsv`, regenerated with the ride (`generateReachRows --only kz.qmdb`): each measured place's own
  tables replayed across its own ground, 3,190 rows where it had 3,372. Nothing was dropped to reach a figure: the
  grid rows are as they were (1,118 points kept of 1,376) and the rows at each event's worst point of the sweep
  fell to 460 points because with the ride the events' worst points coincide more often. The sweep read 35,234 (35,231 before the review's fix; the rows are the same)
  points, no cell early and no end late.
- The sweep had to learn the ride. A neighbour's day rides wherever its reach holds the user, so a place's lateness
  against its own table steps at each neighbour's edge, and a grid of bearings can pass a neighbour by. The first
  sweep did, and `CityUnitsTest`'s offset grid caught it: Saryagash's Dhuhr 4 and Maghrib 5 at its very edge, bearing
  307.5, where the reach of a place 68 km to the west-north-west holds a sliver under 200 m deep of the ground that
  follows Saryagash; the sweep had read 3 and 4. So for every neighbour the sweep now also reads one point where
  that neighbour's day rides and the unit is followed (`ReachRows.neighbours`, `Spec.waits`; searched on every
  degree of bearing at 27 shares of the radius, every half degree at the edge and just inside it). A neighbour's
  day is the same wherever it rides, so with one point for each neighbour that rides anywhere the search finds the
  unit followed, the sweep has read every such neighbour's day. That is narrower than this line first said ("by
  the rule and not by a grid's luck", the second review's finding 5): the search is itself a grid of bearings and
  shares, a neighbour riding only on ground it misses has no point, and the user's own sky between the points is
  still sampled. A sliver missed would understate a limit by a minute and could not make a time early. Two other
  lattices give the same worsts, event for event: `CityUnitsTest`'s offset grid (13,461 points) and the review's
  re-run of `overlapSweep` (67,914 points inside a neighbour's reach).
- `kz-qmdb-envelope.tsv`, new (`generateEnvelopeRows`, `EnvelopeRows.kazakhOverlaps`): 4,160 promise-only rows at
  1,998 places. Each held table replayed inside its reach wherever the place follows another unit (the reach rows'
  grid, a ring just inside its edge, the app's cities); and, whichever place is followed, at the middle of the
  ground its reach shares with every neighbour that has a table held too (both tables there, so each of the 36
  such pairs is held both ways), with every neighbour of another band, with 16 other neighbours spread by bearing,
  and at QMDB's two densest points against every held table whose reach holds them. Its lateness is no unit's
  figure and no limit's; the gate holds the promise alone there.
- `kz-qmdb.tsv` (the own-point and city rows) is untouched.
- The gate on the entry: 1,742 places, 7,682 rows, 1,271,660 place-days (1,265,455 held out; 102,778 in Ramadan, 102,276
  of them held out) and 1,443,940 more held to the promise alone, none early, no end late, no unit over its limit.
  The whole gate: 67,593 rows, 12,002,365 place-days and 3,507,082 more held to the promise alone, none early (the
  line had 63,615 rows, 12,068,065 place-days and 2,063,142: the 182 reach rows fewer are its 65,700 place-days
  fewer, the envelope's 4,160 rows the rest).

**The late limits, said honestly.** `kz.qmdb` stays class D (3 min) with the entry's Fajr 8, Isha 6 and end of
eating 8. Against a place's own table across its reach, the wait for the other tables adds one to three minutes,
so a measured place now carries its own limit for every event that passes those (R41: the gate's worst there, said
with its reason: "the wait for any other place's table whose reach holds the user"), sunrise, Dhuhr, Asr and
Maghrib among them where only Fajr, Isha and the end of eating had one: 70 of the 86 measured units carry one
(`QmdbPlaces.reachLimits`, generated from the stamp). The worst anywhere, before → with the ride: Fajr 10 → 10
(Petropavl and Pulemetovka as before; Kulomzino 9 → 10), sunrise 3 → 5 (Saryagash, Shardara, Zhetysay), Dhuhr 2 → 4, Asr 3 → 5
(Shymkent, Zharkent, Shelek, Zhanatas, Boralday, Taraz, Arys, Lenger), Maghrib 3 → 5 (Shymkent and Saryagash; 4 at
47 places), Isha 8 → 8, end of eating 11 → 12 min before the printed Fajr (ten places of the north and west:
Kostanay, Aksay, Aktobe, Khromtau, Aksu of Pavlodar, Atbasar, Semey, Karaganda, Kandyagash, Embi). Almaty: Fajr 4
→ 5, sunrise 2 → 3, Dhuhr 2 → 4, Asr 3 → 4, Maghrib 3 → 4, Isha 3 → 5, end of eating 2 → 5. Shymkent: 4, 2, 2, 3,
3, 4, 3 → 6, 3, 4, 5, 5, 6, 5. Astana: Fajr 8 and Isha 7 as before, sunrise 2 → 3, Dhuhr 2 → 3, Asr 3 → 4,
Maghrib 2 → 4, end of eating 11 as before. These are the worsts over a place's whole reach against its own table;
at a city's own point the move is the cost below. The limits are the measured worsts, so another lane's Kazakh
rows that move a unit's worst by a minute fail the gate until `reachLimits` is regenerated: wanted, since a limit
is a statement in About. No city and nobody moved up or down a kind.

**At the places' own points (`own-points-worst.tsv`, `CityUnitsTest`).** Of the 332 Kazakh own-point and city-point
rows 304 stand inside another place's reach too, and 300 moved. The worst over them, before → with the ride: Fajr 8 → 9, sunrise 1 → 3, Dhuhr 1 → 2, Asr 2 → 3,
Maghrib 2 → 3, Isha 6 → 7, end of eating 8 → 10; at Almaty's own point Isha 1 → 4 and the end of eating 1 → 4.
`CityUnitsTest` held every Kazakh own point to the limits from before the reach rows (Fajr 8, Isha 6, end of
eating 8, else 3), which a point inside another place's reach can no longer keep. It now holds them as it holds
the Kyrgyz (R205): a row whose point stands in no other place's reach keeps those limits; a row inside another
place's reach is held to its unit's recorded limit; and every row to its own recorded worst.

**What the ride costs (`kazakhRide -Pmode=cost`, read-only).** Every figure in this section is against what Taqwa
showed before the ride (the nearest place alone, as it was from 9 October to 13 November), not against QMDB's
printed table; against a city's own printed table the totals are the paragraph above (at the own and city points:
Fajr up to 9, sunrise 3, Dhuhr 2, Asr and Maghrib 3, Isha 7, the end of eating 10 min before the printed Fajr).
Every day of 2027. The app's list holds 84 Kazakh cities (the brief's 71
was the count inside two measured reaches); 83 stand on a QMDB unit and one, Shalkar, beyond every reach, unmoved.
Of the 83, 76 wait for another place's table and all 76 have a time moved; 7 lie in one reach alone (Aktobe,
Atyrau, Ekibastuz, Zhezqazghan, Ridder, Arkalyk, Balykshi). A time moves on 27,210 of 30,295 place-days (89.8 %);
66 cities move on all 365 days.

| event | place-days moved | +1 min | +2 min | +3 min | worst |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fajr | 71.5 % | 14,559 | 6,573 | 543 | 3 (Shymkent, 18 May 2027) |
| sunrise (earlier) | 77.9 % | 17,940 | 5,654 | 0 | 2 |
| Dhuhr | 69.0 % | 16,741 | 4,151 | 0 | 2 |
| Asr | 71.3 % | 15,784 | 5,819 | 0 | 2 |
| Maghrib | 72.0 % | 15,435 | 6,375 | 0 | 2 |
| Isha | 71.3 % | 14,111 | 7,122 | 365 | 3 (Almaty, 25 May 2027) |
| end of eating (earlier) | 76.5 % | 16,353 | 6,306 | 522 | 3 (Almaty, 28 May 2027) |

The median move, where a time moves, is one minute. No city, no QMDB point and no grid point moves by more than 3
min, so nothing passes the 5 min at which a pair was to be reported instead of ridden. Worst cities, each with
every prayer 2 min later and Fajr, Isha or the end of eating 3, on all 365 days: Shymkent, Turkistan, Esik, Aksu
(Turkistan), Saryaghash, Lenger, Turar Ryskulov, Almaty (Isha and the end of eating 3; 98 reaches hold it, 30 days
ride), Taraz, Taldykorgan, Kentau, Talghar, Merke, Shiyeli, Sarykemer. Least: Baikonur (59 days, 1 min), Satpayev,
Shalqar, Balqash, Ayagoz. QMDB's own 5,676 points (every fifth day): 5,447 wait, 5,445 moved, a time on 93.9 % of
414,348 place-days, each event on 69 to 72 %, worst 3. A 0.05° grid: 88,269 points inside any reach, 66,824 (75.7
%) inside more than one; on those (every tenth day, 2,439,078 place-days) a time moves on 89.8 %, each event on 50
to 53 %, nearly all by one minute, worst 3. Why so much moves: Almaty's own point lies inside 98 reaches of up to
36 km, the places to its west begin every prayer later, and half a degree of longitude is two minutes.

**Whose day does the moving (measured 14 November, the second review's finding 4).** `kazakhRide -Pmode=cost` now
also rides the 87 held tables' places alone. Most of the wait is not for a table Taqwa holds:

| where | stand inside another held table's reach | place-days a time moves, held tables' places alone | share of the days the whole ride moves | share of the minutes waited, by event |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the app's 76 waiting cities, every day | 23 | 7,916 of 30,295 (26.1 %) | 29.1 % | 13 to 17 % (Fajr 4,599 of 29,334 min) |
| QMDB's 5,447 waiting points, every 5th day | 551 | 32,555 of 414,348 (7.9 %) | 8.4 % | 3.9 to 4.4 % |
| the 0.05° grid's 66,824 points in several reaches, every 10th day | 1,371 | 40,013 of 2,439,078 (1.6 %) | 1.8 % | 1.0 to 1.2 % |

So at the app's cities about 85 % of the minutes waited, and 19,294 of the 27,210 place-days moved, are waited
only for a day Taqwa calculates for a village whose printed table it has never seen; over the country's ground
about 99 %. The held tables' places alone move a time by one minute nearly always, three at the worst (Fajr, Isha
and the end of eating). This is the owner's first question below.

**Do the tables agree.** A pair whose two tables differed by more than the ground between them explains was to be
the owner's question, not ridden blindly. `kazakhRide -Pmode=pairs`: of the 87 held tables 36 pairs
share ground, 26,280 days printed in both. The printed difference less the engine's own difference between the two
points: sunrise, Dhuhr, Asr and Maghrib within one minute on every day (rounding); Fajr 2 min apart on 31 days and
3 on 7, Isha 2 on 33 and 3 on 5, all of them in the north (Karaganda and Temirtau, Petropavl and Vagulino, Pavlodar
and Aksu, Temirtau and Saran, Vagulino and Krasny Yar, Bugrovoe and Vagulino), where QMDB's AngleBased twilight
steps with the latitude and the entry's limits already say so. No pair disagrees beyond that, so every pair rides
and no pair goes to the owner.

**What it costs the phone (`kazakhRide -Pmode=time`, JVM on this Mac under a load of about 28).** Before: resolving
a place 164 µs at the median over the app's Kazakh cities, a day 48 µs. With the ride: resolving 914 µs (5.6
times, once per place), a day 315 µs at the median (6.5 times) and 1,273 µs at the worst city; at QMDB's densest
point (40.686322, 68.285832, 45 days riding) resolving 3,185 µs and a day 816 µs; Almaty 2,229 and 556 µs (27
riding), Astana 807 and 447 (8), Shymkent 1,928 and 499 (26). The first place of all, which builds the 5,676
units, 49 ms where it was 26. No memory is held beyond the day's own: the riders are found from the units the set
already holds, and a method is built per rider only while a place is resolved. A month of days at the densest
point is about 25 ms on the JVM where a month at a city was about 1.5; a phone is several times slower.
Measured again after the review's fix (14 November, load about 13): the riders at these points are as many as
before (45, 27, 8 and 26; the 2 % more are elsewhere), resolving 541 µs and a day 213 µs at the median city (worst
701), the densest point 1,922 and 545 µs, Almaty 1,283 and 370, Astana 475 and 291, Shymkent 1,188 and 343, the
first place of all 39 ms: the same cost, read under less load.
Not built, kept as a follow-up should a slow phone show it: south of 46° N the riders all share one method and
could ride as points of it (`startPoints`), a day costing little more than the place's own.

**The gate's memory (R253).** The gate keeps each distinct row setting's fingerprint until the stamp is written,
every method in full canonical words. With the ride a Kazakh row's words carry up to 45 other places' methods:
495,627 characters at the longest and 508 million over the entry's 3,720 settings, and the whole gate ran out of
its 2 GB after 79 minutes. `Stamps.fingerprint` now holds words longer than 65,536 characters as their SHA-256 and
length (letters only, so nothing in it reads as a double); every other entry's longest is 34,966 (ca.cautious),
so the digest moved no other entry's fingerprint (each of the 80 other stamps did change, by its `engineHash`
line alone, since `Registry.kt` and `Units.kt` are core sources: expected; the fix of 14 November is in
`CentralAsia.kt`, no core source, and moved `kz.qmdb`'s stamp alone), and `CanonicalTest` holds that the digest still moves with one rider fewer or one
rider's point moved. The Kazakh part of the gate alone takes about 6 min on this Mac when it is quiet and
the whole gate 15 min 30 s (18 and 35 min under the night's load of nine lanes); the tools' tests took 44 min
under that load, `CityUnitsTest`'s Kazakh grid most of it (18 min 34 s alone). The weekly monitor's prove will
feel both.

**About and the support texts.** Unchanged, and no statement in them became untrue: nothing in the seven languages
says a Kazakh user is given the nearest place alone. About's own figure for a Kazakh city ("up to N min after the
table") reads the stamp and grows with the limits above (Almaty 4 → 5, Shymkent 4 → 6). That figure is the worst
over the starts alone (`measuredStartsWorst`, `AboutTimesScreen.kt`: "never another unit's worst, nor an end's"),
so the ends' figures (the end of eating up to 12 min before the printed Fajr, sunrise up to 5 min before the
printed one) are in the stamp and `reachLimits` and nowhere in About, as for every other entry. And the wait
itself is said nowhere to the user: About's sentences for a Kazakh place ("Taqwa calculates them the way QMDB
does, with a safety margin", `about_authority_unchecked_body`; "Checked on N days so far: never before QMDB's, up
to N minutes after", `about_checked_so_far_with_data`) are true but silent about up to 30 other places' days at
Almaty. The same holds for Kyrgyzstan since R205. Not rewritten here (seven languages, and no statement is
untrue); the owner's third question below.

**For the owner.**

1. The cost, plainly, and whose tables it is for. Against what Taqwa showed before the ride, nearly every Kazakh
   city's every prayer is one or two minutes later (Fajr and Isha up to three) on most days of the year, because
   some village inside the same reach lies to its west. Against the city's own printed QMDB table the totals are
   larger, since the margins Taqwa already kept come first: at the cities' and places' own points Fajr up to 9 min
   after the table, Isha 7, Asr and Maghrib 3, Dhuhr 2, sunrise 3 before and the end of eating up to 10 before
   the printed Fajr; across a place's whole reach 10, 8, 5, 5, 4, 5 and 12. And most of the wait is not for a
   table Taqwa holds: QMDB's table is held for 87 of its 5,676 places, only 23 of the 76 waiting cities stand
   inside another held table's reach, and about 85 % of the minutes the cities wait are for a village whose day
   Taqwa calculates and whose printed table it has never seen. Your sentence was "the later of the two tables";
   what is built is the latest of every QMDB place's day whose reach holds the user, table held or not, because
   QMDB does serve a table for each of those places and the calculation is the one the 87 were checked against.
   Proven: never before any of the 87 held tables. Not proven by a row, only by the same rule: the other 5,589.
   The ways open: (a) keep as built; (b) ride the 87 held tables' places alone, about a sixth of the cost at the
   cities, and a user inside an unheld village's reach may then be shown a time before the table QMDB prints for
   that village, which is what the ruling ends, only unseen; (c) keep as built and capture more of QMDB's tables
   later (its own year API, one GET a place, the places around the app's cities first), so that the proof is like
   for like with Kyrgyzstan's. A shorter riding reach would also cost less and would leave ground inside a
   village's reach shown before its table; not built. Recommended: (a) now, (c) as a follow-up; never (b) without
   your word.
2. The ends. The end of eating now comes up to 12 min before the printed Fajr across the reach of ten northern
   and western places (11 before), and sunrise, Asr and Maghrib up to 5 min from a place's own table at a handful
   of southern places, above class D's 3. All on the safe side. The starts' figure is said in About; the ends'
   are in the stamp only, as for every entry. Recommended: accept the limits; whether About should also say how
   early an end may come is a question for every entry, not for Kazakhstan alone, and nothing was changed.
3. About says nothing of the wait, in Kazakhstan or (since R205) in Kyrgyzstan: a user at Almaty reads that Taqwa
   calculates the way QMDB does with a safety margin, and that it is never before QMDB's and up to N minutes
   after. True, and silent about the other places waited for. Recommended: one sentence in the seven languages
   with the next release that touches About ("where several places' timetables reach you, Taqwa waits for the
   latest of them"), not a blocker for this one.

## The second audit's monitor findings: the whole gate's heap, a source that read nothing, the authority's own capture over a mirror's, a held day re-read otherwise, the printed imsak watched, and the hand-read editions asked before Ramadan (14 November) — rulings R280–R284, branch `engine/monitor-fixes`

Branch `engine/monitor-fixes`, off `engine/ramadan-final` (131317c2c); archive branch `monitor-fixes` (off 69b32218),
whose one commit is the workflow copied from the public template. Findings G17, G18, G19, G20, G22 and G25 of the
second trust audit (`.superpowers/sdd/2026-11-12-overnight/audit2-findings.md`). Nothing fetched from the web (fixtures
only), no gate file, stamp, engine file or `shared/` file changed: no time shown moves, no label changes, no city page
moves. Not pushed.

**R280, the whole gate's heap (G17).** `monitor` was at 2 GB and `prove` at 3 GB while both run the whole gate in
their own JVM (the gate and the tools' tests were raised to 4 GB when 2 GB ran out on the merged line). Both are at
4 GB now. Prove held two whole results at once (the base gate's and each re-evaluation's), and a result holds every
entry's place-days as sets of longs, over a gigabyte at this size: prove now keeps what it needs of the base (the
entries red, the checked timetables, the place-days) inside a helper so no local keeps the result, lets each round's
result and its failing entries go before the gate runs again, and evaluates the base again only on the one path that
writes stamps from it (a demotion with no row kept). The workflow's new step "The runner's memory" logs MemTotal,
MemAvailable, swap and CPUs before the monitor runs and annotates a runner under 6 GB; `monitor.sh` ("the check step
wrote no result ... the JVM ran out of heap"), `prove.sh` ("prove could not run ... its JVM ran out of heap") and
ProveMain's report name an OutOfMemoryError when it is the cause. `HeapGuard` holds the four heaps equal, the base let
go, the step's place and the messages.

The heap was half of G17; the job's time is the other. The monitor job had 170 minutes for the fetch, the monitor's
whole-gate check, prove's base gate and rounds and prove's checks (generateProofStamps, the golden vector, checkStamps,
the tools' tests, the generator, the site's and the app's tests), and the line's gate is five times main's of 9
November, whose run took 129 minutes. The job now has 350 (GitHub's ceiling for a hosted job is 360), the memory step
records the job's start, and prove runs under `timeout` with what is left less 25 minutes: a prove stopped there is put
back in the step (its pinned copies under `archive/tables/pinned/`, every change in Taqwa's checkout), its code is 2 and
the run fails loudly with "prove ran out of the job's time", while the handoff of what the monitor captured is still
packed and committed. `prove.sh` streams prove's errors to the log as they come (`tee`), so a stopped prove still shows
them. On the demotion path with no row kept, the last round's result and its failing entries are let go before the base
gate runs again (the review found the loop's result still reachable there). How long the whole job takes on GitHub's
runner at this size is not measured: this Mac's figures (whole gate 47 min and the tools' tests 37 min while other lanes
ran; the prove dry run 5 h 50 min while it swapped) are no guide either way, and a rehearsal dispatch with prove, or the
first Monday, says it.

Why cloud prove was reported blocked since 2 November: the tools' tests prove.sh runs held live figures (İstanbul's
case, Diyanet Europe's curves and cross-year test, Kuala Lumpur's tile, JAKIM's 2027 test) and failed once the captures
moved on, so prove put everything back every week. That was fixed in the line's base by f81382b8e (tests on pinned
copies and stamps as of a date), and main's 4d2583793 ("the weekly monitor's captures of 2026-11-13 proven (39 rows)")
is the cloud proving again on 13 November. Nothing of it is left in the repo; the merger folds main's two newer commits
(d4c994483, 4d2583793) and the archive's origin/main state into the line, as the audit says.

**R281, a source that read nothing it was given (G19).** The audit's harness made JAKIM (60 zones) and the Kyrgyz
Muftiate (115 localities) report "ok" with zero tables when every cell came back in a notation they cannot read. Now:
JAKIM's days with a cell that is not a time are an error naming how many and the first (the days are not taken; the
live file merges, so the held ones stand), and an answer with days none of which could be read is an error too. The
Muftiate's year with such a cell is an error and is not filed at all (its table replaces the held year, merge off, so
a part year would have thrown the rest away). And `fetch.run_source` fails any fetcher that made requests, filed no
table, recorded no error and noted cells that are not a time (Habous's zero-table case too, before its three-day
unturned rule). `UnreadFormat` holds all four on invented 12-hour times.

**R282, the authority's own capture where a mirror's rows are gated (G18).** Prove decided whether a capture becomes
a row by dates alone, so e-solat's own 2027 table (asked by POST every run from October, the owner's allowance) could
never replace the api.waktusolat.app copy nine zones and their towns are gated on (Kuala Lumpur, Johor Bahru, Kota
Bharu, Kangar, George Town, Kuching, Pulau Aur, Tioman, Cameron Highlands). A row reading a republisher's mirror (its
note names `(mirror)`, or its file is a `-mirror` copy) now holds no day of an authority's own capture: the capture is
planned as new and the gate holds both, so the authority's own days are proven and R185 can demote on them. The new
row's note drops the family's `(mirror)`, and a mirror capture's row carries it. A mirror's capture is held by any row,
as before. `jakim.py` stores e-solat's whole year ahead unmerged (`merge` off at 365 days or more), so the live file
is the authority's alone, day for day, and its index name no longer says mirror. No e-solat 2027 capture of those nine
zones is in the monitor yet (no web in this lane): the first cloud run after the merge takes it. So the mechanism is
fixed and the data is not yet: until that capture is proven, those nine zones and their towns are checked against the
mirror's 2027 only. Whole is counted on the days `checked` took (a day with an unread cell is not taken, so the held one
stands, as R281 says), and a part year that is merged over held days the capture does not print keeps the `(mirror)`
mark, its imsak capture too: those held days may be the mirror's, so prove never lays them on the authority, and R185
waits for e-solat's whole year (a review found a 200-day answer filed as the authority's own over mirror days).

**R283, a held day re-read otherwise (G20).** A capture whose every day the target held planned no row, so an
authority's correction of a held day (e-solat's every-run re-read, Kemenag's re-read month, Habous's re-posted month)
never reached the gate and R185 (c) was true only for days never held. Now, when every day is held, the capture is
compared cell by cell with the holding rows' tables: by event and date, against every holding row on the same clock
that prints that event. A day it prints otherwise than all of them becomes a row of those days alone, pinned as
`<key>.changed-<first day>-<count>.txt` with a comment saying so, its note "N held days re-read otherwise, held as now
printed (ruling R283)". The gate judges it like any row; an early start or late end in it leaves it out and demotes,
exactly as on a new day. A cell the capture leaves empty, or one no held row prints (a slip or a day the hand reading
left out), is no change, and a row on another clock is not compared, so an unchanged weekly re-read still adds nothing.

What it found on the archive at once (the prove dry run below): one capture, Zhezkazgan 2026, whose live file held
QMDB's reply of 9 November, the reply that broke QMDB's own band rule on 302 days (Maghrib at the 48N band's minutes
below 48N) and that `qmdb.py` now refuses as "QMDB answered two ways". Under R283 those 302 held days would have been
planned as a correction, and a glitch could have demoted kz.qmdb's unit. The archive's live file is QMDB's reply of
10 October again (archive commit b2675835: it keeps the band rule, prints exactly what the gate holds, and the state's
and index's hash follow it; every other QMDB reply of 9 November keeps the rule). The cloud archive's main still holds
the 9 November file: see "For the merger".

**R284, the printed imsak watched (G25).** The fetchers dropped the imsak column, so JAKIM's and Kemenag's imsak proof
stopped at the hand-read years and a widened imsak (SBH02's 20 min of March 2026) would not have been seen weekly.
`jakim.py` and `kemenag.py` now keep each table's imsak as its own capture, `<key>-imsak`: two columns, the Subuh (as the
day's table holds it, a slip left `-`) and the imsak as printed, exactly the layout of the hand read-backs under
`archive/tables/imsak/`; columns `- Im`, Perlis's `- E` as my-jakim.tsv reads it. An imsak is kept as printed whatever
its distance from Subuh (leaving out an earlier end is how a late end is excused, R228's reasoning); one more than 15
min before it, or after it (then `-`), is raised; one at it is kept, since Perlis prints no precaution and its imsak is
its Subuh on most days (the read-backs: 0 min on all 365 days of 2026, 0 or 1 min in 2027), which the first version
raised as an error on every run: an error while the day is ahead, a note once past (the
year is re-read every run, so SBH02's March would otherwise be an error every week to December; `common.raise_imsak`).
Prove: only a recipe line whose pattern ends `-imsak` matches such a key (`Recipe.matches`), so `*` and `jakarta-2*`
never read it; an imsak capture holds, and is held by, rows that read ends alone sharing an event (an imsak row no
longer holds a day's starts either); and `archive/tables/imsak/<source>/<capture>/<key>.txt` counts as that source's
`<key>-imsak`, so the hand read-back is the family (columns `- Im` or `- E`), and a later year's key finds it through
the same source while a day's table and an imsak are never each other's family. recipes.tsv reads the imsak at every
JAKIM zone (`*-imsak`, my-jakim.tsv), its 42 zones' towns (my-jakim-cities.tsv) and the 18 Kemenag kab/kota whose imsak
id-kemenag-imsak.tsv holds. The monitor's own check (`TableCheck`) reads an imsak capture's Subuh column as the day's
Fajr, since the gate checks ends alone only on days a start holds; the row it offers to paste keeps `- Im`. MUIS prints
no imsak in its daily data, Brunei has no fetcher (bn-mora-taqwim is read by hand) and Libya's fetcher already keeps
it, so JAKIM and Kemenag are the two. `PrintedImsak` (Python) and three ProveTest/TableCheckTest cases hold it.

On the first run after the merge: each zone's 2026 and 2027 imsak capture is new. 2026's is held by the hand
read-backs and adds nothing unless e-solat now prints otherwise; 2027's, gated so far only on the mirror's imsak (the
nine zones) or on hand read-backs of e-solat, gets rows where it is e-solat's own and the hand rows are a mirror's.
Kemenag's imsak captures fill as months are fetched (current and next month every run, the re-read month, and the next
year from October); 2027 and 2028 of the 18 places stay on their hand read-backs until re-read.

**G22, the hand-read editions in sources.tsv.** tj.default, ci.default and pk.karachi/in.karachi rest on hand-read
editions with no sources.tsv line, and being class D they have no Ramadan horizon, so nothing would have asked for
Ramadan 1448's (Tajikistan's first prompt would have been the 12-month stale line in December 2027). Four manual
lines now: tj-council (tj.default, 2027-01-15: the Council of Ulama's Ramadan 1448 calendar and its Sha'ban and Ramadan
month pages), ci-cosim (ci.default, 2027-01: COSIM's Sha'ban and Ramadan calendars and its Ramadan edition, whose imsak
ci.default now derives), pk-dawateislami (pk.karachi, in.karachi, 2027-02-01: February's cards by one plain GET per city
in that month, ruling R235; the Ramadan cards stay out under R237) and mcw-far-south (default.safe.americas, 2027-11:
the Moonsighting Committee's 2028 calculator for the far-south promise rows, R247). Each raises "Manual source due" on
its date. The catalogue test holds the three due before Ramadan 1448 begins. A fifth, ru-dumrd (ru.dumrd, 2027-01:
DUM RD's Makhachkala pages for January and Ramadan 1448), came from the review: ru.dumrd is new on this line and its
