## The second audit's labels: a checked label is a claim about a day, whose copy the tables were, and the place's own name (14–15 November) — rulings R275–R278, branch `engine/labels`

Branch `engine/labels`, off `engine/ramadan-final` (131317c2c); archive branch `labels`, unchanged: no table was read
or fetched, nothing came from the web. Not pushed. Findings G7, G8, G9, G11, G12, G13 and G21 of the second trust audit
(`site/.superpowers/sdd/2026-11-12-overnight/audit2-findings.md`, on df74232dc). No time shown moved anywhere: every
change is in what the user is told of the times, so the gate's figures are the line's own.

**G9, app = site after a checked run ends (R275).** A city page goes dark on the first day its unit's tables were not
compared on (`Proven.verdict`), but the app kept the class the registry gives the place, so Casablanca from 1 December,
Cairo and ESA's towns from 1 January, Trabzon and the other 61 il centres checked for 2026 alone in Ramadan 1448, and
Algiers after 5 June 2027 showed no label and the card's "reproduced by Taqwa and checked against its published
timetable" on days the site refuses. Now `Resolution.on(date)` asks `CheckedDays` (new, read once from
`ProofStamps`: the unit's own runs where the stamp checks by unit, the entry's otherwise; no stamp, or a unit the
stamp does not hold, is never checked, as `Proven` holds such a page): a class A or B place on a day no run holds is
`D_AUTHORITY` for that day, the "Published method" label, the unchecked card ("… method, not yet fully checked") and
About's unchecked template, whose "Checked on N days so far: never before …, up to M minutes after" keeps the days
that were. Name, unit and measured flag stay. `Resolution.checkedClass` keeps the class it has on checked days, so
`Proven` still names the first unchecked day in its held reason ("ma.habous: no checked table day from 1 Dec 2026",
as before), and Manual adjustments' margin keeps the checked class's figure (2 for B, not D's 3: the smaller margin
asks again sooner, never later). The gate reads `Registry.resolve`, never `on`, so no stamp, limit or fingerprint
moves.

What the user sees change, counted over the app's 34,134 cities (1,653 of them A or B by the registry, every one
unchanged today, 14 November): from 16 November Tunisia's Ben Guerdane, Tabarka and Tala units (3 cities, see R277);
from 1 December Habous's 187 units (169 cities); from 1 January 2027 726 cities in all (Habous 169, ESA 159, London
Unified 150, JAKIM's 21 zones held for 2026 alone 88, Diyanet's 62 il centres 79, INM 40, DUM RT 23, Amman 15,
Brunei 3), the same through Ramadan 1448; from 6 June 2027 Algeria's three class-B bands as well (23 cities). Each
comes back the day a later build carries stamps that hold the month: the label is the build's stamps, so a month the
weekly monitor proves after a release is labelled checked from the next release on (the site from the next run).

**R277: a run is days in a row.** Tunisia's three sampled units are read every third day of 2026 and daily only from 28
September to 15 November; Oman's 2029 tables on the 1st and 15th of each month and 2028 not at all (G13). Read day by
day, the label would flip two days in three and About's date would say "checked through 1 January 2029" across an
unchecked 2028. `CheckedDays.blocks` merges runs that touch and passes over a run of one day, for the label and for
About's "checked through" (`checkedRunEnd`): Muscat on 10 January 2029 says 31 December 2027, and Tabarka is the
published method from 16 November until a build holds more of its days. The cost is the label only: a sampled day was
compared and still counts in every figure.

**G7, whose copy (R276).** JAKIM's 2025 tables of 13 zones and the 2027 tables of nine of them are api.waktusolat.app's
mirror of e-solat, not e-solat itself (every 2026 table and the zone round's 2027 for the other zones are e-solat's
own); the Islamic Foundation's Dhaka year-round table is a PDF on kivabe.com, its Ramadan pages its own. The copy
twin of F26 ("checked against myQuran's copy … not Kemenag's own pages") would be untrue of the e-solat days, so a
third twin says "partly": `RegistryEntry.partlyRepublisher` ("waktusolat.app" on `my.jakim`, "kivabe.com" on
`bd.ifb`), `AuthorityUnit.partlyRepublished` on the 13 zones and Dhaka, `Resolution.partlyRepublisher` where the
place's own tables are among them, and `CheckedClaim.part` beside `own` and `copy`. The card and About's "checked
through" say it of the place (Kuala Lumpur, George Town, Johor Bahru and Kota Bharu: "checked against its published
timetable, partly in waktusolat.app's copy of it"; Ipoh, whose tables are all e-solat's, the plain sentence); About's
tiles and "checked on … days so far" count the whole entry's days, so they say it for every JAKIM and Foundation
place; the site's description, source line, "replays" sentence, the checks page's row and the gate paragraph say it
the same way ("Some of JAKIM's tables were read from waktusolat.app's copy of them, not from JAKIM's own pages").
Four app strings and five site strings in all seven languages (values-in a twin of values-id). `RepublisherCopyTest`
holds the zones against the gate files' own paths and notes, so a zone stops saying it once e-solat's own tables
replace the mirror's rows (G18, the monitor lane's, is what would let them).

**G8.** The Levant default serves Israel alone; the PA Dar al-Iftaa prints its table for 13 Arab towns there, held for
2026 and 2027, and the region's Fajr was refit on them. `safeSideOfKey = "authority_pa_iftaa"`, R209's wording:
Nazareth, Umm al-Fahm and Rahat read "Taqwa holds only part of the timetable the Palestinian Dar al-Iftaa publishes, so it calculates
these times on the safe side of that part", never "no local timetable is known". Not done for Tanzania: the Africa
default serves 50 countries, Darul Ihsan's two tables are test rows the region was not fitted on, and naming it in
Nigeria would be untrue; a Tanzanian entry of its own would be needed (left as it was).

**G11.** "days at 1 places": `about_stat_days_at_one_place` ("days at one place", no figure) where a stamp holds one
place, in the app's checked and cautious tiles and the site's (`Document.kt`); London, Doha, Toronto, Dublin and the
other single-place stamps.

**G12.** Habous's 187 units, Oman's localities, Algeria's seats, bands and rests and JAKIM's 60 zones are
`named = false`, as Egypt's towns since F34: About and the site call the place by the app's own name in the reader's
language, never "في Casablanca", "suivis pour Algiers" or "used in SBH01". The unit's name stays for the gate's
fingerprint, so no stamp moves.

**G21, ruling R69.** The Council of Ulama's misread Shom and Bomdod and COSIM's three misprinted cells
(`tj-default.tsv`, `ci-default.tsv` and this log's Tajikistan entry), e-solat's SBH02 imsak of March 2026 and QMDB's
Almaty Fajr in the Kazakhstan entry are said in minutes and directions; `JakimImsakTest` held three of e-solat's
printed SWK08 Subuh and imsak cells and now holds the rule (the imsak from the printed Subuh comes at least a minute
after the dawn's count and before the end of eating), the gate holding the print. handoff.py's CLOCK regex over
`git diff 4a7e6e9f4..HEAD` of the public files then finds 80 added lines outside `MANIFEST.tsv` (this entry's own
among them) and 247 in it, none a printed cell: rule figures (Tajikistan's 12:45 floor, COSIM's conventional 13:00 and 16:00, which the engine
holds as starts, DUM RT's 12:00), the sun's own times computed by the engine (Abidjan's first-shadow Asr,
Ushuaia's region Fajr), wall-clock times of runs and captures (MANIFEST's server times), and the monitor tests' invented
times.

**Review round (15 November, ruling R278).** Two reviews (no early start, no late end; the honesty of what is said)
found no blocker; what they found is done, but two points:
- *The card speaks of one day.* Kuala Lumpur's 2026 table is e-solat's own and its 2025 and 2027 the mirror's, so the
  card's "partly in waktusolat.app's copy" was true of the place's runs and not of the day shown (every 2027 day,
  Ramadan 1448 among them, is compared with the mirror alone). `AuthorityUnit.republishedYears` (JAKIM's
  `mirroredYears`: 2025 at the 13 zones, 2027 at nine) and `Resolution.wholeCopyOn`/`partlyCopyOn`: on a mirrored
  year's day the card says "checked against waktusolat.app's copy … not JAKIM's own pages", on a 2026 day the plain
  sentence; Dhaka, whose copy and own pages share years, keeps "partly" every day. About's "checked through" is a
  run's end and the site's page a run of months, so both keep "partly". `RepublisherCopyTest` reads the years off the
  gate files' names and holds that no own table of a zone is in a mirrored year.
- *The label changing is said.* Since R275 a day past the runs gets the unchecked About, which had no date: Casablanca
  on 1 December would turn "Published method" with no word why. Now that About, for a checked authority shown so
  (`checkedClass`), adds "Checked against Habous's published timetable through 30 November 2026. The days after it are
  not compared yet, so Taqwa shows them as the published method." (`about_not_compared_after`, seven languages,
  values-in its twin), the end of the latest run before the day (`checkedThrough`, R277's runs), never a later date.
- *Release cut.* `checkStamps` now prints, as a notice, each A/B entry with units whose run holding today ends within
  45 days or that no run holds today (`CheckStamps.labelEnds`, held by a test on invented stamps), so the cut sees which
  tables to read first; `docs/MONITOR.md` says the installed label follows the shipped stamps by date.
- *App = site, held.* The claim is the same runs, day by day: the site judges a page's whole month and counts a lone
  sampled day, the app judges each day and passes over a lone day (R277). `CheckedDaysParityTest` compares
  `CheckedDays.covers` with `Proven`'s `unitChecked`/`checked` at every end of every run, at every unit of every
  stamp: the app's checked day is exactly the site's checked day with a checked day beside it. `GenerateProofStamps`
  now writes a unit with no runs as an empty list instead of leaving it out (left out, the app would have read the
  entry's runs where the site holds the page; no stamp has such a unit today, so `ProofStamps.kt` is unchanged).
- English `authority_pa_iftaa` is "Palestinian Dar al-Iftaa", as the other six languages already were (G8 in
  English could be read as Egypt's Dar al-Ifta); the checks page's "partly" note says "its own pages and, for some
  tables, {copy}'s copy of them" in every language (it had said "not its own pages"); the Council's one printed Peshin
  minute is said as a minute in `tj-default.tsv`, `Generic.kt` and this log (R69).
- Not done: (1) a lighter table than `ProofStamps` for `CheckedDays` (the review's performance point): the iOS widget

  13 Arab towns, About's "too little to show it as checked" is R209's wording as the lane was told to use; the true
  reason is that who follows the Palestinian table there is not surveyed (an owner question). (3) A town inside a
  Habous or Oman reach is named by its own name ("Habous publishes the prayer times used in <town>") as Egypt's F34.

## A GPS fix takes its country from the device zone, not from the nearest city across a border (14 November) — rulings R256–R258, branch `engine/gps-country`

Branch `engine/gps-country`, off `engine/ramadan-final` (131317c2c); archive branch `gps-country`, unchanged: every
table read here was already held, and nothing was fetched from the web. Not pushed. The second trust audit's G4 and
G5 (both blockers).

**Superseded in part (15 November): see R259 below.** The lane's two reviews found that step 2 of R256, which takes
the zone's country *instead of* a nearer city, starts prayers early wherever a phone carries the neighbour's zone in
its own country (Johor Bahru under Singapore's zone: Fajr before JAKIM's on every day). R259 keeps the nearest city
and holds such a place to both countries. The R256 text below is kept as the record of what was built first; its
header-name sentence, its "worse than before in one case only" and its owner question are corrected under R259.

**What was wrong.** A GPS fix carries no country, and the engine picks the timetable by the country alone
(`Registry.automaticEntry`), Algeria's and Iran's units by the region too. `LocationRepository.resolveGpsLocation`,
`LocationRefresher.refresh` and the Prayer screen's old-install backfill all took both from the nearest bundled city
(`CityRepository.nearest`), so a border place whose nearest city stands across the border was handed the neighbour's
entry: 22 of the Kyrgyz Muftiate's 116 localities followed Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan or Tajikistan (at Cholpon-Ata,
nearest Almaty at 68.5 km, Balykchy 75.3; eating ending up to 29–30 min after the Muftiate's Fajr, Maghrib and Isha
early, the audit's figures), Karkamış and Elbeyli went to Syria (Maghrib 6 min before Diyanet's district tables),
Madha and Dibba Al-Baya to the UAE, Temburong to Sarawak (eating ending 9 min after MORA's Subuh), Tel al-Sultan to
Egypt, Farkhana to Spain. The gate never saw it: each row carries its entry's own country.

**The rule (R256), `prayer/FixCountry.kt`.** The device zone is the one fact about the place a phone gives besides
the fix: iOS and Android with location time zone detection set it from the position against zone boundaries, which
follow borders, and IANA's zones are per country.
1. The nearest bundled city, as before, when the zone does not say otherwise: a zone the list does not name (UTC, an
   old alias), or a nearest city whose country is one of the countries whose cities the list puts in that zone. The
   list's zones shared by countries are seven (Europe/Belgrade Serbia and Kosovo, Asia/Jerusalem Israel and
   Palestine, Asia/Bangkok Thailand and Vietnam, and four with a stray city), so a shared zone never moves anyone
   across it. Where the zone's countries all follow one entry at the fix, a country following it too counts as the
   zone's (Western Sahara's cities are in Africa/El_Aaiun, Morocco's in Africa/Casablanca, both Habous); where they
   follow several (Europe/Belgrade), only the zone's own countries do, so a Kosovo town nearer a Macedonian city
   still finds Kosovo.
2. Otherwise the nearest city of the zone's countries, with its own region, within 200 km or three times the nearest
   city's distance where that is further (the Rub' al Khali's Saudi reach points are 650 km from a Saudi city and
   300 from an Omani one); or at any distance when the fix stands inside the reach of a unit of the entry the zone's
   countries follow there. That last clause is Habous's Lagouira and Bir Gandouz: Lagouira is 12 km from Nouadhibou
   and 330 from Dakhla, and a probe of `mr.ministry` against Habous's held Lagouira and Bir Gandouz tables (a scratch
   gate group, not committed) found Mauritania's entry starting Dhuhr up to 5 min and Maghrib a minute before them on
   most held days.
3. The nearest city when the zone's countries have no city that near and no unit there: a zone set by hand, or not
   yet moved after a journey, is not taken as the place.

The search is exact and cheap: the cities sorted by latitude once (`FixCountry.Index`, built on the first fix and
kept), a scan outward that stops when the latitude alone puts every city left further than the best found; it
finds the city a scan of the whole list finds, the first in the list's order on a tie (`FixCountryTest` holds it
against a full scan at 500 random points). The city's name shown in the header is the chosen city's: a Madha user
now reads Shināş (61 km, Oman) where they read Khawr Fakkān (5.8 km, UAE).

**Every path (R257).** Onboarding's "Use my location" (`App.kt` `useGpsFix` → `resolveGpsLocation`, which now takes
the zone through an injectable `currentZoneId`), the refresher after a move or a zone change, and the old-install
backfill (`PrayerViewModel.migrateCityId`, for a stored location with no city id, under the stored zone) all resolve
through `CityRepository.forFix`. A fix stored before R256 is not left waiting for a 5 km move: on a refresh that
finds no move, a stored GPS location whose country is not its zone's (`ZoneCountries`) is resolved again where it
stands, under the same zone, and saved when that gives another city; the point, the zone and the source are kept.
Where the stored country is the zone's own, which is everywhere but at a border or under a shared zone, this costs
nothing. A city picked by hand is never touched (the refresher returns early under `LocationSource.MANUAL`, and a
pick is the city's own `toGeoLocation`). The site has no GPS path: every city page carries its city's own country.

**The tools check (R258), `GpsCountryTest` (tools jvmTest).** Every gate point resolved the GPS way, with the app's
own `FixCountry` over the app's whole city list and the row's zone: 31,182 points (the rows of `default.*` and
`other.*` are left out: they are checked against tables held across a region or the world, at places outside the
countries they are Automatic in, on purpose). 1,639 of them have an app city of another country nearest, so the
nearest-city rule alone would hand them that country; 13 still change country under R256, every one the PA Iftaa's
table of an Arab town inside Israel (Nazareth, Umm al-Fahm, Tiberias, Safed, Beisan, Haifa, Acre, Kafr Qasim,
Tayibe, Beersheba, Jaffa, Lydd, Ramla), where Israel is the right country and Israel's entry is gated against the
same tables (`safe-default-levant.tsv`). They are listed with why in `official/gps-country/elsewhere.tsv`. A point
not listed that changes country fails the test, and so does a listed one that no longer does; the failure prints
the lines to add or remove. Of the audit's own 1,450 foreign-nearest points (1,432 still gate points), those same 13
still change; the rest the audit counted now keep their entry (the other five its list would show follow the same
entry either way: Boujdour and Dakhla, Western Sahara and Morocco; two Preševo-valley points, Serbia's region rule;
Lille, which `tr.diyanet.europe` covers).

**Red first.** With `FixCountry.choice` stubbed back to the nearest city: `GpsBorderTownsTest` 2 of 4 red (the 116
Kyrgyz points under Asia/Bishkek; the border towns), `LocationRefresherTest` 2 of 19 red (a stored fix with the
neighbour's country, a move under the zone), and `GpsCountryTest` red with 1,639 points changing country. The
control tests (the neighbours across the same borders keep their own country; a city picked by hand keeps its own)
stayed green, as they should.

**The tests.** `FixCountryTest` (commonTest, 10): each step of the rule on invented towns, the Western Sahara and
Lagouira cases on the real three cities, the index against a full scan. `GpsBorderTownsTest` (Android host, 4, over
the real `cities.csv`, through `resolveGpsLocation` and the engine's `automaticEntryId`): every one of the 116
`kg.default` locality points (the 115 and Aravan town) under Asia/Bishkek gives KG and `kg.default`; Karkamış,
Elbeyli, Posof, Aralık (TR), Madha, Dibba Al-Baya (OM), Bangar and Batang Duri (BN), Tel al-Sultan
(`ps.gaza.cautious`), Farkhana (MA), Benapole (BD), Motaain (ID), Hili (AE), Taba (EG), Sokh (UZ), Cholpon-Ata and
the Talas valley (Manas, Aytmatov, Amanbaev, Kyzyl-Adyr, Pokrovka, Sheker, Taldy-Bulak, Talas, Bakay-Ata) each with
its own zone resolve to their own country and entry; Jarābulus, Khawr Fakkān, Nahwa, Limbang, Rafah (Egypt),
Melilla, Ceuta, Almaty, Taraz, Al Buraymī and Prizren keep theirs; Almaty picked by hand stays KZ.
`LocationRefresherTest` (+3).

**What moved, and by how much.** No engine source changed (`FixCountry` is outside `prayer/engine`, so no stamp's
`engineHash` moves), and no gate row's times moved: the gate checks each row under its own entry, which is what a
GPS user at that point now follows. What moved is which entry a GPS user at a border point follows. Measured on the
771 gate points of own-table rows that move (1,816 rows, 438,499 place-days, read under the entry the nearest-city
rule gave them, a scratch gate group not committed; 101 more rows whose old entry was cautious could not be read
that way): before R256 Maghrib was early on 260,306 of those place-days, Isha on 265,878, Asr on 49,402 (standard)
and 152,547 (Hanafi), Fajr on 52,560, Dhuhr on 32,426, and the end of eating late on 251,257, sunrise on 9,881; most
of it Uzbekistan's, Kazakhstan's and the UAE's entries on Kyrgyz and Omani ground. Under R256 every one follows its
own entry, which the gate holds: none early, within its limits.

**What the zone cannot settle, said plainly.** (i) A phone whose zone follows the network it is registered on
(Android without location time zone detection) takes the neighbour's zone where it roams onto the neighbour's
network; where that agrees with the nearest city the neighbour's entry is kept, exactly as before. That is the
exposure the 1,639 count measures. Only a bundled border lookup settles it; none is bundled (owner question 1).
(ii) The reverse: a phone across the border carrying this side's zone is given this side's entry (Strasbourg on a
German network). (iii) Within a country the region is still the nearest city's: an Algerian wilaya or an Iranian
province across a provincial line, not measured here (no boundaries are held). (iv) An old phone reporting a renamed
zone (Europe/Kiev) is a zone the list does not name, so the nearest city decides. (v) The fallback to the nearest
city (step 3) is shown never early only where it was probed: at Lagouira and Bir Gandouz it was early, which is why
the unit clause exists; no other held table stands where step 3 is taken among the gate's points.

**For the merger.**
- New files: `shared/.../prayer/FixCountry.kt`, `FixCountryTest.kt`, `androidHostTest/.../location/GpsBorderTownsTest.kt`,
  `tools/.../gate/GpsCountryTest.kt`, `tools/timetables/official/gps-country/elsewhere.tsv`.
- Touched: `city/CityRepository.kt` (`forFix`, its index), `location/LocationRepository.kt` (constructor's
  `currentZoneId`), `location/LocationRefresher.kt` (`forFix`, `recheckCountry`), `feature/prayer/PrayerViewModel.kt`
  (the backfill line), `LocationRefresherTest.kt`, and three lines of `tools/timetables/build.gradle.kts` (the test
  input `gpsCountry`, next to the survey input; the monitor-fixes lane may touch the heap lines of the same file).
- `GpsCountryTest` reads every gate file. A lane that adds gate rows at a place across a border (an edge or ride row
  past a reach, G1–G3) will see it fail with the exact lines to list; list a point that truly lies in the other
  country, with why, and fix `FixCountry` for one that does not. If the labels lane moves the PA Iftaa's rows of
  Israeli towns (G8), the 13 lines move with them.
- No stamp, `ProofStamps.kt`, golden vector or `own-points-worst.tsv` changes; nothing under `site/` or the monitor.
- Rulings R256–R258 are used; R259 is free.

**Owner questions.**
1. A bundled border lookup. The zone settles a border place for iOS and for Android with location time zone
   detection; a phone whose zone follows a roaming network (Madha and Dibba on a UAE network, Temburong on a
   Malaysian one, Tel al-Sultan on an Egyptian one) still gets the neighbour's entry, as before this fix.
   Recommended: before Ramadan, a small bundled country lookup for the held countries' land borders only (a
   simplified line within a kilometre or two, from an open data set, a few hundred KB), consulted only where the
   zone and the nearest city disagree or a foreign city is within ~30 km. It needs a download, which this lane was
   not allowed. Meanwhile R256 as built. It is worse than before in one case only, (ii) above: a phone across
   the border roaming on this side's network.

**Checks (14–15 November, on 60b506af3 with the archive branch `gps-country`).** The whole gate (stamps written):
"100865 rows checked (13730375 place-days, …) and 5756314 more place-days held to the promise alone", none early, no
end late, no unit over its limit, BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 41m 50s; every stamp written byte for byte as committed.
`checkEnvelopeRows`: "27 files, 39715 rows — every committed file is what a run would write." `generateProofStamps`:
"Wrote 81 proof stamps", `ProofStamps.kt` unchanged. `checkStamps`: "81 entries — every stamp fresh and green,
ProofStamps.kt matches the committed stamps. 19 of them not yet proven for Ramadan 1448" (the line's notice,
unchanged). `generateGoldenVector` and `generateOwnPointWorst` were not run: no engine source or unit changed. The
tools' tests with the archive: 485 tests, none failed or skipped (BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 2h 12m 50s under the other

open-findings.tsv and every excused group in excused.tsv, each within its ceilings." `:shared:testAndroidHostTest`:

## Where the device zone and the nearest city disagree, a GPS fix is held to both countries (15 November) — ruling R259, branch `engine/gps-country`

The fix round of the GPS country lane, after its two reviews (early times; honesty). Archive branch `gps-country`
unchanged, nothing fetched from the web, not pushed.

**What the reviews found in R256.** Step 2 took the zone's country *instead of* the nearest city whenever the two
disagreed, up to 200 km out, even where the fix stands in a bundled city of its own country. Android without location
time zone detection takes the zone from the network it is registered on, and near a border phones are often on the
neighbour's; a zone can also be set by hand (a +05 zone picked on a Kazakh phone that never had the March 2024
update). The early review ran the neighbour's entry against each local table as a scratch gate group: Johor Bahru
under Asia/Singapore took `sg.muis` (Fajr before JAKIM's table on every day, 9 min or more), Limbang under
Asia/Brunei `bn.mora` (the same), Gaziantep under Asia/Damascus `sy.awqaf` (Maghrib before Diyanet's on every day,
6 min or more), Shymkent under Asia/Tashkent `uz.board` and Shymkent and Almaty under Asia/Bishkek `kg.default`
(Fajr early on every day held), Manama, Doha and Kuwait City under Asia/Riyadh Umm al-Qura, Al Ain under Asia/Muscat
(sunrise after Awqaf's). R256's own text said it was worse than before "in one case only"; that was wrong, and so
was its claim that the header named a near city (it named the zone's city, Shināş 61 km away for Madha).

**The rule (R259).** Neither the zone nor the nearest city settles the country alone, so where they disagree the place
is held to both:
1. The fix always takes the nearest bundled city: its name in the header, its country and its region.
2. Where the device zone's countries do not include that city's (a country counts in a zone with three of its cities
   there, or as the zone's main one, so Georgia's one city in Europe/Moscow no longer makes Moscow's zone Georgian),
   and one of their cities stands within 200 km (or three times the nearest city's distance, or the fix is inside
   one of that entry's units, as R256), that country is carried as well (`GeoLocation.alsoCountryCode` and
   `alsoRegion`, stored with the location, cleared by a pick or by a fix whose zone agrees). Its region is dropped
   where the units go by the point (Brunei's districts, Algeria's wilayas), so Bangar and Batang Duri reach
   `bn.mora`'s Temburong district rather than Brunei-Muara's.
3. `Registry.resolve` then gives a border resolution (`Registry.border`): each country's Automatic entry resolved as
   it would be alone, every unit, ride and floor of its own included, and the day combined start by start as a paused
   timetable is held to Automatic (`BorderDay`, R52's `PausedTimetable.combine`): each start the later, sunrise, the
   end of eating, imsak and every end the earlier. So it is never before the timetable of the country the place is
   in, whichever fact was wrong, and never ends after it. Class C, "Cautious times", with its own sentences ("This
   place may be on either side of a border…", and on About these times how to choose one side's timetable), no
   figure claimed. The Asr school is the later where the sides' differ (Hanafi), and the other school's Asr is the
   later of the two too.
4. Either country's entry is in scope there (`Registry.inScope`, `placeFor`): a user who knows the side chooses it,
   it is held to the border day until confirmed (R52, R70), and then it is that entry alone.

The old-install backfill takes the nearest city again (it also ran for manual picks; the refresher's re-check adds the
second country for a GPS fix on the next foreground). A link zone's target (Asia/Riyadh for Asia/Kuwait) is
deliberately not merged with its link's country: that would make Asia/Riyadh Kuwait's too, and a Saudi town nearest a
Kuwaiti city under Asia/Riyadh would lose Saudi Arabia (the G4 harm again); held to both, a Kuwaiti phone reporting
Asia/Riyadh is later, never early.

**The tests.** `BorderDayTest` (commonTest, 4): at Cholpon-Ata (KZ + KG), Johor Bahru (MY + SG) and Gaziantep (TR +
SY), on a date every 9 days of 2026, no start before either side's day and no end after it, in both Asr schools;
class C; either side chosen and confirmed is that side alone, paused it is the border day. `GpsBorderTownsTest`
(Android host, 6): the 116 `kg.default` points under Asia/Bishkek all follow `kg.default` (94 alone, 22 held to it
and their nearest city's country); the audit's border towns follow their own country's entry; Temburong reaches its
own district; the reviews' metros (Johor Bahru, Limbang, Gaziantep, Shymkent twice, Almaty, Doha, Al Ain) under the
neighbour's zone keep their own country with its entry as one side; the neighbours across the borders and a manual
pick are unchanged. `FixCountryTest` (12), `LocationRefresherTest` (19).

**The tools check, `GpsCountryTest`, three passes.** (1) Under the row's zone: 31,182 gate points, 1,639 with a
foreign app city nearest, 13 lose their country (the PA Iftaa's Arab towns inside Israel, listed in `elsewhere.tsv`
as before). (2) Under every zone of another country with an app city within 200 km: 22,578 point-and-zone pairs;
every point whose nearest app city is its own country's keeps it (R256 failed this); 3,702 pairs lose their own
country, where the nearest app city and the zone are both the neighbour's. Most are reach and envelope ring points,
which really do stand across the border (KG<-UZ 865, KG<-TJ 667, KG<-KZ 539 are the Muftiate's rings); the rest are
the case only a border lookup settles (OM<-AE 287 around Madha and Musandam, EG<-SA 218 on the Red Sea, KZ<-UZ 244,
KZ<-RU 195, BD<-IN 148). (3) Wherever a point is held to two countries under its own zone (1,626 points, own-entry
rows only), the border day never starts before the row's own entry's day or ends after it, on 27 dates of 2026, and
the cost is printed: the most later than the own entry alone was Fajr 51 min (a Habous ring point by Ceuta or Melilla,
beside Spain's calculated default), Isha 48 (an ESA reach point beside Umm al-Qura), end of eating 48 earlier (a
Swedish envelope point beside Finland's default), Maghrib and sunrise 20, Dhuhr 15, Asr 12 (the Muftiate's ring
beside Tajikistan's entry). Those are the price of not knowing the side, paid only where the zone and the nearest city
disagree.

**What is left, said plainly.** (i) Where the zone agrees with the nearest city but the place is across the border
from both (Madha or Karkamış on the neighbour's network), the neighbour's entry alone is kept, as before R256: pass
(2)'s 3,702 pairs, the ring points among them. (ii) A zone two countries share (Europe/Belgrade, Asia/Jerusalem)
never adds the other. (iii) Within a country the region is the nearest city's (an Algerian wilaya, an Iranian
province). (iv) A renamed zone the list does not name (Europe/Kiev) adds nothing. Only a bundled border lookup
settles (i) and (ii).

**Owner question.** A bundled land-border lookup for the held countries, before Ramadan (a simplified open data set,
a few hundred KB, consulted only where a foreign city is within ~30 km or the zone and the nearest city disagree),
would remove both the cost of R259 at true border places (Cholpon-Ata's Fajr later than the Muftiate's) and the
residual (i)–(ii). Recommended; it needs a download this lane was not allowed. Until then R259 is the never-early
version.

## The real sun floors Asr and caps the sunrise and Dhuhr's end (14 November) — ruling R265, branch `engine/sun-floors-2`

Branch `engine/sun-floors-2`, off `engine/ramadan-final` (131317c2c); archive branch `sun-floors-2`, nothing added to
it (no capture was needed, nothing fetched). Not pushed. The second trust audit's G32, G33 and G34
(`.superpowers/sdd/2026-11-12-overnight/audit2-findings.md`), built as the extension of the owner's 12 November "sun-check
floors: yes" that the lane's task relayed. The owner ruled on Dhuhr and Maghrib (R180), not on Asr or on the ends: R265
is this lane's, the never-early version, and is put to the owner below with its cost.

**R265: the real sun at the user's own point floors Asr and caps the ends it gives.** In `DayPipeline.onRealSun`,
beside R180's two floors:

- *Asr (G34).* Asr in the school the day shows, and the other school's (`asrOther`), is never before the first whole
  minute after the real shadow time at the point (`DayPipeline.realAsr`: the noon shadow read at the exact sun's
  transit, the moment on the exact sun, `AsrModel.NOON_SHADOW` on `SunModel.EXACT`, the sun's geometric centre as every
  authority reads Asr; no refraction, which would put the moment a few seconds later). A cautious day's earliest Asr is
  held with it, and "where timetables differ" names a member at the floor. No floor where the sun casts no shadow (the
  polar night, where the shadow formula still answers with a sun below the horizon), nor on a day a high-latitude or
  clock rule sets Asr, or a polar day: there the authority's rule stands in for the sun, as no Maghrib waits for a sunset
  that does not come (IRN's Makkah hold prints Tromsø's midnight-sun Hanafi Asr up to 59 min before the second shadow,
  with its own sunset to end it; floored, it pushed Asr past that end and the day into the repair). An earlier Asr the
  user confirms stops at the real shadow-1 floor too (`Engine`'s `asrFloor`; in either school, ruling R51).
- *The sunrise and Fajr's end (G32).* Never after the real sunrise at the point, rounded down from the unrounded moment
  (`realSunrise`); no cap where the sun does not rise. The sunrise stays a minute after the Fajr shown: where the sun
  rises within the Fajr shown's minute or before it (a Fajr the day declares it does not show, R82), the sunrise stands
  on the next minute and the Fajr never moves earlier through the repair.
- *Dhuhr's end (G33).* `DayComputer` reads it as an end: the Standard Asr at the ends' points (the user's own, the fixed
  point and the end points, never the start points), the earliest, less any minutes that put the authority's Asr earlier
  than the sky's (a minute that puts it later does not carry the end with it), rounded down; the polar walk the same way.
  `onRealSun` caps it at the real shadow-1 Asr on every day, and where the first shadow comes before the Dhuhr shown (a sun
  a degree above the horizon at noon, its shadow-1 inside the transit's minute) Dhuhr shows no end, as R26's Isha. The
  audit's cases: the Bandama point (c2280405) 15:42 against a first shadow at 15:26:01, Katiola and Korhogo, Sughd
  (c1220571) 12 min after; all now on or before the first shadow, in either school (`SafeDefaultsFloorsTest`). Nothing on
  any screen, widget or page reads Dhuhr's end today.

**What it costs.** The sun-sanity pass (run of 14 November, 47,446 points, 2026-11-14..2027-12-14, both schools,
37,577,232 place-days) counts every move against the day the tables and methods give before the floor. R265's own:

The cascade (another time the floor's raise carried with it through the repair, one it did not set): 6 place-days, all
za.jamiat. Palestine's Asr is up to 4 min after the print at the four printed towns in Israel a degree north of al-Aqsa
(Safed, Tiberias, Haifa, Acre: the table moves them by longitude alone), up to 2 in the West Bank and Gaza, and a minute
on about a third of al-Aqsa's own days (the audit's "about 3 min" was Jenin's 99 s and the jitter point's 153 s). Egypt's
is seconds before the shadow, a minute on 4,314 place-days. Lakemba's is the largest: LMA prints Asr from 12 min before
to 22 min after the Shafi'i Asr on a seasonal curve (`Americas.kt`), so where it prints it before the shadow Taqwa shows
it up to 8 min after LMA; the gate's LMA Asr figure (15, its limit) does not move, the rows' worst days being others.

**The limits re-measured.** No limit was raised to excuse an early time: R265 moves only starts later and ends earlier.
The gate's late limits on ends are honesty figures ("at most N min before the print"), and eighteen units pass them now,
each recorded at its measured worst with R265 as its reason: JAKIM's sunrise at KTN01, KTN02, MLK01, PHG03, SWK01, SWK08,
TRG03 and TRG04 3 min (new), PHG02, SWK05 and SWK06 4 (were 3), SBH02 5 (was 3), SWK03 5 (was 4), as
`JakimZones.Why.REAL_SUN` (replacing those zones' TOWNS sunrise limits, whose reason it carries); Oman's sunrise at Muscat
and Al Hamra 3; Algeria's at Tamanrasset (seat 11) and Relizane (seat 48) 4; the Palestinian table's Asr at Acre, Haifa,
Safed and Tiberias 4. Boumerdès's seat 35 (Arbatache, the audit's case) reads sunrise 2 before the print now (was 1),
inside class D's 3: no limit needed. About's "at most N minutes" figures move with the stamps: by unit, ps.iftaa's Asr 2→3
at 7 towns and 2→4 at the four, tn.inm's 1→2 at 6, za.jamiat's Asr (both schools) and sunrise 1→2 at 8, ca.mac's Asr 2→3,
bh.council's, ps.gaza.awqaf's and za.voc's Asr 1→2, no.irn's Hanafi Asr 2→3 at one; sunrise (an end, "before"): om.mara

**Sun sanity.** Three checks join the pass: `asr-before-shadow`, `sunrise-after-real-sunrise` and
`dhuhr-end-after-shadow` (`SunSanity.FLOORED_UNLESS_EXCUSED`): unexcused, any is a broken engine and fails the pass; on
a day the day itself excuses (a rule sets its Asr, a polar day, a Fajr declared not shown) it is an excused group with
ceilings. Seven are listed in `excused.tsv`: IRN's Tromsø Asr (rule, up to 59.4 min; polar, 33.8) and the far north's
sunrise a minute after a declared Fajr (Norway's cautious up to 2.5 min at Harstad, Sweden's 63 s at Boden, IRN at Mo i
Rana, Diyanet's Luleå and Oulu). The pass's first run found two engine faults, both fixed before the run that is listed:
caps rounded from a millisecond-rounded instant stood up to half a second after the sun (they are rounded from the
unrounded moment now), and Dhuhr's end was left after the first shadow on days a rule set Asr or the shadow came before
the Dhuhr shown.

**Tests.** `RealSunFloorTest`: Asr raised in each school and only Asr; a rule's or a polar day's Asr not floored; no
real Asr in the polar night; the sunrise capped to the minute the sun rose in, Fajr's end with it, and a minute after a
declared Fajr; Dhuhr's end capped and dropped where the first shadow precedes Dhuhr; the property walks (every entry's
units, each school on alternate days since the second round, and the equator-to-pole places in both schools) hold
all of it. `SafeDefaultsFloorsTest`: Dhuhr's end and Asr
at Abidjan, Katiola, Korhogo, the Bandama point, Khujand and the Sughd point, 2027 and 2028. `SunSanityTest`: the three
checks, their excuses and their failing unexcused. The tests that compared a place with its table's own point
(`PointTableTest`, `KyrgyzMuftiateTest`, `LevantProofTest`) read the table's sunrise and Asr before the real sun at the
table's point floors them, since that is the sun at another point; `ArcticDawnWalkTest` ties its walk to the pipeline with
the floor in. `EndsTest`, `DayComputerTest` and `HighLatitudeTest` read Dhuhr's end rounded down.

**For the owner.**

1. *R265 itself.* The 12 Nov ruling floored Dhuhr and Maghrib; this lane carried it to Asr and the ends because the case
   is the same (a whole-minute print for one point, before the shadow or after the sunrise at another). Recommended: keep
   it. Meanwhile it is built and on. The cost is above: Asr later on 309,821 of the pass's 37.6 million place-days
   (0.8 %), nearly all by a minute where the print stands seconds before the shadow, up to 4 min in Palestine's towns in
   Israel and 8 with Lakemba chosen in Sydney; the sunrise earlier on 414,950 (1.1 %), up to 3 min at Maran.

   now matches MUIS's print on 7 % of days, from 66 %; South Africa's Automatic Asr on 45 %, from 82 %), so for class

   R265 and say it in About and on the site (one line: where a print is before the real sun at your point, by seconds,
   Taqwa waits for the sun's minute); until then the label overstates how exactly the print is followed.
2. *Lakemba.* LMA prints Asr up to 12 min before the first shadow on parts of the year. With R265 Taqwa shows LMA's Asr up

   already covers it.
3. *IRN's midnight-sun Asr.* Where IRN's Makkah-hold rule sets Tromsø's Asr, R265 stands aside (an excused group, up to
   59 min before the second shadow in June). Recommended: keep the authority's rule there, as for Maghrib.

**Not done.** Nothing in About or on the site says the sun now decides a minute here and there (R180's question 2 and 5
stand, widened to Asr and the sunrise). The gate cannot see a late sunrise any more where the print is on or after the
sun (the cap holds it), so its late-end tests moved to the end of eating, which no sun caps. Refraction is left out of
the shadow (a few seconds later at Asr altitudes; no authority's Asr counts it).

## The second audit's edges: past every reach, belt and ride the nearest locality's own day rides beside the edge, and Ceuta and Melilla wait for Habous's tables (14–15 November) — rulings R260–R262, branch `engine/edges`

Branch `engine/edges`, off `engine/ramadan-final` (131317c2c); archive branch `edges` (from `ramadan-final`, 69b32218),
one commit (the Habous script's Sebta and Melilla steps). Not pushed. Nothing was fetched: every table read was already
held. The second trust audit of 14 November (`audit2-findings.md`, G1, G2, G3 and G6; G26 is not about an edge and is
another lane's), each measured again here before anything changed, with a new read-only instrument, `edgeSweep`
(`units/EdgeSweep.kt`: each unit's own tables on 16 bearings at 0.5, 5, 10, 20, 40 and 60 km past its inner line and
just past the end of the new ride, wherever it is the nearest unit and the place is on the edge, read as shown and as
shown before the rule; the second nearest unit's table beside it; and the app's cities past every inner line).

**What was wrong.** The Kyrgyz Muftiate, ESA and the Omani ministry print by locality and draw no boundaries. Each
unit's line is this engine's: Kyrgyzstan's reach (a minute of longitude, about 21 km; R205 rode the other reaches only
inside them, and past them the edge was the user's own point a minute later, `beyondEveryUnit`, with no table read:
G1), Egypt's belt (twice a town's reach, R213: G2) and Oman's ride (half again the circle, R210: G3). Just past each
line the place came back to its own sun and the edge's allowances alone, against the nearest locality's printed table:

- Kyrgyzstan (2,475 points, 1,806,750 place-days of the 2026 and 2027 tables): Fajr before the table on 124,238 cells
  (worst 8 min), sunrise after it on 104,828 (4), Dhuhr before on 20,588 (2), Asr 67,466 (4), Maghrib 101,354 (4), Isha
  148,926 (6), the end of eating after it on 164,596 (6). The audit's points 26 km east and west of Kochkor, Maghrib a
  minute early and the end of eating a minute late on Ramadan 1448 days, among them. Every app city is inside a reach.
- Egypt (2,563 points, 622,087 place-days): Fajr 48,559 (6), sunrise 101,590 (5), Dhuhr 45,014 (5), Asr 47,082 (5),
  Maghrib 45,787 (5), Isha 49,916 (5), the end of eating 114,687 (6). Seven app cities stand past every belt (Kom Ombo,
  Mallawi, Dayrut, al-Qusiyah, Dayr Mawas, Zaafarana, an-Najaylah); an-Najaylah, 62.4 km from Marsa Matruh's point,
  ended the fast after its printed Fajr on every day of 2026 (ESA's own pages; by 2 min on 78), and began Maghrib before
  Sidi Barrani's (66.4 km) on 165. The R213 entry's owner question 5 said "a minute": corrected there.
- Oman (2,267 points, 1,030,398 place-days): Fajr 57,892 (5), sunrise 114,063 (3), Dhuhr 45,746 (2), Asr 50,211 (3),
  Maghrib 52,521 (4), Isha 53,457 (3), the end of eating 110,765 (4). No app city stands past a ride.

**The rule (R260).** The Lead's decision under the owner's standard: past a unit's line the edge keeps reading the
nearest locality's table beside its own day. Built once (`Units.ridingBeyond`) and applied where each authority's inner
rule rides nothing (`CentralAsia.kyrgyzstanUnits`' edge, `Egypt.beside`, `Gulf.omanUnits`' edge): the nearest unit's
own day at its own point rides beside the place's own day as a day alongside (`Alongside`: every start the later, sunrise
and every end the earlier), and with it every unit no more than a quarter farther than the nearest (`EDGE_NEAR_FACTOR`
1.25: a place about as near two printed localities may follow either, an-Najaylah's two towns), each out to five
minutes of longitude from its own point (`edgeRideKm`: `RIDE_REACHES`, the owner's own figure of 17 October for how far
a table printed for its own point still rides past its bound; about 103 km in Kyrgyzstan, 120 in Egypt, 127 in Oman).
Farther the place is the plain edge, as before. Why the same rule in all three: the evidence is the same in each (an
authority that prints by place, no boundary published, a place past the line nearest one printed place) and the
owner's ride is the one figure he has given for this question; the inner lines stay each authority's own (R205, R213,
R210 untouched). Five minutes of longitude is the owner's figure for a table printed for its own point riding past its
bound; carrying it to these three authorities' edges is the Lead's extension, pending his confirmation (owner question
3). No start gets earlier; only sunrise and the ends move, earlier; the edge keeps its class (D), its label ("Published
method") and its lack of a figure; no reach row changes (inside every reach nothing moves), so `generateReachRows` was not run again.

**After.** On the same points (each the nearest unit's, on the edge and past every inner line), against the nearest
table: no start before it and no end after it, on any event, in all three. Points past the nearest unit's own line but
inside a farther unit's bigger belt or ride were not among them: R262 below. What it costs, each event's days moved against the engine before the rule (a start later, an end earlier):

| | Kyrgyzstan | Egypt | Oman |
|---|---|---|---|
| days moved: Fajr / sunrise / Dhuhr / Asr / Maghrib / Isha / end of eating | 18 / 15 / 10 / 13 / 13 / 17 / 18 % | 16 / 31 / 13 / 14 / 14 / 15 / 32 % | 10 / 18 / 9 / 9 / 9 / 9 / 19 % |
| median move, every event | 0 min | 0 min | 0 min |
| worst move: Fajr / sunrise / Dhuhr / Asr / Maghrib / Isha / end of eating | 10 / 5 / 4 / 5 / 5 / 7 / 8 | 6 / 5 / 5 / 5 / 5 / 6 / 6 | 5 / 4 / 3 / 4 / 4 / 5 / 5 |

The worst moves stand 40 to 60 km past a line, against a table 60 to 80 km off whose latitude moves Fajr and Isha by
minutes; half a kilometre past a line the worst is 2 min, but for Oman's end of eating (3 on 42 cells) and
Kyrgyzstan's Fajr (3 or more on 718 of 657,000 cells, up to 5). The app's cities affected are
Egypt's seven alone, every day of 2027 against the engine before (median, worst): an-Najaylah sunrise and the end of
eating 2 and 2 min earlier on every day, Fajr 1 and 2 later (208 days), Dhuhr 1 and 1 (332), Asr 1 and 2 (289),
Maghrib 1 and 2 (287), Isha 1 and 3 (359), in Ramadan 1448 at most 2; Zaafarana sunrise and the end of eating a minute
earlier on 244 and 229 days; Dayrut and Dayr Mawas sunrise up to 2 min earlier on 177 and 162 days, the end of eating
a minute earlier on 200 and 134, Isha a minute later on 22 and 15; al-Qusiyah sunrise and the end of eating a minute
earlier on 168 and 117; Mallawi the end of eating a minute earlier on 3; Kom Ombo nothing.

**What it does not close.** (1) *Past the ride* (just past five minutes of longitude: 70 points in Kyrgyzstan's high
mountains, 159 in Egypt's deserts, 80 in the Rub' al Khali and Oman's far desert) the plain edge is still before the
nearest table on many days (Fajr up to 10, 7 and 6 min), as everywhere a table more than a hundred kilometres off is
read against a place; nobody's practice there is known. (2) *The second nearest locality where it is more than a
quarter farther than the nearest* does not ride, so the place can still be before it: just past the line, Kyrgyzstan
631 points (Maghrib before that table on 73,268 cells, worst 3; Isha 82,132, 5; the end of eating after it on 85,370,
5), Egypt 344 (Maghrib 10,604, 4; the end of eating 21,779, 6), Oman 428 (Maghrib 26,043, 3; the end of eating 41,758,
5). That is the same reading inside every reach (R205, R167, R165 ride a second table only where its own reach holds
the place); riding every table within three minutes of longitude instead would hold those too, at more lateness
(owner question 1). (3) Kazakhstan's QMDB edge uses the same `beyondEveryUnit` and was not measured here (the audit
did not run it; not this lane's finding).

**Past the nearest unit's own line, inside a farther one's (R262, 15 November, the lane's second review, finding 1).**
R260 rode the nearest unit only where the inner rule rode nothing (`.ifEmpty`), so a place just past the nearest
locality's belt or ride but inside a farther locality's bigger one got that farther table alone and was late against
the nearest: 3 km past Quriyat's 30 km ride, inside Muscat's 45 km ride, the end of eating a minute after Quriyat's
printed Fajr on 24 days of 2027 (two of Ramadan 1448) and sunrise on 40; half a kilometre past Tanta's belt, inside
Cairo's, the end of eating a minute after Tanta's on some days of 2026. The review's sweep (16 bearings, 0.5 to 15 km
past each line) found the nearest not riding at 14 of 2,074 Omani points (5 of them late) and 1 of 2,076 Egyptian; no
app city stands there. `Units.withNearestBeyond`: wherever `ridingBeyond`'s nearest unit is missing from the inner
rule's list, it and any unit about as near join that list (`Egypt.beside`, `Gulf.omanUnits`' edge); where the nearest
already rides, the list is kept as it is. A day alongside only makes a start later or an end earlier, so no start gets
earlier; class, label and figure unchanged. Kyrgyzstan cannot have the gap: every reach is the same minute of
longitude, so a place inside a farther reach is inside the nearest one too. `edgeSweep` and `edgeRings` no longer skip a
point inside another unit's inner line (the sweep reports those rings apart, and reads "before" as the inner rules
alone), so the gate now holds that ground: see the rows below. `GulfEgyptProofTest` holds the two cases against both
tables and the edge, and for every Omani locality, just past its ride wherever it is the nearest, that it rides.

**Red first, then the gate's rows.** `generateEnvelopeRows`' `edgeRings` (`EnvelopeRows.EDGE_LINES`): each unit's own
rows on the 8 bearings just past its inner line, midway to the end of the new ride and just inside it, wherever no
reach or inner line holds the place and the engine reads the unit's table there, and at the app's cities past every
inner line (an-Najaylah against both towns); asked of the engine's own resolution, so a ride changed in the engine
moves them (`EnvelopeCoverageTest`). `kg-default-envelope.tsv` 1,364 rows more (6,026), `eg-esa-envelope.tsv` 5,338
(19,649), `om-mara-envelope.tsv` 1,670 (5,740): none broken. With `ridingBeyond` made to ride nothing, the same three
files break on every event: Egypt 211,010 cells, Kyrgyzstan 346,622, Oman 252,496. With R262 (15 November) the rings
inside a farther unit's line are written too: `eg-esa-envelope.tsv` 12 rows more (Tanta's table just past its belt,
inside Cairo's), `om-mara-envelope.tsv` 18 (Al Hamra, Bidbid, Quriyat and Barka just past their rides, and Quriyat's at
the audit's As Sifah point), noted as R262's; 2,615 promise place-days more, none broken. `egyptBelt` keeps the belt's rows
only (a place past every belt is R260's). Tests hold the rule, never a figure: `KyrgyzMuftiateTest` (the audit's
Kochkor points and every locality's ground just past its reach and 30 km on, never before the locality's day nor the
edge's, every thirteenth day of 2027; past the ride nothing), `GulfEgyptProofTest` (an-Najaylah against both towns'
days on every day of 2026, the six other cities' nearest town, Siwa past its belt and past the ride, the 2.05-reach
rule; Oman's audit points against Adam's day, the rule for every locality, past every ride exactly what
`ridingBeyond` gives), `EnvelopeRowsTest`.

**Ceuta and Melilla (R261, G6, the Morocco entry's owner question 5).** The app places both in Spain, whose safe
default (`default.safe.europe`, its 18° dawn less 2 min) ended the fast 2 to 3 min after the Fajr Habous prints for
Sebta (ville 24) and Melilla (ville 40) on all 122 held days; no start was early. Habous prints a table for each, so the
never-early reading is that the cities' Muslims may pray by it. Sebta and Melilla are now read exactly as every Habous
place (`HabousCities.spain`, fitted by the archive's `habous_units.py spain-rows` and `spain-build`, which reproduce the
committed lines: Sebta at 35.9 N, -5.32, dip 0.7; Melilla at 35.32 N, -2.94, dip 0.4; October held out with 41 s or
more to spare at sunrise and Maghrib; the national margins hold their four prayers and the end of eating), and within
10 km of either point (`Maghreb.spainAt`, `SPAIN_HABOUS_KM`: each city and its ground, short of Tarifa and Gibraltar)
its own day rides beside Spain's: sunrise and the end of eating never after it, a start later only where Spain's would
come before Habous's (on the days held, none does). The cities keep Spain's entry, class D_NONE, label and measure;
they are not Moroccan units. Proof: `safe-default-europe-promise.tsv` (kept by hand: the four month files at the app's
two points and at Habous's), 244 promise place-days, none broken; without the ride, 122 late ends. Cost, every day of
2027 against Spain's day alone: the end of eating earlier on every day, by 4 min at the median and at most 7 at Ceuta,
6 at Melilla (summer, when 19° and 18° stand furthest apart; at most 4 in Ramadan 1448); Ceuta's sunrise a minute
earlier on 91 days; no start moves. A Moroccan town whose nearest bundled city is Melilla (Farkhana, the audit's G5)
gets Melilla's table beside Spain's day too, which is safer, not a fix of G5 (that is the gps-country lane's).
*What R261 does not close* (the lane's second review). (1) It is held for October and November 2026 alone, and
November is the month the points were fitted on: the monitor does not read villes 24 and 40 and the promise file is
kept by hand, so December onward, Ramadan 1448 included (the "at most 4" above is the fitted day's, not a print's),
rests on that autumn fit and no row checks it against Habous until a later month is added (MONITOR.md says how; the
monitor-fixes lane may make the fetcher read both villes). What is shown is never later than Spain's day alone. (2)
The labels have not followed it: at both cities the card still says no local timetable is known, and About still says
Taqwa found no official Sunni timetable and names Spain's 18° dawn as where eating ends, while the end shown is
Habous's 19° table's (up to 7 min earlier). That is the G8 pattern and the labels lane's (a per-place "calculated
beside" signal set where `Maghreb.spainAt` rides the Habous table, reusing `authority_habous` and the existing
`prayer_whose_calculated_beside_body` and `about_calculated_beside_body` strings); left open here, said in the R261
KDoc.

**The numbers.** The line before this lane: 100,865 gate rows, 13.7M place-days, 5.76M promise-only, none early.
With it (R260 to R262): 109,275 rows (8,402 envelope rows and 8 promise rows more), 13,730,375 place-days checked

**For the owner.**
1. **How many localities ride past a line (R260).** Built: the nearest and any no more than a quarter farther, out to
   five minutes of longitude. The stricter never-early reading would ride every locality within three minutes of
   longitude (R40's class D bound, the envelope's), closing (2) above at more lateness for places just past a line.

## The second audit's proof findings: every unit is proven across its reach, a fit row is never held out, the Ramadan check names cautious entries, and envelopes are checked at a release (14–15 November) — rulings R270–R274, branch `engine/proof-honesty`

Off the Ramadan line at 131317c2c; archive branch `proof-honesty` (no archive commit was needed). Not pushed. The
second trust audit of 14 November (on df74232dc) found the line's proof claiming more than it measured: G26, G27,
G28, G29, G30, G14 and G24 are this lane's. No start is early and no end late anywhere; one place's times move (Dubai
Rural, R271, by 30 s to the safe side). What moves is what the proof says, and it moves up: About's "at most" rises at
285 units of 29 entries, the release is refused until the owner rules on the figures over 4 minutes, and the Ramadan
guard names what it used to let through.

**R270 (G26). Every entry the gate checks whose measured units reach past their own points has reach rows, and each
unit's limit is its reach's measured worst** (`ReachRows.SPECS`, 29 new specs and 29 new `-reach.tsv` files; the new
task `generateReachLimits` writes `ReachLimits.kt`, which `lateLimitFor` reads beside a unit's recorded exceptions).
The audit named seven: Habous (187 places), JAKIM (60 zones), the Foundation (64 districts), Algeria (30 measured units;
a seat's points are read with its wilaya's region, since the app hands a place a seat's fitted day by region alone,
R219), DUM RT (19 towns), Tunisia (6) and Jamiat (9). The new rule in `ReachRows.outstanding` ("any gated entry whose
measured units have a radius over 0 and no spec") named 24 more gated entries (and Muhammadiyah, which has no gate row
and claims no figure). 22 of them are measured now: Brunei, Dubai, Qatar, Amman, the PA's towns, Libya, Bosnia, and the
tables printed for their own points whose reach is R40's (a class's minutes from longitude alone): Cape Town's MJC and
VOC, Moscow, Tirana, Dublin's ICCI and IFI, Paris, Brussels, Vienna, Zürich, Toronto's IFT, IIT and MAC, Sydney and
Auckland. Two are `PENDING` instead: Norway's IRN and Diyanet's European cities, whose reach
rows reach far-north points where the engine's own day comes out of order and is repaired (Tromsø's Isha not before the
next end of eating on 25 Jul 2026; Luleå, ten days of June 2027): an engine matter, not a limit. The sweep, which stops
on any early start or late end, passes for both (its lines are quoted under the review's checks below); their reach
files are not committed, and the release hold names them. Every new spec sweeps densely (the finer sweep at
every unit and 72 bearings by 11 shares besides): the coarse sweep missed a minute at Chefchaouen (Fajr) and Ouezzane
(sunrise) that `CityUnitsTest`'s offset grids found; with the dense sweep the offset grids find nothing beyond (none
early, none over its limit, no start past its unit's figure, at 29 entries). The sweep found no early cell and no late
end at any of them, but one (Dubai Rural, R271).

828 unit-events in 224 units are raised (Fajr 119, sunrise 145, Dhuhr 69, Asr 120, Maghrib 130, Isha 117, the end of
eating 103, imsak 25); none is lowered. Over 4 min, the ceiling of R255 ("a fifth minute needs a ruling"), 233 of them,

- DUM RT, all 19 towns: Fajr 120–139, Isha 62–66, the end of sahur 125–134 min. Every town's reach meets a white-night

**The two reviews (15 November), and what changed.** Neither found an early start or a late end. Applied:
- *No unruled figure reaches a page.* `ReachRows.unruled` names a unit's reach limits over 4 min that `RULED` does not
  accept, and `Proven.verdict` holds that city's page with the figures in its reason, as the release is held: the site's
  `--check` had passed Kazan's 135. Six pages are held on 15 November: Kazan (Fajr 135,
  Isha 64, end of eating 134), Rabat (sunrise 5), Kuala Lumpur (WLY01 Fajr 6), George Town (PNG01 sunrise, end of eating
  and imsak 5), Johor Bahru (JHR02 6) and Kota Bharu (KTN01 5); `generate` writes 67 cities (6 held) and 163 pages. A
  ruling in `RULED` brings each back with no other change. (The first commit of this fix named four of them.)
- *The manual adjustment's stronger question* starts at the unit's recorded exception (`ownLateLimitFor`), not its reach's
  figure: from the reach's, a Kazan user moving Fajr 60 min earlier would have met only the mild question. Whether it
  should follow About's figure is the owner's (question 3 below).
- *What keeps a reach limit honest, as R254 and R255 had it:* the 25 group files of the raised entries join
  `OwnPointWorst.GROUPS` (own-points-worst.tsv: 8,599 rows, 6,293 before), so a regression at a city's own point fails
  `CityUnitsTest` however wide its reach's limit, and those entries join `HELD_BY_PLACE`, so a row `prove` adds at an own
  point is held to its place's worst, not to the reach's figure. `checkStamps` now fails on every run while
  `ReachLimits.kt` is not what the committed stamps give, and `generateReachLimits` prints every figure it moves: on the
  merged line a raise is reported, never absorbed.
- *G14's test* fails on a Kazakh point two places share instead of passing it unread, and counts the city rows it leaves
  to the reading above. Smaller: Gulf.kt's dangling KDoc, AboutTimesScreen's `atMostMinutes` KDoc, the envelope note's
  dead branch, the `checkStamps` task comment ("none is owed"), MONITOR.md (Muhammadiyah, the red to expect from the new
  reach rows, the site hold), and this entry's claims on the pending reaches (now quoted) and on the stronger question.

Rejected, with the evidence:
- *Cut each over-ceiling reach to 4 min* (the single tables of R40 and Algeria's two bands). Beyond a table's reach
  `beyondTable` (Units.kt) shows the user's own point a minute later with the table's point bounding the ends alone; the
  table no longer bounds the starts there. A cut would therefore let starts east of the cut fall before the print of a
  table those places now follow, and would not make anything less late (the lateness is the user's own sun: at 50–60 km
  north of a 50° N table in summer it runs later than the table). It lowers a figure by measuring less. Demoting is the
  owner's (R185 demotes a whole entry). The figures stay measured, the release and the pages wait for his ruling.
- *Generate `ReachLimits` from the reach rows alone.* The stamp's unit worst is what the gate holds every row of the unit
  to and what About says; the drift the review feared at an own point is now caught by own-points-worst and
  `HELD_BY_PLACE` before `generateReachLimits` runs, and a stale file by `checkStamps`.
- *Name London LUPT and Singapore in `outstanding()`* (ground from a region rule or a whole country, not a unit radius).
  Outside G26's named rule ("measured units of radius > 0 and no spec"); their sweep is a polygon's, a lane of its own.
  Left open below.
- *Count the Muftiate's 2027 tables once* (G29's second half). The 2027 files are the Muftiate's own fetch for 2027's
  dates (their heads name muftiyat.kg's 2027 calendar), not a table Taqwa mapped onto a year, so `DERIVED` would
  mislabel them; counting a day-for-day repeat once is a rule for every entry. Left open below (it adds 115 to the
  checks page's tables figure).
- *Tests that read `lateLimitFor` pass by construction.* Tests hold rules, never live figures; the currency of
  `ReachLimits.kt` is now `checkStamps`' to hold. `outstanding()`'s default `unspecified` is ungated, but its one release
  caller, `CheckStamps.main`, passes the gated set.

## Far-north days in order (16–17 November) — rulings R292–R295, branch `engine/far-north`

Off the 1.7.0 engine line at 3f24de56d; no archive commit (nothing in the archive was needed). Not pushed. The release
was refused for two `PENDING` entries, Norway's IRN (Oslo, Trondheim, Tromsø) and Diyanet's 33 European cities: their
reach rows met far-north days the engine put out of order (the proof-honesty entry above: Tromsø's Isha not before the
next end of eating on 25 Jul 2026, ten days of June 2027 north of Luleå). The proof-honesty entry's recommendation (5),
"the far-north lane takes them before the cut", taken up here (the owner's answers of 16 November did not cover it). Both kinds of day are now in order at the source (R292, R293). Diyanet's
reach file is committed and gated, and its release refusal is now only its 174 reach figures over 4 min, which await the
owner's ruling. IRN stays `PENDING`, for a reason the engine cannot remove: at three points of Tromsø's reach on the
offset grid of `CityUnitsTest` (2026) the sun is down for a minute or three, too short for any day in order (For the
owner (1)).

**Reproduced.** `generateReachRows --only no.irn` and `--only tr.diyanet.europe` on 3f24de56d: "no.irn: 3 units, 48
points kept of 48 on the grid and 22 worst points of the sweep (7082 swept, 3 units finely), 70 rows, 0 cells early or
late in the sweep" and "tr.diyanet.europe: 33 units, 491 points kept of 528 on the grid and 223 worst points of the
sweep (72304 swept, 33 units finely), 3133 rows, 0 cells early or late in the sweep". The days the gate named, read
through `DayPipeline` at their points (a scratch probe on the compiled tools classes, not committed), were two causes,
not one:

- **Tromsø (IRN), 25 Jul 2026, 29 km west of the city.** The sun sets at 00:51:21 (26 Jul) and rises again at 00:56:54:
  a night of five and a half minutes. IRN's clock rule holds Maghrib at Makkah's sunset + 5 on that date (R82), hours
  before the real sunset, so the Maghrib shown was the day's own: the local sunset plus IRN's ordinary five minutes and
  the 42 s margin, 00:58, after the sun had risen again. Isha (00:59) came after the next day's end of eating (00:55, the
  minute before the real sunrise, since IRN's Makkah-time Fajr is after it and declared not followed), so Isha had no end
  (R26), which the gate counts as out of order. Read 2026–2035 at the 70 reach points: 8 such days, all in the week
  before or after the midnight sun.
- **North of Luleå (Diyanet), June 2027.** Diyanet's sun is read once a day at 0h UT (`SunModel.DAILY_0H_UT`, the model
  its tables follow); where the sun grazes the horizon its sunset comes well before the real one, or not at all (then a
  polar day borrows Maghrib from a lower latitude): at the gate's points Diyanet's Maghrib came 4 to 17 min before the
  real sunset (13 min on 23 Jun 2027 at 65.74° N). DayComputer's point 9 put Isha a
  minute after that Maghrib and declared it not followed; then R180's floor (`DayPipeline.onRealSun`, added after point 9)
  raised Maghrib to the minute after the real sunset and left Isha behind, and `Invariants.repair` put Isha after it,
  which the gate counts as out of order. Read 2026–2029 at the 714 reach points: 36 such days, all at Luleå's unit.

No limit, margin or table was wrong; both are the engine's own order at the edge of the midnight sun.

**R292. On a night the sun sets for minutes, Tromsø's Maghrib and Isha come before the next dawn**
(`DayComputer.clocked`). Under a clock rule, where the Maghrib shown is the sun's (after the rule's) and the Isha after
it would not come before the next day's end of eating, Maghrib is the minute after the sun has set at every start point
where it sets (never before the rule's, IRN's) and Isha the rule's where after it, else the minute after Maghrib. Only
where that fits: on a night shorter still nothing moves and Isha keeps no end (R26). The next day is read with `capIsha
= false`, which also stops the check (it needs only its end of eating). Only IRN's Tromsø unit has a clock rule. IRN's
own rule at those latitudes is Makkah time, which the sun forbids for Maghrib (R82, R180); the minute after the real
sunset is the earliest Maghrib that is neither before IRN's nor before the sun, and no safe side of later starts and
earlier ends can fit a night of five minutes: the next day's end of eating cannot move earlier than the dawn the night
gives, nor the Isha later than it. The cost is the other way: on those nights Maghrib and Isha are 5–6 min earlier than
the day's own rule made them, still after the real sunset and hours after IRN's printed times.

**R293. A declared Isha follows the Maghrib the real-sun floor raises past it** (`DayPipeline.onRealSun`). Where the
floor raises Maghrib to or past an Isha the day already declares not followed (point 9), Isha moves to the minute after
the raised Maghrib and Maghrib's end with it, as point 9 moves it. An undeclared Isha is still left for the repair, so a
wrong slot or margin still fails the gate (review D round 1). The repair gave the same Isha: no time moves.

**What moves for users.** (1) Tromsø's unit (IRN, Automatic within its reach): on the nights the sun first sets again
(mid-May, late July), at the points of the reach where the sun is down only minutes, Maghrib and Isha move 5–6 min
earlier and Isha gains its end. On a grid of 4,915 points across the unit (0.005° by 0.025°), 8–25 May and 18 Jul–2 Aug
of 2026–2031: 812 of the 1,002,660 place-days inside the unit move (Maghrib and Isha 5 min earlier on 221, 6 on 591;
the 7,521-point rectangle around it, 1,534,284 place-days, moves nowhere outside the unit), nothing else on any day; the unit's own point and Tromsø's city do not move. (2) Diyanet Europe: no time moves; on the June days north of
about 65.5° N where the floor raised Maghrib, Maghrib shows its end (the Isha after it) and the day is no longer
repaired: 239 of 3,303,946 place-days on a coarse grid of Norway, Sweden and Finland (Automatic and both entries, 1
May–15 Aug 2026 and 2027), the only changes on it; no Automatic day on that grid moved (Automatic inside Tromsø's reach
is IRN, item (1)). The golden vector did not move ("2071
place-days over 120 points", the file unchanged). (3) About and the site: Diyanet's stamp now holds its reach, so
About's "at most N" rises at every one of its units (starts' measured worst, before → after): Aalborg 5 → 9, Aarhus 4 →
9, Amsterdam 4 → 9, Antwerpen 4 → 8, Bergen 5 → 11, Berlin 4 → 8, Brussels 4 → 8, Copenhagen 4 → 9, Freiburg 3 → 8, Gent

**For the owner.** (1) **Nights too short for any day in order (IRN, Tromsø's reach).** Where the sun is down for less
than about four minutes, the week before and after the midnight sun, no day can have Maghrib after the real sunset
(R180), Isha after Maghrib, and the next day's end of eating after Isha and at or before a Fajr that is before the real
sunrise (R90, R265): Isha shows no end (R26) and the gate counts the day out of order. It is the sun, not a table or a
limit. And on every such night (246 place-days on the grid) the Maghrib and Isha shown are 3–6 min after the next day's
sunrise, and after its Fajr and end of eating: R292 leaves those nights at IRN's five minutes and the margin after the
real sunset, so the Maghrib alert comes in daylight. Options: (a) a declared cell: a day whose night cannot hold Isha
before the next end of eating declares Isha's end not shown, as `notFollowed` declares an authority time, and the gate
counts it declared, never broken; no time moves, so Maghrib and Isha stay after the next sunrise; (a′) the same
declaration, and Maghrib pulled to the minute after the real sunset (never before IRN's) wherever that is before the next
day's Fajr, as R292 pulls it: on the grid 119 of the 246 nights (the other 127 are too short even for that, and keep
today's times), each such Maghrib 5–6 min earlier (5 on 39, 6 on 80), still after the real sunset and hours after IRN's printed time;
(b) keep it out of order: IRN stays pending and the release refused, since no cut of the reach avoids it (the band of
such nights moves with the date and year across the whole unit); (c) let Maghrib follow IRN's Makkah time on such a
night: a Maghrib before the real sunset, against R180. Under (a) or (a′) the declaration is computed from the real sun
alone (the real sunset and the next real sunrise, never the day's own times), and the gate recomputes it rather than
trust a flag on the day, so a late Maghrib margin or an early end of eating cannot hide behind it; IRN's reach then
joins the gate with its 19 figures over 4 for (3). Recommendation: (a′), which says what is true (Isha has no window
that night) and puts Maghrib at night wherever the night holds it; (a) if no start should move earlier. (2) **R292 moves
two starts earlier on those nights.** On the nights the sun sets for minutes, at points of Tromsø's reach, Maghrib and
Isha are 5–6 min earlier than before (812 of the 1,002,660 place-days inside the unit in the windows on the grid),
still after the real sunset and hours after IRN's printed times; no safe side fits a five-minute night. Recommendation: keep it. (3) **The reach figures over 4 min.** Diyanet's 174 (and IRN's 19
once it joins) refuse a release until ruled (R270): most are 5 to 17 min across a 40–60 km reach at 50–70° N, the user's

row reads them, and the repair only moves a start later or an end earlier. Recommendation: a lane of its own after the
