## Reach polygons and repeated years (16 November) — rulings R297–R300, branch `engine/reach-polygons`

Off `engine/ramadan-final` at 3f24de56d: the proof-honesty entry's open item (6), "recommended before the cut". No
archive commit, nothing fetched, not pushed. No time moves anywhere: the golden vector is unchanged; what moves is what
the proof measures and says.

**The root cause.** (a) `ReachRows.SPECS` sweeps a measured unit's circle, and G26's hold (`unspecified`) names only
"measured units of radius over 0 and no spec". A figure claimed across an area has no circle: London Unified's unit
`gb.london.lupt` has radius 0 and `choose` picks it by the M25's polygon (R44), and MUIS and the Supreme Council have no
units at all, their one table computed at a fixed point for the whole country. Nothing swept them, and nothing named
them: London's figure was its own point's and the twelve edge rows a hand had placed, Singapore's its own point's alone,
Bahrain's the fixed point's and eight towns'. (b) The Muftiate's 2027 tables are muftiyat.kg's (the Kyrgyz Muftiate,
`kg.default`; the brief for this lane said Kazakhstan's QMDB, which repeats nothing): the 2027 calendars are the
Muftiate's own fetch for 2027's dates, printing 2026's times day for day, so no `DERIVED` head says so and
`AcrossEntries` counted each as a published table of its own (230 where 115 were printed); R272's `@fitted` line kept
them out of the held-out counts by hand, for that entry alone.

**R297. A figure claimed across an area is read across it, and a release waits while one is not.** `ReachAreas.AREAS`
(`units/ReachAreas.kt`) holds each claim: London's M25 (the app's own polygon), and Singapore's and Bahrain's own ground
(`ReachAreas.GROUND`, drawn coarsely, a few hundred metres offshore along a coast and up to a few km where it takes in
the water between islands, by their named extremes: Tuas, Sembawang, Tekong and
Raffles Lighthouse; Budaiya, Amwaj, Ras al-Barr, Durrat al-Bahrain, Umm an Nasan and the Hawar islands), wherever a GPS fix there is placed
in the country alone (`FixCountry` under the country's own zone: no other country held beside it). Each figure is read
across the country's ground as `ReachAreas.GROUND` draws it; the app's nearest-city cell beyond it (sea out to 35 km
from Singapore, 120 km from Bahrain), where the app says the same figure, is not read: which of the two it is read over
is the owner's decision (below, with what the cell reads). `generateReachRows`
(`--args="--only gb.london.lupt"`, `sg.muis`, `bh.council`; under a minute to two each) reads every grid point of the claim (0.4,
0.25 and 0.25 km), then a grid four times finer around each event's worst points, and writes the claim's four extremes and
each event's worst point to `gb-london-lupt-reach.tsv` (11 points, 33 rows), `sg-muis-reach.tsv` (10, 50) and
`bh-council-reach.tsv` (6, 6), each own table at each point, held out. The sweep found no early start and no late end. The
hold: `ReachAreas.areaClaims` names the gated entries that say a figure (class A or B, or a measured published method)
across ground no circle bounds, of the kinds it knows: a measured entry with no units, a measured unit of radius 0, a
measured set kept measured beyond every unit, and since R300 (below) a measured unit its set's `choose` hands to places
beyond its circle; `ReachRows.unswept` puts any of them without an `AREAS` line into `outstanding()`, so
`checkStamps -Prelease=true` refuses it. The first three kinds name exactly London Unified, MUIS and the Supreme Council
on the registry, all three read (as first committed, the hold knew only those three kinds, and this entry said it named
every claim; the review below found the fourth); a test holds the rule on entries made up for it, both ways. `recipes.tsv` grows London's and Singapore's area rows with every
capture, as their own rows grow; Bahrain's book is read by hand, and a new book's row goes on the area file by
`generateReachRows --only bh.council`. `CityUnitsTest` holds every area row to a claimed point reading every own table,
the recipe twins, every app city of Singapore and Bahrain on the drawn ground, and, with the archive, a grid offset from
the sweep's (twice its step, shifted 0.6 of it) to nothing early, nothing over its limit and no event past the stamp.

What the sweep measured (minutes after the table for a start, before it for an end; before → after):

| Claim | Points read | Moved | Unchanged |
|---|---|---|---|
| London Unified, the M25 | 14,353 + 8,407 finer | end of eating 4 → 5 (51.61 N 0.25 E: the eastern edge's earlier dawn and the northern edge's summer dawn together, which the recorded exception named one at a time) | Fajr 5, Isha 5, sunrise 3, Dhuhr 2, Asr 3 and 3, Maghrib 3 |
| MUIS, Singapore | 15,722 + 5,848 | Fajr 2 → 3, sunrise 2 → 3, Dhuhr 2 → 3, Asr 3 → 4, Maghrib 2 → 3, Isha 2 → 3 (the starts in the west and south-west, the user's own sun up to a minute later than the fixed point's: Fajr and Dhuhr at Tuas's west tip, 1.28 N 103.61 E, Isha beside it; Asr 4 at 1.21 N 103.67 E and Maghrib at 1.18 N 103.70 E, both over water a few km off Jurong Island and the southern islands inside the coarse ground; sunrise 3 just off the east coast, 1.29 N 103.94 E, where the user's own sunrise is earlier than the fixed point's) | end of eating 2, imsak 1 |
| The Supreme Council, Bahrain | 17,465 + 4,093 (16,854 + 4,158 before the review moved the ground's south-east edge) | sunrise 1 → 2, end of eating 1 → 2 (at 25.71 N 50.72 E, on the west edge of the box drawn round the Hawar islands: water between Hawar and the main island, inside the drawn ground) | Fajr 2, Asr 2 (at Ras al-Barr, 25.78 N 50.58 E), Dhuhr, Maghrib and Isha 1 |

**R298. An entry with no units keys its area's measured worst by its own id.** Singapore's limits had to rise past class
B's 2 and its Asr exception's 3, and `ReachLimits.kt` held units alone. `lateLimitFor` (`Authority.kt`) now reads an
entry with no units under its own id, the registry's entry only (a variant a tool or test builds under the same id
takes its own limits: `GateFixtureTest`'s made-up MUIS); `generateReachLimits` writes it from the stamp's own events
for the area claims and printed "sg.muis/sg.muis fajr 0 -> 3, sunrise 0 -> 3, dhuhr 0 -> 3, asr 0 -> 4, maghrib 0 -> 3,
isha 0 -> 3 (raised)" and "gb.london.lupt/gb.london.lupt end_of_eating 0 -> 5 (raised)"; `Proven.verdict` holds such an
entry's pages while a figure over 4 waits for a ruling, as it holds a unit's. London Unified's and MUIS's groups join
`OwnPointWorst.GROUPS` (8,599 → 8,618 own-point rows), so a regression at the own point fails `CityUnitsTest` however
wide the area's limit. Singapore's 3s and 4 are within R255's ceiling; London's end of eating 5 is not, and is the
owner's (below): it is not in `ReachRows.RULED`, so a release is refused for it and the site holds London's page.

**R299. A year printed again day for day is the same table, counted once, in one place.** `gate/Repeats.kt` says which
tables repeat another: the same entry at the same place (member, unit and point) with the same columns, at least 28
days, every day printed the same on the same month and day of one earlier year. A family is an original and every table
joined to it by a repeat (two captures of the first year are both in it). Every reader of the proof takes it from there:
`AcrossEntries` counts a publication made only of repeats as no published table (the stamp's `tables`, the checks
page's total); `Counted` makes every table of a family a fit cell for an event wherever any of them is, so a repeated
year is never held out, never a held-out Ramadan (the guard reads `Counted`), and neither are the stamp's held-out days
and cells; the repeat's days still count as the dates they are, each compared against what the authority prints for
it. On the archive it finds the Kyrgyz Muftiate's 115 (no head said so), and every perpetual table already marked
`DERIVED` or fitted by hand (Dubai's, the PA Iftaa's, Jamiat's, Dublin's IFI, Dar al-Fatwa's, Banuri Town's, Dhaka's
permanent table), and nothing else; `@fitted` lines for such years are no longer needed and stay.
What moved: `kg.default`'s `tables` 230 → 115, and the PA Iftaa's 2027 tables are no longer held out for Dhuhr and Asr
(their `@fitted` line named Fajr, sunrise, Maghrib, Isha and the end of eating; the year repeats al-Aqsa's perpetual
table, which every margin was fitted on). No Ramadan verdict moved: the same 18 entries are refused for 1448.

**R300. A unit its set hands out beyond its own circle claims its figure there too** (the review of R297, below). The
radius sweep (`ReachRows.SPECS`) reads a measured unit's circle; a set whose `choose` gives a measured unit of radius
over 0 to places farther than its `radiusKm` says that unit's "at most N" on ground no sweep reads.
`ReachAreas.chosenBeyond` finds such places; `CityUnitsTest` looks for them, for every set with a `choose` and a measured unit
with a radius, among the app's cities of the entry's countries (with their regions), JAKIM's named places and a 0.05°
grid over the entry's countries (their cities' box widened by half a degree, each point placed as its nearest city is,
kept where that is the entry's country; 34,134 cities, 9 named places, 311,521 grid points), and holds
`ReachAreas.CHOSEN_BEYOND` to exactly the entries it finds. It finds three: `sa.ummalqura` (Tayma's unit, at KACST's
28.63 N, chosen within a minute's reach of the town at 27.62 N, 111 km south: 67 places), `my.jakim` (a zone chosen
within 10 km of any town its list names, 5 km of a hill zone's named place: 1,244 places, 46 of its 56 zones) and
`bn.mora` (one grid point, 5.33 N 114.58 E, sea about 50 km north of Tutong and 63 km from Brunei-Muara's point, past
its 60 km: Tutong's circle holds it and its nearest app city, Sengkurong, is in Brunei-Muara, whose district the region
picks). Algeria's wilayas and QMDB's cities, the review's other candidates, pick a unit only within its own circle (a
core band within its radius, else the wilaya's rest, which claims no figure; a city's table within its reach), and the
search confirms it. The grid is coarse: a claim thinner than about 5.5 km between the sampled places would not be
found. `areaClaims` names the entries `CHOSEN_BEYOND` lists (the unit's figure is claimed whether or not the entry is
measured beyond its units: JAKIM's is not), and where `AREAS` reads one, every place found must be a point one of its
claims reads, for the unit chosen there. A fourth kind of claim, `ReachAreas.Chosen`, keeps the points a fix is placed
in the country alone (as for a country's ground, now with the nearest city's region) where `choose` hands the claim's
unit. `AREAS` reads Tayma's town (box 27.35–27.90 N, 38.22–38.86 E, 0.25 km; 30,492 + 6,344 points) into
`sa-ummalqura-tayma-reach.tsv` (8 points, 16 rows), grown by `recipes.tsv` with each Tayma capture; no start early, no
end late. It measured Fajr 6 (at the disc's south edge, 27.40 N 38.52 E, where the user's own dawn comes later than at
KACST's point a degree and a quarter north), Maghrib and Isha 5 (27.50 N 38.33 E, the west), sunrise 4, Asr 4, the end
of eating 3 and Dhuhr 2; `generateReachLimits` printed "sa.ummalqura/tayma fajr 0 -> 6", "sunrise 0 -> 4", "asr 0 -> 4",
"maghrib 0 -> 5" and "isha 0 -> 5 (raised)". Fajr 6, Maghrib 5 and Isha 5 are past the ceiling and not ruled, so a
release is refused for them (the owner's, below). Two claims are not read and stay named by the hold, so a release is
refused for each: JAKIM's towns (no sweep per zone is built) and Brunei-Muara's sea past its circle (the gate resolves a
row's point without a region, so a row there resolves to Belait or Tutong, not the district the app picks; the sweep
stopped on exactly that, "bn-mora.tsv:16: the point resolves to Belait, not Brunei-Muara"). A unit read this way gives
the area's reason for its reach limit, as the R297 claims do (`AREA_READ_UNITS` in `Authority.kt`, held to `AREAS` by a
test).

**What moves for users.** About in Singapore says "at most 4 min" after MUIS's timetable (3 before), and so does
taqwa.world's Singapore page (app = site). London's About is unchanged (its starts' worst is still Fajr and Isha 5; the
end of eating is no start), but London's page on taqwa.world is held until the owner rules on the end of eating's 5
(`Proven.verdict`, R270). Bahrain's published-method "up to 2 min" is unchanged (its starts), and Bahrain has no page.

measured worst 2), the end of eating's 3 (corrected 17 November: this said "3 before", which is Dhuhr's limit, not
About's figure); Tayma has no page. Nothing moves in Malaysia or Brunei: their claims are named by the release hold, not

(holes, months, the document's strings); with London held they failed for the hold, not their rule. They now pass

counts MUIS's reach file.

**For the owner.** (1) **London Unified's end of eating reads 5 min before the table across the M25** (at its north-east,
near 51.61 N 0.25 E, where the eastern edge's earlier dawn and the northern edge's summer dawn meet; the recorded
exception said 4, measured at the edges one at a time). It is a measured figure past the 4-minute ceiling, so a release is
refused and London's page on taqwa.world is held until he rules (`ReachRows.RULED`); About in the app is unchanged
(it counts starts: Fajr and Isha 5). Recommendation: accept it as measured, as R291 did the 246: the end shown is the
user's own dawn, earlier than the table, never later; nothing else would make the end less early.
(2) Singapore's figure rises to "at most 4 min" (3 before): all six starts' limits 3 or 4, from the west and south-west
(Asr and Maghrib over water inside the drawn ground) and sunrise off the east coast; within the ceiling, so not his to
rule, but it is what About and the Singapore page now say. Recommendation: none needed beyond (3).
(3) **Ground or the app's whole cell, one rule for both countries.** The app hands a GPS fix the country of its nearest
bundled city, so a phone on Singapore's or Bahrain's zone is placed there out to sea, and About says the country's
figure there. `ReachAreas.GROUND` reads only the drawn ground: land and the water between the country's own islands,
which for Singapore takes in the water off Jurong Island and the southern islands (where Asr's 4 and Maghrib's worst
are) and for Bahrain the box round the Hawar islands (where sunrise's and the end of eating's 2 are), but not open sea.
Read over the whole cell (16 November, the diagnostic, not committed: a box round each cell, every point a phone on the
country's zone is placed in the country alone):
- Singapore (box 0.90–1.52 N, 103.45–104.15 E, 0.5 km; 7,625 + 7,428 points; the cell reaches 0.94 N and 103.50 E into
  the Riau islands' waters): Fajr 3 (1.14 N 103.58 E), sunrise 3 (1.12 N 103.86 E), Dhuhr 3 (1.11 N 103.61 E), Asr 4
  (0.94 N 103.76 E), Maghrib 3 (0.98 N 103.73 E), Isha 3 (1.02 N 103.70 E), end of eating 2, imsak 1: the ground's
  figures exactly. About would still say "at most 4".
- Bahrain (box 25.38–27.22 N, 50.05–51.75 E, 1 km; 14,086 + 4,456 points; the cell runs from 25.42 N to 27.18 N and
  50.12 E to 51.69 E): Fajr 5 at 25.68 N 50.16 E (south-west, by the Saudi coast near Al-Uqair, sea or shore to check on
  a map; it may be Saudi land west of Al-Uqair: the nearest app city is Dar Kulayb, Bahrain's, at about 55 km, and At
  Taraf, Saudi, at about 56 km, so a phone on Bahrain's zone there is placed in Bahrain), Dhuhr 2 and Asr 4 beside it (25.67 N 50.17 E, 25.66 N 50.18 E), Maghrib 3 at 25.43 N 50.43 E, Isha 2 at 25.46 N
  50.40 E, sunrise 6 at 26.69 N 51.63 E and the end of eating 7 at 26.74 N 51.67 E (open Gulf north of Qatar, about 120 km
  east-north-east of Manama). Against the ground's Fajr 2, sunrise 2, Asr 2 and end of eating 2: read over the cell,
  About would say "up to 5" (not 2), and Fajr 5, sunrise 6 and the end of eating 7 are past the ceiling; no start
  early, no end late either way. Since the review of the fixes (17 November, below) a release is refused for those
  three until he rules: `checkStamps -Prelease=true` names `bh.council` (`ReachRows.BEYOND_AREA`), so no build says
  "up to 2" there before then; accepting the three as measured, or reading the cell, clears it.
Recommendation: read the cell for both until the app stops saying a figure where it is not measured: it is the only
reading under which About's "at most N" is measured everywhere the app says it to a phone on the country's own zone
(Singapore unchanged, Bahrain "up to 5", three rulings for Bahrain's cell, which should be accepted as measured, never
early: two at sea, sunrise 6 and the end of eating 7, and Fajr 5 at the Saudi shore, sea or land unchecked). The lasting fix is a bundled
border lookup, so a fix at sea is not placed in a country at all; the ground rule is then the right one.
(4) **Tayma's table read within a minute's reach of the town: Fajr 6, Maghrib 5, Isha 5** (R300; sunrise and Asr 4
were raised within the ceiling). At the disc's south edge the user's own dawn comes up to 6 min after the table computed
at KACST's point 111 km north; the time shown is the later, never early. About in Tayma says "at most 6 min" (5
before, the town point's own Fajr; corrected 17 November from "3 before"): what changes is Fajr 5 → 6 and Maghrib and
Isha 3 → 5 (sunrise and Asr 3 → 4, within the ceiling). The town's Fajr 5 is the limit recorded for it on 9 Oct 2026
(ruling R57), already over 4 before the R270 ceiling existed: an own recorded limit, which the ceiling's hold does not
read; the 6 is a reach figure, and it does.
A release is refused until he rules. Recommendation: accept the three as measured, as R291 did.
(5) **JAKIM's zones are said across their towns' discs, which nothing reads.** A place within 10 km of a town a zone's
list names takes that zone (5 km of a hill zone's named place), and 46 of the 56 zones are chosen past their own circle
(1,244 places among the app's cities, the named places and the grid; the towns' discs cover about 54,000 km², about
33,600 of it outside the zones' circles, from the town list on 1 km cells). The towns themselves are read
(`my-jakim-cities.tsv`), the ground between them is not, so About's JAKIM figures are measured at the named places only.
The release hold names `my.jakim` until it is read. A sweep per zone over its towns' discs is buildable (a `Chosen`
claim per zone, one file; about as many points at 1 km as the three area sweeps together), but was not built in this
fix pass, and its figures will likely pass some zones' ruled ones, which would come to him. Recommendation: build that
sweep in its own lane before the 1.7.0 cut, and rule on what it measures; the alternative, a recorded acceptance that
the towns' rows stand for their zones, leaves About's JAKIM figures claimed between the towns, not measured.
(6) **Brunei-Muara is said 63 km out at sea, where the gate cannot read it.** Brunei's districts go by the region of the
nearest city wherever any district's 60 km circle holds the place, so at 5.33 N 114.58 E (sea north of Tutong, nearest
city Sengkurong) the app says Brunei-Muara's figure past its 60 km; a gate row has no region, so a row there resolves to
another district, and the sweep cannot run. The release hold names `bn.mora`. Recommendation: change Brunei's `choose`
so a region picks its district only within that district's circle, else the nearest district whose circle holds the
place (which the radius sweep reads); no app city moves (none is chosen past its circle), only fixes at sea, and the
hold clears.

**For the merger.** (1) Generated here and shared with every lane: `stamps/*.json`, `ProofStamps.kt`, `ReachLimits.kt`
(London's, MUIS's and Tayma's lines), `own-points-worst.tsv` and the four area files. On the merged line: `generateReachRows
--args="--only <entry>"` for an area claim whose own rows, polygon or engine moved, then the gate (`-Pentry`),
`generateReachLimits` (report every "(raised)"), the whole gate, `generateProofStamps`, `generateOwnPointWorst`. (2)
`Gate.evaluate` builds `Repeats` from every row there is: a lane adding a year that repeats an earlier one need add no
`@fitted` line, and the stamp's `tables` falls by it. (3) `Authority.kt`'s `lateLimitFor` changed (R298), so the engine
hash of every stamp moves on any branch that merges it: run the whole gate. (4) The far-north lane's `no.irn` and
`tr.diyanet.europe` are untouched here. (5) Rulings R297–R300 used; R301 left unused. (6) R300 adds
`sa-ummalqura-tayma-reach.tsv` and a Tayma line to `ReachLimits.kt`: on the merged line, after a Tayma capture or a
change to Saudi units, `generateReachRows --args="--only sa.ummalqura"` writes both reach files; `checkStamps
-Prelease=true` names `bn.mora` and `my.jakim` (R300), `bh.council` (its cell, `ReachRows.BEYOND_AREA`) and Tayma's
three figures over 4 until the owner's items (3)–(6) are settled; whoever settles item (3) removes Bahrain's line from
`BEYOND_AREA` (and, if he chooses the cell, reads it as `ReachAreas.AREAS`' Bahrain claim). (7) The committed area

run again on the final code (below), and a merged line runs them again as in (1).

## The owner's rulings of 17 November — rulings R302–R309, branch `engine/rulings-nov17`

Off `engine/ramadan-final` at d1eaa4689 (the merged 1.7.0 line). No archive commit, nothing fetched, not pushed. The
owner accepted all nine recommendations of the two entries above, verbatim "Yes I accept all 9 with your
recommendations". Numbered as he was asked them: (1)–(3) and (5) are the far-north entry's "For the owner" (1)–(4),
(4) and (6)–(9) the reach-polygons entry's (1) and (3)–(6). Each is implemented here except (5), which is later, and (8),
the JAKIM sweep lane's:

1. **R302. A night too short for Isha's end declares it, and Maghrib comes at night where it can** (the far-north
   entry's (1), option (a′)). `DayPipeline.nightTooShortForIsha(point, date, zone)` reads the real sun alone, never a
   day's times: the night is too short when the minute after the real sunset plus two minutes (Isha the minute after
   Maghrib, and an end after it) reaches the next real sunrise rounded down to its minute, since the next day's end of
   eating is at or before a Fajr before the sunrise shown, itself never after the real sunrise (R90, R265). On such a
   night `DayComputer.clocked` (R292's block, under the clock rule) pulls Maghrib to the minute after the sun has set at
   every start point (never before IRN's) wherever that is before the next day's Fajr, and Isha to the minute after it,
   with no end (R26); where even that Maghrib is not before the next Fajr, nothing moves. The gate recomputes the
   declaration at each row's point (a lambda on `EntryStats.placeDay` and `promiseDay`, evaluated only for a day with
   no Isha end and not repaired) and counts such a day declared (`EntryStats.shortNights`, the stamp's `shortNights`
   with its dates, a line in the gate's report), never out of order; a day without its Isha end on any other night, or
   repaired, is out of order as before, so a late Maghrib margin or an early end of eating cannot hide behind the
   declaration. The gate declares for `no.irn` alone (`EntryStats.SHORT_NIGHT_ENTRIES`), the entry the owner ruled on:
   any other entry's such day stays out of order (review m1; see For the owner (1) on Norway's Cautious times). The label: About's IRN Tromsø note (`about_not_followed_irn_tromso`, all eight string files) gains a
   sentence saying that on the few nights around the midnight sun when the sun sets for only a few minutes there is no
   time for Isha before the next Fajr, so its end is not shown (the app shows no prayer's end on screen; the sentence is
   what the declaration says to a user; the seven translations of it are the builder's own and unreviewed, and what
   a user sees on those nights is For the owner (2)). Then `no.irn` left `ReachRows.PENDING` (now empty) for `SPECS`.
2. **R303. R292 stays as built** (the far-north entry's (2)): on the nights the sun sets for minutes, Maghrib and Isha
   5–6 min earlier than the day's own rule made them, still after the real sunset. Nothing changed.

   (`widened(180 + 60)`), unmeasured, a published method. The R300 point (5.33 N 114.58 E, Brunei-Muara's region,

declare `no.cautious`'s short nights (no gate row of it meets one today; one that did would be out of order).
Options:
- (a) Extend R302 to `no.cautious`: add it to `EntryStats.SHORT_NIGHT_ENTRIES`, and give its About a sentence of its
  own for those nights.
- (b) Keep R302 to IRN alone: `no.cautious` keeps the pulled times without a sentence, and the gate would refuse such
  a night if a row ever met one.

Recommendation: (a). It is the same night and the same sun, and About should say it wherever the times move.
(2) **What IRN's Tromsø sentence tells a user (review m4).** The sentence added under R302 ends "so its end is not
shown". But the app shows no prayer's end on screen, so that does not describe what a user sees. On 119 of the 246
nights, Isha is shown at the next Fajr's minute and its alert is skipped. On the other 127, Maghrib and Isha are
shown 4–6 min after the next sunrise, and both alerts are skipped. Offered wording, in place of the added sentence:
"On the few nights around the midnight sun when the sun sets for only a few minutes, there is no time for Isha before
the next Fajr: Isha is shown at the next Fajr, with no alert, and on the shortest of those nights Maghrib and Isha
come just after the next sunrise, with no alert." Recommendation: the offered wording. The seven translations of
whichever he picks need a native reader: those of the current sentence are the builder's own and unreviewed.

**For the merger.** (1) Rulings R302–R309 used. (2) Generated and shared with every lane: `stamps/*.json` (every
engine hash moved), `ProofStamps.kt`, `ReachLimits.kt` (IRN's three units, Bahrain's, Brunei-Muara's lines) and the
reach files `no-irn-reach.tsv` (new), `sg-muis-reach.tsv`, `bh-council-reach.tsv`, `bn-mora-reach.tsv`. (3)
`CheckStampsTest` pins the area hold's owed list to `my.jakim` alone; the JAKIM sweep lane empties it (done at the
merge of `engine/jakim-sweep`, below: the list is empty). (4) The JAKIM
lane merging after this one runs the whole gate, `generateReachLimits` and the stamps again (the engine hash moved

## JAKIM's zones read across their ground (17 November) — rulings R310–R312, branch `engine/jakim-sweep`

Off `engine/ramadan-final` at d1eaa4689 (the merged 1.7.0 line). No archive commit, nothing fetched, not pushed. The
owner's ruling 8 of 17 November ("accept all 9 with your recommendations"; the reach-polygons entry's item (5)):
build the sweep per zone before the 1.7.0 cut and rule on what it measures. Until now `checkStamps -Prelease=true`
refused `my.jakim` ("claims a figure across an area ... that no reach row reads", R297, R300): a place within 10 km of
a town a zone's list names takes that zone, and the 1,244 places `CHOSEN_BEYOND`'s search found past the zones'
circles (about 54,000 km² of towns' discs) were read nowhere but at the towns themselves. No time shown moves: the
golden vector is unchanged. What moves is what the proof measures and what About says.

**R310. Every JAKIM zone is read across all the ground the app hands it.** `ReachAreas.JAKIM_ZONES` holds one area
claim per measured zone (all 60), of a fifth kind, `ReachAreas.Handed`: a point is the zone's where a GPS fix there is
placed in Malaysia alone (`FixCountry` under Asia/Kuala_Lumpur, or Asia/Kuching east of 109.5° E: the nearest app
city is Malaysian and no other country is held beside it) and `Jakim.units` hands the place the zone by the app's own
rule (`UnitSet.unitFor`: the nearest town the zone's list holds within 10 km, a place it names, a hill zone's within
5 km, else the nearest circle that holds it), and the registry resolves it measured. So each claim is the zone's
circle and its towns' and named places' discs, as the app hands them, not the circle alone (which the radius file
still reads, unchanged). Each point is read against that zone's own tables in the archive (`my-jakim.tsv`'s rows at
the zone: the 2025 mirror, 2026, the 2027 captures and the printed imsak), with the neighbouring zones riding beside
it as the app computes the place (`Jakim.withNeighbours`), so a figure measured here is the place's. Every zone's
tables are in the archive: no zone lacked one. The grid is 1 km over each zone's box (its circle and a 10 km disc
round every town, named place and its point, widened by 3 km so no claimed point lies on its outer line; the sweep
stops otherwise), then four times finer (0.25 km) within a step of each event's worst points, as R297's sweeps do.
1 km covers a 5 km hill disc with about 78 points and a town's 10 km disc with about 314, and keeps the gate's cost
small: the gate holds only the kept points' rows (each zone's four extremes and each event's worst point), not the
grid. All 60 zones' rows go to one file, `my-jakim-zones-reach.tsv` (claims may now share a file:
`ReachAreas.fileText`, and `generateReachRows` writes a file's claims together), grown by `recipes.tsv` with every
capture as the radius file is (the nine zones' own lines twinned, and the `index` lines for the other 51).
`CityUnitsTest` holds every row of a shared file to one claim of it, every measured zone to a claim, every row to a
point of its claim reading every own table, the recipe twins, every place `CHOSEN_BEYOND`'s search finds for JAKIM to
a point a claim reads for the zone chosen there, and, with the archive, every claim on the grid offset from the
sweep's (2 km, shifted 0.6) to nothing early, nothing over its limit and no event past the stamp.

**R311. A claim other tables ride beside keeps the reason that names them.** `AREA_READ_UNITS` (`Authority.kt`) gives
a unit read across an area the area's reason, which says no other table rides; JAKIM's neighbours do. The zones'
claims are `ridden`, so their reach limits keep the circle's reason ("toward the edge of the reach the user's own
sun, and the tables that ride beside this one, decide the time shown"), and the test holding `AREA_READ_UNITS` to
`AREAS` leaves ridden claims out. `Authority.kt` is not changed.

**R312. What the sweep measured over 4 is the owner's, not ruled here.** `ReachRows.RULED` is not touched: the 32
unit-events the sweep raised past 4 min that his rulings have not accepted (below) stay refused, so
`checkStamps -Prelease=true` names `my.jakim` for them and the site holds the pages of the zones that carry one
(`Proven.verdict`, R270), until he rules.

## The merge of the two lanes and the owner's rulings of 17 November, evening — rulings R313–R315, branch `engine/ramadan-final`

`engine/ramadan-final` fast-forwarded to `engine/rulings-nov17` (e3fcbb20a, R302–R309), then `engine/jakim-sweep`
(2fc41fba1, R310–R312) merged into it (0905062c1). No archive commit, nothing fetched, not pushed. The owner, on the
two recommendations of the entries above (verbatim "Okay cool, yes I accept both recommendations"): the JAKIM entry's
For the owner (accept the 32 figures over 4 as measured) and the rulings entry's For the owner (1) (option (a) for
Norway's Cautious times). The rulings entry's For the owner (2) (IRN's Tromsø wording) is done here with the wording
that entry recommended, which he confirmed (verbatim "Yes let's keep the clearer wording").

**The merge.** Conflicts, each resolved so that both lanes' behaviour and tests stay:
- `ReachAreas.kt`: the rulings lane's `Cell` (in place of `Country` and the drawn `GROUND`, every box held to hold its
  claim whole) and the JAKIM lane's `Handed` claims for the 60 zones (`FIXED + JAKIM_ZONES`, `ridden`, shared files)
  side by side; `claimed` and `claimName` take both kinds. KDocs no longer false after the merge: `AREAS` (JAKIM's
  towns are read), `CHOSEN_BEYOND` (none is owed: Tayma's by its `Chosen` claim, JAKIM's by `JAKIM_ZONES`, Brunei's
  gone since R309; the JAKIM review's minor 1) and `JAKIM_STEP_KM` ("about 85,000 points", the sweep's 85,370; its
  minor 2).
- `CheckStampsTest`: the owed list (`ReachRows.unswept`) is now empty, each lane having emptied its own half
  (`my.jakim` by R310, `bn.mora` by R309).
- `CityUnitsTest`: one KDoc for both (a country's cell holds its app cities, every box holds its claim, claims may share
  a file); the body merged on its own, so every area claim, the 60 zones included, is held to no claimed point on its
  box's outermost grid lines without regenerating its rows.
- `BUILD-LOG.md` and `MONITOR.md`: both sides kept, the JAKIM entry after the rulings one; the two "For the merger" (3)
  notes now say the owed list is empty, and MONITOR no longer says JAKIM's towns or Brunei-Muara's sea are unread.
- Generated files (`ReachLimits.kt`, `stamps/my.jakim.json`): one side taken, then the chain below regenerated them.
  `ReachLimits.kt`'s count reads 1200 unit-events in 289 units (the two lanes' additions together).

**R313. JAKIM's 32 figures over 4 are accepted as measured** (the JAKIM entry's For the owner). The rulings lane moved
the engine hash (`DayComputer`, `Muis.kt`), so on the merged line `generateReachRows --args="--only my.jakim"` read the
zones again: "my-jakim-zones-reach.tsv: 60 claims, 85370 points on the grid and 168366 on the finer one, 379 points

s", both files byte for byte the lane's. The whole gate and `generateReachLimits` ("(0 unit-events moved)") left

`ReachRows.RULED` did not cover with the lane's table: 32 and 32, every one equal, none missing, none new. `RULED`

**R314. Norway's Cautious times declares R302's short nights too, and says them** (the rulings entry's For the owner
(1), option (a)). `EntryStats.SHORT_NIGHT_ENTRIES` is `no.irn` and `no.cautious`. `DeclaredCellsGateTest` now holds
that `no.cautious`'s day without an Isha end on a night too short for one, own or promise-only, is declared (and its
day on any other night still out of order), and that an entry no ruling names (`tr.diyanet.europe`) on the same night
is out of order, own and promise-only, with no `shortNights` in its stamp. No stamp moved for it: no gate row of
`no.cautious` meets such a night.
About: the Cautious template had no note of its own (`NotFollowedNote`, which gives IRN's Tromsø sentence, is the
authority templates'), so `cautiousNoteRes` gives `about_cautious_short_nights` where a member's placed method carries
IRN's Tromsø clock rule (`IrnArctic.NOTE_KEY`), which is exactly where R302 moves the member's Maghrib and Isha (the
rule stays behind past Tromsø's reach), after the Maghrib guard sentence. `AboutTimesUiStateTest` holds it at Tromsø
(resolved by id), and nowhere at Oslo's or Bodø's Cautious times or at IRN's own Tromsø. What it says was checked on
the review's probe of the 246 nights inside Tromsø's unit (`no.cautious` after R302): Maghrib and Isha both before the
next Fajr on 181 (the 119 R302 moved, where Isha falls on the next end of eating's minute, and 62 more), Isha at the
next Fajr's minute on 37, Maghrib at the next Fajr and Isha a minute after on 28; `NotificationPlanner` skips a
Maghrib or Isha alert exactly when its start is at or after the next day's Fajr (R83). The sentence says what is
visible and nothing about ends: "On the few nights around the midnight sun when the sun sets for only a few minutes,
Maghrib and Isha come before the next Fajr on most of them, with their alerts; on the shortest of those nights, Isha,
or Maghrib and Isha, may come at or after the next Fajr, with no alert."
Two things the owner was not told: (i) no user meets this sentence today. Within Tromsø's reach Automatic follows IRN
alone (`Regions.tromso`), and `no.cautious` is no row of the Timetable screen anywhere (no entry lists it nearby, and
where it is Automatic its own row is Automatic's), so it is resolved there only by id (the gate, probes, tests). (ii)
`SHORT_NIGHT_ENTRIES` is sun-only, so it would also declare `no.cautious`'s short nights beyond Tromsø's reach (north
of it, Alta to Kirkenes, Svalbard), where `no.cautious` is Automatic and R302 moves nothing; no gate row meets one
there today, and About says nothing there.

**R315. IRN's Tromsø sentence says what is shown** (the rulings entry's For the owner (2), its recommended wording).
`about_not_followed_irn_tromso`'s last sentence, R302's, becomes "On the few nights around the midnight sun when the
sun sets for only a few minutes, there is no time for Isha before the next Fajr: Isha is shown at the next Fajr, with no
alert, and on the shortest of those nights Maghrib and Isha come just after the next sunrise, with no alert." Checked
first against the code and the review's probe of the 246 nights: on the 119 R302 moved, Isha is the next Fajr's minute
and Maghrib the minute before it, so `NotificationPlanner` (shared by Android and iOS) skips Isha's alert and keeps
Maghrib's; on the other 127 Maghrib is 4–6 min after the next sunrise shown and Isha after it, both at or after the next
Fajr, and both alerts are skipped. True as worded. The owner confirmed this wording (verbatim "Yes let's keep the
clearer wording").

**R321's outcome (lane 2, fixes 2 of 2).**

*The cause.* Not the night check: the sun. At 69.895, 18.852 on 16 May 2026 the sun's lowest point is −0.83324°, at
22:40:32.7Z (corrected 20 November, the final review's minor 6: this said 22:40:28Z), above the real horizon's −0.8333°: it does not set there that night, the first of the midnight sun at that
point. `SunClock.altitudeTime` (EXACT) said it set at 22:40:58Z all the same. Its fixed-point iteration reads each
step's hour angle with the declination at the step before, so on a night the sun only grazes an altitude it creeps
toward the lower culmination (22:15:40, 22:36:18, 22:39:05, 22:39:55, 22:40:21, 22:40:58Z) and its sixth step,
returned as the crossing, has the sun at −0.833205°: no crossing. The bracket it falls back on judged the next morning
correctly (no sunrise on 17 May), so `DayPipeline.realSunset` gave a sunset and `realSunrise` no sunrise after it. Every
member's sun read the same false sunset: the day showed the sun's Maghrib and Isha, Isha a minute before the next
day's end of eating, so R292 had nothing to pull and R302's check (no next sunrise) said false. Isha came
more than its ruled 250 min after IRN's printed Isha (the shown clock times taken out 20 November under R69, and the
exact minutes 21 November, R69 read strictly: the owner's answer). The same cause had a second
face: the bracket took the lower culmination (transit ∓ 12 h) for the sun's lowest point, while the moving declination
puts the lowest up to about half a minute away and up to about 1e-4° lower near the polar circle. So on a night the sun
dips by less than that, one side found its crossing (by the iteration) and the other did not (at 70.132, 18.852 in the
night of 27 to 28 July 2026 the sunrise was found and the sunset was not), and the night check met the same sunset with
no sunrise, or the reverse.

*The fix* (`SunClock.altitudeTime`, EXACT only). An iterate stands as it is where the sun is at the altitude to within
1e-6° (`SETTLED_DEG`). Otherwise it stands only where the sun crosses the altitude at all: below it at its own lowest
point that night (a golden-section search within an hour of the culmination, `lowest`) and above it at transit
(`reaches`). Where the iteration finds nothing, the bracket bisects from that same lowest point. So a night's evening
and next-morning crossings are found or not together (corrected 20 November, the final review's minor 1: not yet. A settled
iterate stood without the question, and within about a week of the solstices the iteration settles onto the sun's lowest
point, so on a night the sun misses an altitude by under 1e-6° one side was still found, as at 65.802, 12.533 in the night
of 25 to 26 June 2026; since the final review's minors every crossing near a culmination asks it, below). No settled
iterate moves. A scan of 220,336,270 crossings
(40–80° N, every day of 2026, at 18.852° E, 25° E and 150° W, the real horizon and 0.5–21° below it) compared the old
algorithm with the new one. 116 crossings went, every one where the sun at its lowest is above the altitude (corrected 20
November, the final review's minor 6: the range that stood here, 2.1e-6° to 1.5e-4°, is the removed iterates' own offset
from the altitude, not the margin the sun stays above it by at its lowest; on R321's night these are 9.5e-5° and 6.3e-5°). 90 came, every one where it dips below by under about 1e-4°, which the culmination bracket missed. Every
other crossing is the same to within 41 µs (the bisection's new starting point).

*Tests* (each failing before the fix, for the reason it states). `SunClockTest` "a crossing the sun does not make is not
found under ruling R321": the FAIL night's sunset and the next morning's sunrise are null, as are four non-crossings of
the scan (a sunset, a sunrise, a 14° dusk and an 8.5° dawn), while two real grazing crossings stay where they were
(corrected 20 November, the final review's minor 4: two of the four, at 67.588° and 69.905°, were null before the fix too,
three decimals having rounded them out of the scan's band; they are now 67.5875° and 69.9045°, where the old code
reported a sunset at 22:41:26.7Z and a sunrise at 22:51:40.8Z).
`RealSunFloorTest` "the real sun sets only where it rises again after under ruling R321": the FAIL point has no real
sunset and no next sunrise, and on every night of May and late July from 69.3° to 70.2° (a thousandth of a degree
apart) the real sun sets exactly where it rises again the next morning. The second part failed at 70.132° on 27 July
until the bracket started from the sun's own lowest point. `IrnArcticTest` "a place off the app's grid is read at its
three-decimal point under ruling R321" is the snapping proof below. `ReachWatchedTest` (tools): every point a spec
watches is a row of its reach file (it failed before the rows were regenerated), and Tromsø's watched points include the
FAIL point and are all on the app's grid.

*The probe, before and after* (the Tromsø reach probe through the real Registry, Gate and PrayerEngine paths, `a_all`,
minutes after IRN's table; the stamp row 57/9/325/250/249 is RULED's).

Every grid passes, with 0 early cells, 0 out of order, and the gate and engine cross-checks at 0 mismatches. The old

*R319 re-checked on every night the fix moves*, clause by clause on all four grids (the probe counting each place-day).
- Nights pulled by R292 and not too short: Maghrib and Isha both before the next Fajr, with their alerts: refine 10,584,
  micro 1,993, dense 959, edges 994.
- Too short and pulled (R302): Isha exactly on the next Fajr, Maghrib before it: 821, 926, 93, 134.

So R319's sentence stays true as worded. "Most" holds on every grid: 11,405 of 12,566 such nights on the refine grid,
2,919 of 4,115 on the micro grid (corrected 20 November, the final review's minor 3: those counts took in the nights R302
pulls, where Isha is on the next Fajr with no alert. The clause's own count, Maghrib and Isha before the next Fajr with
their alerts, was 10,584 of 12,566 (84 %) on the refine grid, 959 of 1,141 on the dense grid (with R321's regenerated
reach rows among its points), 994 of 1,178 on the edges
and 1,993 of 4,115 (48 %) on the micro continuum: "most" holds on the app's own grids, not on the continuum, which the
app never shows. After the final review's minors, below). Nothing in the strings changes.

*How the app snaps a location.* `SettingsRepository.setLocation` stores the latitude and longitude rounded to three
decimals (`roundedTo3dp`, `storedCoordinatesAreRoundedToThreeDecimals`), and `PrayerEngine.canonical` rounds every
place it is handed the same way before resolving it (`EngineTest`'s day at the stored point). The new `IrnArcticTest`
case shows it on the probe's own off-grid point: at 69.8318, 19.446 on 1 August 2026, `PrayerEngine.dayTimes`
resolves to the point 69.832, 19.446 of `no.irn.tromso` and returns exactly that point's day. The probe's off-grid end of
eating (over its ruled 249 there before the fix, at most 249 after it) is therefore never shown to a user. That lattice point lies in
the refine grid, whose worst end of eating is 248.

## The final review's minors (20 November) — no new ruling, branch `engine/ramadan-final`

The final review of R318–R321 (clean: no blocker, no major) left six minors, and the owner's answer of 18 November
("Yes, all four") stands for them: R321 is to be mended at the source, with nothing new ruled and any figure over its
ruled number going back to the owner. This lane (step 2 of 3 after the merge of 1.6.0) took all six; the whole chain,
stamps and limits, is step 3's. The corrections to R321's outcome above are made in place, each marked.

**1. One question for both sides of a night** (the review's minor 1). R321 asked whether the sun crosses only where the
iteration had not settled to within 1e-6° (`SETTLED_DEG`). Within about a week of the solstices the iteration settles
onto the sun's lowest point, so on a night the sun misses an altitude by less than that one side was still found: at
65.802, 12.533, on the app's own grid (Helgeland, Norway's Cautious ground), the sun stays 6.3e-8° above the real horizon
in the night of 25 to 26 June 2026, and a sunrise at 23:12:45Z was reported with no sunset before it; at 18.852° E the
same happened for the horizon at about 65.73–65.87° N and for 18° at about 48.6–48.75° N on 13–26 June.
- What changed (`SunClock.crossing`): every crossing near a culmination asks the one question, settled or not (`bracket`:
  above the altitude at this date's transit, below it at the night's own lowest point), and that lowest point is found
  from the evening's side for the next morning too (`dayBefore`, `nightLowest`), so the evening's crossing and the next
  morning's read one and the same moment and altitude, bit for bit. Only a step settled an hour of hour angle or more from
  both culminations, short of 85°, skips the question (`clear`, `CLEAR_HOUR_ANGLE_DEG`, `CLEAR_LATITUDE_DEG`): there the
  sun at transit is above the step's altitude and at its lowest below it by far more than 1e-6° (over half a degree at
  Tromsø, still a tenth of a degree at 85°), and on the reviewer's Python port of SunClock, brought to this code, the
  question never answered otherwise for 122,906 such steps at random places from 85° S to 85° N, nor for 15,540 from 80°
  to 89.95°. Where the sun crosses, the step is kept as it was; a morning crossing with no step moves with the
  bisection's new starting point (corrected 20 November, the sun review's minor 1: this said "by microseconds"). Away
  from a night's edge it moves by at most about 0.13 ms; within about 2e-6° of one, where the sun's altitude is flat
  near its lowest point and the Julian day's 40 µs rounding turns it into small steps, by up to about 0.1 s (−73 ms to
  +88 ms). Of the review's 8.2 million samples about night edges (40–80° N, every day of 2026), 6 moved a shown minute
  the wrong way against 19147e170, 5 starts a minute earlier and 1 end a minute later, the only such moves there beside
  the crossings this item removes or adds: in five both moments lie within 0.8 ms of a whole minute, and in the sixth
  (64.782093, 12.533, 5.5°, the morning of 19 May 2026) the sun dips only 2.7e-15° below the altitude, so neither
  version's moment is more the sun's own than the other's (`Taqwa-work/engine-lanes5/review-sun/wrongway.txt`).
- Why sharing the lowest point matters: found separately from each side's own transit (as R321 found them), the two
  lowest points differ by up to 0.09 s and their altitudes by up to 3e-10° (on the port, 3,000 random nights; the Julian
  day's own rounding, 40 µs, moves the declination a step at a time), so a night within that of an altitude could still
  be read two ways.
- The five claims the review named are corrected: SunClock's KDocs (the crossing's, `SETTLED_DEG`'s), `DayPipeline.
  nightTooShortForIsha`'s, and the build log above. The R321 commit's own message (0d3a9609d) says the same as the build
  log did and stands as history.
- Tests (each failing first): SunClockTest "the evening's and the next morning's crossing of a night are found or not
  together settled or not" (65.802, 12.533: `(null, 1.782429165215339E9)` before; and one case in each band, 65.795243
  on 16 June and 48.66981 on 26 June, with a night the sun dips 1.6e-7° below still found on both sides);
  RealSunFloorTest "the real sun sets only where it rises again after at the solstice too" (the real sunrise
  23:12:45.215Z with no sunset before it, before; the band 65.700–65.950° N at 12.533° and 18.852° E, 10–30 June, after).
  SunClockSidesWalkTest (host): in the band ±3e-6° about each night's edge, sampled 3e-8° apart, at three meridians,
  for the horizon, 12° and 18°, mid-May to the end of July, no night has one side alone.

**2. A start reads the later of the step kept and the sun's own moment, an end the earlier** (the review's minor 2, and
lane 2's open item).
- The sizes, both sides. Where the iteration does not settle, or settles within an hour of a culmination, its step can
  stop off the sun's own moment, as a rule an evening's before it and a morning's after it: on Tromsø's grid up to 18.1 s
  early in the evening (69.671, 18.856, a watched point, on a night of May 2026; 16.6 s at 69.453, 19.55 on 18 May) and up to
  13.8 s late in the morning (69.465, 19.4, the morning of 25 July); within 0.03° of each night's edge from 40° to 80° N,
  up to about a minute either way near 80° N (58.4 s early at 79.8498° N, 13 April, the horizon). Lane 2's "11 s early,
  14 s late, about 15 s" understated the evening's. Settled alone did not make a step the sun's moment near a
  culmination, where the altitude barely moves: a step within 1e-6° of an altitude the sun only just reaches stood up to
  about 4 s off it (corrected 20 November, the sun review's minor 2: this said "up to 3.1 s". At the real horizon a step
  settled at 9.6e-7° stood 4.10 s before the sun's moment at 65.869595° N, 18.852° E on 14 June 2026, and one at 0.5°
  4.16 s; the lane's own port had found a sunrise 3.05 s late at 65.8784° N on 27 June 2026 and an 18° dusk 2.3 s early
  at 48.8047° N on 12 June), so such a step is read as an unsettled one is. Only a step settled an hour or more from both
  culminations stands alone: within 29 ms of the sun's moment on 557,081 such steps at random places between 89° S and
  89° N (all on the port; corrected 20 November, the merge review's minor 4: this said "to 88° N", and the worst, at

**What moves for users.** Only on the nights the sun or a twilight only just reaches its altitude, and on the days that
follow such a night or borrow its latitude: by a minute at most where a night keeps its crossings, but where that
minute tips R302's too-short check (Maghrib and Isha up to 6 min later, below), and where a night changes its kind by
up to 175 min either way where lanes 6 and 7 measured, a start up to 49 min earlier and an end up to 175 min later on
the app's grid (corrected 20 November, the merge review's minor 1(b): this said "and by a minute at most but where a
night changes its kind", which bounded nothing on those nights; what lane 6 measured follows this paragraph. Corrected
again that day, lane 6's review, minor 1 and nit 3: this said "where a night keeps its kind", which the 6 min below
contradicts, and "as measured" with no word of where; lane 6 measured the north's June edges, and not every angle there:
"What was not compared" below. Corrected a third time that day, after lane 7: this said "where lane 6 measured". Lane 7
measured every place a table governs on every date its tables print (an area's tables out to their farthest rows only
after lane 7's review, minor 1: "The review of lane 7" below), and every move it found is inside these figures on the
app's 0.001° grid, where every phone's place is; 1e-7° off a curve, where no phone is, a start came 51 min earlier:
"Every governed grazing night, measured" below).
In Tromsø's reach, on the nights the midnight sun begins and ends, Maghrib and
Isha come up to a minute later, or up to 6 min later where a night pulled before (R292) is now one of the very shortest
(Maghrib and Isha after the next sunrise with no alert, as R319 says), on the grids measured (qualified 20 November,
lane 7's review, nit 5: 1e-7° off a curve lane 7 found them 6 min earlier at 10 points, from item 2's moment alone:
"Every governed grazing night, measured", point 4); the end of eating, Isha's end and the sunrise come
up to a minute earlier; a night now too short for Isha's end no longer shows one; and where IRN's Fajr is after the sun
has risen and is declared, the Fajr shown before an earlier sunrise is a minute earlier with it. Elsewhere the same can
happen on the few nights a year a place's twilight or sun only just reaches its altitude (18° near 48.6° N in June and
further north in spring and late summer, near 48.6° S in December and further south from about November to February, the
horizon near the polar circles; the south added 20 November, lane 6's review, minor 1, and the other months that day,
lane 6's recheck, minor A: this said "18° north of about 48.6° N in June and south of about 48.6° S in December"), and
on a night the sun misses an altitude by under 1e-6° there is now no crossing on either side, so the day follows its
rule as on the nights on its polar side (corrected 20 November, the merge review's minor 1: this said "either side"; the
nights on the other side do have the crossing). Such a night comes only near a solstice: at every governed place, on
every date its tables print, lane 7 found one only between 13 and 28 June and between 14 and 28 December (and once at
float noise, below), and at every point it tested (every app-grid point within 2e-5° of an edge, and points 1e-7° off
it) R321's SunClock read every other night within 1e-6° of an edge as items 1 and 2 do (added 20 November after lane
7; corrected that day, lane 7's review, nit 3: this said "and on every other night within 1e-6° of an edge", more
than lane 7 tested; on lane 5's port the review found the kinds differing at 18° on 12 June 2026 and 29 June 2027 too,
by up to 5e-8°, and at float noise, about 1e-10°, on nights all year). No About sentence and no string changes; About's
figures are the stamps', which step 3 rewrites.

*Where a night changes its kind, measured* (added 20 November with the correction above). Lane 6's measure lane, read
only, compared 982024b1e (R321's SunClock) with e5b5711f2 (items 1 and 2) in exported trees; its files are in

- The bands. Every altitude a day asks of `SunClock` at the user's point was logged, through a tap that changes no time
  and was never committed, under every Settings choice at 277 app cities between 44° and 78° N. Each altitude grazes at
  the latitude where the sun only just reaches it: over the nights of 10–30 June 2026, 96 bands, 55 of them used by app
  places near where they graze. The real horizon (every method, R180's floor and R265's caps, Duha) grazes at
  65.68–66.22° N, every method's 17° red twilight (Maghrib's end) at 49.51–49.98° N, and the Other methods' and the
  entries' angles and curves between 46.5° and 66.3° N. Added to them: the horizon's December noon edge
  (67.15–67.65° N), Duha's 6.5° one (60.0–60.3° N), 76–82° N every half degree at eight places (every seventh day of
  2026 and the days about the start and end of the polar day and night), and the twelve gated units whose reach meets
  a band.

  place-days at the horizon's edge, where the day turns polar, and Maghrib's or Isha's end appears or goes 4,957 times.
- Why. Every wrong-way move is on a day that asks a crossing whose kind changed, but on 811 place-days of one-minute
  ties (Fajr held the minute before an earlier sunrise, R90; Maghrib's end at an Isha a minute later): a crossing R321's

  night at the horizon turns the day polar, and it borrows the times of 0.5° south (Maghrib and Isha earlier; the
  sunrise, Fajr's end and the end of eating later). A polar day up to 4° further north, which borrowed that latitude's

  eating or Isha. Most moves last one day; Isha's last up to 5 days in a row under Automatic and 9 under an Other

review's six minors (step 2, the section above) and the whole stamp chain on the merged line with the minors in, with
this entry (step 3). The owner's answer of 18 November ("Yes, all four") stands for all of it: nothing new is ruled,
and a figure over its ruled number goes back to him. Nothing is pushed: the line reaches main squashed (R60), since its
history holds the Algeria Ministry's printed minutes (9339211fd, R69).

**What changed.**
- `SunClockSidesWalkTest` (the merge review's minor 1(a)). The walk asserted that each start is the later of the two
  moments and each end the earlier, which `Crossing.start` and `Crossing.end` make so by construction, so it could not
  fail. It now finds the sun's own moment by itself, with none of SunClock's code: SolarMath's altitude, its hour angle
  written in the test, read every 0.05 s from a second before the crossing's two moments to a second after, and the one
  pass the side's way halved twenty times. A start more than a millisecond before that moment fails, as does an end more
  than a millisecond after it, or a crossing the sun does not pass once within that second. The millisecond: a clear
  step is the iteration's moment, never bisected, and was at most 0.64 ms off the sun's on the sun review's 4.7 million
  clear steps up to 85° N; the bisection resolves to 10 µs; where the sun moves at least 1e-6° a second, the altitude's
  float noise (about 3e-10°) moves a moment by 0.3 ms at most. A crossing where it moves less, at the edge of a night
  or a noon, is left out and counted. On the walk's 141,885 crossings every one is read and none left out: a start is at
  most 0.16 ms before the sun's own moment and an end at most 0.21 ms after it. The clear-step check stands (2,273 steps
  near a culmination moved, none clear of both). The walk takes 1.1 s (0.35 s before). On the sun review's Python port,
  the same reading gives the same two figures, and with every time read on the kept step, as before lane 5's item 2,

## Every governed grazing night, measured (lane 7, 20 November) — no new ruling, branch `engine/ramadan-final`

Lane 7 compared 982024b1e (R321's SunClock) with e5b5711f2 (lane 5's items 1 and 2) at every place a table governs (an
area's tables out to their farthest rows with repair 1: "The review of lane 7" below), on every date its tables print,
which lane 6 had not done ("What was not compared" above, rewritten with this entry). (Corrected 20 November, lane 7's
recheck, nit A: the parenthesis was missing here and in point 1 of "The review of lane 6" above.)
The line's engine is e5b5711f2's: the commits since change comments, tests, this log, a label, the Ramadan check's
wording, a generator whose output is byte for byte the same, and the stamps' hashes. Two hunts ran side by side:
"north", the night edges of every governed reach north of the equator, and "noonsouth", every governed place south of
the equator (night and noon edges) and the noon edges north of 55° N. Both ran read only: no commit in either
repository, no device, no web request, Gradle `--offline --no-daemon` on JDK 21 in exported trees, one heavy job at a
time. Their files are in `Taqwa-work/engine-lanes7/north` and `Taqwa-work/engine-lanes7/noonsouth` (`README.txt` the
index of each), and this entry's re-reads in `Taqwa-work/engine-lanes7/record`. This entry is the record lane's.
Nothing is ruled, no string changes and nothing is over its ruling; this commit is the log alone, so no stamp moves.
Neither hunt reported a blocker: under Automatic and every authority entry no case is early, and no end is late,
against a governing table by the gate's own test.

**What was covered.**
- The governed set, from the gate's own inputs. Every gate row (133,978) was read into its tables, each with its
  point, every day it prints (read as the gate reads it) and its reach: the area `ReachAreas` draws where a claim
  reads the table (London's M25, MUIS's and the Supreme Council's cells, Tayma, JAKIM's zones), else its unit's
  circle, else class D's reach, and never less than its farthest replaying row (corrected 20 November, lane 7's
  review, minor 1: this held for circles alone, and to the metre their radii are written in; an area's tables were
  read in the area, so London Unified's envelope rows (Folkestone and Reading in no hunted reach, four more only in
  Diyanet London's circle, hunted on its dates from 14 September 2026), Tayma's at KACST's own point and JAKIM's at
  1–3° N were not hunted on their tables' dates; repair 1 read each area again as a circle out to its farthest row,
  and every circle 1 m wider: "The review of lane 7" below). North of the equator that is 4,653 (table, entry,
  member) groups in 1,782 reaches, and repair 1's 64 circles; south of it, 770 tables.
- Night edges in the north, on every printed date (2012–2031) and the 11 nights before each: 773,204 reach-nights.
  The 168 reaches at or north of 44° N were hunted on curves, at 25 samples each (64 on a 6 km grid in London's M25),
  585 more where a 3 km grid (120,551 points) met a choice's unit or method at no sample (42 reaches), and a sub-reach
  for `fr.gmp` in the French part of Ghent's reach. The 1,614 reaches south of 44° N were read at their northernmost
  point on every night: no altitude a day asks comes within 4.35° of its edge there.
- The south, both edges. Only the seven Patagonian reaches of the Committee's promise tables can graze (Río Gallegos,
  Stanley, Punta Arenas, Ushuaia, Puerto Williams, Isla Hornos and Drake 58° S), and they were hunted on every date
  those tables print, 2026 and 2027. At every other governed place south of the equator (759 tables at 221 points:
  Indonesia, Australia, New Zealand, southern Africa, South America to Comodoro Rivadavia) the night is at least
  20.18° deep, deeper than any altitude asked there, and the noon at least 20.18° high, above Duha's 6.5°. In
  Patagonia the lowest noon is 8.17° high (Drake's reach), so no noon edge falls there either.
- Noon edges in the north. From 55° N to 59.71° N the lowest noon is at least 6.85° high, so none falls there; further
  north only Duha's 6.5° (at 13 reaches from 60° N up) and Tromsø's horizons come to one. No governed reach lies north
  of 69.91° N, so lane 5's settled noon crossings at 70–79.6° N fall in no table's reach.
- Altitudes. Every crossing a day asks, logged by lane 6's observer tap (it changes no time) in both trees: in the
  north under Automatic and every authority entry Settings offers, in the south under every choice, the Other methods
  included. An angle a place reads for itself was read from the engine at every probe point and solved across the
  reach (a scan every 0.004° of latitude, then bisection: 733 sign changes, 116,198 candidates). In the south the
  Moonsighting model's own angles stay at least 1.66° above the sun's lowest point at every sampled point and date,
  and the engine keeps them 0.002° short of the shallowest night, so they cannot graze. A day that asks at a fixed
  point (a unit's own) comes within 1e-4° of its edge in 54 cases, the closest by 2.9e-5°: none within 1e-6°.
- Areas as areas. `ReachAreas.claimed` decided where an area's tables hold a point (257 northern groups), in the hunt
  and in the stricter reading below (lane 6's review, nit 6). Singapore's, Bahrain's, Tayma's and JAKIM's areas lie
  at least 38.7° from any night or noon edge, beyond every altitude asked there. Out to their farthest rows (repair 1)
  they reach 29.86° N at most, the night there at least 36.7° deep and the noon 36.7° high, and at those circles'
  northernmost points no ask comes within 18.2° of its edge on any printed night.
- The polar days that borrow an edge latitude. At Tromsø, 193,126 borrowers were placed 0.5° to 5° north of every
  curve, each polar that day: 5,461 crossings at their borrowed latitude changed kind, and no day moved, since the
  choices there borrow from a fixed point. IRN's polar days, read at its unit's point, come within 1e-4° of an edge
  on no printed date; no latitude a day borrows lies inside Luleå's reach; and at Tromsø's polar-night latitudes,
  0.5–4° south, a borrowed latitude needs a sunrise too, so no borrowing changes.
- The rate limit's carry: in the north, every night up to the 12th after each place that changed kind or moved
  (every move stops within 5 days); in the south, 7 days after each changed grid point, and two whole years at the 29
  points below, where nothing carried under Automatic.

**How.**
- Curves and the net. At every 0.01° of longitude across a reach, and at its two extremes (in the north its box's,
  which fall short of a circle's own by up to 1.7 m in 6 reaches; repair 1 solved a step further each side and found
  nothing there: below), the latitude where the margin (the sun's lowest, or highest, less the altitude) is zero;
  inside the reach, a point 1e-7° to each side of it (a hair point) and every point of the app's 0.001° grid within
  2e-5° of it, solved again at its own longitude (the net). The north asked 1,252,483 candidate crossings. The south
  and the noon edges came to 1,079 nights or days with an edge in a reach, 117,875 curve points, 235,750 hair points
  and 44,499 grid points.
- The app keeps a place to 0.001° and computes it there (`SettingsRepository`'s `roundedTo3dp`, `Engine.canonical`),
  so a phone's day is always at a grid point. A hair point shows the mechanism, which only an unrounded gate row
  could meet; the two are counted apart below.
- Kinds. In the north each candidate was asked of both trees' own SunClock (R321's `altitudeTime`, items 1 and 2's
  `crossing`), and lane 5's port agrees on 5,000 of them; in the south lane 5's port was asked, and it agrees with the
  scalar port on all 61 grid changes and with the engine's own crossings at the 29 points under Automatic.
- The day. Lane 6's `BandMeasure` in both trees, every time the day shows (the fifteen and Duha's three), on 7,649,370
  place-days in the north (Automatic and every authority entry) and 8,034,538 in the south (every choice).
  `PrayerEngine.dayTimes` gave the same day on all 12,992 and 68,208 place-days it was asked for, and no index line
  (resolution, unit, method) differs between the trees.
- The tables. The gate's own test: `Gate.evaluate` on the governing rows replayed at each case's point over every day
  they print (a reach's own rows, a cautious entry's members, envelope and promise rows). Beside it lane 6's stricter
  reading: every table whose reach holds the point, declared cells held, areas read as areas. No printed time was
  written anywhere (R69); IRN's tables were given a verdict alone.

**What was found.**

  above the altitude by 2.4e-9°", the north's smallest; the south's is 6.0e-10°, at a grid point in Stanley's reach,

  edge. In the other months, March to September, 331,153 lay as near (Copenhagen's −17° in May and August among them),
  and none changed. South and noon: 9,176 points, 61 of them on the grid. 15° changed in Río Gallegos's and Stanley's
  reaches alone, on the evenings of 14–19 and the mornings of 23–28 December 2026 and 2027; Duha's 6.5° on the

- Wrong-way moves in the north (a start earlier or an end later), under Automatic and the entries: 50,820, and 8 more

## A year of ayahs for the widget (19 November 2026)

The ayah widget's pool is 365, one ayah for each day of a year, so a round within which no ayah repeats lasts a year (Mohamed's decision). The 265 new references are appended to `AyahPool.REFS` after the hundred, in Mushaf order, so no index a live install rotates through moves; the ayah widget spec's §3 has the amendment, the whole list, the 22 left out and why, and the upgrade note. They come from a survey of every ayah within the budgets (5,402 of the Quran's 6,236): a finder, two skeptics and an editor left 287 that meet the 12 September bar, and three judges (the card as drawn, the meaning, the year read as a whole) and the editor chose 265 of them, one of which, 41:30, Mohamed swapped for its twin 46:13 the next day (below; the figures here are for the pool with 46:13). The survey's files, the editor's `selection.md` and this step's scripts and measurements are in `apps/Taqwa-work/ayah365/`, outside the repo.

- **The card, measured.** The Android renderer's own auto-fit (`AyahCardRenderer`'s `fit`, compiled from this tree with the project's Kotlin and run inside an app process on an Android 16 emulator, with the app's Hafs and Manrope files) laid out all 365 in the six translations, the tafsir and with the translation off, at 420, 450 and 480 dpi.
  - At the 4×3 design size, 320 × 236 dp, the translation ends in an ellipsis for 8 of the hundred in English and 35 of the 265 (French 8 and 34, Indonesian 17 and 59, Turkish 6 and 28, Urdu none, Bengali 6 and 26, the tafsir 10 and 25; with 41:30, Indonesian 60 and Turkish 29). No Arabic is cut and no footer dropped.
  - At a roomier 340 × 330 dp 4×3, about an S23's, every one of the 265 shows its whole translation in every language.
  - At the widget's declared minimum, 250 × 180 dp (its `minWidth` and `minHeight`), the Arabic at 17 sp leaves no line for the translation on 32 of the hundred and 114 of the 265 (115 with 41:30), the same ayahs in every translation, which then show the Arabic and the footer alone; on 2 of the hundred and 14 of the 265 it leaves no room for the footer either, the translation off included. The 265 run longer in Arabic (42 have 20 words or more, against 6 of the hundred), and the editor's 250 dp device checks, 3:193 and 17:44 in Bengali, 22:37 in Urdu and Bengali, and 39:29, 6:60, 8:24 and 57:28 in Urdu, are all among the 114.
  - Against the pool's own worst card at the design size, two of the 265 lose one line more: 22:37 in French, at 420 dpi only, and 3:193 in Bengali. Both stay, as the editor left them. Each of the 22 left out has a fault of its own, and 2:274, the strongest of them, also has a Bengali misspelling (আশংঙ্কা, where the Bengali translation's other 24 read আশঙ্কা) beside its Saheeh stray space.
  - The iOS widget was not run. A Core Text count on the Mac fits both whole on Large, whose eight lines hold every translation of the 365 but five in the tafsir, three of them the hundred's (3:193's Bengali takes six, one more than any of the hundred). Medium shows three lines of translation by design, and cuts many of the hundred too.
- **The mirror** is about 230 KB of UTF-8 with Saheeh International, 310 KB with the tafsir (the longest) and 180 KB with the translation off, where the hundred made about 60 KB. On the emulator SharedPreferences wrote each in 1 to 32 ms and read it back cold, in a new process, as the same string, and `AyahPoolMirror.deserialize`, which each widget draw runs, read the 365 entries back in 1.1 to 2.0 ms (measured on 20 November for the pool with 46:13, `followups/logs/instrument-prefs-deserialize.log`; the build step's own timings kept no log). On iOS the App Group's plist holds it as UTF-16, under 350 KB, far below the 4 MB at which iOS is reported to refuse a preferences domain (a limit not checked here). The app's widget-reload key hashed the mirror and counted its characters on each reload: 11.9 ms on the Mac mini for the 365 with Saheeh International, where the hundred took 3.1 ms (timed on 20 November, `followups/logs/reload-key-bench.txt`). Since 20 November the key takes the mirror's UTF-16 length instead of counting its characters; what that saves, and how often the key is rebuilt, are in the follow-ups' entry below.
- **Counts.** `AyahPoolTest` holds 365, `AyahRotationTest` the rotation's rules at the pool's own size, and `AyahPoolDbTest` the budgets for all 365. The README and the privacy policy in seven languages say 365, the policy dated 19 November, and the privacy gate's backups rows and its M3 constant with them.
- **Tests:** `:widgetcore:allTests` and `:widgetcore:testAndroidHostTest` (142 tests on the iOS simulator, 144 on the host), `:shared:testAndroidHostTest` with `AyahPoolDbTest` and `AyahPoolMirrorWriterTest` alone (13) and whole (2,510), all green; `scripts/check-versions.sh`, the privacy gate and its tests, and the store listing check and its tests pass.

## The owner's five decisions on the 365 (20 November 2026)

The 365's build step (above) left Mohamed five recommendations. His answer, on 20 November 2026: "Yes I accept all five as recommended".

- **46:13 in place of 41:30.** The two are twins, "Our Lord is Allah", then steadfastness, and no fear and no grief; the survey's duplicates pass had merged 46:13 into 41:30, so it was outside the 287 and no judge read it. 46:13 is the shorter (13 Arabic words and 148 Saheeh characters, against 19 and 226) and clean in all six translations, where 41:30 has Saheeh's stray space (`Allah "`), the kind of slip that helped drop 2:274, a quote that never closes in English and one in French, a parenthesis that never closes in Urdu, and Diyanet's 41:30-32 (341 characters) under it. `AyahPool.REFS` loses 41:30 and takes 46:13 between 45:37 and 47:2, so the appended block stays in Mushaf order; the hundred do not move, and none of the 265 has shipped. The spec's §3 lists the 365 as they ship and records all five decisions ("Amended 20 November 2026"). In `apps/Taqwa-work/ayah365/`, `owner-swaps.txt` records the swap, `keep265.txt` has it applied (the editor's own list is kept in `followups/`), and `build365/append-pool.py --check` and `editor/verify-selection.py` now read the swap and pass: 46:13 is outside the 287 and merged into 41:30 in `ayah-dups.txt`, the editor's 265 and 22 are still exactly the 287, and `AyahPool.REFS` is the hundred followed by `keep265.txt`.
- **22:37 stays**, though its French shows 3 of its 6 lines at 420 dpi on the 320 × 236 dp cell; the only alternative, 2:274, has slips in two of its texts.
- **The eight cards that open on a speech frame stay:** 2:32, 7:23, 7:128, 12:86, 15:56, 20:25, 26:62 and 28:16.
- **Diyanet's grouped Turkish passages stay, pool-wide:** 20 of the 265 show one (21 before the swap), and 5 of the hundred do. The recommendation's "7 pool cards" are the hundred's grouped passages outside the tafsir: those 5 and 94:6's French and Bengali (94:5-6), seven passages on six cards. The same scan finds that Tafsir al-Muyassar also stores one text under neighbouring ayahs, under 13 of the hundred's cards and 23 of the 265's; the decision did not name it (`followups/figures.txt`).
- **More translations end in an ellipsis on the smallest sizes**, Android's 320 × 236 dp and iPhone's Medium, and that is accepted; at about 340 × 330 dp none of the 265 is cut.
- **The figures, recomputed for the pool with 46:13.** The card was measured again in full with the build step's harness, on a second Android 16 emulator (a scratch AVD with the same configuration and system image): its rows for the 364 cards the two pools share, all 52,416 of them, are identical to 19 November's in every measured column, and differ only in the index of the 13 cards from 41:46 to 45:37, one lower since 41:30 left the place before them (`followups/measure/fit-compare.txt`, `followups/review-fixes/fit-index.txt`). At 320 × 236 dp the translation is ellipsised for 59 of the 265 in Indonesian (60 with 41:30) and 28 in Turkish (29), the other languages unchanged, and 46:13 is whole there in every language. At 250 × 180 dp 114 of the 265 leave no line for the translation (115), and 46:13 shows two lines there, ellipsised, so the ellipsised count is one higher in every translation (English 105 of the 265, for one); the footer counts, the 340 × 330 dp result and the pool's worst cards are unchanged. The Core Text estimate for iOS gives the 364 the same line counts as before; Large is unchanged, and one card fewer needs more than Medium's three lines in English (63 of the 265), French (71), Turkish (30) and the tafsir (80). The mirror is 228,981 bytes of UTF-8 with Saheeh, 311,368 with the tafsir, 179,648 with the translation off and 89,531 of `followedBy`, a few hundred bytes less each, so still about 230, 310, 180 and 90 KB; on the emulator SharedPreferences committed each in 1 to 32 ms and `deserialize` read the 365 entries in 1.1 to 2.0 ms. Long Arabic (42 of the 265 at 20 words or more, against 6 of the hundred) and the themes are unchanged; the 365 now draw on 81 surahs, al-Ahqaf's 46:13 among them. The entry above carries the figures that moved, and the editor's `selection.md` has them all in a dated section, "Mohamed's decisions (20 November 2026)"; the scripts and results are in `apps/Taqwa-work/ayah365/followups/`.
