## The 365's follow-ups (20 November 2026)

The review of the 365 (19 November) left six items open; this step settles them, beside the owner's decisions above. Its scripts, measurements, logs, screenshots and two APKs are in `apps/Taqwa-work/ayah365/followups/`.

- **The iOS reload key.** `reloadWidgets()` in `iOSApp.swift` folds the ayah pool mirror into its reload key by `hashValue` and a length, and the length is now `utf16.count`, the bridged string's own, where `count` walked the whole mirror for its graphemes. Timed on the Mac mini on 20 November (`followups/reload-key-bench.swift`: the mirror bridged from an `NSString` as `UserDefaults` hands it over, the median of seven rounds of fifty calls), the key's ayah part took 11.9 ms with Saheeh International and 14.1 ms with the tafsir before, and 4.0 ms and 4.9 ms after; the hundred's took 3.1 ms before. The build step's 20 ms was taken on a busier Mac: its own bench, run again beside this one, gives 3.9 ms for the hash and 7.9 ms for the count with Saheeh.
- **How often the key is rebuilt.** On every `reloadWidgets()` call, on the main thread. The Prayer screen's tick runs once a second while the screen is started, but calls `refreshWidgets()` only when the widget snapshot it serialises has changed (`PrayerViewModel.kt:318`): each time its countdown passes a whole minute or its ring one of the 120 steps it takes from one prayer to the next (`WidgetMirrorWriter.kt:58-62`), mostly at different seconds. A model of that arithmetic with a tick a second (`followups/read-order/snapshot-rate.py`, `snapshot-rate.txt`) gives twice a minute while that screen shows with the prayers two hours apart, 1.1 to 2 times a minute when they are further apart, and more when they are closer: 2.25 times a minute at 95 minutes and 2.7 at 70, as Maghrib to Isha can be. Every other caller calls it after its own write, changed or not: each write of the ayah pool mirror (every app start, a translation or a language change), a setting that moves the times, the widget background, the location backfill, a language change and the background refresh, which then calls `reloadWidgets()` again itself, as the root view's `onAppear` does. The comments that said once a second (`iOSApp.swift`'s `installWidgetRefreshHook` and `reloadWidgets`, `WidgetRefresher.ios.kt`) now say this.
- **The Android pool in a file of its own.** `KeyValueStore.android.kt` keeps `ayah_pool` and `ayah_seed`, every key `AyahPoolMirror` and `AyahPoolMirrorWriter` use, in `taqwa_widget_ayah_pool`, and everything else in `taqwa_widget_mirror`. A pool key is written to its own file and then removed from the mirror file if an older build left it there; it is read from its own file first and the mirror file after, so a widget drawn after the update and before the app runs still finds the pool and the seed. The seed is never rewritten once it exists, so an updated install keeps its seed in the mirror file. Every Android reader and writer comes through `createWidgetKeyValueStore()`, and none names a file: the ayah widget's `ensureMirror` and `readAyahRender` and the prayer widget (`TaqwaAyahGlanceWidget.kt`, `TaqwaGlanceWidget.kt`), the Settings › Widgets previews (`AyahWidgetPreview.kt`, `WidgetsSettingsScreen.kt`), the pool's writer in `AppEffects.kt`, `PrayerViewModel`, the widget background in `SettingsRoutes.kt`, and `WidgetMirrorRefresher` in `PrayerAlarmReceiver`, `SystemEventReceiver` and `NotificationTopUpWorker`. AOSP's `SharedPreferencesImpl` (the SDK's android-36 sources: `commitToMemory`, lines 576-593, and `writeToFile`, lines 760-776; the same in 37.0) drops a `putString` of the value a key already holds, so nothing changes, no new memory generation is made and nothing is written to disk: after the split, the app's rewrite of an unchanged pool at every start costs no disk write, and the snapshot's writes rewrite only the small file. Nothing of our own was added for it. `AndroidKeyValueStoreTest` (`:widgetcore` androidHostTest, 9 tests) holds the rules.
- **The update, on the emulator** (`followups/upgrade-check.sh`, `logs/upgrade-check.log`; this step's own Android 16 emulator). `before.apk` wrote the 365-entry pool and its seed into `taqwa_widget_mirror.xml` (239,970 bytes). Installed over it, `after.apk` changed nothing until the app ran. Its first run wrote the pool to `taqwa_widget_ayah_pool.xml` (239,911 bytes) and left `taqwa_widget_mirror.xml` holding only the seed (129 bytes), the same seed: the writer had found it in the old file and not written another. A second run with nothing changed left both files' modification times as they were, to the nanosecond.
- **Backups.** `allowBackup` is false, and `data_extraction_rules.xml` excludes `root`, `file`, `database`, `sharedpref` and `external` whole, for cloud backup and for device transfer; there is no `fullBackupContent`, and no rule names a file. The new file is excluded exactly as the old one is, so the policy's Backups sentence ("Taqwa opts out of Android's app backup") stays true in all seven languages. Neither the policy nor `tools/privacy-check.py` names `taqwa_widget_mirror.xml`, so neither changed.
- **iOS keeps the one App Group domain.** A `UserDefaults` write there is handed to `cfprefsd`, which persists the domain out of the app's process, so the app does not pay for the plist being rewritten, and a second domain would have the widget extension read two. `cfprefsd` still writes the whole domain, pool included, when it persists a snapshot change; how often it does, and at what cost, was not measured.
- **`REFS` pinned.** `AyahPoolOrderTest` (`:widgetcore` commonTest, so on the iOS simulator and the host) holds `AyahPool.REFS` as it ships in 1.7.0, all 365 by value: it fails if any of them moves or goes, and lets entries be appended after them. `AyahPool`'s KDoc said removing entries was fine; it now says the list only grows at its end.
- **The preview's claim.** `AyahWidgetPreview.kt` said its three Arabic sizes are what the longest ayahs in the pool need. An estimate of the preview's layout for all 365 in every translation (StaticLayout with the app's Hafs face on the emulator, by the preview's own rules: `followups/measure/harness/ayah365/PreviewMeasure.java`, `measure/preview-summary.txt`) finds every ayah's Arabic inside the card at each width the picture is laid out at, 312, 339 and 376 dp (phones up to 384, 411 and 448 dp wide), but not every translation as well: with Saheeh International, 33 of the hundred and 109 of the 265 are taller than the card at 312 dp, 12 and 48 at 339 dp, and none at 376 dp (with Indonesian 49 and 154, 19 and 84, 1 and 3; with the translation off, none at any width). On the emulator the day's card, 35:3 in English, fits at 448 dp, and at 384 dp shows three of its five lines of translation, the third cut by the footer's rule, as estimated (`followups/shots/`). The comment and the spec's §9 now say so.
- **No more than a round.** The README, the spec (§1, §3, §5 and both upgrade notes), `AyahRotation`'s KDoc, `AyahPoolTest`'s comment and the 365's own entry in this log now claim no more than that no ayah repeats within a 365-day round: across a round's boundary only the next day is guarded, so an ayah can come back two days later. The spec's 19 November upgrade note said the rotation moved to 365 on the day the update lands; it moves the first time the app runs after the update, when the app rewrites the mirror, since until then both widgets draw from the hundred's (Android's widget rewrites only a missing or older-version mirror, and the iOS extension never writes), and the 12 September note now says the same. The privacy policy makes no repeat claim and is unchanged.
- **APKs** (`followups/apk/`): `before.apk`, a debug build of 536e56d36, the swap and the decisions, whose `KeyValueStore.android.kt` is 1.6.0's (`git diff 3fa6fb063` of it is empty), built in a temporary worktree since removed; and `after.apk`, a debug build of these follow-ups. Both are signed with the same debug key (`~/.android/debug.keystore`), so one installs over the other.
- **Tests and checks.** At 536e56d36: `:widgetcore:allTests` and `:widgetcore:testAndroidHostTest` (142 on the iOS simulator, 144 on the host) and `:shared:testAndroidHostTest` with `AyahPoolDbTest` and `AyahPoolMirrorWriterTest` (13), green. With the follow-ups: `:widgetcore:allTests` and `:widgetcore:testAndroidHostTest` (144 and 155), `:shared:testAndroidHostTest` whole (2,510) and `:androidApp:assembleDebug`, green; `scripts/ios-build.sh` built the app for the iOS simulator, the reload key's change with it, and its bundle checks passed; `scripts/check-versions.sh`, `tools/privacy-check.py` (263 rows approved, clean) and `tools/test_privacy_check.py` (47 tests) pass; `build365/append-pool.py --check` and `editor/verify-selection.py` pass.
- **After review (20 November).** The review found two of the hundred's figures carried over by hand, and `followups/figures.py` now prints both (`followups/figures.txt`): Diyanet stores a grouped passage under 5 of the hundred's cards, not 7, a count that also took in 94:6's French and Bengali (in the decisions' entry above, the spec's decision (4) and `selection.md`), and Tafsir al-Muyassar under 13 of them, not 15 (the entry and `selection.md`). The rest is wording, corrected in place: the 46:13 measurement's shared rows are identical to 19 November's in every measured column, and the index of 13 cards is one lower (`followups/review-fixes/fit-index.txt`); the 19 November mirror bullet gives 20 November's logged timings, where the build step's own kept no log, and points to this entry for how often the reload key is rebuilt; the spec's decision (3) gives its reason as the editor's reading of the 12 September bar, which the recommendation carried; both upgrade notes say that the switch day almost always shows a different ayah, since the old and new rotations agree only by chance, and the 12 September note is marked as amended; and the privacy gate's comment on the 365, like the opening of `selection.md`, says one ayah for each day of a 365-day round. In `apps/Taqwa-work/ayah365/`, `editor/build-selection.py`, which wrote the editor's 19 November files and knows nothing of the swap, now refuses to write while `owner-swaps.txt` exists, and `followups/selection-20nov.md` keeps a copy of `selection.md`. Only documents and a comment changed, so Gradle and the iOS build were not run again; `tools/privacy-check.py` (263 rows approved, clean), `tools/test_privacy_check.py` (47 tests), `scripts/check-versions.sh`, `build365/append-pool.py --check` and `editor/verify-selection.py` pass (`followups/review-fixes/logs/`).
- **The read order, after the code review (20 November).** The review of the follow-ups' code (`followups/review-code.md`) found that `getString` read a pool key from its own file first and the mirror file second, so a read could straddle the move at the first pool write after the update: it found the own file still empty, the writer then put the pool there and removed it from the mirror file, and the read found the mirror file empty too, so once per install the widget could draw one blank ayah card until the redraw that follows the write, or write the pool once more. `getString` now reads the mirror file first and the own file second, and returns the own file's copy whenever there is one, so a stale copy left in the mirror file still loses to it. The write puts before it removes, and SharedPreferences changes a file's map in memory inside `apply()`, under that file's lock, which `getString` takes too (the android-36 sources of `SharedPreferencesImpl`: `apply` calls `commitToMemory`, and both it and `getString` hold `mLock`; `ContextImpl` keeps one instance of each file for the process), so a read of the mirror file that finds the key removed comes after the put, which the read of the own file then finds. The bullet on the Android pool above gives the first order. `AndroidKeyValueStoreTest` (11 tests, from 9) logs both fake files' edits in one list and checks that each pool key's put comes before its removal (`aPoolKeyIsPutInItsOwnFileBeforeItLeavesTheMirrorFile`), and runs the move between a reader's two reads, for the pool and the seed, and checks that the reader gets the old value or the new one, never null (`aReadStraddlingTheMoveNeverComesBackEmpty`). With the put and the removal swapped only the first fails, and with the two reads swapped only the second, "ayah_pool read as null while it moved" (`followups/read-order/mutation.txt`). The test that restated `AYAH_POOL_KEYS` is now `everythingTheAyahPoolMirrorWritesGoesToThePoolsOwnFile`, which writes through `AyahPoolMirror`'s own `write` and `writeSeed` and fails when `write` also writes a third key, as the old one could not (the same file), and the stale-copy test covers the seed as well. The same pass corrected four comments: the store's list of writers now names the widget background and `WidgetMirrorRefresher`'s callers in `AppEffects` and `SettingsRoutes`; its note on the mirror file says that an updated install keeps its seed there for good; the preview's clause on 376 dp says none, as `measure/preview-summary.txt` gives for Saheeh International; and where the bullet on how often the reload key is rebuilt, the comments it names, `KeyValueStore.android.kt`, `AndroidKeyValueStoreTest` and the spec's §4 called the snapshot minute-granular, changing about once a minute, they now give its countdown's minute and its ring's 120 steps, from the model in `followups/read-order/snapshot-rate.txt`. Checks: `:widgetcore:allTests` and `:widgetcore:testAndroidHostTest` (144 on the iOS simulator, which Gradle found up to date, since this step changed none of their sources, and 157 on the host), `:shared:testAndroidHostTest` (2,510) and `:androidApp:assembleDebug`, green; `scripts/ios-build.sh` built the app for the iOS simulator and its bundle checks passed; `tools/privacy-check.py` (263 rows approved, clean), `tools/test_privacy_check.py` (47 tests) and `scripts/check-versions.sh` pass. `followups/apk/after2.apk`, a debug build of this step, is signed with the same debug key as `before.apk`, and its `getString` reads the mirror file first (`followups/read-order/`).

## The owner's answers of 21 November — rulings R322–R328, branch `engine/ramadan-final`

On 21 November the owner answered the items left for him on 20 November (the record lane's points 1 to 3 under lane
6's entry, lane 7's points and the R69 question of lane 6's review), taking the Lead's pick on each. Nothing in this
entry changes code or a figure; R327 is carried out in the entry that follows. His other answers that day (the site's
watch section, its features grid, the Home watch card's wording and the font comparison) are not the engine's.

**R322. R319's "just after" covers up to 7 min.** On the very shortest nights around Tromsø's midnight sun, Maghrib
now comes up to 7 min after the next sunrise on the app's grids, where R319 was given on 4 to 6 ("R319's very
shortest nights, by the minute" above). `about_not_followed_irn_tromso` keeps R319's sentence as it is.

**R323. A night the sun only grazes follows the method's own rule.** Under Automatic and the authority entries, the
times that move the wrong way on such nights (the record lane's point 2, lane 7's points 2 and 6) are accepted as
measured: they came from a crossing the sun does not make, they follow the nights beside them, and no printed cell of
a table that governs such a place breaks where lanes 6 and 7 measured. The figures put to him are the app grid's (a
start up to 49 min earlier, an end up to 94 min later); lane 7's 51 at points 1e-7° off a curve, which a phone cannot
reach, stays in its entry. No About sentence about these nights was put to him, and none is added.

**R324. A confirmed Other method keeps its own rule on those nights (R52).** Where a confirmed Other method (the old
picker's seventh-of-the-night rule, ISNA's 15° in Patagonia) now crosses a table that governs its place on the first
night its own rule takes over (the record lane's point 3, lane 7's point 8), the crossing is accepted as the cost of
the user's own confirmed choice: R52 holds a chosen method to Automatic only until the user confirms it past the
earlier-than check, and the gate checks no Other method.

**R325. The Islamic Foundation of Toronto's table chosen around Edmonton is the user's choice** (lane 7's point 1).
On some June nights its Isha comes before the printed Isha of Edmonton's mosques; Settings keeps offering `ca.ift` and
its Toronto siblings there, and they are not held to Edmonton's tables.

**R326. R247 stands: the Committee's tables govern at their own points** (lane 7's point 7). Automatic computes at the
user's own point, so away from a table's own city it can come a few minutes before that table where the sun there is
earlier, as in 1.6.0. No ride across class D's reach is built; the Committee's Saint-Pierre tables and Habous's Ceuta
and Melilla rows stay at their points too.

**R327. R69 is read strictly** (lane 6's review, nit 7). No printed time of a timetable the engine reads stands in the
public tree, and no text lets a reader work one out: a place, one day and an exact offset from a printed time do not
stand together. The Lead's pick named a few build-log lines and one engine comment; the sweep took in all the text
1.7.0 adds, since the same pattern stood elsewhere. The fixed national clocks the engine encodes stay, as rules rather
than a table's days: COSIM's Zouhr and Asr, the Tajik Council's one Peshin minute (put to him as "Tajikistan's fixed
Dhuhr", with the Dhuhr floor and the town figures that follow from it) and DUM RT's Dhuhr.

**R328. 1.7.0 ships with its stamps as they are; Habous's December and the 2027 tables come in 1.7.1** (R275's "For the
owner", answered the same evening). The stamps the release carries end where their tables end: `ma.habous`'s on 30
November 2026, and those of the authorities whose printed year is 2026 on 31 December. Past a checked run a class A or B
place shows "Published method" for the day (R275), so from 1 December Morocco's places read "Habous method, not yet
fully checked" and from 1 January 2027 about 726 cities read their authority's published method, until a build carries
the new tables; the times do not move with the label. On taqwa.world the same rule holds the city pages (G9): Morocco's
six show November alone and are held from 1 December, and the pages whose tables end with 2026 are held from 1 January,
until the build that carries the tables reaches main. 1.7.1, an update of data alone, gates Habous's December table and
the 2027 tables in early December (a follow-up is booked for 1 December).

**For the record: the 12 November Kemenag rounds.** The release's largest move toward earlier times had no entry of its
own (the release audit's users lens, a nit). The rounds of 12 November made 109 and then 119 more kab/kota class B units
(proof 7c, "Round of 12 Nov 2026"; R186, R211–R212), so a city 1.6.0 held under Kemenag's published method, with the
edge's safety minutes, now reads its own checked table. At Pontianak, Balikpapan, Padang, Mataram, Ambon and Manado
every start comes earlier than in 1.6.0 on every day of November and December 2026 (Maghrib by 7 min, the other starts
by 3) and sunrise 7 min later; no start comes before the city's own table, and `id.kemenag`'s stamp has none broken
through 2028. Nothing changes.

## R69 read strictly (21 November) — the owner's answer of 21 November, branch `engine/r69-strict`

The owner's answer of 21 November reads R69 strictly: no printed time of any timetable the engine reads stands in the
public tree, and no text lets a reader work one out; every such timetable counts as restricted. The national clocks the
engine keeps as rules stay as they are (COSIM's Zouhr and Asr, the Tajik Council's one Peshin minute with the Dhuhr
floor that follows from it, DUM RT's Dhuhr): a rule, not a table's day. In the docs, gate-file headers and comments this
line adds, in SBH09's two limit reasons, in main's older text in the five files the third commit swept and in the
passages the two repairs name (all below; main's older text elsewhere was not swept), a place, one day and an exact
offset between a table's printed time and a time the public engine gives no longer stand together, nor does a pointer
that joins them (the same place's day named in another passage, a fitted margin's binding day, a plan that dates a
proof's row). What still lets a reader work a printed minute out is listed at the end: what stamps, generated files and
code hold, and what a test of each candidate day against a margin's seconds can pick out where no passage names the day.
Limits, worst cases without their day, ranges, counts and fitted curves stay.

How the line was swept: four finders read the text this line adds over main, and each rewrite was checked against its
passage; where the same figure stood again close by (the Tajik floor's relation to the Peshin, SBH09's starts, Dubai
Rural's days, İstanbul's row in the proof note), that passage was rewritten the same way. That was the first commit. Two
adversarial checks then read it, and a second commit takes what they found in docs, headers and comments: a Tromsø night
still named beside its point in other passages, a fitted margin's binding day in a gate header, the Tajik floor's
derivation from the Peshin, a pointer to the day of İstanbul's row, and this entry's own claims. A third commit, after
the second check, takes what was left: SBH09's two limit reasons, its own and its neighbour's, which said the four days
were held as printed (its own, that each start was the print's) and now say the starts are held to the print, never
before it, as the comments do; the night named beside Kazan's grid worst and the seconds of the old Bishkek Dhuhr
margin, which the second check found; and main's older text of the same kind that it found in passing (Kazakhstan's
fitted margins with their binding days, a perpetual table's binding row in Lebanon), with every other passage of that
kind in the files that hold them: this log (by a scan for a named day beside an offset or a binding word, each hit read
in its paragraph), `CentralAsia.kt`, `Levant.kt` and proof notes 7f and 7e (each read whole). Main's older text was not
swept as a whole, only those files.

Two more checks read the third commit, and a repair takes what they found. Facts the third commit had rewritten stood
whole in files it had not read, with more of their kind beside them: Qatar's day of Ramadan 1448 with its seconds, and
beside it Dhuhr's binding day and two held-out website days (`Gulf.kt`, `qa-calendarhouse.tsv`, proof 7a); Palembang's

What still stands, and why:
- Tajikistan. R327 keeps the Tajik Council's one Peshin minute as a national clock, so what follows from it stands as a
  rule: the Dhuhr floor's derivation, the towns' lateness after their own Peshin, the limits, and `Generic.kt`'s Dhuhr
  limit reason with its copies in `tj.default.json` and `ProofStamps.kt`. The first two commits took the floor's
  derivation out of this log's Tajik entry, `Generic.kt`'s KDoc and `tj-default.tsv`, and left the eastern towns'
  lateness, the Dhuhr worst and the limits there as bounds; that is stricter than R327 asks, and it stays.
- SBH09's two limit reasons changed in the third commit; their copies in `my.jakim.json` and `ProofStamps.kt` follow
  when the chain runs.
- What the chain generates, read for this: no generated file prints a time or names the day of a worst. The stamps hold
  counts, the checked days as runs, a late histogram in whole minutes, the exact share, each event's worst and the
  limits with their reasons; `ProofStamps.kt` the worsts, the limits and the runs; `ReachLimits.kt` a unit's worst
  across its reach where it passes the unit's own limit; the reach and envelope rows coordinates, paths and notes;
  `QmdbPlaceList.kt` coordinates and kilometres; `own-points-worst.tsv` (`generateOwnPointWorst`) each row's own worst
  per event, in whole minutes, for the gate files `OwnPointWorst.GROUPS` names (the file's header lists them), and
  `CityUnitsTest` holds every such row to it; not every gate file is there (`id-kemenag`, `tj-default`, `ci-default`,
  `kw-awqaf`, `mr-ministry`, `ae-awqaf`, the cautious and safe-default files and a few more are left out). That settles
  most of it, not all. A histogram counts whole minutes, so where every cell of an event at one table falls in the same
  minute, the stamp gives that minute on every day it lists, at every point the gate rows read; and where one table was
  read on one day, its worst, with the rows' points, gives that day's printed minute. Besides the fixed clocks R327
  keeps (`ci.default`'s Dhuhr and Asr, `ru.dumrt`'s Dhuhr), the stamps hold such events at `iq.sunni` (its one day at
  Baghdad), `us.isna` (ICSGV's one day, the Unity Center's sunrise and end of eating), `sy.awqaf` (the Umayyad Mosque's
  Fajr and the held-out cell), `in.karachi` (Jaipur's Asr, the held-out Maghrib and end of eating), `pk.karachi`
  (Chakwal's and Zhob's Asr, Gilgit's sunrise and Maghrib) and `bn.mora` (the held-out Fajr, sunrise and Dhuhr);
  `ProofStamps.kt`, which keeps no histogram, repeats the one-day units and the events whose every cell is on the
  printed minute. `own-points-worst.tsv` does the same row by row. A row that reads one day gives that day's printed
  minute for each event it reads: besides `iq.sunni`'s, `sy.awqaf`'s and ICSGV's, `kg.default`'s Bishkek homepage table,
  whose day its four rows' notes in `kg-default.tsv` name, and `lb.fatwa`'s dated capture and `bn.mora`'s December row,
  whose days their paths name (`bn.mora`'s also its gate file and the reach rows' notes). A worst of 0 gives an event's
  printed minute on every day of the row's table at that point: `uz.board`'s two live days, `eg.esa`'s Kharga, Rafah and
  Taba Novembers and seven more month tables, fifteen of `om.mara`'s 2029 tables, `gb.wifaqul`'s Manchester month,
  `ba.iz`'s Sarajevo, `ma.habous`'s Rabat, `dz.marw`'s Algiers, `be.cautious`'s late quarter, `ps.gaza.awqaf`'s sunrise,
  `us.isna`'s King Fahad Maghrib and `ly.awqaf`'s Bayda sunrise; `ru.dumrt`'s rows at 0 are DUM RT's Dhuhr, a clock R327
  keeps, on its open tables. Libya's one day at Benghazi and Sabha is the owner's own open table. These are the stamp
  writer's, the generators' and the chain's to change, and the owner's call, not a hand's, and are left open.
- An entry whose margins were fitted on one dated sample (`iq.sunni`'s Baghdad, `sy.awqaf`'s Ramadan imsakiya) has every
  margin it did not widen bound on that day, which the gate rows or the stamps name, so its margins in the code give
  that day's printed minutes; and the margins `sy.awqaf` widened, through the excess-plus-5-s step, give the printed
  minutes of its held-out day (the Umayyad Mosque's, the stamp's last), which its `@fitted` line and R214's fit cells
  name. No comment changes that; it is left open with the above.
- A margin is exact to the second on its binding day, so where the days it could be bound on are few, a test of each one
  at the place can pick it out though no passage names it: a small fit set the stamp lists (among them `ps.gaza.awqaf`'s
  six days, `uz.board`'s twenty, `kw.awqaf`'s twenty-five at Kuwait City, `mr.ministry`'s eight days of Ramadan 1444 at
  Nouadhibou for its sunrise, `ae.awqaf`'s one day at ten areas, whose fit values a test asserts, and the website
  captures `qa.calendarhouse`'s Fajr and end of eating were widened to), or a margin set for one season
  (`qa.calendarhouse`'s Ramadan Maghrib, set in Ramadan 1447 and raised by seconds for 1448). Where an earlier margin or
  day was early and the shipped one is never early, the two bounds can leave a single printed minute between them on
  that day (Kharga's Dhuhr in early November 2026, whose minutes ESA's almanac formula and `own-points-worst.tsv` give
  anyway, Qatar's day of Ramadan 1448, vaktija.ba's leap day at Sarajevo). The two repairs dropped the windows the
  checks named; windows of about a month stand elsewhere, in this log and in main's older text (proofs 7c and 7g among
  them). The fit sets, the seasons and the bounds rest on the stamps, the gate rows, the code and the rulings, so text
  alone cannot close them: they are the owner's call, beside the one-day fits, with whether the month windows go too.
- A method rebuilt from the tables to the printed minute is neither one day nor one of the clocks R327 keeps:
  `kg.default`'s rounding conventions on 2023's sun, at points recovered within a printed minute's rounding
  (`CentralAsia.kt`, `KyrgyzLocalities.kt`, `kg-default.tsv`), rebuild the Muftiate's tables to the minute on most days,
  and ESA's almanac noon at its fitted points gives its Dhuhr to within a second (this log's Kharga entry); and each row
  of `own-points-worst.tsv` at 0 above is a table the engine rebuilds to the minute for that event. The owner's call.
- Main's older text outside the files named was not swept. The repair's scan met DUM RT's white nights, named with their
  minutes in proof 7b and in `Russia.kt` (three limit reasons among them); they repeat what DUM RT's open 2026 tables
  (CC BY 4.0, `official/open/RU-DUMRT/`) already hold in the tree.

## 1.7.0 onto main (24 November) — ruling R329

1.7.0 (46) went live on the App Store on 24 November while Play still reviewed it, and the owner chose to put it on
main that day, so its city pages go live on taqwa.world. Its store builds are `release-1.7.0`'s `825be46b3`, cut from
main at `9b7ac2595` and tagged `build-46` and `ios-build-46`; main had since taken the site's watch section
(`53b1ecda0`) and the weekly monitor's proof of 23 November (`55365f5e6`, the archive's `180f5f11`). As 1.6.0 did,
`825be46b3` goes onto main as one commit cherry-picked onto `55365f5e6`, and the archive's `ramadan-final` is merged
onto the archive's main, so the monitor's capture commits stay as they are.

- **The proof files both sides touched.** `gate/my-jakim.tsv` keeps both sides, the monitor's rows first; its note on
  what is left out now says Labuan's 2027 imsak row waits for the next data release (1.7.1). The stamps of `ly.awqaf`,
  `my.jakim` and `tn.inm` and `ProofStamps.kt` are the chain's on the joined tree: each moves from 1.7.0's by the
  monitor's captures (`my.jakim` one table more, WLY02's 2027; `tn.inm` and `ly.awqaf` the days captured) and
  `ly.awqaf` by R329's limit, and no `engineHash` moves.
- **Labuan's 2027 table under 1.7.0's rules.** The monitor gated JAKIM's WLY02 2027 table at its unit; 1.7.0 asks more
  of a zone's tables, and this table now meets it: it is read at the zone's two towns (`my-jakim-cities.tsv`, Labuan and
  Bandar Labuan), carried by the unit's reach rows (`generateReachRows --only my.jakim`: 18 rows in
  `my-jakim-reach.tsv`, 5 in `my-jakim-zones-reach.tsv`), and grown by a capture (four `recipes.tsv` lines for WLY02, as
  WLY01 has). Its 2027 imsak row comes with 1.7.1's data.
- **R329. Across Tripoli's area the sunrise may come up to 4 min before the Awqaf's** (the owner's answer of 24
  November). With the days the monitor captured on 23 November, the review's grids off the reach rows (`CityUnitsTest`)
  find points of Tripoli's area whose sunrise comes up to 4 min before the print on some days, one over class D's 3.
  The sunrise shown there is the earlier of Tripoli's and the place's own, so where the sun rises before it does at
  Tripoli it is the place's; a sunrise before the print is the safe side for the end of Fajr, and the printed days are
  the Awqaf's own, not a fault to excuse, so the limit is widened on Tripoli's unit for sunrise alone (`Maghreb.kt`).
  About's "at most" figures are the starts', so no sentence changes.
